Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):

The first of them begins in Surat Yunus:
{Alif-Lam-Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.} (1)

﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ are three letters. Surat al-Baqarah was preceded by ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾, and ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ appears at the beginning of Surat Al 'Imran; at the beginning of Surat al-A'raf there is ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad﴾, and here ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ appears at the beginning of Surat Yunus. We note that ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾, ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad﴾ and ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ are all names of letters.

Everything that has a name also has a named referent (musamma). My name is al-Sha'rawi, which is correct, and the named referent is my image. When the name is uttered, the image of the named referent comes to mind. When you say "al-sama'" (the sky), the mind goes to "that which is above you." When you say "al-masjid" (the mosque), there comes to mind the enclosed place for prayer.

So there is a difference between the name and the named referent. Every person, whether illiterate or educated, has the capacity for speech, but only one who has been taught pronounces the names of letters. In English, we ask those who are learning it to spell out the names of the letters.

So: everyone—every speaker—knows how to pronounce the named letters, but the one who knows the referents and knows the names is of the class of a teacher. And you know that when you say "akaltu" (I ate), this word is composed of (hamza, kaf, lam, ta').

If some surahs of the Qur'an begin with ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾, these are names of letters, not the referents of letters, and Muhammad (ﷺ) was unlettered, who did not learn. Who, then, taught him the names of the letters?

It is, therefore, a sign that—by the acknowledgment of all—he was unlettered and did not sit before a teacher, and no one told him anything, and then he afterwards pronounced the names of the letters: "Alif, Lam, Mim." If you look at what is pronounced by the names, you will find that fourteen letters are repeated, and they are half of the letters of the alphabet.

And it is remarkable that the description of the letters of the alphabet came after the Qur'an had been revealed.

We have divided them into muhmalah (unpointed/undefined), mahmusah (whispered), raqiqah (thin), and rakhwah (soft) letters. This division took place after the Qur'an was revealed. By induction, you will find that the fourteen letters that come at the beginnings of surahs represent all types of letters: thin (raqiq), emphatic (mufakhkham), voiced (majhur), whispered (mahmus), and elevated (musta'li). God began with them in various forms: sometimes He begins with a single letter: ﴿Sad, by the Qur'an containing the reminder﴾ (Sad), and He says, glorified is He: ﴿Qaf, by the glorious Qur'an﴾ (Qaf), and He says: ﴿Nun, by the pen and what they inscribe﴾ (al-Qalam).

So: three surahs began with a single letter.

And there are surahs that began with a single letter.

And there are surahs that began with two letters, such as ﴿Ta-Ha﴾, ﴿Ya-Sin﴾, ﴿Ta-Sin﴾, ﴿Ha-Mim﴾.

And there are surahs that began with three letters: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾, as with Surat al-Baqarah, Surat Al 'Imran, Surat al-'Ankabut, Surat al-Rum, and Surat al-Sajdah. And there are surahs that began with ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾.

Three surahs agree in Alif and Lam and differ in "Mim and Ra": ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ at the beginning of Surat Yunus, and ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ at the beginning of Surat Yusuf, and ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ at the beginning of Surat Ibrahim, and ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾ at the beginning of Surat al-Hijr. And there are surahs that began with four letters, such as ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad﴾ at the beginning of Surat al-A'raf, and likewise Surat al-Ra'd began with ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Ra﴾.

And there are surahs that began with five letters, such as Surat Maryam: ﴿Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad﴾. Likewise Surat al-Shura began with ﴿Ha-Mim (1) 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf (2)﴾.

Sometimes a letter or two letters at the beginning of a surah are not counted as a verse by themselves, but as part of a verse. There are two surahs that begin with letters and these are counted as a verse, such as ﴿Ta-Ha﴾ and ﴿Ya-Sin﴾. As for Surat al-Naml, it begins with ﴿Ta-Sin﴾ and is not counted as a verse by itself.

So: sometimes the letters are pronounced alone as a complete verse, sometimes the letters are part of a verse, and sometimes five letters come, such as ﴿Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad﴾. All of this shows you that the Qur'an is tawqifi (divinely determined). Its verses did not come in a single pattern; let us be attentive to the fact that the Truth, glorified is He, sent down these letters in this way. The Qur'an's verses will not come in a single pattern; let us be attentive to the fact that the Truth, glorified is He, sent down these letters in this way. Likewise, we find the word "ism" (name) in the Qur'an in ﴿In the name of God﴾, written without an alif (bism), though the alif is an original alif: you pronounce it when you read, but the letter drops in writing. But it does not drop when we write the first verse of Surat al-'Alaq: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created (1)﴾ (al-'Alaq).

Another example: if you survey the word "tabaraka" in the Noble Qur'an, you will find an alif after the ba', and it comes once without an alif. And the word "al-banat" (the daughters) you find once with an alif and once without an alif. All of that is so that we understand that the matter has no mechanical uniformity in writing; for if it were mechanical uniformity in writing, it would have come in one system.

The Truth willed this matter so that the writing of the Qur'an would be a miracle, just as its words and structures were a miracle. Some have said that the Arabs contemporary with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were not people skilled in writing. We say: if they had been without knowledge of writing, they would not have written "bism" without an alif in its place. They knew that the Qur'an must be written as Gabriel (peace be upon him) brought it down to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): a writing determined by revelation (tawqifiyyah), that is, as God, glorified is He, commanded.

Another wonder: all the verses of the Qur'an are built on continuity (wasl). You do not read the end of any verse with sukun (silence); rather, you turn to find the word at the end of any surah vocalized with something other than sukun.

The example is: ﴿Wa-huwa rabbu al-'arsh al-'azim﴾, where the final letter came with kasra, not sukun, so that you read it connected to what follows, and you read it as follows: ﴿Wa-huwa rabbu al-'arsh al-'azim bismillah al-rahman al-rahim﴾.

This vowel indicates that all the verses of the Qur'an are connected to one another. Beware of making the Qur'an ﴿'idin﴾ (fragmented) (8), so that you take some of its verses separated from others; rather, the whole Qur'an is connected. There is no obligatory pause (waqf lazim) in the Qur'an; rather, all the verses are built on continuity. Even if the last word ends with a fatha, you read it in the accusative, and after it ﴿bismillah al-rahman al-rahim﴾. We do not make the final letter sakin in any surah, because it is connected to what follows.

Even in the rule of tajwid: if there is iqlab, we pronounce it as iqlab, and if there is izhar (9), we pronounce it as izhar, because the verses of the Qur'an are built on continuity.

Someone may say: if the Qur'an is built on continuity, then the verses that begin with the letters of the alphabet should have been built according to the method of the alphabet, so we would not say "alif lam mim" but "alim." We say to such a person, in reply: No. The letters of the Qur'an with which the surahs begin must be pronounced as they are: we pronounce "alif," then pause; we read "lam," then pause; we read "mim," then pause, because these letters came this way, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) taught them to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) this way, so that we do not say it is a monotonous speech. Rather, there is wisdom in that with God, whether you understand it now or do not understand it.

The Qur'an was sent down to an Arab nation, and some remained in their disbelief, opposing the Messenger of God and watching for any slip by which they might enter to cast doubt upon the Qur'an. But did you hear, despite the presence of the leading disbelievers, that even one of them said: what is the meaning of ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾?

None of the disbelievers said that, despite their eagerness to bring criticisms against the Qur'an. Rather, they acknowledged the logic of the eloquence of the Noble Qur'an, which indicates that they understood something of ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ by their Arab faculty; if they had understood nothing from it, they would have criticized the Qur'an. But they did not do so.

Also, the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who were people eager for understanding, did you hear that anyone asked the Messenger of God about the meaning of ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾? It did not happen, which indicates that they were moved by its speaker through God's secret in it, not by their minds' understanding of it; for what comes from God has no opposition from the soul, and even if the intellect accepts it, it does not reject it, with the soul at rest with it. We gave an example before, when we said: when the people of Pharaoh slaughtered the sons of the Children of Israel and spared their women, what did the mother of Musa do? God inspired her with what the news of which came in the Qur'an:

﴿And We inspired the mother of Musa: Suckle him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river...﴾ (7) (al-Qasas)

Bring any mother and tell her: when you fear for your child, throw him into the sea. Of course, no mother would carry out this suggestion.

It would have been possible for the mother of Musa to try to hide Musa by any means.

As for casting him into the sea in the expectation that it would save him from slaughter, this is an unimaginable matter. But this was a command from the Merciful by inspiration and revelation, so Satan does not come to oppose it at all; for this reason the Truth, glorified is He, reassured her, because the verse came: ﴿When you fear for him, cast him into the river...﴾ (7) (al-Qasas).

It is as though there was a preparation that teaches her readiness for the matter before it happens, and when the matter came.

﴿When We inspired your mother with what is inspired (38), that you cast him into the chest, then cast him into the river...﴾ (39) (Ta-Ha).

The speech here is speech of haste, because this is the time of execution, and He, glorified is He, reassured her that He issued His commands to the sea to cast him onto the shore: ﴿Let the river cast him onto the bank...﴾ (39) (Ta-Ha).

And the Truth issued His commands to the enemy to take him, so that he would raise him: ﴿The river shall cast him onto the bank, and an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his shall take him...﴾ (39) (Ta-Ha). Thus: what comes from the Merciful never receives any refusal at all.

Likewise, the believer receives ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ through God's secret in it, not through the understanding of his intellect.

I advise whoever wants to read the Qur'an for worship not to occupy himself with the meaning, unlike the one who says "read in order to derive rulings" (ististinbat); for whoever wants to derive rulings is the one who stops at the wording and seeks its meaning. So if you read the Qur'an for worship, read it with God's secret in it, so that you do not confine the Qur'an to your information, and so that you do not take it in a deficient way with your human deficiency. Therefore, in reading for worship we take the wording; not every reader of the Qur'an is a specialist in language, to know the origin of every word, and many of us are unlettered, wanting to worship through the Qur'an. So let him take the Qur'an with God's secret in it.

To take an example from our life—and to God belongs the highest likeness—we find the army assigns it a name: "the password." This word may have no meaning, but no one moves, goes out, or joins the camp unless he says it. Let the word be "adas" (lentil), for example. Whoever knows it knows that it is a means of saving from death, and when a fighter returns to his battalion and says the word "adas," the gate guard knows that he is one of them; as for the one who does not know it, he may be killed. And the one who says it does so with the secret taught to him by the one who gave it to him.

The ancient Arab may understand things from the tawqifi letters at the beginnings of some surahs, and language has parallels in this; for example, when he reads poetry and comes upon a poet who says:

Ala, hibbi bi-sahnika fa-asbihina (Ah, pour out for us in your bowl, and let us drink in the morning)

and says: Ala la yajhalanna ahadun 'alayna, fa-najhala fawqa jahli al-jahilina (Ah, let no one act ignorantly toward us, lest we act ignorantly beyond the ignorance of the ignorant)(17)

What is the meaning of "ala" here, and why did it come? The meaning is clear without it, but the ancient Arab recited this verse and knew that speech is a means of making things understood between speaker and hearer. The speaker is master of the situation in whether he speaks or does not speak, and the hearer is taken by surprise by the speech. If you address your words to the hearer, his mind may be occupied, and until he pays attention to your words, a detail of the speech may escape him; so you alert him to what you said, so that he pays attention to absorb all that you said(18).

So: what prevents God, glorified and exalted is He, from wanting to prepare minds with ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾, so that we listen, and then the verses carrying the method come after that?

And what prevents us from understanding that the unlettered Prophet does not know how to pronounce the names of letters, so that if he pronounces them, it is only after God's teaching him?

And why should we not also understand from it that the means of understanding do not end until the Hour arises? For if they ended with humans, the speech of God would have had its attribute defined by human understanding, whereas He, glorified is He, willed that we draw from the meanings of His words much over the ages. The Qur'an is the speech of God, the speech of God is His attribute, and His attribute is not limited in perfection. If you knew all its significations, you would have confined perfection to knowledge; but the Qur'an has no end(19).

And why should we not understand that the Qur'an, which the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, declared to be the miracle of Muhammad (ﷺ), is of the same kind as that in which his people excelled?

1 Some scholars gathered these disjoined letters that are at the beginnings of surahs and removed the repeated ones, so their total came to fourteen letters, and they formed from them a sentence that came out thus: "Nass qati' hakim lahu sirr" (A decisive, wise text that has a secret).
Scholars have differed about the meaning of these letters in several opinions:
1- That they are among what God has kept to Himself in knowledge.
2- That they indicate the names of the surahs.
3- That they indicate the names and attributes of God, the Exalted: the alif is the key of God, the lam is the key of His name (al-Latif), the mim is the key of His name (al-Majid)..

2 These letters have attributes according to the manner of their pronunciation; among them are attributes that have opposites, such as: (jahr – hams) – (shiddah and rakhawah) – (isti'la') – (infitah, itbaq) – (isma', idhlaq). As an example of this: hams is the weakening of the voice when pronouncing the letters, in which there is the letter kha'; these are: fa', ha', ta', ha', shin, sad, sin, kaf, ta', and gathering them is their saying: "fahathahu shakhsun sakata" (a person struck him and he fell silent). Whatever is outside these letters are "jahri letters," that is, there is strength in pronouncing them. See the details of this in the book "Hidayat al-Qari ila Tajwid Kalam al-Bari" by Shaykh 'Abd al-Fattah al-Sayyid al-Marsafi (pp. 79–93), may God forgive him and have mercy on him..

3 Tawqifi means that God caused Muhammad (ﷺ) to know something in the Qur'an: the openings of the surahs, the separations between verses, and the arrangement of the surahs in the mushaf. This was not left to the Messenger's (ﷺ) ijtihad, nor to the ijtihad of the Companions; rather it was a communication from God to him through the tongue of Gabriel..

4 The word (bism) occurs in the Qur'an 4 times in God's saying: {Read in the name of your Lord who created (1)} (al-'Alaq), and ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Great﴾ in three places (al-Waqi'ah: 74/96) and (al-Haqqah: 52).
The word (bism) without the alif occurs three times in the Qur'an (al-Fatihah), and His saying: ﴿And he said: Embark therein; in the name of God is its course and its mooring...(41)﴾ (Hud), and ﴿Indeed it is from Sulayman, and indeed it is: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate (30)﴾ (al-Naml),
in addition to all the places of the basmalah at the beginnings of the surahs of the Qur'an, if we count the basmalah as a verse at their beginning..

5 The word "tabaraka" occurs in the Qur'an 9 times, of which two places are without alif, in His saying: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour (78)﴾ (al-Rahman), and His saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion...(1)﴾ (al-Mulk). As for the other seven places, they are: ﴿Blessed is God, Lord of the worlds (54)﴾ (al-A'raf), ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators (14)﴾ (al-Mu'minun), (al-Furqan (1) (10) (61)), Ghafir (64), (al-Zukhruf (85))..

6 The word "al-banat" occurs in the Qur'an 12 times, of which three places are without alif, namely: ﴿And they attributed to God partners, the jinn, though He created them, and they invented for Him sons and daughters without knowledge...(100)﴾ (al-An'am), His saying: ﴿And they attribute to God daughters—glory be to Him—while for themselves what they desire (57)﴾ (al-Nahl), and His saying: ﴿Or has He daughters while you have sons? (39)﴾ (al-Tur).

7 This is an important science of the sciences of the Qur'an, the science of the drawn script (rasm al-khatt). Scholars have spoken of it and explained its subtleties, and they insist on not abandoning what the earliest predecessors settled on in the rules of the Qur'anic orthography, and that this orthography has hidden wisdoms about which scholars have spoken. See: al-Burhan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an by al-Zarkashi (1/376–431) and al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an by al-Suyuti (4/145–166).

8 'Idin: that is, scattered parts; from it is His saying: ﴿Those who have made the Qur'an into 'idin (91)﴾ (al-Hijr). The commentators mentioned other opinions in the verse, among them that the People of the Book divided it into parts, believing in some and disbelieving in others..

9 That is: you find the endings of verses vocalized and not silent, and likewise the endings of surahs; otherwise there is an obligatory pause within some verses, such as His saying: ﴿Only those who hear respond; and the dead, God will raise them; then to Him they will be returned (36)﴾ (al-An'am).

10 Izhar and iqlab: two rules of Qur'anic tajwid when pronouncing the sakin nun or tanwin.

**1.** As for **al-izhar** (clear pronunciation, *al-izhar*): when one of the throat letters (*al-huruf al-halqiyyah*, the letters whose articulation point is the throat) follows a sukun nun or tanwin, clear pronunciation is obligatory. These letters are the hamza, the ha, the ha', the ghayn, and the kha'. Thus, when the sukun nun or tanwin meets one of these letters, it must be pronounced clearly.

**2.** As for **al-iqlab** (conversion, *al-iqlab*): this is when a ba' comes after a sukun nun or tanwin, so the nun or tanwin is converted into a mim, with the nasalization (*al-ghunnah*) being clearly pronounced. An example is ﴿Tell Me...﴾ (Al-Baqarah) and ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ (At-Taghabun, 4).

**11.** It is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "If religion were based on opinion, the underside of the khuff would be more deserving of wiping than its upper side. But I have seen the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wiping over the upper surface of his khuffs." Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (123), and by al-Daraqutni in his Sunan (1/199).

**12.** **Istihya' al-nisa'** (sparing the women): that is, letting them remain alive. From this is the words of Allah, ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a group among them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters﴾ (Al-Qasas, 4). This was done as a humiliation of the Children of Israel, a belittling of them, and out of fear that the boy whom he had feared would emerge among them, and would be the cause of his destruction and the loss of his rule.

**13.** The root **wahy** (revelation) occurs in the Qur'an in 75 verses. See *al-Mu'jam al-Mufahras li-Alfaz al-Qur'an al-Karim*, pp. 746–747.
Linguistically, *al-wahy* means: indication, writing, a written message, inspiration, hidden speech, and anything you convey to another; it also refers to a sound among people. *Awha ilayhi* means he sent him and inspired him. It also means informing in secret, sending, commanding, indicating, gesturing, and emitting a sound little by little. Wahy is used for other than God's informing His prophets, as in His words, ﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee...﴾ (An-Nahl, 68). The wahy here means inspiration. As for the meaning of informing, it is the revelation specific to the prophets and messengers.

**14.** **Al-tabut**: the chest (box).

**15.** **Al-yamm**: this is applied to water that is salty, or to a large river of sweet water. What is meant here is the Nile River in Egypt. **Sahil al-yamm**: its bank.

**16.** He is Amr ibn Kulthum, Abu al-Aswad, a pre-Islamic poet of the first rank. He was born in the north of the Arabian Peninsula, led his people Taghlib while still a youth, lived a long life, and died around 40 years before the Hijra. Among his most famous poems is his Mu'allaqah (*al-A'lam* by al-Zirikli, 5/84).

**17.** These verses are from the Mu'allaqah of Amr ibn Kulthum. Its verses number 103, and it is in the al-Wafir meter.

**18.** Here, **"ala"** (ألا) is an opening particle that expresses alerting and indicates the certainty of what follows. It has four other meanings: wishing, interrogation for negation, urging, exhortation, reproach, and denial.

**19.** He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say, "If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as replenishment"﴾ (Al-Kahf, 109). And He says: ﴿And if every tree on earth were a pen, and the sea were replenished after it by seven more seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ (Luqman, 27).

Then the Almighty says:
﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people, and give good news to those who believe that they will have a sure standing before their Lord"? The disbelievers said, "This is indeed a clear sorcerer."﴾ (2)

What, then, is so strange (1) that Allah revealed to a man from among you that he should convey to you Allah's warning and His good tidings? What is it that you find astonishing? And where is the point of wonder in it?

The specification of this wonder is what the context mentioned at the end of the previous surah, that:
﴿A messenger has come to you from among yourselves...﴾ (128) (al-Tawbah). That is: from among humans, from among the Arabs, from among your own tribes, and from among yourselves, one whose whole character you know. So what is strange about Allah sending him as a messenger to you? You had entrusted him with your affairs before the revelation came down from Allah. It is as if you had respected his noble nature, and as if you had, in many matters, accepted from him what he brought of rulings.

The proof of this is that when you disagreed over the building of the Ka'bah, and every tribe said, "We have a better right to place with our own hands the most sacred thing in the Ka'bah, which is the Black Stone," the tribes then fell into dispute. They agreed only to make the first person to enter the judge. Allah willed that the first to enter should be Muhammad ibn Abdullah. How then could Muhammad ibn Abdullah resolve this problem, when no revelation had yet come down to him? It was the natural disposition (fitrah) that made him fit to receive Allah's revelation afterwards. So what did he do to end the dispute?

He brought a cloak, placed the stone upon the cloak, and then said to each tribe: "Each of you take hold of an edge of the cloak and carry the stone to its place." That is the sound natural disposition. We also see our master Abu Bakr when they said to him, as he was returning from the journey he was undertaking: "Your companion has claimed to be a prophet." He said: "If he has said it, then he has spoken the truth."

From what events did Abu Bakr's judgment come? Did he hear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a miraculous speech? Did he hear the Qur'an from him? No. Rather, he affirmed him the very moment he announced that he was a messenger. For he had tested him in everything and found him truthful, and had tested him in everything and found him trustworthy. Muhammad would not be truthful among humans and then lie about Allah.

Likewise Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Such-and-such comes to me, and I fear that such-and-such may be the case." She explained to him that the premises of his life did not suggest that Allah would forsake him, disgrace him, or give the jinn power over him: "You join the ties of kinship, you bear the burdens of others, you help the destitute, you support the wronged, and Allah will never disgrace you." (3) Thus Lady Khadijah became the first jurist (faqih) to deduce rulings in Islam.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people...﴾ means: the wonder is that such a thing should come from them, and the Qur'an marvels how this wonder could come from them. Since it marvels at how this could come from them, it is logical that they should not have been astonished, because you are beyond the level of what you know of humans. It is like when you see a beautiful piece of craftsmanship and say, "How beautiful this craft is!" and wonder, "What made this craft so beautiful to an unimaginable degree?"

You say that because the craft has reached such a level of beauty that you cannot believe anyone present could make it. An example of this: you find someone saying, "How beautiful the sky is!" while he is marveling at something that exceeds his imagination. Someone may also marvel at something ugly that should never have occurred to his mind. That is why the Qur'an says: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah...﴾ (28) (al-Baqarah).

That is: tell us, how did you accept disbelief for yourselves? Because disbelief is a strange matter that contradicts the natural disposition.

Here the Almighty says: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed to a man from among them...﴾ (2) (Yunus).

Here we ask: how do you marvel, when We have brought you a messenger from among yourselves: ﴿grievous to him is what distresses you, anxious over you, to the believers full of kindness and mercy﴾ (128) (al-Tawbah).

Is this not what is required in a guide? So how can you marvel? (5)

Your wonder shows that your insight is unable to judge things. It was not right that the Messenger should be received with wonder, and we marvel at this wonder of yours.

When you marvel at wonder, you nullify the marvel itself.

﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed...﴾ (2) (Yunus): that is, Our revealing to a man from among you was strange in your eyes, though it should not have been a strange matter, because it is a logical and natural matter.

Then what is revelation (wahy)? We have already explained that revelation is informing in a hidden manner. There is also clear informing, such as when you say to your son: "My son, listen to this and do that."

That is clear informing. And there is informing in a hidden manner: for example, a guest enters your house, and then your servant forgets to greet him, so you signal to the servant with a gesture that means he should hasten to offer the guest greeting, such as refreshments or sweets. In this way you have informed your servant in a hidden manner.

The Almighty revealed to inanimate things. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its violent shaking (1), and the earth brings forth its burdens (2), and man says, "What is wrong with it?" (3), on that day it will report its news (4), because your Lord has revealed to it (5)﴾ (al-Zalzalah). That is: He, glorified and exalted is He, has informed it in a hidden way, and it has understood in a manner we do not know.

He reveals to animals too, for He says: ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee...﴾ (68) (al-Nahl). You cannot say, "I heard Allah revealing to the bee," because revelation is informing in a hidden manner. He is most knowing of the manner in which this revelation occurred, and the bee understood from Him, and it is no concern of yours. So do not ask about the mode of this revelation: ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee: take for yourselves dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they build (68)﴾ (al-Nahl).

That is: they understood from Allah through what He placed in them of instincts.

He, glorified is He, reveals to the angels, for He says: ﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels...﴾ (12) (al-Anfal).

He, glorified is He, also reveals to non-prophets, as He revealed to the mother of Musa: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa: suckle him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river...﴾ (7).

And He, glorified is He, revealed to all the messengers.

So He, glorified is He, reveals to inanimate things, reveals to animals, reveals to angels, reveals to righteous non-prophets, and reveals to prophets and messengers.

Revelation, as informing in a hidden manner, requires an informant, who is Allah, the Almighty, and a recipient, who is either the earth, or the bee, or the angels, or some righteous non-prophets, or the messengers and prophets.

Revelation may also come from other than Allah. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorated speech in deception...﴾ (112) (al-An'am). So the devils inform one another in a hidden manner.

The Almighty says: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you...﴾ (163) (al-Nisa'): the one to whom it was revealed is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this is a revelation specific to the Messenger. So do not say, "I did not hear what was revealed to Muhammad, and I do not know how the revelation came down," for Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and conveyed to him that he should announce what had been revealed to him. And if you yourself were able to hear revelation from Jibril, then what need would there be for sending a messenger?

The high energy and power sent to the one receiving revelation requires a capacity to bear it. We give the example of a human who transmits energy from a high, strong source to a weak source: he does not transmit the energy from the strong to the weak all at once, or else the weak would not be able to bear that energy coming to it from the strong. Therefore we bring a transformer that bears the energy of the strong and then transmits to the weak what suits its capacity. An example of this is our purchase of an electrical transformer when we transmit electricity from a high-voltage energy source to another weak source of low voltage, such as the small lamp you light in the house at night so that it gives light in the appropriate degree, lest we collide with things, which we colloquially call "wannasa." So the function of the transformer is to receive from the strong energy source in order to shine upon the weak energy source.

Now, if Allah, the Almighty, is the one who reveals to the Messenger, and the Messenger is a human who cannot receive directly from Allah, then there must be an intermediary that has been elevated to the degree that allows it to receive from Allah and that can meet with humans. This is the characteristic of the angel.

Despite this, the effort and fatigue afflicted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the beginning of his receiving revelation. He (ﷺ) would sweat until sweat poured from his forehead, and when the revelation departed from him he would say: "Cover me, cover me!" (11) and he would tremble.

The Companions used to say: when revelation came down upon the Messenger of Allah while he was sitting, and his knee might be upon the thigh of one of the Companions, that Companion would feel a weight on his leg from the intensity of the pressure of the Messenger's knee. And if revelation came down while the Messenger was riding a mount, the mount would groan beneath him.

So revelation would exhaust the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and after the fatigue had lifted from him, the sweetness of what had been revealed to him would remain, so he would long for revelation again.

Allah willed that the Prophet (ﷺ) should long for revelation, so revelation paused for a period of time. When the Prophet longed for revelation, that meant he had charged himself with a receptive energy to receive this revelation with its burden.

To Allah belongs the highest likeness always. Consider the effort you exert on a journey to someone you love, during rain, with the ground muddy and full of thorns, yet you complete the journey without paying attention to the exhaustion and fatigue in it.

Allah willed to make His Messenger desire revelation, despite its effort, because it is the meeting of an angel with humans. This meeting takes two forms. Either the angel is transformed into a human state, and this form involves no strain upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because the transformation takes place at the upper level, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remains as he is. For example, Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while some Companions were with him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "What is faith? What is Islam? What is excellence (ihsan)?" Then the questioner vanished, and the Companions asked the Messenger of Allah about this questioner. He said: "This was Jibril; he came to you to teach you the matters of your religion." (16)

This is the first form of revelation, and the transformation in it was on the side of the sending, so there is no hardship in it for the Prophet (ﷺ).

As for the second form, it involved hardship for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because the angel remains in his own nature, while the transformation occurs in Muhammad (ﷺ), and the transformation required a chemical process that afflicted him with exertion, so after the revelation departed he would say: "Cover me."

Allah willed to be gentle with His Messenger, so revelation paused for a period of time. The disbelievers among the Arabs said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him." This was stupidity on their part, because they had acknowledged that Muhammad was a lord. Since they had acknowledged it, their non-belief was arrogance and stupidity. They wanted by that to attribute deficiency to Muhammad (ﷺ), so they said: "Allah has forsaken Muhammad."

Allah willed that revelation cease from Muhammad (ﷺ) for this period, in order to expose them before themselves and before others, so that their intentions would be revealed and their lack of insight and their absence of sound logic would be proven. For when they acknowledged that Muhammad was a lord, they should have appealed to their minds to realize that they had admitted divinity, but they wanted by this acknowledgment to attribute deficiency to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

If we were to refer them to their minds, to the universe in which they lived, and to the material phenomena perceptible to them, they would know that events must have a time and a place, because an event requires a time and a place, and if no event exists, there is no time or place.

That is why I always say to whoever asks: "Where was Allah?" I say to him: you bring the question of "where" from time, and the question of "place" from space, and this cannot occur except with the existence of an event. And since Allah is not an event, no time determines Him, and no place contains Him, because time was, and space was with Him. Events belong to humans: they are the ones who settle in place, and time passes over them.

The time in which any event occurs is called "a time-container" (zarf zaman) (20), and

1 A strange thing: that which is not familiar to people. A human only marvels at a thing when its position is great in his eyes and its cause is hidden from him. The polytheists marveled at matters their minds could not comprehend, so the Qur'an needed to negate wonder from this matter and to demonstrate the opposite of what was in the minds of these polytheists. The matters were:
The matter of Allah's oneness, glorified is He, and they said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one god? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ (5) (Sad).
The matter of sending a man from among them, that is, a human, and they said: ﴿And they marveled that a warner came to them from among themselves...﴾ (4) (Sad).
The matter of resurrection, and they said: ﴿And if you marvel at their saying, "When we have become dust, shall we indeed be in a new creation?"...﴾ (5) (al-Ra'd).

2 Muhammad (ﷺ) was 35 years old at that time, that is, five years before his mission. The tribes of Quraysh had disputed over who would place the Black Stone in its position, and they prepared for fighting. The Banu Abd al-Dar and the Banu Adi pledged to die, and they placed their hands into a bowl filled with blood. The matter remained like this for four or five nights.

Ibn Ishaq narrates in the Sirah (1/197) that Quraysh accepted Muhammad's arbitration in this matter: "Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah said: O assembly of Quraysh, make whoever enters first through the door of this mosque the one who judges between you in what you dispute." They did so, and the first to enter upon them was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When they saw him they said: "This is the trustworthy one; we are pleased. This is Muhammad." When he reached them and they informed him of the matter, he (ﷺ) said: "Bring me a cloth." It was brought, and he took the corner stone (i.e., the Black Stone) and placed it in it with his own hand. Then he said: "Let each tribe take hold of a side of the cloth, then lift it all together." They did so, until they reached its position, and he placed it there with his own hand, and then built upon it.

3 The hadith of the beginning of revelation from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3, 6, and other places), and by Muslim in his Sahih (160).
With this statement, Lady Khadijah had summarized the Messenger's mission in words: living among people's troubles, supporting the oppressed and helping the deprived, so that she bears the burdens of all.
Joining the ties of kinship is elevating the wombs and relatives, and it is the warmth of humanity in which society lives with the feeling of the community and the tenderness of brotherhood. Supporting the wronged is the balance of justice, and the saying is Islam. Thus the words of the Shaykh are confirmed: this is a matter from which the message of Islam is deduced from the state of the Messenger before the completion of revelation.

4 Istinbat (deduction) in jurisprudence (fiqh): the jurist's extraction of the legal rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah) from the depths of the evidences through his own effort (ijtihad) and understanding. From it is His saying: ﴿...those of them who would investigate it would know it...﴾ (83) (al-Nisa'). Linguistically, istinbat means extracting water from the bottom of a well when it has been dug.

5 Ibn Abbas narrated, concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse, that when Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger, the disbelievers denied it and said: "Allah is greater than that His messenger should be a human like Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse. Among what the polytheists said was: "Did Allah find no one to send except the orphan of Abu Talib?" See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi (p. 152), Tafsir al-Qurtubi (4/3232), and Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/406).

6 al-Zajjaj said: it is permissible that it was named nahl (bee) because Allah, mighty and majestic, gives people (nahl) the honey that comes out of its bellies.

7 Zukhruf: adornment. The intended meaning here is deception and falsification, and "zukhruf al-qawl ghurura" means: a fine speech through adorning falsehood.

8. Al-ghurur (deception): whatever deceived you, whether a human, a devil, or something else. Al-ghurur also means the Devil, as in ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ (Luqman 33). Al-ghurur also means falsehoods. It is permissible for al-ghurur to be the plural of gharr, like shahid and shuhud. Al-ghurur also means this world and its enjoyments. And al-ghurur means enticing someone with a false promise and wishful thinking, as in ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord?﴾ (al-Infitar 6) and ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾ (Luqman 33). Al-ghurur also means trickery and making evil and sins appear attractive. "Gharrara bi-nafsihi wa-malihi taghriran wa-tughratan" means he exposed himself and his wealth to ruin without knowing it. Al-gharar means danger. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the sale of gharar, which is like selling fish in water or birds in the air. Al-taghrir means driving oneself into gharar.

9. On the authority of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "O Messenger of Allah, how does the revelation come to you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and it is the hardest on me. Then it departs from me, and I have retained what it said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2) and Muslim (2333).

10. Tafassada al-araq means the sweat flowed from his forehead. Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "I saw him when the revelation came down to him on a very cold day, and it departed from him, and his forehead was dripping with sweat." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2) and Muslim (2333) from the hadith of Aisha; the wording is al-Bukhari's.

11. The meaning of al-tazmil here is seeking protection and removing the fear, terror, and trembling that struck his body because of what he saw, by wrapping his body in garments and covering it. Zammala al-shay' means he concealed it. Zammalahu fi thawbihi means he wrapped it in his garment. Al-tazammul means wrapping oneself in a garment; one who has tazammala with his clothes has covered himself. In the hadith about the martyrs of Uhud: "they wrapped them in their garments" (wa-mallawhum fi thiyabihim), meaning they wrapped them in them. Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/431) from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Tha'laba.

12. Ta'utt al-naqah minhu means the she-camel groaned under the weight of the riders. On the authority of Asma bint Yazid, she said: "I was holding the halter of al-Adba', the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when al-Ma'idah was revealed to him in its entirety, and the camel nearly broke its neck from its weight." Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (6/455).

13. Yusra 'anhu al-ta'ab means the fatigue leaves him, that is, it goes away from him.

14. Futur al-wahy means the revelation stopped. Al-fatrah is the period between two prophets. In al-Sihah, it is the time between each two messengers of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, during which the message was interrupted. From this is the statement of Allah, Exalted: ﴿O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you after a lapse in the messengers﴾ (al-Ma'idah 19).

15. Ard mawhalah means land that has become muddy, that is, struck by mud, which is thin clay produced by the effect of rain or water falling on the ground.

16. On the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, he said: "One day while we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a man appeared to us with very white clothes and very black hair. No sign of travel was visible on him, and none of us knew him. He sat down before the Prophet (ﷺ), leaned his knee against his knee, placed his palms on his thighs, and said: 'O Muhammad, tell me about Islam.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Islam is that you testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer, give zakat, fast in Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House if you are able to reach it.' He said: 'You have spoken truly.' He said: 'We were amazed that he asked him and then confirmed his answer.' He said: 'Tell me about faith.' He said: 'That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in divine decree, its good and its evil.' He said: 'You have spoken truly.' He said: 'Tell me about excellence (ihsan).' He said: 'That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you....'" The hadith is recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (50) and Muslim in his Sahih (8). The point of evidence in the hadith is that Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in human form, and this was not difficult for him (ﷺ).

17. On the authority of Jundub al-Bajali, he said: "Gabriel was delayed in coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the polytheists said: 'Muhammad has been abandoned.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it covers, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ (al-Duha 1-3)." Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih (1797) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (3345), who said: "a hasan sahih hadith." Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4/522) cited from the chain that Muslim and al-Tirmidhi used to Jundub a version with the wording: "The polytheists said: 'Muhammad has been abandoned by his Lord.'"

18. Al-salaf means exceeding the limit in claims and arrogance.

19. Qalaytuhu means I detested him to the utmost degree, so I abandoned him. Al-qalay means hatred.

20. Al-zarf is the time or place in which an event occurred. The grammarians call it "al-maf'ul fihi" (the object of location), meaning that the event or action has occurred (or occurs, or will occur) at a certain time and in a certain place.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 3 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, arranging [all] matter. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then will you not remember?﴾ (10:3):

After this, the Truth turns away from relating the astonishment [of the disbelievers] that Allah revealed to His Messenger, and likewise the matter of accusing the Messenger of sorcery. It directs them to a matter greater than this one, and that they should have seen the wonder in something other than the revelation to the Messenger (ﷺ).

That is: you should have contemplated this wondrous matter, which is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and reflected on their craftsmanship(1), and on how they came into being.

If Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and made you, O human, to arrive into a world, and prepared it for you, making it your companion, then you should have turned your attention to this matter before anything else.

We have previously given an example and said: Suppose a person boarded an airplane, then its fuel ran out and it crashed in the desert, and salvation was decreed for him. He looked around and found no water, no food, nor any sign of the means of life. Then sleep overcame him. When he awoke from his sleep, he found a table upon which were the finest foods and the finest drinks. Would he not ask himself, before he eats and drinks: Who prepared and brought all this food and all this drink?

This universe has been prepared for you, O human. Would it not be right for you to think about the One who prepared this universe for you, and created for you everything that is within your reach and capability, and subjected all of that to you? The Truth has informed you: Did you not see that He created the heavens, and created the earth, and the sun, and the stars? When this message reached you, either it is true, so you should carry out what the Creator has commanded; or if this speech is not true, then who created [all of this]? If there were another god besides Him who created the universe and heard such a message, and did not move to demonstrate the truth of the matter, then that other would not deserve to be a god(2).

As long as no opponent to Him, glorified is He, has appeared, then He is the Creator; for a claim, if it comes from one party and no opponent to it has appeared, then its claimant is the one who issued it, until an opponent appears to it.

We have also given an example and said: Suppose a group of your friends came to visit you, then they left from your home, and you found a wallet and did not know to whom it belonged. Then you sent your servant to ask those who had been visiting you, and each of them said: My wallet has not been lost from me, except for one who said: Yes, it is my wallet. Thus the ownership of this wallet is established for this speaker, until the opposite is proven.

The situation here is like this: when the Truth, glorified is He, informed us that He created the heavens, the earth, the sun, the moon, and the stars, and placed in the earth the provision of mankind, and no one opposed Him, then it is necessary that we affirm that He is the Creator.

If Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has created for you this entire universe subjugated(3) [to you], would you not leave Him the freedom to choose a messenger to you? Then what is the basis for objection?

The Truth exposes their logic when they said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a man of importance from one of the two cities?﴾ (43:31). So then: they have acknowledged that the Qur'an is beyond reproach, but they are resentful and live in distress, because this Qur'an has come through the hand of an orphan of Abu Talib(4).

The Truth also exposes them, bringing what came from their own tongues: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky...﴾ (8:32). And they did not say: O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then guide us.

So the enmity is toward the Messenger of Allah, and it is a logical enmity; for each one of you, if he owned something precious and dear to him, would find no trustworthy person for it except Muhammad.

So then: why do you not deceive yourselves on the matter of entrusting Muhammad with precious things, even if you do not believe in his truthfulness? Why did you entrust him with your treasures? Is he not Muhammad ibn Abdullah, who emigrated and left Ali ibn Abi Talib behind, so that he could return the trusts to their owners?

So then: neither Muhammad falls below the level of prophethood and trustworthiness, nor does the Qur'an fall below that level, by your own testimony; for your testimony is the statement and the deed.

Here the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days...﴾ (10:3), and in another place in the Qur'an He, glorified is He, says: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ (40:57).

Since this wondrous creation has come from Him, then the actions that are less than that must be acceptable from Him, glorified and exalted is He, and must be for some wisdom. Let us have you judge by yourselves, while you say: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a man of importance from one of the two cities?﴾ (43:31).

So then: there is no doubt on your part that the Qur'an is beyond criticism; rather you criticize the matter that it came through the hand of Muhammad (ﷺ), and you wished that the Qur'an had come through another whom you would accept. In this matter you are not logical, because you want to interfere in the distribution of Allah's mercy and in His sending down of revelation upon whom you wish, rather than upon whom He, glorified is He, wills.

By this you want to control the supreme mercy of Allah in choosing a messenger to convey His message to you, and you forget that in this world you do not distribute the provisions; therefore the Truth says: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord?...﴾ (43:32).

If you want to distribute the mercy of Allah, then know this statement from Allah: ﴿It is We who have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world...﴾ (43:32).

This simple matter, the distribution of livelihood in this world, is something in which the Truth, glorified is He, has exercised control(6). So how could you then hope to distribute the supreme matter, which is the supreme mercy of Allah in sending a messenger?

The Truth, glorified is He, says in the verse about which we are speaking [in these reflections]: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah﴾.

When you hear the word "rabb" (lord), the mind turns to creation and to nurturing. That is why we use this word and say: "So-and-so is the rabb (lord) of this family," meaning he is the one who takes charge of raising it. The word "Rabb," in its absolute sense, refers to Allah(7). He is the Creator who brought into existence from non-existence and sustained from non-existence(8), and by this attribute He is the Lord of all His creation: the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient.

Since Allah, glorified is He, is the Lord of all creation, He is also the Provider for all His creatures. He is the One who called His creatures into this world, and He is the One who gives every creature the provision that Allah has decreed for it. He, glorified is He, commands the laws(9) and causes of the universe to give to it or not to give. If a person plants the land and cultivates it well, Allah, glorified is He, gives the command to the earth to yield provision to this creature.

And every creature that takes the means, Allah grants it success in those means.

I always say to those who see the progress of disbelievers in worldly affairs, and ask: Why do the disbelievers advance in worldly affairs while we fall behind? I say to them: They have taken from the bounty of lordship (rubūbiyya) through the means, and you have not taken from the bounty of lordship. You, O Muslims, must take the means, which are the bounty of lordship, so that the disbeliever does not outpace you to them, and do not sit in the position of spectators; rather it is incumbent upon you to outpace the disbelievers to the bounty of lordship.

As for the bounty of divinity (ulūhiyya), it is that a person acknowledges that Allah is the one truly worthy of worship, and that He is the one obeyed in "do" and "do not do." This bounty is not attained except by one who believes in Him.

So then: Allah is the Lord of all, but He is the God of those who believe in Him. Thus there is a distinction between the bounty of God, which is the method embodied in "do" and "do not do," and the bounty of lordship, which is embodied in material matters, and which is shared among all people: the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. And when the disbeliever takes the means well, he reaps their results.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof, but he has not in the Hereafter any share﴾ (42:20).

So then: it is obligatory upon the believers to receive the bounty of lordship by taking the means well, so that they reap the result, and so that the people of disbelief do not get ahead of them; for when the disbeliever outpaces you in taking the means, he may exploit that to impose upon you what endangers your religion.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah...﴾ (10:3). That is: the One who nurtured is the One who obligated, and you must listen to His method.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿who created the heavens and the earth in six days...﴾ (10:3). The phrase ﴿six days﴾ appears in all the verses of the Qur'an that speak about the duration of the creation of the earth and the heavens. But there is a verse that gives details, and it appears from its style that the creation took eight days, and it is in Surah Fussilat: ﴿Say: Do you disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days(10) and attribute to Him equals(11)? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed within it firmly set mountains upon it and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance(12) in four days, equal for those who ask.﴾ (41:9-10). These are six days.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly." So He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.﴾ (41:11-12).

Thus the total becomes eight days. This is the superficial understanding; for the verses of summary all speak of the creation in six days. You know that every summary is explained by its details, except for the number, for its details are carried over to its summary. The earth was created by Allah in two days, and He placed upon it firm mountains and blessed it, and every subsequent creation is a completion of the first. So the first two days are included within the four days, and the remaining creation took the last two days, and the total became six days.

So then: time is the completion of time. That is why you find that a day on the planet Venus is longer than its year; for its year, by Earth's timekeeping, is two hundred and twenty-five days, while the length of its day by Earth's timekeeping is two hundred and forty-four days.

So then: the day on the planet Venus is longer than its year. The secret of that is that the planet Venus follows a rotation that differs in speed from the speed of the rotation which the Earth follows: the rotation of Venus around itself is slow, and its orbit around the sun is fast.

So then: every existing thing has a system.

And what, then, is the day? In our reckoning, the day is the Earth's rotation around itself, a rotation in which night and day occur... But we find that the Noble Qur'an uses the word "day" and separates it from "night," saying: ﴿Travel therein by night and day, safe﴾ (34:18). Here the Truth made the day for light and toil, and the night for darkness and rest. And astronomical reckoning calls night and day together a day.

The Qur'an makes clear that there is a day for this world and a day for the Hereafter, and the day of this world is what we reckon from one sunrise to another sunrise. Likewise there is a day with Allah which, by the reckoning of this world, is equal to a thousand years of what mankind counts: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ (22:47).

The Truth, glorified is He, says in another place: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years﴾ (70:4).

So then: times are many and varied, and differ from one measure to another, and from one planet to another. What Allah has shown us in the Qur'an about times indicates their difference, not contradiction or conflict(17).

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says in the verse about which we are reflecting: ﴿then established Himself above the Throne﴾. The scholars paused for a long time at the word "istawa" (established/rose) (18), and they surveyed the entire Qur'an to count it in the Book of Allah; they found it has come in twelve surahs: al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, Yunus, al-Ra'd, Ta-Ha, al-Furqan, al-Qasas, al-Sajdah, Fussilat, al-Fath, al-Najm, and al-Hadid.

The first surah in which the mention of Allah's establishment upon the Throne appears is al-A'raf. The Truth says: {Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. He causes the night to cover the day, pursuing it swiftly, and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds} (7:54).

1 The Noble Qur'an establishes, through verses that call to reflection and contemplation upon the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: {Do they not look at the camels, how they are created? And at the sky, how it is raised? And at the mountains, how they are erected? And at the earth, how it is spread out? So remind; you are but a reminder} (88:17-21).

2 The Lord of Might, glorified and exalted is He, has emphasized this meaning in many verses, saying in Surah al-Naml: ﴿Is He who created the heavens and earth and sent down for you water from the sky, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of delight? It was not for you to cause their trees to grow. Is there a god with Allah? Rather, they are a people who make equals [with Him]. Is He who made the earth a stable place and placed within it rivers and placed upon it firmly set mountains and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a god with Allah? Rather, most of them do not know. Is He who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you successors upon the earth? Is there a god with Allah? Little do you remember. Is He who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea and sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him. Is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and who provides for you from the heaven and earth? Is there a god with Allah? Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."﴾ (27:60-64). He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Had there been within them any gods except Allah, they would have been ruined...﴾ (21:22).

3 Musakhkhar (subjugated): that is, made submissive and subdued for the service of human beings. Among His words, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the One who created the heavens and earth and sent down from the sky water and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you, and subjected for you the ships to sail through the sea by His command, and subjected for you the rivers. And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, constant [in their courses], and subjected for you the night and day﴾ (14:32-33).

4 Among what the polytheists said about this: "Allah did not find anyone to send except an orphan of Abu Talib." So this was revealed: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man among them, "Warn the people..."?﴾ (10:2). Narrated by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3232).

5 By the two cities here is meant Makkah and al-Ta'if. The statements differed in identifying these two men. It was said: they are al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. It was said: they are Umayr ibn Amr ibn Mas'ud and Utbah ibn Rabi'ah. It was said: Ibn Abd Yalil. The intended meaning is a great man from whichever of the two towns he was. See Ibn Kathir (4/127).

6 From Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has distributed your characters among you, just as He has distributed your provisions among you. And indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives the world to whomever He loves and to whomever He does not love, but He does not give faith except to the one He loves." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/387), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (1/33) (2/447) (4/165), and he authenticated it and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Al-Haythami attributed it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/228) to Ahmad and said: its narrators are trustworthy, though there is disagreement about some of them.

7 Rabb in the language is applied to: the owner, the master, the manager, the nurturer, the guardian, the bestower of blessings, and the companion. It is not applied without qualification except to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When it is applied to other than Him, it is qualified, as in "rabb of such-and-such," like "rabb al-ibil (owner of the camels)" and "rabb al-ghanima (owner of the spoils)." See Lisan al-Arab.

8 'Adam, 'adam, and 'adam: the loss of a thing and its non-existence. This root does not occur in the Qur'an, but its meaning does, such as His words, exalted is He: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ (76:1).

9 Nawamis al-kawn (the laws of the universe): the secrets that Allah placed in the universe, of laws that organize the movement of its parts and components. Also, al-namus: the confidant of the king's secret, or the man who is informed of his secret and inner affair and is singled out with what he conceals from others. From this comes al-namus: Gabriel, because Allah, exalted is He, singled him out with the revelation and the unseen, which no one else is informed of.

10 "The day of creating the earth is among the four days after it, and the meaning is in completing four days, which together with the two days of creating the heavens make six days... Sunday and Monday for the creation of the earth, Tuesday and Wednesday for the setting [of provisions] mentioned in the verse and what follows it, and Thursday and Friday for the creation of the heavens." Said by Abu Yahya Zakariyya al-Ansari in his book "Fath al-Rahman bi Kashf ma Yaltabis fi al-Qur'an," p. 373. See also Ibn Kathir (4/93).

11. **al-Andad** (plural of *nidd*): likenesses, equals, and counterparts. The *andad* are the idols worshipped besides God.

12. **al-Rawasi** (sing. *rasiyah*): the mountains that are firmly fixed and established. The Lord of Majesty spoke of the wisdom behind creating these mountains, saying: ﴿And We placed in the earth firmly set mountains, lest it shake with them﴾ (21:31), meaning: so that it would not move and tremble with them, and thus no life would be fit for them upon it.

13. **al-Aqwat** (sing. *qut*): what sustains the human body of food. It is intended to mean provision in general.

14. **Qada al-shay'** (*qadahu*): he made it and measured it. So *faqadahunna* here means: He created them, knew them, made them, completed them, and perfected their creation.

15. **Ta'ruj**, meaning: ascends. *'Araja* (*ya'raju*, *'urujan*) means to ascend. And in the verse ﴿from God, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾ (70:3), *al-ma'arij* means the ascents and the stairways. Qatada said: *dhi al-ma'arij* means "Possessor of bounties and blessings." It was also said: the *ma'arij* of the angels are their ascents, by which they go up and ascend. Al-Farra' said: *dhi al-ma'arij* is an attribute of God, because the angels ascend to God, so He described Himself with that. All the readers recite the *ta'* in His saying ﴿the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴾ (70:4) ("ta'ruju"), except what was reported from Abdullah, and likewise al-Kisa'i recited it.

16. The commentators have several opinions regarding the word *al-ruh* in the verse here:
- Jibril (Gabriel). In this case it is a case of mentioning a specific item after a general category (i.e., the angels mentioned before it).
- A generic noun for the spirits of the children of Adam, for when they are taken, they are raised up to the heaven.
- A creation of God's creation who resemble people but are not people.

17. ﴿The day whose measure is a thousand years﴾: that is, every day from the days in which God created the heavens and the earth. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and 'Ikrima, and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal explicitly stated it in his book *al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyya* (a refutation of the Jahmiyya, a theological sect).
- As for the day whose measure is fifty thousand years, there are four opinions:
  1. It refers to the distance between the Mighty Throne and the lowest of the low, which is the floor of the seventh earth.
  2. The duration of this world's existence from the time God created this world until the Hour is established.
  3. It refers to the Day of Resurrection, which God made equal to fifty thousand years for the disbelievers.

18. Imam Malik ibn Anas was asked: "*Istawa*, how did He establish Himself?" He replied: "The *kayf* (how) is not conceivable, the *istiwa'* (establishment) is not unknown, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation." And the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And when he reached his full strength and became *istawa*﴾ (28:14). Abu Mansur said: the usage of the Arabs is that *al-mujtama'* (the one who has gathered his strength) among men and *al-mustawi* (the one who has reached full maturity) is the one whose youth is complete, and that is when he reaches twenty-eight years. It is possible that reaching forty is the ultimate point of *istiwa'* and perfection of intellect. (*al-Lisan*, a dictionary, entry *sawa*.)

19. *Ghashiytu al-shay'* (*taghshiyatan*): I covered the thing when I concealed it. *Ghashiyahu al-amr*, *taghashshahu*, and *aghshaytuhu iyyah* (all meaning that the matter overcame or covered him). He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿He covers the night over the day﴾ (7:54). Al-Lihyani said: it is read as *yughsha* (ghasha), and it is read in *al-Anfal*: ﴿He covered you with drowsiness﴾ (8:11), and it is read as *yughshikum* and *yughshakum*. The *ghisha'* of everything is what covers it, like the covering of the heart, the saddle, the saddlebag, the sword, and the like. *Ghashiyahu* (*yaghshahu*, *ghashyan*) means when it came to him, and *ghashshahu* (*taghshiyatan*) means when it covered him. *Ghashiya al-shay'* means when it clothed it. He said: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ (92:1), and He said: ﴿By the night when it covers it﴾ (91:4). (*al-Lisan*, entry *ghasha*.)

20. *Hathithan*: hastening, eager. A man is *hathith* and *mahthuth*: a sharp, quick person in his affair, as if his soul urges him on. *Al-hath* means hurrying in succession, and it was said: it means seeking speed. *Hathhu* and *ahthathahu* mean he urged him and encouraged him to do something. (*al-Lisan*, entry *hath*.)

21. ﴿The stars are subjected﴾: running, running along their courses. The subjection (*taskhir*) of the sun, the moon, and the stars for people means benefiting from them in reaching their places of growth, and taking them as guides in their paths. *Al-taskhir* means making something submissive. (*al-Lisan*, entry *sakhara*.)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 4 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you. The promise of Allah is true. He originates creation, then repeats it, that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾ (1)

When He, glory be to Him, says ﴿To Him is your return﴾, this is an announcement to all creation that all matters are known to Him, glory be to Him. He has sent down the obligation, which may be obeyed or disobeyed. Whoever obeys rejoices at His words, ﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾, and whoever disobeys grieves, because he will meet the punishment of the disobedient when he returns to Allah. (2)

We find the Qur'an saying once "yarji'un" and once "yurja'un" (3). Whoever does righteous deeds rejoices in returning to Allah, while whoever disobeys and disbelieves grieves, fears, hesitates, and tries not to return. But he returns in spite of his nose (i.e., against his will). The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿On the Day they will be thrust (4) into the fire of Hell with a violent thrusting﴾ (al-Tur, 13). His words here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, are: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you...﴾ (Yunus, 4). This return is called in the same verse: ﴿The promise of Allah is true...﴾ (Yunus, 4).

Someone may say: but a promise is applied to a matter that will come with good news. If the return is for the obedient, then this is good. But the disobedient will not see good in the return, so why did Allah not say: the return for the disobedient is a threat?

I say: The Truth, glory be to Him, only alerts man to what awaits him in the future, admonishes him, and leaves him the choice. This is an offering of good, and thus the whole matter becomes a promise. The construction in which the prepositional phrase is placed first, although its proper place is later, indicates the exclusivity of the collective: all of us return to Him, glory be to Him, like His words: ﴿You alone we worship...﴾ (al-Fatihah, 5).

So, the obedient rejoices in Allah's reward for him, and the disobedient must examine himself before he returns to Allah. Let me give an example, and to Allah belongs the highest example. You alert students to study. The one who truly studies rejoices at the examination, because he will pass it. The one who does not study may examine himself and turn to studying out of fear of failing. Reminding is a kind of warning, to make him feel the gravity of the situation and be restrained. Thus, the reminder becomes a promise, not a threat.

The Truth, glory be to Him, adds to the description of His promise that it is true, saying: ﴿The promise of Allah is true﴾. Someone may ask: is not every promise from Allah true? We say: yes. Every promise from Allah is true. The Truth, glory be to Him, chose here to describe His promise as true in order to remind us that the truth is that which is firmly established. If it seems to you at some times that falsehood is dominant and the master, know that falsehood has no permanence and no lordship.

He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or goods, is a foam like it. Thus Allah strikes the parable of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but that which benefits the people remains on the earth. Thus Allah sets forth parables﴾ (al-Ra'd, 17).

When the rain falls, we find every valley taking water according to its need. When the rain falls and gathers, we find straw floating, along with weeds and things that have no benefit, because the water at the moment of descent cleanses the place it descends upon. Therefore light and useless things float up.

Likewise, falsehood floats on the surface, but it benefits nothing and does not shake the truth, which settles, benefits the earth and the people. The floating of falsehood is a warning to the soldiers of truth. Falsehood is like pain that signals illness, and the most dangerous diseases are those without pain, which then grow until their treatment becomes difficult and impossible.

Thus, pain, like falsehood, alerts the soldiers of truth. That is why you notice that when Islam is provoked by any enemy, you find enthusiasm stirring among all people: movement, cooperation, and forgetting of grudges, in defense of Islam.

In diseases transmitted by certain viruses, you find doctors inoculating people with the same microbes and viruses of the disease in weak doses, to stimulate the body's resistance. Thus falsehood is a soldier of the truth, just as pain is a soldier of well-being.

If the Truth is the One who says: ﴿To Him is your return (8), all of you﴾, then it must be the true promise, because He, glory be to Him, possesses all that He promises, and He, glory be to Him, is free from lying and deception, for He is the One who says: ﴿And who is more truthful in speech than Allah?﴾ (al-Nisa', 122).

And because He is mightier than what He created and than those He created. His capabilities do not fail Him, for He owns the whole universe.

The word "return" (raj'a) in His words, exalted is He, ﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾, indicates that one is upon something, then separates from it, and afterward returns to it. So there is existence first, then departure from existence, then a return to the original existence. If you are in a place, then you go to another place, and then you return to the first place, this is the return.

The statement here indicates that we will all die, in confirmation of the words of the Truth: ﴿Everyone upon it passes away (26), and there remains the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor (27)﴾ (al-Rahman, 26-27).

The disbelievers said what the Qur'an mentions: ﴿When we have died and become dust, that is a far return (3)﴾ (Qaf, 3).

As if they regarded the idea of resurrection as remote, and they also said: ﴿When we are lost in the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?...﴾ (al-Sajdah, 10) (9). That is, they questioned: after death and burial and the dissolution of the body (10) into elements that mix with the elements of the earth, is there resurrection and rising (11) after all that?

Here came His, glory be to Him, words: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾, to indicate that the departure into existence is by birth into life, then after leaving life comes its opposite, which is death, and after that, resurrection.

The disbelievers stopped at this point and regarded it as remote, so Allah wished to explain this matter to us, because it is the completion of adherence to the method. As if He were saying to us: beware lest you think that you have taken life, escaped with it, and enjoyed it, and then the matter ends (12)? No, there is a resurrection and a reckoning. That is why He said: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you, the promise of Allah is true...﴾ (4). If someone says: how will that be? The true word comes: ﴿He originates creation, then repeats it﴾. So He who was able to create from nothing, would He be unable to restore from existence? It is the Truth who says: ﴿And I created you before, when you were nothing﴾ (Maryam, 9).

So if He wishes to restore you, do not ask how, because your particles still exist. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Were We incapable with the first creation? Rather, they are in confusion about a new creation (15)﴾ (Qaf, 15). Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, derives from the first creation the possibility of the second creation. If you wonder that after the Truth has brought into being your parts, particles, and attributes, then look at the first creation: He created you from nothing, so would He be incapable of restoring you from something? ﴿Were We incapable with the first creation?﴾

The philosophers came and raised an uproar (15), so the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, came with proofs from the universe and said: ﴿You see the earth lifeless...﴾ (al-Hajj, 5), that is, a dead land with no life in it at all.

﴿But when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells (16) and puts forth from every beautiful pair﴾ (al-Hajj, 5).

So it is no wonder that life comes forth from death, and you see that every hour. The life you see before you is nothing but a cycle, because when Allah created the universe, He created its elements, and there is nothing added to these elements.

Take one substance: water. Since Allah created water, it has neither increased nor decreased.
