Man and animals drink from it, and if each one in his life took some amount of water, the water would remain as it is, because this man secretes what he has drunk in the form of sweat and various secretions, and all of that comes out of him, and what remains is equal to his weight.

So, what you took of water comes out of you mixed with other things, as a result of the reaction that gives you the energy of life. After that, the water evaporates. The process of evaporation is the distillation (17) of water. If you want to distill water, you heat it to boiling point, so it turns into vapor, and then you condense it so it returns to water again.

So water has a cycle. We irrigate the crops with it, and they take up the water and become green. The surplus water beyond their need comes out of them through transpiration (19), and then they dry, after the water has left them by evaporation, and all of this happens without anyone noticing this evaporation.

When you bring a glass of distilled water from the pharmacy, you take on much trouble, needing a stove, a vessel, and tubes, and then other cold water to condense the vapor. But this is a process that occurs in the universe millions of times, and no one is aware of it.

After the water evaporates, it becomes clouds, then the rain pours down, and it is distilled water.

That is why you find that the area of water covers three-quarters of the earth, to serve the remaining quarter (the dry land), because Allah wants the surface of the earth to be wide, and this expanse helps distillation, evaporation, and condensation.

It is like when you bring a glass of water and place it in a room, then you are away from the room for a month. When you return to it, you may find the glass has lost about half a centimeter. But if you take that same glass of water and pour its water out to spread on the floor of the room, you will find the floor dry within a few hours. Thus we find that the wider the area, the faster the evaporation.

So, the amount of water that Allah created is as it is. It has not increased and will not decrease. It turns in the cycle the Truth willed. Thus we see that a thing returns to its origin again, and this can be seen in every aspect of life. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿By the scatterers (1) dispersing, and the bearers of burdens (2), and the runners with ease (3), and the distributors of a command (4). Indeed, what you are promised is true (5)﴾ (al-Dhariyat, 1-5). He swears here by the winds that carry the clouds and send rain on every cloud at the specific place appointed for it by Allah's command. The Truth, glory be to Him, draws our attention here to the cycle of water, which is the foundation of life, to show that His promise will certainly be fulfilled.

Reflect on the rose: you find softness and freshness in it, because there is much water in it, and it has a beautiful color and a fragrant smell that spreads. When you pick it, its petals fall and dry, because the water in it evaporates. What the rose took of water returns to the store again, and likewise its scent remains in its withered petals until it ends, and likewise its color, and then a new rose comes forth.

So the life of every creature in existence and the world in its movement arises from this cycle. If your life's water is cycling, do you find it unlikely that you yourself, with your components, would cycle? Suppose a person existed and died, when the soul leaves the body, the corpse is buried, and the water in it evaporates, and the substances of the corpse dissolve with the elements of the earth to become dust. Would the Truth be unable to restore to existence the parts of this person? Of course, He cannot be incapable.

Life, then, is the interaction of these cycles with those elements. Nothing has been added to them, and nothing has been subtracted from them.

Read the Qur'an with insight, and you will find His, the Truth's, words: ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record﴾ (Qaf, 4).

Thus the Truth explains to us that all the elements exist in the universe. They may increase in one creature more than another, but the total sum of all elements is constant. If science has arrived at the conclusion that there are sixteen elements that compose living things, these elements are fixed in quantity. And if they discover an increase in their number, the increase in the number of elements will also be fixed in quantity for each element.

The scholars said: the sixteen elements are: oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, magnesium, potassium, sodium, and others.

All these elements return to their origin after living things die and decompose.

Thus the words of the Truth come true: ﴿We know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record...﴾ (Qaf, 4).

Some philosophers tried to raise a second objection and said: suppose a man died and his elements decomposed in the earth. Do not the elements go into other living things, like a tree that produced a fruit or something else, and then a human ate it...
