Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And man is ever hasty.(11) (17:11)﴾ (al-Isra'), and He said: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it.(1) (16:1)﴾ (al-Nahl).

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 10, verse 12 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says:
{And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us regarding a harm that touched him. Thus has been made attractive to the transgressors that which they used to do.} (10:12)

The Truth, glory be to Him, depicts the state of people who are not constantly bound to God and to the method of God: those who turn to God in moments of crisis, then forget faith and its obligations afterwards. Our lives are full of this type of person.

In our village, for example, the one who supervised the health care of the people was the barber-surgeon (ḥallāq al-ṣiḥḥa), until one of the sons of the village graduated from the faculty of medicine. The barber-surgeon then began to spread unseemly things about him. One day the peasants noticed the barber-surgeon leaving early, carrying a large bundle, so they wanted to know what was in it, and they discovered that the barber-surgeon's son was ill, and he wanted to take him to the doctor. He, then, was not deceiving himself, despite his attempt to deceive the people of the village with false rumours about the doctor.

Likewise is man with the method of God: he may deceive others in a moment of ease, but he does not forget God in a moment of hardship. When harm comes to him, and when means become scarce for him, he finds nothing but the word "O Lord!" And you find it from the most hardened of the wicked (fujjār)(1) and the most severe of the stubborn; you find each one of them calling upon God at the time of harm.

This is what the Truth, glory be to Him, says here: {And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side.}

The example from the lives of these disbelievers is that they called down harm upon themselves, even though they would wish to end their lives. Why then do they call upon God when they have disbelieved in Him? It is a plain lie. A person, when he is constrained within himself, may call down harm upon himself, just as al-Mutanabbī(2) said: "Enough of an affliction for you is that you see death as a healer, and that the fates (al-manāyā)(3) be your wish." That is: it suffices that a person reach the level where he wishes for death.

We note that the Truth, glory be to Him, has addressed man's position regarding harm in more than one place: one verse singles out man in one meaning, another verse singles him out in another meaning, and a third verse depicts man's condition in yet another way.

He, glory be to Him, says: {And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance (munīban)(4). Then when He bestows upon him a favour from Him, he forgets what he had called upon Him for before...} (39:8).

And the Truth says in the verse about which we are reflecting: {And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us}, and He, glory be to Him, says in another place: {And whatever favour you have is from God; then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out (tajarrūn)(6) [53]. Then when He removes the harm from you, behold, a group of you associate others with their Lord [54]} (16:53–54).

So the Truth brings it sometimes singular and sometimes plural, and sometimes singular in various forms, sometimes plural in various forms; and sometimes He mentions it on land, and sometimes at sea: {And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him...} (17:67).

Thus the verses encompass the various states of man: when harm befalls him and he finds no refuge, neither in himself nor in the environment around him, he finds no one to turn to but his Lord. Regrettably, this man is a disbeliever in God.

The verse about which we are reflecting gives us multiple images: the Truth, glory be to Him, says: {calls upon Us lying on his side}, that is, while reclining, {or sitting or standing}. Thus the verse addresses man in his conduct in the universe. The verse accords with the stages of human formation: the small child cannot turn over by himself, rather his family turns him so that he sleeps on his side; and when he grows a little, he turns by himself. Then comes the movement of the second power: the child sits, then stands without walking, and then walks after that.

The verse here gives a precise depiction of three states: {lying on his side, or sitting, or standing}, and the movement of walking is not mentioned, because one who is moving to walk is not made to sit by harm; but whoever passes through the other stages, standing, sitting, or lying on his side, harm may reach him.

These are the stages of the unravelling of the manifestations of life: man lives childhood, then the vigour of youth, then weakness and grey hair come upon him, so he cannot walk with the strength of a young man, if he is still able to stand; then old age enters, so he sits and cannot stand; then old age advances, so he neither walks, nor stands, nor sits, and remains on his side, and his family may turn him.

Thus, the unravelling of everything comes in reverse of its construction: just as man's stages were built, lying on the side, then sitting, then standing, then striving and movement, so they end in reverse, because unravelling is always the reverse of building.

From this we derive the inference of God's truthfulness in informing His creatures about the manner of creation, since we did not witness the process of creation, in fulfilment of His words, exalted is He: {I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation, nor would I have taken the misguiders as helpers} (18:51).

Since the Truth did not make anyone witness how the heavens and the earth were created, nor the creation of man, we do not take information about the manner of creation apart from the Qur'an. Therefore we do not accept the hypotheses which claim that the earth was a piece of the sun that separated from it and then its temperature dropped; all these are hypotheses whose soundness will never be proven. And the Truth, glory be to Him, has said: {I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation...} (18:51).

This saying shows that the human mind cannot reach knowledge of how the heavens and the earth were created, and the creation of man, while it is cut off from the method of heaven. So if they tell you how you were created in a manner different from what is in the Qur'an, say: "You have lied"; and if they tell you how the heavens and the earth were created other than what came in the Book of God, say: "You have lied"; for God is the One who created the heavens and the earth and man, alone, and no one was with Him, and none of these witnessed a scene so as to inform you of it. And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: {Nor would I have taken the misguiders as helpers} (18:51).

The misguiders are those who tell you untrue hypotheses about the evolution of the ape until it became a human, and that the earth was a piece of the sun that separated from it; all these hypotheses were stated by those whom the Truth, glory be to Him, named: {the misguiders}. Had God not said this verse, and then people came saying: "Man was originally an ape," we would have said: "The Qur'an did not address that," and it would have been possible for us to believe them. But God, glory be to Him, willed for us to have immunity against this misguidance.

The creation process is hidden from us; those who created us, glory be to Him, informed us about it, for there was no witness with Him who saw this scene to tell us. And the creation through which there is life is undone by death; but death is a scene we witness, and any unravelling of a thing, as we have known, comes in reverse of its construction. If we build a twenty-storey building, and then wish to demolish it for one reason or another, we demolish the twentieth storey first, then continue the demolition after that; what was built first is demolished last, because the unravelling of everything comes in reverse of its construction.

Since death is the unravelling of life, when the soul leaves the body and the corpse is left without burial, the corpse stiffens, then becomes a carcass (jīfa)(10), then the water evaporates from it, and the body dissolves into its primary elements in the earth. These are the stages of death.

The Truth has informed us about the manner of creation: He made clear that God, glory be to Him, created man from earth and water, so he became clay; then the clay was levelled, and the Truth formed him in the form of a man and breathed into him the spirit (rūḥ)(11). The last of the stages of his bringing into being is the spirit; therefore the departure of the spirit is the first stage of death.

In this verse God, exalted is He, mentioned the state of man lying on his side, standing, and sitting, and did not mention walking, because the one who walks has power, so harm is not in his essence; and if harm befalls him, it comes from something else. Harm is the opposite of benefit, and the beneficial is what keeps a thing in its wholesome, pleasant, and comfortable soundness, whether in the essence or in the outside.

When your essence is upright and its faculties and organs are all sound, you have no harm; but when a defect occurs in any organ, troubles begin. This is why it is said of well-being (al-salāma) that it is that you do not feel you have organs at all; for when you feel that you have an eye, for example, know that it is hurting you; and when you feel your ear, know that it is hurting you. And you grind food with your molars and eat without being aware of them; and the day you become aware of them, this means that pain has begun.

Thus man does not feel the loss of well-being unless he knows and notices that he has an organ among his organs, so he says: "Ah, my eye!" and "Ah, my ear!"

We say: the pain of the eye is a distinctive pain, and likewise we say of any organ; as for one who does not complain about his organs, he does not feel them, because they perform their functions in the proper way. Well-being among those around you is represented in their bringing you enjoyment and serenity without turbidity; and thus their benefit to you becomes apparent (4).

Every person has an innate pride, shown by the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: {Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient} (96:6–7). Man is only humbled when he suffers some affliction, and his transgression comes only when blessings are complete externally and internally; and if blessings begin to withdraw from man, his pride scatters. Whoever displays himself before people may hope to rise from his bed to take a few steps, but cannot.

Man is self-sufficient only through what is intrinsic to him, not through what is bestowed upon him; therefore he must not be deceived, for the Supreme Bestower may withdraw His gift; He may take away your health, and we have often seen healthy people fall ill, rich people become poor, and people of rank lose their standing.

So, therefore, vanity must be eliminated; as long as everything in you is a gift from the Supreme Bestower, glory be to Him, the Bestower may take back what He gave, and as soon as a blessing is taken from a person, he awakens. So there is no reason, then, for anyone to be deceived, lest he hand himself over cheaply to ruin.

And the saying: you may have antagonised a doctor, who is the only one in the place where you live, and some may try to reconcile you with this doctor, but you refuse; then illness comes to you, and you turn to him, because God has granted him the sound measure of diagnosis through knowledge. So you must not be deceived or exalt yourself over anyone.

But man is man; therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says: {And when harm touches man...} (10:12). The disbeliever, as soon as harm touches him, falls into the pit of humiliation. As for the believer, he is always with his Lord, and when harm touches him he calls upon God always and does not forget Him; therefore He is gentle with him, glory be to Him, unlike the disbeliever who calls upon God only at the time of harm. And where was the disbeliever when God called him through the messengers to faith?

Forgetfulness is a matter inherent in man's first natural constitution (fiṭra)(15), for man is weak and lives in a surrounding environment. He loves benefit from outside himself, and when this external benefit is withheld from him, he takes benefit from his own self, from the movement of his parts and their serving one another. Then he finds no refuge except to believe in the One who first created him. Consider the Qur'anic expression: {And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him...} (17:67).

Thus, whoever worships other than God, glory be to Him, goes astray at his object of worship, and does not know how to rescue those who worship him; therefore the polytheist returns to God and finds no one but Him, glory be to Him, for He is the One who rescues man in the moment of danger, because the Lord, the Creator, is more merciful toward His creation; and this mercy rescues man even if he is a disbeliever. This is sound speech, for we bore witness to God's oneness in the realm of atoms (ʿālam al-dharr)(16), when God took from us the first covenant (17): He said to us: {Am I not your Lord?} (7:172), and we said: {Yes} (7:172).

This is the faith of the natural constitution, before heedlessness or imitation arises; therefore, when the false gods scatter around the disbeliever, he returns to himself and calls upon God, and even seeks an intercessor to ask Him to pray...

1 al-fujjār: plural of fājir, one who commits many sins and misdeeds. Fujūr originally means deviation from the truth. Ibn Shumayl said: fujūr is riding toward what is not permitted. God, exalted is He, said: {Rather, man desires to continue in sin before him} (75:5), and: {Indeed, the wicked are in Hellfire} (82:14). (Lisān al-ʿArab, root f-j-r, adapted.)

2 al-Mutanabbī is a poet of the Abbasid era who had a notable standing in poetry.

3 al-manāyā: plural of manīya, which is death; al-muna means destiny: "God decreed (manā) for you something," i.e., ordained it for you. Hence the term manīya (death) is applied, because it is ordained for a specific time. (Lisān al-ʿArab, root m-n-y.)

4 munīban: returning to God in repentance. One who turns back to God in repentance is munīb: he comes to Him repentant and returns to obedience. God, exalted is He, said: {And turn back to your Lord and submit to Him} (39:54), and: {And He sends down for you provision from the sky, and none is mindful except one who turns back} (40:13).

5 khawwalahu Allāh niʿmatan: He granted him a blessing, made him its possessor. It derives from takhwīl, which means making someone an owner. The meaning: when God removes harm from him and bestows blessings upon him, he forgets God's favour upon him and falls into sins. (Lisān al-ʿArab, adapted.)

6 tajʾarūn: you raise your voices in supplication and entreaty to God. (Lisān, root j-ʾ-r.)

7 He, glory be to Him, also said: {God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and grey hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent} (30:54).

8 ḍalla yaḍillu fa-huwa ḍāll, and aḍalla yuḍillu fa-huwa muḍill, and he does not suffice with his own misguidance but misguides others too. Aḍallahu: made him astray. Ḍalāl is the opposite of guidance and right direction. God, exalted is He, said: {Did you mislead these servants of Mine, or did they themselves stray from the way?} (25:17); and: {And Al-Sāmirī misled them} (20:85); and: {And they do not mislead except themselves, and they are not aware} (3:69).

9 al-ʿaḍud in man and others is the forearm, from the elbow to the shoulder. The meaning of ʿaḍud here is: aid and support. God, exalted is He, said: {He said: We will strengthen your arm through your brother and give you both authority...} (28:35).

10 al-jīfa: the corpse of a dead person when it has rotted and has a smell. Plural: jīf and ajyāf. (Lisān, root j-y-f.)

11 On this God, glory be to Him, says: {He who perfected everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay [7], then made his offspring from an extract of base fluid [8], then formed him and breathed into him of His spirit, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts; little do you give thanks} (32:7–9).

12 On the authority of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: "The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe." Narrated by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (41), and narrated by al-Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ (10) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ.

13 āfa: a blight, sickness, corruption, deficiency, or defect. It is said: the blight of refinement is arrogance, and the blight of knowledge is forgetfulness.

14 al-jāh: standing and rank. God, exalted is He, said: {And he was honoured in the sight of God} (33:69).

15 From this is the saying of God, mighty and majestic: {And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no determination} (20:115). Thus the human species is constituted with forgetfulness, and for this reason the Sharīʿa overlooks forgetfulness, error, and what a person is compelled to do. On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, has overlooked for my community error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do." Narrated by al-Ḥākim in his Mustadrak (2/198). al-Ḥākim said: sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not narrate it; and al-Dhahabī concurred. Ibn Rajab al-Ḥanbalī graded it ḥasan in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa al-Ḥikam (p. 442), Mu'assasat al-Risāla edition, 1991.

However, forgetting in the sense of neglect and heedlessness toward God's commands and adherence to God's method is not overlooked by God; rather, man is held accountable for it. He, mighty and majestic, says: {So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything, until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were struck dumb in despair} (6:44).

16. The Day of the Covenant ('Alam al-Dharr; the primordial day on which the descendants of Adam were brought forth): it is the day on which God brought forth the offspring of Adam from his loins and spread them out. He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this," or say, "It was only that our fathers associated [others with God] before, and we were [only] descendants after them. Then will You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?"﴾ (Al-A'raf 7:172–173).

17. The first covenant is the bearing of witness by the descendants of Adam's children and the taking of their pledge that God is the Lord of all creation. Here, faith in the oneness of God (tawhid) was innate (fitrah) in them, by which the heart is at rest, the intellect is reassured, and the soul finds repose. As for the second covenant, it is the imposition of obligations through the hand of the Messengers, in the form of "do" and "do not do," and it is an extension of the first covenant. All of this is gathered in His saying: ﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance from wherever you will; but do not approach this tree..."﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:35). From here came the command and the prohibition (al-amr wa'l-nahy), upon which the basis of accountability rests.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 13:

He, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they did wrong, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they would not have believed. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.﴾

So beware lest your own souls embellish for you that you persist in your enmity towards Muhammad (ﷺ); for you will not reach any harm to him, and Allah will complete His light, so let him be safe from anything novel in creation. The word "generations" (qurun) is the plural of qarn (generation). Qarn derives from muqarana (association), and every group who are associated in something we call a "qarn". The qarn may also be in terms of time, which is why they reckoned a qarn as one hundred years, and the people who gather within one hundred years are called a qarn. Or the qarn is a group who are associated in something that unites them, however long their span may be.

His saying, the Truth: ﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they did wrong, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they would not have believed.﴾ Would they have believed had Allah, may He be exalted, granted them respite? No. Allah has eternal knowledge, knowing things according to what they will be, whether by compulsion or by choice.

An example from our life and customs (and to Allah belongs the highest similitude): we find that when a person wants to build a house, the matter differs according to his capacity. The poor man, for instance, asks for two rooms, so the builder plans to build two rooms. If the person is of middling means, he goes to an engineer who designs for him according to his means. If the person is wealthy, he summons an engineer who builds him a house according to the capacities and desires of this wealthy man, and the engineer designs a model of the building before he begins, in which every detail appears, even the colours of the windows, doors and rooms.

The world, before Allah the Most High created it, had its form predestined from eternity with Him, glory be to Him. This is the absolute power of the Truth, may He be exalted, and the reality of the cosmos comes according to what the Creator, glory be to Him, has predetermined from eternity, even if there is a choice for the creature, the disbeliever, for Allah, glory be to Him, knows it.

It is established that the pen has dried even regarding matters of choice, and He, glory be to Him, knows what affairs are driven by compulsion and what He decrees for His creatures without their choice; as for matters of choice, He has given His creatures choice. He has known what they will do in the unseen, so He arranged the matter according to knowledge.

Beware lest you think that by this He wished to oblige you. No, He knew that you would choose. Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, knew from eternity who would persist in his soul, and it had preceded in His knowledge that the people of the earlier generations whom He destroyed would not believe. ﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they did wrong.﴾ Wrongdoing (zulm) means transferring a right from its owner to another. Rights bestowed by the Creator upon humans may be wronged among them, but the highest degree of wrongdoing is when someone wrongs the right of the Supreme God to be one God, and transfers that to another. That is the summit of wrongdoing; therefore He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Indeed, association (shirk) is a great wrong﴾ (Yunus 31:13 as cited in the commentary). They wronged in the first matter of belief, or they wronged in rights between themselves and their own souls, in confirmation of His saying, the Most High: ﴿But people wrong themselves﴾ [Yunus 10:44].

Each one of them is both wrongdoer and wronged at the same time, because the human being has multiple faculties, and among these faculties is the faculty of innate faith and the faculty of immediate self-interest. When the faculty of immediate self-interest prevails, the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama) emerges to bring the matter back to its rightness. But if it is a soul that commands evil, it seeks only the fulfilment of appetites, because it is a soul that commands (al-nafs al-ammara) to evil. If the soul is reassured by the judgment of Allah, the Most High, and is content with it and carries out what Allah, glory be to Him, has said, then it is the soul at peace (al-nafs al-mutma'inna). Whoever wrongs his soul is one who follows the desires (shahawat) of his soul, and he has given it immediate enjoyment, to receive afterwards a deferred misery; thus he has wronged his soul.

﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they did wrong, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾: and the Truth, glory be to Him, did not leave them, but sent messengers supported by miracles to give them insight. Yet Allah, the Most High, knows that they will not believe; therefore He said: ﴿but they would not have believed﴾, meaning: were He, glory be to Him, to leave them alive, they would not believe, for He created them and eternal knowledge had known that they would never choose faith.

The Truth, glory be to Him, is the Exalted Knower who knows things according to what they are, not according to what He compels His creatures to. Had His knowledge, glory be to Him, been according to what He compels creatures to, the matter would have been finished.

The example, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: you are in the house and wish to go on a trip with your wife. If the children are small, you lock the door on them after saying to them: your food is in the refrigerator, meat, fish, cheese and olives. After you and your wife leave, you say to her: our children will only eat cheese and olives, because they will take the easy food. Had there been nothing in the refrigerator but cheese, you would not have said that, for this is the kind of food that is compelled.

But since the matter is one of choice, you infer from the children's previous conduct. When you return, you find that your children have acted according to what you judged, although you left them the choice. An example of this in the Qur'an is His saying, the Truth: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor what he gained. He will burn in a fire of blazing flame﴾ (al-Masad 111:1-3). In this is a judgment from Allah, the Most High, that Abu Lahab will die a disbeliever. This is a declared judgment, recited in the prayer, and we memorise it. Abu Lahab was the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was a disbeliever like the other disbelievers. Many disbelievers did embrace Islam. Did not Umar embrace Islam? Did not Ikrimah, son of Abu Jahl, embrace Islam? Did not Amr ibn al-As embrace Islam? Did not Khalid ibn al-Walid embrace Islam? So what prevents Abu Lahab from embracing Islam too? No, he did not embrace Islam, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knew from his Lord that this would not happen from him. Nor was it possible for Abu Lahab to deceive and announce his Islam in denial of the Qur'an, because the Truth had known from eternity the conduct of Abu Lahab.

﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they did wrong, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they would not have believed. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.﴾ His saying: ﴿Thus﴾ means: like this recompense which was for the earlier nations who were destroyed in past generations, He recompenses those who transgress, for matters in the cosmos are one. The matter of faith exists from the first time messengers were sent until the world ends.

1. The criminals (mujrimin) are the disbelievers, because they denied the signs of Allah, wronged and were arrogant. The root jarm of a person means that his sin is great, i.e., he committed sin. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿And We drive the criminals to Hell...﴾ (Maryam 19:86) (Lisan al-Arab, root j-r-m).
2. Taswil (embellishment) of something for them: their souls make the error appear fine to them. Taswil means beautifying falsehood, adorning it and making it beloved to a person so that he does it or says it. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Nay, your souls have embellished a matter for you, so patience is fitting﴾ (Yusuf 12:18), and He said: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them, Satan embellished for them and gave them false hope﴾ (Muhammad 47:25) (Lisan al-Arab, root s-w-l).
3. Qarn: a community that comes after another community. The qarn is the people of each age, derived from iqtiran (association), as if it is the span within which the people of that age are associated in their lifespans and conditions. It is said: a qarn of time is one hundred years, and other things have been said. Its plural is qurun. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established on the earth as We have not established you, and We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain, and made rivers flow beneath them; then We destroyed them for their sins, and produced after them another generation﴾ (al-An'am 6:6). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of you is my generation (meaning my companions), then those who follow them," meaning those who took from the successors (tabi'un).
4. Amad: the end point; amad means the limit of a term. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿And do not be like those who were given the Book before, for the term grew long upon them and their hearts hardened...﴾ (al-Hadid 57:16) (Lisan al-Arab, root a-m-d).
5. Ghayb: what is hidden from the eyes even if it is established in the hearts. Ghayb is what is hidden from you and is not hidden from the Knower of the unseen. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿who believe in the unseen...﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:3), and He said: ﴿Indeed Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth...﴾ (al-Hujurat 49:18) (Lisan al-Arab, root gh-y-b, adapted).
6. Lawwama: an intensive form of la'ima (one who blames), meaning one who blames much. The self-reproaching soul is the one that frequently blames its owner for his errors. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection, and I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾ (al-Qiyamah 75:1-2).
7. Ammara: an intensive form of amira (commanding), meaning one who commands much. The commanding soul is the soul that dominates and overpowers its owner, and its mention occurs in the Qur'an in His saying: ﴿Indeed the soul is a commander of evil...﴾ (Yusuf 12:53).
8. The soul at peace (al-nafs al-mutma'inna) is the one that has become tranquil through faith, content with its Lord and obedient to Him; it is steadfast and calm through the good reward from Allah, glory be to Him. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ (al-Fajr 89:27-28) (Lisan al-Arab, root t-m-n, adapted). The knowers have mentioned that souls are seven: the commanding soul, the self-reproaching soul, the inspired soul, the soul at peace, the pleased soul, the pleasing soul, and the perfect soul.
9. Ishtaha al-shay' shahwatan: he loved it and desired it. Its plural is shahawat (desires). Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Adorned for people is the love of desires: women, children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver...﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:14).
10. Ajil is the opposite of 'ajil. Al-ajila is the Hereafter and al-'ajila is this world. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come to them...﴾ (al-'Ankabut 29:53). The specified term is the Day of Resurrection (Lisan al-Arab, root a-j-l, adapted).
11. Abu Lahab is one of the paternal uncles of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); his name was Abd al-Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and his kunya was Abu Utba. He was called Abu Lahab because his face was reddish and bright, as if it were a flame.
The occasion of revelation of the surah in which he is mentioned: the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to al-Batha, climbed the mountain and called out "O people of the morning!" and Quraysh gathered to him. He said: "Do you see that if I told you that an enemy is coming upon you in the morning or evening, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Is it for this that you gathered us?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ to its end. Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (208) from Ibn Abbas.

The True One, glory be to Him, then says:

﴿Then We made you successors (khala'if) in the earth after them, that We might see how you would act.﴾ (10:14)

﴿Khala'if⌋ is the plural of khalifa(1), which means one who succeeds another. When the True One, glory be to Him and exalted, described man, He issued the first statement about man, when the angels said: ﴿Indeed, I will place upon the earth a khalifa...﴾ (2:30).

Allah, glory be to Him, is All-Powerful, All-Hearing, and All-Knowing, and He possesses all the attributes of absolute perfection. You may have power, and the effect of your power may extend to others, but you cannot extend your power itself to anyone else. If you are strong, you cannot grant a weak person a portion of your strength. All you can do is give him the effect of your power. If he is unable to carry something, you may carry it for him; if he is unable to walk, you may take him by the hand. But you cannot give him a part of your own inherent strength, so he remains incapable while you remain capable, just as you are.

This is the condition of creation. You find one person rich and another poor, and the rich gives to the poor from his wealth. A scholar gives some knowledge to the ignorant, but he does not bestow upon him the faculty of knowledge. As for the Supreme Truth, glory be to Him, He alone is able to bestow from His absolute power a limited, granted power upon creation. He, glory be to Him, has given the effect of high power to the celestial spheres He created, in which man has no part: the sun, the moon, the stars, the winds, and the rain.

The True One, glory be to Him, has given man a share of His power in the matters around him, so he has become able to perform certain actions that correspond to this granted capacity. Thus the True One, glory be to Him, has extended to him from His power so that he may be able to act, from His wealth so that he may give to the poor, from His knowledge so that he may teach the ignorant, and from His forbearance so that he may forbear with one who harms him.

Therefore, creatures do not extend their attributes to others, but they do extend the effects of their attributes to others. The attribute remains here a strength and there a weakness. As for the One, the Unique, He is the one who can bestow power from His might upon the powerless, so that he acts. So is the whole universe like this?

The universe consists of two parts. One part Allah, glory be to Him, has bestowed upon man without any room for him in it. Truth established it by His power, and this part of the universe is upright in its order, with a uprightness that admits no defect, such as the order of the celestial spheres and the heavens, the revolution of the sun and the moon, the wind, and others. It suffers from no fault or defect, and this part can be corrupted only through human intervention.

Another part of the universe the True One, glory be to Him, has left to man, when he establishes it by the power bestowed upon him by Allah.

You will not find corruption in the creation of Allah, the Exalted, without finding a human hand in it. As for the matters in which man has no hand, they are upright. For this reason the True One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And the sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation.﴾ (55:5). The observatories determine the position of the earth between the sun and the moon, and the position of the moon between the earth and the sun, with a precision that matches His words, ﴿by precise calculation,﴾ because man has no part in these matters.

As for what I am in, I have a choice, and we must intervene by the method of Allah, the Exalted, so that our movement may be upright, like the uprightness of movement in the higher worlds in which we have no part.

Therefore, what corrupts the worlds is human intervention in what surrounds him and what he is affected by and affects, contrary to the method of Allah. For this reason the True One, glory be to Him, said: ﴿The Most Merciful (1). He taught the Qur'an (2). He created man (3). He taught him expression (al-bayan)(5) (4). The sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation (5).﴾ (55:1-5). That is: these worlds were created by calculation, and you can measure your times and your calculations on their basis. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation (5), and the stars and the trees prostrate (6), and the heaven He raised and set up the balance (7). That you not transgress within the balance (8). And establish weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance (9).﴾ (55:5-9).

So that the affairs of your worldly life may be upright in your movement within the universe, just as the higher affairs have been upright for you, weigh all matters with justice, so that the balance will not be disturbed for you. For what corrupts the universe is that you intervene in what Allah has given you as gifts: power, knowledge, and movement, contrary to the method of Allah. So approach the affairs of your life by the method of Allah in "do" and "do not do"(7), so that the lower universe may be upright for you as the higher universe has been upright for you.

Here the True One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth﴾, and man has succeeded Allah, the Exalted, in the earth. For example, he plows the earth and waters it, and so crops grow for him. When man takes the means of Allah, he attains the result of taking the means, but with arrogance, when things respond to him, so he thinks that he is capable by himself, not by the means of Allah.

The True One, glory be to Him and exalted, gives, by the bounty of His lordship, both to the believer and to the disbeliever, because He, glory be to Him, is the One who brought man into existence. However, He, may He be exalted, distinguished the believer, not merely by the bounty of means, but by the method and the obligation represented in "do such-and-such" and "do not do such-and-such." If one takes both bounties from Allah, he will have a good reward in this world and the Hereafter. If he takes only the second bounty, that of "do" and "do not do," he takes the Hereafter, but his worldly life remains different.

Whoever wishes to take the good of both this world and the Hereafter, let him take the bounty of the lordship of Allah, the Exalted, by taking the means, and the bounty of divinity by following the method.

However, the affliction of the khalifa on earth is that he sees things responding to him, so he transgresses(8) and thinks he is self-sufficient in the universe. We say to him: since you think you are self-sufficient in the universe, then preserve your soul, your strength, and your wealth.

But you will not be able to do that. For if you rebel against the commands of Allah by disbelief, for example, why do you not rebel against sickness or death?

Therefore, you are subdued to the Most High against your will, and you must take from the matters that descend upon you by decree, to bridle you and subdue you, until you take the matters in which you have a choice, the method of Allah, glory be to Him.

If the khalifa on earth thinks he is self-sufficient in the universe, then he should learn from what he sees in the universe. For you may appoint a lawyer as your agent in contracts and dealings, and he disposes of all matters without referring back to you and does not present you with a statement of what he has done, so you cancel the agency. Then such a lawyer realizes that every action he takes without the agency has become unacceptable. So what about Allah's delegation of khilafah to man? The True One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Then We made you successors in the earth﴾. So if you have succeeded those who perished, it is necessary for you to take warning and a lesson, that Allah, the Exalted, is dominant over His command(9), and that you should not oppress the messengers, but rather take the method. Or at least, do not oppose them if you do not believe in the method they brought from Allah. Leave them to proclaim the word of Allah, and let them shape the movement of the believers in their messages in this universe according to what Allah, glory be to Him, wills, while you are free to believe or not to believe.

﴿So whoever wills, let him believe; and whoever wills, let him disbelieve...﴾ (18:29). The proof of this is that when Islam conquered many lands, it left them free to embrace Islam or to remain upon their religions, even though it had entered their lands by invitation or by force. Yet it did not compel anyone in religion. The Muslims took from them the jizya(10) in exchange for the Muslims' protection of them.

If Islam had spread by the sword, no one would have been left upon his religion. But Islam did not coerce anyone, and it protected freedom of choice, not by the sword. Because those who did not believe in Islam lived in a society in which the Islamic state took responsibility for all their needs of life, and the Muslim pays zakat to the public treasury (bayt al-mal), so whoever does not believe, yet benefits from the services that the Muslim society provides, must pay the jizya in exchange for those services.

When a person believes he is a khalifa and remains mindful of that, he remembers that the authority of the One who appointed him as khalifa is capable of revoking this khilafah from him.

Therefore, take the matter with submission, and help the Prophet (ﷺ) in his call, and believe in him first. If you do not believe in him, then leave him so that he may proclaim his call, and do not oppose him, and do not turn people away from him, because the Truth is the One who says: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth after them, that We might see how you would act.﴾ (10:14).

Whenever a matter comes that Allah explains with the phrase ﴿that He may know...﴾ (5:94), or ﴿that We may see...﴾ (10:14), know that Allah is Knowing and All-Knowing. He knew all matters before they existed, and He knew the things in which people have choice. He is the One who says: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance(11) that people may establish justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great military strength and benefits for people, and that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen...﴾ (57:25).

The True One, glory be to Him, has known everything from eternity, and when Allah says ﴿that He may know﴾, this does not mean that there is a new knowledge that He did not have and that will arise for Him. Rather, it means knowledge of witnessing and of your acknowledgment, so that no one may say: why does Allah hold us accountable for what He knew from eternity? Rather, Allah brings the choice that determines for the servant the criteria by which the believer may enter Paradise and the disobedient may be called to account and recompensed.

Thereby man knows that the True One, glory be to Him, willed this, so that every servant may know the knowledge of actuality, not the knowledge of acquisition.

Therefore, the mention of the words ﴿that He may know﴾ and ﴿that We may see﴾ in the Qur'an means knowledge of actuality, knowledge of witnessing, and knowledge as proof against the servant, so that he cannot deny what has occurred. The word of the Truth: ﴿And that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen...﴾ (57:25). This verse explains to us the instruments of the orderly rule of the divine judgment: messengers who came with proof and clear evidence, and iron was sent down for subjugation. The True One, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great military strength and benefits for people...﴾ (57:25).

He linked this with the messengers, saying: ﴿that Allah may make evident who supports Him﴾. Support is not achieved except by strength, and strength comes by iron(12), which remains iron until the Hour is established. It is the metal of might, and they will not invent anything stronger than it. The knowledge of Allah, glory be to Him, here is knowledge of an event from you, which you cannot deny, for if He, glory be to Him, had informed of a matter without an event from you, you might have lied. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿that Allah may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen﴾, and in this there is a kind of beautiful precaution.

His, the Exalted's, words ﴿that Allah may make evident who supports Him﴾ are as if Allah asks you to support Him. But beware of understanding that He, glory be to Him, is weak, God forbid. Rather, He is strong and mighty. He is the One who says: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands...﴾ (9:14). Rather, He, glory be to Him, wants the enemies of faith to be humbled before you, because He, glory be to Him, is capable over them.

Therefore, the True One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿that Allah may make evident who supports Him﴾, which means only that Allah's knowledge of who supports His method should be an unseen matter, so that no one may say that the victory of the method came by chance. Rather, the True One, glory be to Him, wants to make the support of His method to be by the believers, even if their number is small and their multitude is few.

Therefore, the word of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth after them, that We might see...﴾ (10:14): that is, a seeing of actuality, not a seeing of knowledge.

1. Khalifa may also be pluralized as khulafa'. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah...﴾ (7:69).
2. A'dayta fa-'adaa: wa-'adawtuhu a'dūhu: I passed beyond it to another; and asta'daytu al-amir 'ala al-zalim: I asked the ruler for help against the oppressor, and he 'a'dani 'alayhi: he aided and supported me, so al-isti'dad is seeking strengthening and support. (Al-Misbah al-Munir, pp. 397-398.)
3. Al-'atab: destruction, which occurs in people and in other things. In the noble hadith, the mention of 'atab al-hady, which is its destruction, and it may be used to express a defect that befalls it, preventing it from walking, so it is slaughtered. What is meant by 'atab here is corruption, defect, or error. (Lisan al-'Arab, root '-t-b, adapted.) Allah, glory be to Him, says: ﴿He who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any imbalance...﴾ (67:3).
4. Al-hisban: calculation. "The sun and the moon by precise calculation" means: by reckoning and stations that Allah has determined, which they do not exceed. Al-Zajjaj said: "bi-hisban" indicates the number of months, years, and all times. Abu al-'Abbas said: hisban is a verbal noun of hasiba, yahsibuhu, hisaban and hisbanan. Al-Akhfash and Abu al-Haytham said: al-hisban is the plural of hisab. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿He cleaves the dawn and has made the night for rest and the sun and moon for calculation...﴾ (6:96). (Lisan al-'Arab, root h-s-b, adapted.)
5. Al-bayan: that by which a thing is shown through indication and other means. Bana al-shay' bayanan: it became clear, so it is clear; likewise abana al-shay' ibanatan, so it is mubin. Al-bayan is eloquence and clear expression with intelligence; al-bayan is the manifestation of the intended meaning in the most eloquent wording. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿This is a clarification for mankind and guidance and instruction for the righteous﴾ (3:138), and He says: ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is its clarification﴾ (75:19). (Lisan al-'Arab, root b-y-n, adapted.)
6. Najm al-shay': it rose and appeared. Every thing that rises and appears is called najm. Therefore the exegetes differed in interpreting "najm" in the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-najm is what spreads over the surface of the earth (meaning: vegetation). Mujahid said: al-najm is that which is in the sky. See Lisan al-'Arab, root n-j-m, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/270).
7. "Do" and "do not do" are the basis on which the legal obligations depend: the obligatory (fard), the required (wajib), the recommended (mandub), the desirable (mustahabb), the prohibited (haram), the disliked (makruh), and the permissible (mubah).
8. The Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses (6) when he sees himself self-sufficient (7)﴾ (96:6-7). An example of this is the owner of the two gardens, about whom the Lord of Might said: ﴿Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fail therein at all, and We caused to gush forth within them a river (33)﴾ (18:33). But he transgressed by the blessing of Allah, saying: ﴿I do not think this will ever perish (35), and I do not think the Hour will be established; and if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than these as a destination (36)﴾ (18:35-36).
9. Allah, glory be to Him, urged people to reflect on the end of earlier peoples and what happened to them in their times, in many verses of the Qur'an, among them: ﴿There have already passed before you precedents; so proceed through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers (137)﴾ (3:137), and ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them...?﴾ (12:109). Allah, glory be to Him, has settled the question of the conflict between truth and falsehood in His saying: ﴿And Allah is dominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know﴾ (12:21).
10. Jizya: a sum of money imposed upon an adult male, placed upon the People of the Book who are under the covenant and protection of the Muslims. Islam imposed it upon them in exchange for the zakat imposed upon the Muslims, and in return for the Muslims' defense of the protected people (dhimmis) and their protection in the Islamic lands where they reside. It is obligatory upon one who is male, legally responsible, and free. It is not obligatory upon the poor and needy among the People of the Book. See al-Sheikh Sayyid Sabiq, Fiqh al-Sunnah (3/112-117).
11. Al-mizan: justice, measure; and al-mizan: the instrument by which things are weighed, its plural being mawazin. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah is the One who sent down the Scripture in truth and the balance...﴾ (42:17), and He says: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection...﴾ (21:47). (Lisan al-'Arab, root w-z-n, adapted.) Reviewed by His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Sanrawi, consultant at al-Azhar, and Mr. Adel Abu al-Mu'ati.
12. Al-hadid: the well-known metal from which various useful implements are made. The True One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great military strength and benefits for people...﴾ (57:25), meaning: in it is hardness and strength, and it is a means of victory and construction, and it may be a means of destruction if placed in the hand of one who has no conscience and no faith.

He (glory be to Him) says after that:

﴿When Our clear signs are recited to them(1), those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."(15)﴾

We know that the signs (ayat, sing. ayah, meaning a sign, a proof, or a wondrous thing) are of three kinds. The first kind is cosmic signs, which are the wonders in the universe, and which God (glory be to Him) calls signs. An ayah is a wonder among wonders, whether in its intelligence, beauty or creation. The Truth (glory be to Him) has named the cosmic phenomena signs. He, exalted, says: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, the sun and the moon...(37)﴾ [Fussilat]. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves...(21)﴾ [al-Rum]. These are cosmic signs.

There are also signs that are the evidence for the truthfulness of the messengers (peace be upon them) in conveying from God, and these are the miracles (mu'jizat), because they break the familiar law of the universe known to people. Everything has a nature, so when it departs from its nature, this calls for attention.

Just as the Qur'an relates about our master Abraham (peace be upon him) that his enemies seized him and threw him into the fire, and the Truth (glory be to Him) saved him from the fire, so he came out of it unharmed. The purpose was not that Abraham should be saved from the fire. For if the purpose had been that Abraham (peace be upon him) be saved from the fire, other things would have happened, such as that the Truth (Mighty and Majestic) would have prevented them from seizing him. But they seized him, lit the fire and threw him into it. Had God (exalted be He) wished to extinguish it, He would have done so with a little rain, but that did not happen, for God left them in their error(3). And because He is the bestower of the fire's burning, He (glory be to Him and exalted) said to it: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe upon Abraham(69)﴾ [al-Anbiya']. Thus their failure is made manifest before them.

So: the word ayat applies to cosmic signs, applies to miracles, and also applies to the verses of the Qur'an, since the Qur'anic verses are from God, the miracles are from God, and the creation of the universe is from God. Is there any sign that contradicts another sign? No. Because the One who created the universe, sent the messengers with miracles, and revealed the Qur'an is one God. Had the matter been otherwise, contradiction would have occurred among the signs. The Truth (glory be to Him) is the One who said: ﴿...Had it been from other than God, they would have found in it much discrepancy(82)﴾ [al-Nisa'], and His saying (exalted be He): ﴿When Our clear signs are recited to them...(15)﴾ [Yunus]: that is, clear signs.

Then the Truth (glory be to Him) says: ﴿Those who do not expect to meet Us say...﴾. We have known that raja' (expectation, hope) is seeking a matter that is loved and that may possibly occur, as a person hopes that his son will enter the faculty of medicine or the faculty of engineering. The opposite of raja' is another loved thing, but the person knows it is impossible, and this is tamanni (wishing). So the loved things are then of two kinds: matters that are wished for, which are impossible matters, though a person declares that he loves them; and a second kind, matters that we love and that may occur, and these are called raja'.

﴿Those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ are those who do not believe, neither in a god nor in resurrection. They said: ﴿It is only our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time(24)﴾ [al-Jathiya].

And they said: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected...?(82)﴾ [al-Mu'minun]. If a person does not believe in resurrection, then he does not believe in meeting God (glory be to Him), because whoever believes in resurrection believes in meeting God, and prepares himself for that meeting through worship and righteous deeds. But the disbelievers, who do not believe in resurrection, will be taken by surprise by the God whom they denied, and the surprise will be difficult for them. Therefore He (glory be to Him) said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage(5) in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing...(39)﴾ [al-Nur]. The mirage (sarab) is when a person walks in the empty desert and imagines that there is water before him, and whenever he walks he thinks the water is in front of him, but when he reaches the place he finds that the water has receded. This process is related to the question of the reflection of light: the light is reflected so as to depict water while it is not water. ﴿...until, when he comes to it, he finds nothing there, but he finds God with him...(39)﴾ [al-Nur]. He is surprised by the presence of God (glory be to Him), who was not in his mind. He is one of those who do not expect to meet God, and he is among those of whom it was said: ﴿And they say, "When we are lost in the earth(7), shall we indeed be in a new creation?" Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord(10)﴾ [al-Sajda].

Although the universe that we see necessitates the question of resurrection, because we see that everything has a cycle. The beautiful rose, full of freshness, wilts after it loses its moisture and its colour is lost, and then it becomes dust. When you smell the rose, this means that the fragrance in it evaporates with the water that leaves it as vapour, then it wilts and decomposes after that.

So the rose has a life cycle. If you look at any element of life, such as water, you will find that the amount of water present is the very amount present when God created the heavens and the earth; it has neither increased nor decreased. We have explained that before. Everything you benefit from has a cycle, and each cycle hands over to another cycle, and you benefit between these cycles, through demolition and construction.

Those who do not expect to meet God, and do not believe in resurrection, nor in reward or punishment, do not pay attention to the universe in which they live(8), because contemplating the universe and reflecting on its conditions obliges them to believe that it is a cycle that may return.

He (glory be to Him) says: ﴿As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it...(104)﴾ [al-Anbiya']. And those who do not expect to meet God are addressed by what the Qur'an mentions of their words: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it...(15)﴾ [Yunus]. They here make two demands: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this﴾ and ﴿or change it﴾. That is, they seek something other than the Qur'an. Let us note that the speaker is God (glory be to Him), so do not understand that the two statements are equal.

﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it﴾ are two requests. The first request: that they seek a Qur'an other than the one revealed. The second request: that they want to replace one verse with another verse. They had asked for the removal of the verses that mock the idols, and likewise the verses that threaten them with a bad end(10).

God (glory be to Him) answers one side of what they asked, namely the second request, and says: ﴿Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord"﴾. The Truth (glory be to Him) did not respond to their words: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this﴾.

The standard of the answer would have been: "It is not for me to bring a Qur'an other than this, or to change it." But He confined the reply to the second request, ﴿or change it﴾, because bringing a Qur'an requires changing the whole. But substitution is the easier matter. He negated the easier one so that they would accept that the harder request is negated by its very nature.

The Truth (glory be to Him) commanded His messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord"﴾: that is, the matter of substitution is possible, but it is not from the Messenger of God (ﷺ)(11). Rather it is by command from God (glory be to Him and exalted). As for the command to bring a Qur'an other than this, it is not possible.

So: substitution is possible on condition that it does not come from the Messenger (ﷺ). For this reason the Truth (glory be to Him) said: ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse(12), and God knows best what He reveals...(101)﴾ [al-Nahl]. This is what this verse mentions: ﴿Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord"﴾. The word ﴿talqa'﴾ (on my own accord) derives from liqa' (meeting). You say: "I met so-and-so" (laqitu fulanan), and the verbal noun comes from the same root or its letters. They call the word talqa' here "direction".

The Truth (glory be to Him) says in another verse: ﴿And when he turned towards Madyan(13)...(22)﴾ [al-Qasas]:

﴿Towards Madyan﴾ means in the direction of Madyan. And talqa' may come with the meaning of "meeting", because when you say "I met him", it means that you and so-and-so met in one place, and when we turn towards a specific place, we are found in it. Some people think that every word that comes with two meanings carries a contradiction. We say: No, there is no contradiction, rather it is a separation of direction. Like the saying of the Truth (glory be to Him): ﴿So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque...(144)﴾ [al-Baqara]. Shatr means direction, and it also means half. One says: "So-and-so took half his wealth", meaning his half, and "I turned towards such-and-such", meaning towards that direction.

These meanings are not contradictory. When any one of us stands in any place, that place becomes the centre of his field of vision, and everything around it is a circle that ends at the horizon.

The circle of each person's vision differs according to the strength of his sight. The circle of vision ends when it seems to you that the sky has met the earth; this is the horizon that belongs to you. If your sight is strong, your horizon widens, and if your sight is weak, the horizon narrows.

One says: "So-and-so has a narrow horizon", meaning his vision is limited. Each one of us, when he stands in a place, becomes the centre of what surrounds him of visible things. Therefore there is more than one centre: what faces you is half of the visible universe, and behind you is the other half of the visible universe. If it is said that shatr is half, then shatr is also direction.

Here the Truth (glory be to Him) says: ﴿Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me"﴾: that is, he (ﷺ) does not bring the Qur'an from himself (ﷺ), rather it is revealed to him.

The Truth (glory be to Him) ends the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day...(15)﴾ [Yunus]: that is, if he (ﷺ) had brought something from himself, this would be disobedience to God (exalted be He). We know that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was not known to be a poet, nor a writer, nor an orator. After the revelation came down to him from God, the Qur'an came in the utmost eloquence.

The revelation came down when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was forty years old, and there is no genius whose manifestation is postponed until this stage of life. The Prophet (ﷺ) could not have postponed his genius until that age, because he could not guarantee that his life would be prolonged.

1 Ayah: a lesson or evidence, and ayah: a miracle or a wondrous thing. The plural is ayat and ay. God (exalted) said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons...(53)﴾ [Fussilat]. The signs here are the clear proofs of God's oneness and the perfection of His power and self-subsistence. [Lisan al-'Arab: root ('ya), adapted].
2 Talqa': a verbal noun from laqiya. It is said: "Your talqa' pleases me," meaning your meeting. It is used as an adverb of place meaning the direction of meeting and facing.
3 Al-ghayy: error. Ghawa, yaghwa, ghayan and ghiwaya: he persisted in error. God (exalted) said: ﴿Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred(2)﴾ [al-Najm]. Tagha wa al-qawm: the people gathered and cooperated in evil. Istaghwahu bi al-amani al-kadhiba: he sought his error and misled him with false wishes. God (exalted) said: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become clear from error...(256)﴾ [al-Baqara]. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit: root (gh-w-y), adapted].
4 Al-dahr: a long period of time, and the duration of worldly life. God (exalted) said: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?(1)﴾ [al-Insan]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile time, for God is time," meaning: whatever befalls you from time, God is its doer and not time. So if you curse time, it is as if you intended God, exalted above what they say or describe. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (d-h-r), adapted].
5 Sarab: what is seen at midday from the intensity of heat, like water in the desert, clinging to the ground. It is an illusion of the eye. It is called sarab because it flows (yasrub), that is, it moves in a way that deceives the viewer from afar, so he thinks it is water when it is not water, but an optical and visual illusion arising from the psychological state of the person when he is extremely thirsty and in a barren desert. So any movement from afar he thinks is water and runs towards it, only to be surprised by the absence of anything.
6 Qay'a: a wide, level land that grows no trees. Al-Farra' said: qay'a is the plural of qa', and qa' is what is spread out of the land. God (exalted) said: ﴿And He will leave it as a smooth, level plain(106)﴾ [Ta-Ha]. [Lisan: root (q-r-').., adapted].
7 Dalalna fi al-ard: Abu Mansur said: the origin in Arabic speech is that one says "adlaltu al-shay'" when one hides it, and "adlaltu al-mayyit" when one buries the dead. So dalal has among its meanings corruption, disobedience, the opposite of guidance and right direction, and among its meanings concealment and burial. It is as if they were saying: "When we are buried and hidden under the earth, shall we live again?" Then the Truth (glory be to Him) answers them with His saying: ﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him...(27)﴾ [al-Rum]. [Lisan: root (d-l-l), adapted].
8 God (exalted) has related this about them: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it(105)﴾ [Yusuf]. He (glory be to Him) also says: ﴿And We made the sky a protected canopy, yet they turn away from Our signs(32)﴾ [al-Anbiya'].
9 On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood among us giving a sermon and said: "O people, you will be gathered to God barefoot, naked and uncircumcised," then he recited: ﴿As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it, a promise upon Us; indeed We will do it(104)﴾ [al-Anbiya']. The hadith is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6524) in similar form, and by Muslim (2860), and the wording is Muslim's.
10 This agrees with what al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (4/3245) on this verse. He said: In their saying there are three aspects:
First: they asked him to change the promise into a threat and the threat into a promise, and the lawful into the unlawful and the unlawful into the lawful. Said by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari.
Second: they asked him to remove from the Qur'an the blame of their gods and the ridicule of their intellects. Said by Ibn 'Isa.
Third: they asked him to remove from it the mention of resurrection and rising. Said by al-Zajjaj.
11 God (glory be to Him and exalted) says concerning Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings(44), We would have seized him by the right hand(45), then We would have cut from him the aorta(46), and not one of you could have held Us off from him(47)﴾ [al-Haqqa]. This is an affirmation that Muhammad (ﷺ) cannot add or subtract in what is revealed to him from God, otherwise God would have seized him and cut the sinew of his heart and caused him to die.
12 This is the abrogation by substitution (naskh al-tabdil), for the ease of people or for a wisdom that God (glory be to Him) knows. Ease and the removal of hardship are among the objectives of the Sharia. He (glory be to Him) says: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in religion any hardship; it is the religion of your father Abraham. He named you "Muslims" before...(78)﴾ [al-Hajj]. And He (exalted) says: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth one better than it or similar to it...(106)﴾ [al-Baqara]. Naskh in the Qur'an is of kinds:
1. What has been abrogated in both its recitation and its ruling. 'A'isha said: among what was revealed was "ten known sucklings", then it was abrogated by "five known sucklings".
2. What has abrogated its ruling while its recitation remains. This is very rare in the Qur'an, and some people have exaggerated it without justification.
3. A category that abrogates the laws of earlier communities and what was the situation in the pre-Islamic era. See al-Suyuti, al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an (3/59-77).
13 Madyan: the name of the town of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him).
14 Shatr of a thing: its side. The shatr of everything is its direction and aim. I aimed at its shatr, meaning its side. "Shatr al-Masjid al-Haram": towards it and facing it. God (exalted) said: ﴿And wherever you are, turn your faces towards it(144)﴾ [al-Baqara]. Shatr of a thing means its half; the plural is ashtur and shutur. I divided it: I made it into two halves. Shatarahu malahu: he shared his wealth with him equally. In the hadith: Sa'd asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for permission to give all his wealth in charity. He said: "No." He said: "Half?" He said: "No." He said: "A third?" He said: "A third, and a third is much." And in the hadith: "Purity is half of faith", narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari (223), because faith manifests through the inner aspect, and purity manifests through the outer aspect. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (sh-t-r), adapted].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 16:

Almighty Allah brings us the decisive proof that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) follows only what is revealed to him, saying: ﴿Say: I follow only what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.﴾ [Yunus 10:15]. Then comes the command from Almighty Allah to respond to the disbelievers:

﴿Say: Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?﴾ [Yunus 10:16]:

Here Muhammad (ﷺ) conveys to those who demanded changing the Qur'an or altering it: I have lived my whole life among you, and I possessed no eloquence, no poetic gift, and no literary skill. Whoever has a talent does not conceal it until he reaches forty. You saw that he (ﷺ) did not sit with a teacher. Rather, when you accused him and said: ﴿It is only a human being who teaches him...﴾ [al-Nahl 16:103], Almighty Allah exposed you by revealing in the Qur'an His saying, may He be exalted: 

﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic speech.﴾ [al-Nahl 16:103]. The Prophet (ﷺ) did not leave the Arabian Peninsula, nor did he read the works of anyone. So where did the Qur'an come from?

It came from Allah, Glorified is He, and you ought to reason about this. There is no need for the accusation that the Qur'an is from Muhammad, because you did not test him as an orator or a poet. Rather, everything that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought, after the message was revealed to him, is a communication from Allah.

Naturally, perfection cannot be attributed to a person and then denied of him. The custom is that a poet might steal a poem from another poet, or a writer might appropriate an article from another. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informs you that the perfection of the Qur'an is not from him; he is merely its conveyor. They should have reasoned about that matter with its premises and its conclusions, and not given free rein to their thoughts so that they lie and obstinately deny. The matter is very simple.

Almighty Allah says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?﴾ [Yunus 10:16].

So, the premise by which Almighty Allah wishes to persuade the disbelievers is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent by Allah as a messenger from among themselves. If you say: ﴿He raised among them a messenger from themselves...﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:164]: that means he (ﷺ) is of the kind of humans, not of the kind of angels; or ﴿from themselves﴾ means from the Arab nation, not the non-Arab nation; or ﴿from themselves﴾ means from their own tribe, whose members denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

So, his life (ﷺ) is well known and familiar to you; he was never absent from you for a period, so that you could say he was sent on a mission to learn knowledge from another place. He did not sit with a teacher among you or outside you, and he did not recite a book. If this is the case, then you should take from this a premise and say: From where did this wisdom come to him suddenly?

You know that talents and genius do not arise in the forties; rather, the signs of genius appear at the end of the second decade and the beginning of the third decade. So who delayed genius in the case of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that he would utter this eloquent speech that has rendered you incapable, when you are the nation of eloquence and the nation of articulacy, trained in it since long ago, and you were unable before what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought?

You should have said: We never knew him to teach anything of this. Then, if he had resolved the riddle for you and clarified that the Qur'an is not from me, you should have believed him, because he (ﷺ) attributes it to its Creator and Lord, Glorified is He. The proof that you are confused in judgment is that when he tells you the Qur'an is a communication from Allah, you deny him and say: No, rather it is from you. Then when revelation pauses for a time, you say: His Lord has forsaken him. Why were you convinced that he has a Lord who connects him to revelation and abandons him without revelation?

You, then, have denied the state of connection to revelation, yet you acknowledged the Creating God when revelation was absent from him. You should have paid attention and returned to your minds to judge these things. Almighty Allah has mentioned this matter in many of His verses. He, Glorified is He, says: ﴿You were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would take care of Mary.﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:44]. And He, Glorified is He, says: ﴿You were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command...﴾ [al-Qasas 28:44].

And He, Glorified is He, says: ﴿Nor were you a resident among the people of Madyan...﴾ [al-Qasas 28:45], and He, Glorified is He, says:

﴿You did not recite any book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand; for then the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:48].

So from where did that eloquence come? You should have taken these premises so as to judge that he is truthful in conveying from Allah. Therefore, Almighty Allah concludes the verse which is the subject of our reflections with His saying: ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾

When Almighty Allah, Exalted is He, alerts you to use your intellect, this is evidence of confidence that if you use your intellect, you will arrive at the intended conclusion. Allah, Exalted is He, is far above deceiving His servants. One who deceives a person is the one who tries to afflict his intellect with heedlessness; but the one who alerts the intellect is the one who knows that the proof of the truth appropriate to what he says can be reached by reason.

The saying of Almighty Allah at the end of the verse, ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾, indicates to us that the matter about which they denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arose from their not using their intellects. Had they used their intellects in applying the perceptible premises which they believe in and accept, they would have arrived at the faith-based conclusion that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was stating.

And had they reflected and said: Muhammad grew up among us, and we did not know him to read, nor to recite a book, nor to sit with a teacher; he was never absent from us for a period in order to learn; he remained a long time until the age of forty without being reckoned for any speech, eloquence or expression; so from where did this strong impetus come to him?

They should have asked him himself: From where did this come to you? And since he told them that it came to him from Allah, they should have believed him.

The function of the intellect is always derived from its etymology: "al-'aql" (intellect) is derived from "'iqal" of the camel. The 'iqal of a camel is the rope with which the two legs of the camel are tied, so that it does not rise and stand up; so that we may direct its movement to where we wish it to move, instead of its walking aimlessly, without purpose or intention, while we tie its legs so that it rests and does not move until we need it in a movement.

So the intellect has come to govern the faculties, because every faculty has an inclination toward something. The eye has the faculty to see everything, and the intellect says to it: There is no need for you to look at that, for it is a sight that will harm you. The ear loves to hear every saying, and the intellect says to it: Do not listen to that, lest it harm you.

Thus the intellect is the controller over the rest of the limbs. Likewise the word "hikmah" (wisdom) is derived from "hukmah" (bridle), which is the bit placed in the mouth of a horse so that it does not bolt, and its movement remains measured, so that it moves only in the direction you want.

So Almighty Allah willed that man be distinguished by intellect and wisdom, in order to establish the balances for the faculties of the soul. So take the perceptible premises which you believe in, witness, and accept, and apply them to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that you may deduce that he brought his speech from Almighty Allah.

1 Lahada fi al-din, alhada and iltahada: he deviated from it, turned away, and kept away. Ilhad: disputation and contention. Almighty Allah says: ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs are not hidden from Us..﴾ [Fussilat 41:40] and He says: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names..﴾ [al-A'raf 7:180]. Ilhad also means injustice and oppression. He says: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment..﴾ [al-Hajj 22:25]. Ilhad linguistically means inclination away from the goal. His saying: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic speech..﴾ [al-Nahl 16:103]. The root of ilhad is inclination and deviation from a thing. Al-multahad: refuge, because the one seeking refuge inclines toward it. [Lisan al-'Arab, root (l-h-d), adapted].
2 'Ajm: al-'ajam and al-'ajm: the opposite of the Arabs and Arabic. A man who is 'ajami or a'jami is non-Arab. Abu Ishaq said: al-a'jam is one who does not speak clearly or articulately, even if he is Arab. The 'ajami is one who is of the kind of non-Arabs, whether eloquent or not. He says: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them, they would not have been believers in it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara 26:198-199].
3 Yantahilu al-shay': he attributes it to himself. Nahalahu al-qawl: he attributed it to him. A poet "nahala" a poem when it is attributed to him while it is the saying of another. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (n-h-l)].
4 'Anan: the 'anan of the bridle is the strap by which the animal is held; plural: a'innah. 'Anan also means rope. The intended meaning here: likening thoughts to a camel that has a 'iqal or 'anan; if you loosen it for it, it goes and sets off as it wills and desires without guidance.
