The 'anan for animals is like the 'aql for a human; if the intellect is corrupted its possessor goes astray, and if a person does not restrain his thoughts, he goes astray. [Lisan al-'Arab: root ('-n-n), adapted].
5 The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was unlettered, who could neither read nor write. Almighty Allah says: ﴿And you did not recite any book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand; for then the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:48].
6 In this regard Almighty Allah says: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; anxious over you; for the believers, kind and merciful.﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:128].
7 Al-martadun: those who have practice, whose tongues have been trained in eloquence and rhetoric.
8 Qalahu rabbuhu: He hated him and abandoned him. Therefore his Lord said to him: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you].﴾ [al-Duha 93:3].
9 Aqlamuhum: their arrows. It was said: their pens with which they used to write the Torah. Al-Zajjaj said: the aqlam here are the qidah (arrow-lots), arrows on which they put marks by which they would know who would take care of Mary, by way of lottery. The arrow was called qalam because it is pared (yuqlamu), i.e., trimmed. Whatever you cut from something piece after piece, you have "qalamtahu"; from this comes the pen with which one writes, and it was called qalam because it is trimmed time after time. From this it is said: "qalamtu adhfari" (I trimmed my nails). Almighty Allah says: ﴿And if whatever trees are upon the earth were pens and the sea [were ink], replenished thereafter by seven more seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted.﴾ [Luqman 31:27]. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (q-l-m), adapted].
10 Yakfulu: he supports, and al-kafil: the one who provides for. Almighty Allah says: ﴿And Zachariah became her guardian.﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:37].
11 Al-gharbi: the western mountain where Almighty Allah spoke to His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, at the tree which is on the eastern side of the bank of the sacred valley (Tuwa). [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/391, adapted].
12 Thawiyan: residing. Al-thawa': residence; thawaytu bi al-makan: I resided in the place. Almighty Allah says: ﴿And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:151]. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (th-w-a), adapted].
13 Al-'aql: restraint, the opposite of foolishness; 'aqala ya'qilu, so he is 'aqil. Ibn al-Anbari said: the intelligent man is one who gathers his affair and his opinion; it is derived from "'aqaltu al-ba'ir" when I gathered its legs. It was said: the intelligent one is the one who holds himself back and restrains him from his desires. Al-'aql: firmness in affairs.
14 And He, Glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all those one will be questioned.﴾ [al-Isra 17:36].
15 Hikmat al-lijam: what surrounds the jaws of the horse; it was named so because it prevents it from running violently. It was said: al-hikmah is a piece of iron in the bridle placed over the horse's nose and jaw, preventing it from disobeying its rider. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (h-k-m)].
It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "There is no human except that on his head is a hikmah in the hand of an angel; if he humbles himself, it is said to the angel: Raise his hikmah; and if he becomes arrogant, it is said to the angel: Lower his hikmah." Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12939), and cited by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (8/82), who said: its chain is hasan.

Then the Almighty says, after that:

﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ (17)

Here the Qur'an makes clear, on the tongue of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Would I lie about Allah? If I have not lied to you, in my affairs with you and in matters you have tested of me, would I lie about Allah?! Is it reasonable that one who did not lie at the beginning of his life would lie in old age? And if I have not lied to you, then would I lie about Allah?

And if I did not lie while my thinking was immature, in my childhood before I reached manhood, then I certainly cannot lie now. If you accuse me of that, then I am not wronging myself by accusing it of lying, and you would become the liars, because you have called me a liar regarding the Qur'an being a message conveyed from Allah. And if I had said that it came from myself, it would have been logical for you to deny that, because it is a claimed honour. But I refer it to another, to One who is higher than me and you."

His words, the Truth: ﴿Who does greater wrong﴾, meaning: none does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah the Glorified, because the liar lies only to deceive those before him. Would anyone lie to one who knows things as they really are? No one is capable of that. Whoever lies to human beings who are equal to him wrongs them, but the greater wrong is that of one who lies against Allah the Glorified.

Al-iftira' (invention, fabrication) is deliberate lying. It is possible for a person to state a matter he believes, but which is not in fact the case, having been told it by someone he trusts, and later it becomes clear that it did not happen. This is a lie in a sense, but it is unintentional; whereas al-iftira' is deliberate lying.

For this reason, when the scholars of language divided declarative speech (khabar) and performative speech (insha'), they said that to the speaker of a declarative statement one says "You spoke truly" or "You lied": if the statement corresponds to reality it is true, and if it does not correspond to reality it is false.

His words, the Truth: ﴿invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs﴾ show them the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: If you say that I claimed the speech is from Allah, while it is not from Allah, then this means the speech is a lie and comes from me. So what is the position of one who denies the signs of Allah?

The lie comes from you, for if you call me a liar and claim that I say this is from Allah, while it is not from Allah, and you persist and deny the signs, saying they are from me when they are not from me but from Allah, then the sin is upon you.

Lying may come from the side of the speaker or from the side of the listener, and the Messenger (ﷺ) intended a fair distribution in more than one place, as the Truth says, displaying the courtesy of prophethood: ﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ [Saba': 24]

There is no courtesy in presentation greater than this. It shows that his cause and their cause will never meet: one of them is true and the other false. But who determines which cause is true and which is false? It is Allah the Glorified.

You find Him, glorified, saying on the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿or in clear error.﴾ In this there is a request that they present the matter to their minds, so that they may know which of the two causes is guidance and which is error.[3]

In this there is the elevation of debate to the better manner by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The Almighty says: ﴿Say, "You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do."﴾ [Saba': 25] That is: each one will be asked about his own deed. Your crime, I will not be asked about it, and my crime, you will not be asked about it. He attributed the crime to his own side and did not say, "You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you commit." He did this so that the debate would be elevated; he chose the manner that refines, not one that provokes the opponent so that he becomes obstinate. This is part of wisdom, so that he does not say to the opponent what causes his tension and obstinacy, and the debate continues without benefit.

Here the Almighty says: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah?﴾ If the wrong comes from my side, Allah will call me to account for it; and if it comes from your side, then know the saying of the Almighty: ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ He did not specify who the criminal is, and left the judgment to the listener.

As when you say to a person with whom you have a dispute: "I will present the matter to you, and you judge": when you delegate the judgment to him, he will only reach what you want. And if the matter were not so, you would not have presented it to him.

1 Iftara: fabricated, invented. Al-fira': lying. "Iftara" indicates intensity in lying.

2 This is from the category of laff wa-nashr (arrangement and correspondence), one of the forms of badi' (rhetorical embellishment) in the Qur'an. Its definition: "that two things or several things are mentioned, either in detail by stating each one, or in summary, by using a word that includes several, and then things are mentioned corresponding to that number, each referring back to one of the earlier items, leaving it to the listener's mind to assign each to what suits it" (al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an by al-Suyuti, 3/280, 279). Here it is detailed, like His saying: ﴿He made for you the night and the day, that you might rest therein and seek of His bounty...﴾ [al-Qasas: 73], where resting refers to the night and seeking refers to the day.

3 The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used this method with the polytheists; they would say to them: "By Allah, we and you are not upon one matter; one of the two parties is surely guided." Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (3/538), from the saying of Qatadah. It is an invitation to the polytheists to engage their thought and reason.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says after that: ﴿They worship besides God that which can neither harm them nor benefit them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with God." Say: "Will you inform God of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾ (10:18). The word ﴿they worship﴾ requires the existence of a worshipper, the existence of a worshipped one, and the existence of a meaning of worship. The worshipper is lower in rank than the one worshipped, and the manifestation of worship and servitude is entirely obedience to a command and turning away from what He forbids.

This is the origin of worship and the means of drawing near to God.

For worship to be in its correct place, the worshipper must acknowledge that the one worshipped is higher in rank in judging things. If the matter is between equals, they call it a request (iltimas).

So there is a commander and one commanded. If they are equal, the one commanded needs to be persuaded. But if there is a prior judgment that the commander is higher than the one commanded, like a teacher in relation to a student, or a doctor in relation to a patient, then in this situation the one commanded obeys the commander because he understands the matter about which he is commanded.

Likewise the believer, because the meaning of faith is that he believes in the existence of a capable God who possesses all the attributes of absolute perfection. When you believe this, the person carries out what God commands, so as to obtain His pleasure, love and reward. If he does not carry it out, he will incur the anger and punishment of the one worshipped.

So if you do what He commands and avoid what He forbids, you gain reward from Him, and if you oppose Him, you receive punishment. Therefore the one worshipped must be higher than you in power, and must be able to carry out reward and punishment, and the One who is capable of that is God, may He be exalted.

As for the idols they used to worship, what did they command them to do? They commanded nothing, so it is not fitting that they be worshipped, because the meaning of worship requires a command and a prohibition, and the idols commanded nothing and forbade nothing. Rather, it was the polytheists who proposed the commands and prohibitions, and this is an unseemly matter, because the one worshipped is the one who must define the aspects of commands and prohibitions.

So it is folly for anyone to worship the idols, because they neither harm those who oppose them nor benefit those who worship them. They have no command and no prohibition.

Those who placed themselves in this position forgot that each of them has the power to benefit the idol and to harm it. One of them can make the idol, repair it if it breaks, or break it by throwing it to the ground. In this case the worshipper is more capable than the worshipped of harm and benefit, and this is the very essence of intellectual regression.

So such worship is a kind of folly, and if this matter were presented to sound reason, sound reason would reject it.

When you argue with them and establish for them that those idols neither harm nor benefit, you will find someone who insists, saying: ﴿These are our intercessors with God.﴾ By this statement they acknowledge that God is the One who benefits and harms, but should they not have sought an intercessor for themselves with God, and should the intercessor not enjoy status and affection with the one to whom he intercedes?

Then what do they say about the fact that the one to whom intercession is made is the very One who forbids taking idols as gods and forbids worshipping them?

And is there any intercession without the permission of the one with whom intercession is made? For this reason the command came from the Truth, glorified is He, to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say: "Will you inform God of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"﴾ [Yunus].

So where did you get this matter, the matter of the idols interceding for you with God? It is a matter that has no existence. He, glorified is He, has not informed you that there are idols that intercede, and this is not something that has occurred. Your saying this involves deliberate lying and fabrication.

He, glorified is He, is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and He knows everything in the universe. The matter of the intercession of idols is not within His knowledge, and it has no existence. Rather, it is a fabricated, claimed matter.

His saying here, the Truth: ﴿Will you inform God﴾ is like His saying, the Truth: ﴿Say: "Will you inform God about your religion?"﴾ [al-Hujurat] (49:16). This statement is a rebuttal to those who said and say that what is required is legislation suited to the age, and whenever the age becomes corrupt they demand new legislation. Since they are the ones who legislate, it is as though they wish to teach their Creator how religion should be. This is audacity and ignorance regarding the power and wisdom of the One who created the universe and made it firm with a system.

His saying, the Truth: ﴿Say: "Will you inform God of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth? Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him."﴾ contains a declaration of His transcendence, glorified is He. He is the Creator of everything, the Creator of dominion and the realm of the unseen, and He knows everything. The matter of the intercession of idols is a fabricated matter with no existence, so it is not within God's knowledge. The Truth, glorified is He, is far above having in His dominion a matter with a certain meaning that He does not know. He, exalted is He, is also far above having partners associated with Him, because a partner exists only to help the one who makes him a partner. We see, for example, a man of wealth who runs his money in some trade, but his money cannot bear all the responsibilities of the trade, so he seeks a partner.

Glorified and exalted is He, strong and capable, and He has no need of anyone in owning and managing the universe. Then what do these claimed partners, who lie about God, do?

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: "If there were with Him other gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne."﴾ (17:42) This wise statement alerts the polytheists that, on the dialectical assumption that these partners have power and capacity to act, they would still do nothing except by seeking the One of the Throne, that is, by His command, glorified and exalted is He. When they wrongly imagined that each sphere has control over some domain of existence, and that the stars have control over existence, and that each zodiac sign has control over existence, then in the end there must be seeking permission from the Owner of the dominion and the realm of the unseen.

It is a disappointment for those who entertained such assumptions, and along with them the philosophers who acknowledged that there are things in the universe that a human cannot create, or claim to have manufactured, because the human species came after these creations. Man arrived after the sun, the moon, the stars and the earth, so there must be a power higher than man that created these beings. All these beings need a Originator, and we have not found a factory for making the sun, the moon or the earth, nor have we found anyone who claimed to have made or created them.

But the philosophers who accepted the existence of a Creator of the universe did not reach His name or His method. The power of the Truth, glorified is He, is absolute, and He has no need of a partner. If we want to contemplate even a small part of the effect of God's power that He bestowed upon man, let us contemplate the manufacture of the electric lamp.

Each of us knows that there is no seed we place in the earth that grows into trees of lamps. Rather, the manufacture of the electric bulb required the effort of scientists who studied the science of energy, and who derived from equations the possibility of conceiving the making of the electric lamp, and who worked to evacuate the air from the glass vessel in which the filament that glows inside the lamp is placed. Thus we find that the manufacture of a single electric lamp requires the effort of scientists and the work of factories, all for lighting one room for a period of time. What then of the sun, which lights the whole universe? If the most trivial things require a huge quantity of knowledge, research, technical and applied capabilities, and developed industries, then what of the sun, which lights half the terrestrial globe every half day, and no one can extinguish it, and it needs no maintenance from humans? If you wish to attribute it to a source, you will find none but God, glorified is He.

What you invent and make can never divert you from God, and the truly intelligent person is the one who makes his inventions and manufactures a proof of the truthfulness of God in what He has informed.

And since the Truth, glorified is He, created the sun (among what He created), when it rises all people extinguish their lamps, because it is the lamp that guides everyone. If that is the act of one of God's creatures, then what of every blessing from among His other creatures? The light of the sun represents the sensory guidance that protects us from colliding with things, so that they do not destroy us and we do not destroy them. Likewise, the Truth, glorified is He, illuminates for us meanings and realities.

Beware of saying: "Such-and-such philosopher came with such-and-such a theory, so take it." Rather, let your intellect work and measure what came in that theory against what was revealed in the Book of the Truth, glorified is He. If the theory enters the field of application and it is established that it has confirmation from the Book, then say: "The Truth, glorified is He, has guided so-and-so to discover a new secret of the secrets of the Qur'an," because the Truth wants us to understand things and study them with precise study, so that we take the aspirations of the intellect to bring us closer to God, not to drive us away from Him, God forbid.

And when the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Glorified and exalted is He above what they associate﴾, that is because association (shirk) requires seeking assistance. Seeking assistance comes either from an equal or from a higher one, and there is no equal to God, exalted is He, and no higher than God, glorified is He.

1 Al-Jawhari said: Shirk is disbelief. Ashraka yushriku ishraakan, so he is a mushrik, and they are mushrikun. In a hadith: "Shirk is more hidden in my community than the crawling of an ant." Ibn al-Athir said: he means showing off in action, as though he associated someone other than God in his work. In a hadith: "Whoever swears by other than God has associated." [Lisan al-Arab, entry shirk, adapted].
2 Al-humq (folly): placing a thing in other than its proper place. Al-humq is the opposite of intellect or a lack and weakness of intellect. Al-humqa': wine, because it leaves its drinker in folly. The ahmaq (fool) is derived from inhimaq al-suq when the market becomes stagnant, as though his intellect became corrupt until it stagnated. Ibn al-A'rabi said: the root of humq is stagnation. It is also said: "humq" is stagnant intellect. Humq also means delusion. Inhamaqa al-rajul: the man became weak in the matter. [Lisan al-Arab, entry humq].
3 He, glorified is He, says: ﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He approves.﴾ (20:109). The polytheists' claim that the idols intercede for them with God is a false claim, and along with its falsehood, it is an acknowledgment by them that intercession is only from God, glorified is He. And the intercession of God is only for a beloved one and one who is loved, whom He knows, by obligation and grace.
4 Ibtaghaw: they sought. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿They had already sought discord before, and turned affairs against you.﴾ (9:48) [Lisan al-Arab, entry bagha].
5 The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "God."﴾ (31:25). He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And He is the One who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon.﴾ (21:33). He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And if He willed, He would have made it still; then We made the sun over it an indicator.﴾ (25:45).

Al-Sha'rawi, *Tafsir al-Sha'rawi* (surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 10, verse 19 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:
﴿Mankind was but one community, then they differed. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them concerning that in which they differ.﴾ (19)

A verse in Surat al-Baqarah similar to this verse has come, although the style differs. The Truth, glorified is He, said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Mankind was one community, and Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners.﴾ (213). Those who read the Qur'an superficially and without depth may not pay attention to the verses that are similar to it in general meaning. These verses balance one another, so there is no contradiction between one verse and another.

For this reason, among modern thinkers there are those who say: "People were all disbelievers. Then the intellect progressed, trying to discover the most powerful of beings in order to worship it. They found that the mountain is the high, hard being, so they worshipped it. Other people said that the sun is the most powerful of beings, so they worshipped it. Others worshipped the moon, another group worshipped the stars, and some took trees as gods. Every group looked toward a different direction, seeking power in it."

They take from this that man was guided by his reason to the necessity of religion, and then this reason continued to progress until it reached monotheism.

We respond to the proponents of this view: You, by this, wish to separate creation from its Creator, as if Allah, who created creatures and provided them with the sustenance of their material life, had withheld from them the sustenance of their spiritual life. This is neither acceptable nor reasonable. How can He guarantee them material life and not guarantee for this materiality values that guard it from savagery and protect it from corruption and corrupting?

And His saying, the Truth: ﴿Mankind was one community, then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth, to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed. And none differed over it except those who were given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of envy among themselves. So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ (213) [al-Baqarah].

Therefore, some understood that people were one community in disbelief, and when the prophets came, people differed, because some of them believed and some of them remained in disbelief. But if those who said such a thing had made good inference and understanding from Allah, they would have found that the intended meaning of the verse we are presently reflecting upon is: ﴿Mankind was but one community, then they differed; so Allah sent the prophets to bring them out of disagreement and return them to agreement upon the original covenant of faith, in which they bore witness to the lordship of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He⁽²⁾; because the origin of the matter is faith, not disbelief⁽³⁾.

As for one who takes the verse of Surat al-Baqarah as evidence that people were disbelievers first, we say to him: Read the verse in its entirety, so that you find His saying, the Truth: ﴿Mankind was one community, then Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth, to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed..﴾ (213) [al-Baqarah].

Thus we see that the differing that occurred among people is mentioned in the al-Baqarah verse at the end, while the differing is mentioned in this verse at the beginning. This is evidence that people were one community upon faith⁽⁴⁾. There are no people more favored than others before the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, and the justice of Allah would not leave people floundering in their affairs in disbelief and then send messengers to other people with guidance. So people are equal before Allah. And since the Truth, glorified is He, has brought creation of mankind into existence, He must send down for them a method. For this reason, when we read the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah⁽⁵⁾, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾ (96) [Al 'Imran], we find in it a refutation of those who say that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was the first to build the Ka'bah. Because the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, did not leave creation from Adam until Ibrahim without a House to which they would make pilgrimage⁽⁶⁾. Rather, the Truth placed the House so that people would make pilgrimage to it from the time of Adam until the Hour is established. The One who placed the House is not from among mankind; rather, the Creator of mankind willed the placing of the House. What our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, did was raise the foundations of the Sacred House.

That is: he established the elevation of the House after the place of the House had been identified in length and breadth, confirming the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And when We settled⁽⁷⁾ for Ibrahim the place of the House..﴾ (26) [al-Hajj]. Thus the saying of the Truth, glorified is He, is confirmed, that the House had existed for mankind before Adam, and it is for mankind until the Hour is established. Thus we know that the Truth, glorified is He, created creation and sent down for them the method, and that the origin of mankind is faith. But disbelief is what came upon humans through two doors: the door of heedlessness, and the door of blind imitation of forefathers.

The proof of this is that when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, spoke about the covenant of the seed, He said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants⁽⁸⁾ and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this," (172) or say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ (173) [al-A'raf]. So then: the disobedience to the judgment of faith enters through two doors. The first is the door of heedlessness, meaning that you know something but you have not kept it constantly at the focal point of your awareness⁽⁹⁾, because your mind receives information and absorbs it in one time, if you are not scattered in thought over more than one matter. If you are clear in thought and attentive to the information that reaches you, your mind absorbs it in one time. It is important that the mind be empty at the moment it receives new information.

For this reason, we find a difference between one person and another in retaining information. One receives information while his mind is empty of any other information, so it is fixed in the focal point of awareness. Another is compelled to repeat reading the information until his mind is empty of other things, so the information settles in the focal point of awareness. When another piece of information comes, the first information moves to the margin of awareness until it is called back again.

If a student, for example, wants to absorb the new information he reads, he must shake off from his mind all other preoccupations⁽¹⁰⁾, in order to focus on what he studies. For if he sits down to study while his mind is occupied with what he will eat for lunch, or with what happened between him and his friends, or with what clothes he will wear when he leaves the house, or with other preoccupations, here the student will be compelled to reread the lesson more than once, until the lesson encounters a part free of the focal point of awareness, so that it settles there⁽¹¹⁾.

And we may find a student on the morning of the exam, hearing from his classmates that the exam may come from such-and-such part of the syllabus; so he opens the textbook to that part and reads it once. It settles in the focal point of awareness, and he enters the exam, and finds the question in the part he read once before he entered the committee room, so he answers the question accurately.

For this reason, the intelligent pupil is one who does what psychology calls "the process of retention" (istishab), that is: he reads the lesson, then closes the book, to ask himself: "What is new information on that page?" and tries to recall it, and tries to identify even the new terms on that page, and what new ideas corrected for him information or ideas that were wrong and present in him. Thus the student retains his information with focus and attention.

Likewise, the outstanding teacher is one who explains the lesson and then pauses to ask the pupils, in order to arouse their attention, so that none of them becomes occupied with what is outside the lesson. The outstanding teacher is one who delivers his lesson in a way that attracts the pupils, just as a narrated story attracts them, so that the academic information does not remain mere dry information.

In this way the mind continues without heedlessness. Heedlessness reaches religious matters, because in man there are desires that clash with commands and prohibitions, so the person forgets some commands and some prohibitions until there comes the rust⁽¹²⁾ of which the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts.﴾ (14) [al-Mutaffifin].

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him (ﷺ), explained this by the noble hadith: "The trust descended into the root⁽¹³⁾ of men's hearts, then the Qur'an descended, and they learned from the Qur'an and learned from the Sunnah." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) told us about the lifting of the trust, saying: "A man sleeps a sleep, and the trust is seized from his heart, so its trace is erased, like the trace of a spot⁽¹⁴⁾" (15). That is: like the sting of fire. Thus it continues, until the rust comes upon the heart.

So then: heedlessness creeps into the human soul, and whenever a person is heedless at one point, then he is heedless of another, and so on. But he who is not heedless is one who remembers the ruling, applies it, and tastes its sweetness⁽¹⁶⁾. An example of this: the Muslim whom Allah the Exalted expands his heart for prayer; if he does not pray, he remains burdened and in constriction.

For this reason it is reported in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Trials are presented to hearts like a mat, strand by strand. Any heart that absorbs them has a black spot put in it, and any heart that rejects them has a white spot put in it, until they become two hearts: one white like smooth rock, which no trial will harm as long as the heavens and the earth endure, and the other black and inverted, like a cup turned upside down, not recognizing good and not rejecting evil except what it has absorbed of its desire" (17).

So then: heedlessness is the first door through which Satan enters, and so he distances the person from the rulings of Allah. And if the father is heedless, the children imitate their fathers, and heedlessness comes to them as something inherited. Thus the heedless one becomes an example for those after him.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, said about the children who follow the heedlessness of their fathers: ﴿Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers upon.﴾ (170) [al-Baqarah]. The habit of imitating fathers is a false matter, because if we traced the matter of faith back to Adam, peace be upon him, the first father of all mankind, we would find that Adam, peace be upon him, implemented everything required by Allah⁽¹⁹⁾. If you say: ﴿Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers upon﴾, this statement obliges you not to deviate from natural faith; otherwise you would be among the liars, not scrutinizing what entered upon natural faith of heedlessness or heedlessnesses, followed by imitation without examination.

The Truth, glorified is He, has willed that every word in the Qur'an have a precise intended meaning. The Truth, glorified is He, says, speaking of the path of the disbelievers in the Qur'an: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community, and indeed we are following in their footsteps.﴾ (23) [al-Zukhruf]. He did not say "guided" (muhtadun) but said "following" (muqtadun). The one who follows among them is one who has made his father a power, but the one who is guided is one who thought his father was upon the truth.

So then: the one who follows is one who does not care about the sincerity of his father's faith, but merely imitates him. And imitation of fathers is of two kinds: imitation as absolute following having no connection to guidance or misguidance, and imitation as the correct guidance of the law of Allah, the Exalted.

A disagreement has occurred concerning Adam, peace be upon him: was he a messenger or only a prophet⁽²⁰⁾? Some said: the first of the messengers was Nuh (Noah), peace be upon him. We say: Is it reasonable that Allah would leave the peoples who preceded Nuh, peace be upon him, without a messenger?

Indeed the Truth, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿And there is no community but that a warner has passed among them.﴾ (24) [Fatir]. What confused those exegetes who said that the first messenger was Nuh, peace be upon him, is that they thought superficially, and understood that a messenger comes to those to whom he is sent. Since there were no humans before Adam, how could Adam be sent with a message, and to whom would that message be?

These exegetes did not realize that Adam, peace be upon him, was a messenger and a model for his children. The Truth, glorified is He, said to him: ﴿..Then if guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ (38) [al-Baqarah]. And glorified is He said to Adam, peace be upon him: ﴿..Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer.﴾ (123) [Ta-Ha].

Since the Truth, glorified is He, has mentioned guidance, this is a mention of the method, and he (Adam) applied it in conduct, which his children imitated. These exegetes also neglected to extrapolate...

1 Those who held that people were one community upon disbelief, then differed in worshipping manifestations of power, then realized that cosmic powers are transient and so were guided by reason to Allah, the Exalted. These people forgot the first covenant in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this,"﴾ (172) [al-A'raf]. But people were one community upon the natural disposition of faith: ﴿The nature of Allah upon which He created mankind. No change is there in the creation of Allah..﴾ (30) [al-Rum]. Then they differed by worshipping other than Allah; so Allah sent the messengers. Otherwise, sending messengers would be pointless if people were one community upon disbelief and were guided by their intellects to Allah, the Exalted. This is a deficient understanding..

2 And this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this,"﴾ (172) [al-A'raf].

3 Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "Between Nuh and Adam there were twenty centuries, all upon a law of truth, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners." Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (1/250)..

4 The mention of the differing at the beginning in the verse of Surat Yunus and its delay in Surat al-Baqarah: the primary matter is that the community was one upon the religion of Allah and His method, and difference is incidental; for this the messengers came. As for the position of our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in the verse of al-An'am, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when the night covered him, he saw a star and said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "I like not those that set." (76) Then when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people who are astray." (77) Then when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free of what you associate with Allah. (78) Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Him."﴾ (79) [al-An'am]. Our master Ibrahim was in the stage of faith through guidance, then through reflection he reached the faith of inference, until he reached the faith of certainty..

5 Bakkah: the site of the Sacred House. Makkah: the entire sanctuary, which includes the houses. Some exegetes, such as Mujahid, held that both are one, and that the meem is a substitution for the baa'. It was said: Bakkah is derived from al-bak, meaning crowding, i.e., their crowding at the place of circumambulation. Al-bak also means breaking the neck; it was so named because it used to break the necks of tyrants who committed injustice there. Adapted from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi (2/1486)..

6 Yahujjuna ilayhi: they intend it by saddling their mounts toward it for worship and veneration. Al-Jurjani said in his book *al-Ta'rifat* (p. 72): "Hajj: intending a magnified thing; in the Sharia it is intending the House of Allah, the Exalted, with a specific attribute at a specific time with specific conditions in specific places."..

7 Bawwa'na lahu: We settled him in the place of the Sacred House and guided him to it. Tabawwu' means that a man shows another man a place in which to descend. Bawwa'na lahu: We prepared the place for him and empowered him over it. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And thus We established Yusuf in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed..﴾ (56) [Yusuf]. [Lisan al-'Arab: (b-w-'), adapted]..

8 The descendants (dhurriyyah) of a man: his offspring; the plural is dhurriyyat and dhara'i. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Descendants, some of them from others..﴾ (34) [Al 'Imran]. Dhurriyyah is derived from dhara'a Allah al-khalq, meaning He created them. So dhurriyyah is a noun comprising a human's offspring, male and female. Its root is hamz, but they dropped it, so they used it only without hamza. It was also said: dhurriyyah originally derives from dharr, meaning scattering, because Allah scattered them on the earth, i.e., dispersed them. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (dh-r-r)]..

9 Ba'ara al-shay': he hid it and stored it. From this comes the term for a pit: al-bu'rah. From it, the focal point of awareness (bu'rat al-shu'ur), i.e., the pit and center of awareness in which a person keeps his information and feelings toward the events that confront him. See Lisan al-'Arab (root: b-'-r)..

10 Therefore the scholars directed students of knowledge to reduce the ties that keep them occupied with worldly life. Such ties, as Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali says in his *Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din* (in the Book of Knowledge), are preoccupying and distracting: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:4]. And however much thought is dispersed, it falls short of grasping realities. Hence it was said: "Knowledge does not give you some of itself until you give it all of yourself." Thought scattered over disparate matters is like a stream whose water has dispersed, so the ground absorbs part of it and the air snatches part of it, and nothing remains of it that gathers and reaches the farms. Al-Zabidi said in *Ithaf al-Sada al-Muttaqin*: "[Moving] from one discipline to another before completing the first..."

11 The emptying of the mind and thought from preoccupations and distracting thoughts is something the Prophet's ḥadīth (saying; report of the Prophet's words, actions or approval) urged in regard to prayer. On the authority of 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no prayer in the presence of food, nor while one is being pressed by the two evils." Recorded by Muslim in his *Sahih* (authentic collection; 560). Al-akhbathan (the two evils) are urine and feces. Likewise, in the study of knowledge, the student must give it his whole mind and concentration, so that nothing distracts him from it.

12 Al-rayn: the stain and defilement, like rust that covers the heart. Al-Hasan said: it is sin upon sin until the heart turns black. Adapted from *Lisan al-Arab* (entry: r-y-n). Al-rayn is the rust that rises on a sword and takes away its shine. It is used figuratively for a veil that covers the heart because of sins. Ran al-sada' 'alayhi means the rust overcame it and covered it entirely. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, but what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 83:14].

13 The root (jadhr) of everything is its origin. From it is the ḥadīth: "the roots (jadhr) of men's hearts," meaning in their origin. (*Lisan*, entry: j-dh-r)

14 Al-wakta: a mark on a thing, like a spot differing from its color; plural: wakt. In the ḥadīth: "No one swears, even on the like of a gnat's wing, except that it becomes a wakta in his heart." And in the ḥadīth of Hudhayfa: "...and its trace remains like the trace of the wakt." [*Lisan*, entry: w-k-t]

15 Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his *Sahih* (6497) and Muslim (243), from the long ḥadīth of Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman; these are two portions of it.

16 The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke of this sweetness, saying: "Whoever has three qualities will find the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything else; that he loves a person only for the sake of Allah; and that he hates to return to disbelief after Allah has rescued him from it, as he hates to be thrown into the Fire." Agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari (16) and Muslim (43), from Anas ibn Malik.

17 Recorded by Muslim in his *Sahih* (144) and Ahmad in his *Musnad* (5/405, 386), from the ḥadīth of Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman.
*Mithl al-safa*: the smooth, broad rock.
*Murbadan*: black mixed with dust.
*Ka-l-kuz*: an Arabic word, not Persian, meaning a cup with a handle.
*Mujakhiyan*: inclined, i.e., deviating from uprightness and moderation. The heart that does not recognize good is likened to the inclined cup, in which nothing remains, because when a cup tilts, what is in it pours out. [See *Lisan al-Arab*, entry: j-kh-y]

18 *Alfaya*: we found. One says alfaytu al-shay' when one finds, encounters or meets a thing. See *Lisan al-Arab*, entry: l-f-y.

19 Adam (peace be upon him) fulfilled what was required of him. As for his eating from the tree he had been forbidden, it was forgetfulness, and forgetfulness is something that occurs and passes. Therefore Allah taught him words, and He accepted his repentance and guided him, as shown by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿But he forgot, and We found in him no firm resolve﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:115]. This does not contradict that he fulfilled all that was required.

20 There is a difference between a prophet (nabi) and a messenger (rasul). The prophet is one who receives revelation without a book being sent down to him or being commanded to convey a specific message to his people. Therefore every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger.

21 *Khala*: passed away; that is, passed on and was sent forth. It is said: al-qurun al-khaliya, the past generations. From it is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿That was a nation that has passed away; for it is what it earned, and for you is what you have earned﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:134], and His saying: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent forward in the days gone by﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:24].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 20:

Then He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿They say: "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say: "The unseen belongs only to Allah, so wait; I am with you among those who wait."﴾

The ayah, as we have known, is the wondrous thing, and it may be a cosmic sign (ayah kawniyyah), a sign of miraculous power (ayat i'jaz), or a Qur'anic verse containing rulings.

Why did they not believe the verses of the Qur'an, which were a miracle for them?

We say: receiving the Qur'an is a branch of affirming the Messenger (ﷺ), and confusion arose among them because they thought that the ayah is the perceptible cosmic sign that is witnessed, and they did not know that the signs with which the earlier messengers came were sent to suit the times of their messages and to suit their positions with respect to those to whom they were sent.

The earlier messengers before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and upon all the messengers be peace, were each sent to a people limited in time and place; therefore the signs they brought were perceptible signs, and each sign was of the kind in which the people to whom they were sent excelled.

As for the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), it is for the whole of time and the whole of place (ʿāmmat al-zamān wa-ʿāmmat al-makān). Had Allah, glory be to Him, given him a perceptible sign, those who witnessed it would have believed in it, and it would have become mere report for those who did not witness it.

We, as Muslims, for example, did not believe that Musa (peace be upon him) struck the sea so that the sea split for him, except because the Qur'an said so; for every perceptible event happens once, and whoever witnesses it believes, while whoever does not see it, if it is told to him, may deny it and may affirm it. But we affirmed it because the One who said it is the Truth, glory be to Him, and He has conveyed it to us in the Qur'an. Our trust in the One who said it is what made us affirm the miracles of the messengers before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Some may ask about the reason no perceptible miracles were sent with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We say: Allah, glory be to Him, willed to send the Messenger (ﷺ) with a lasting miracle that remains until the Hour is established, and it is the miracle of the Qur'an. The books of biography (sīrah) relate that water gushed from between his fingers (ﷺ); whoever believes, let him believe, and if you read it and do not believe it, know that you are not the one addressed by it, for it was addressed to those who were contemporaries of it, and it came to strengthen faith among the contemporary people, because they were in need of their faith being reinforced. The books of biography also tell us about the handful of food from which a large number of men ate; whoever accepts the narration, let him accept it, and whoever does not accept it, this sign did not come to him, but it came to those contemporary with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

This does not prevent the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from having perceptible miracles like his brother messengers, which we are obliged to believe in through trust in the one who reported them.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿They say: "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ And when "lawlā" (1) enters upon a nominal clause, the intent is the non-existence of something due to the existence of something else, as when a person says to another: "Lawlā Zayd ʿindak la-ataytuka" (Had it not been for Zayd being with you, I would have come to you), and thereby his going to so-and-so is negated due to Zayd's presence with him. Thus "lawlā" is a particle of prohibition due to existence; likewise the word "lawmā", if you find it entering upon a nominal clause, know that it denotes the prevention of something due to the existence of something else. But if "lawlā" enters upon a verbal clause, know that it is an urging and exhortation.

Here they have said: ﴿Why has not a sign been sent down to him?﴾ as though they do not acknowledge the Qur'an, and they sought a perceptible sign. Therefore we find the Truth, glory be to Him, saying in another place in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿Why was he not given the like of what was given to Musa?﴾ (48) [al-Qasas]. This is confirmation that they sought the perceptible sign, because they knew of the perceptible signs of the messengers before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But their saying this was clinging to disbelief, although they had witnessed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in all his conditions, and perceptible signs did occur and those who believed in him saw them, and their adherence to faith increased.

Those who asked Muhammad (ﷺ) to bring them a perceptible miracle like the miracle of Musa (peace be upon him) forgot that Musa (peace be upon him) was sent to a limited people, the Children of Israel.

As for Muhammad (ﷺ), he was sent to mankind entirely; therefore it was necessary that his miracle be renewed in its bounties and carry the method suited to every time and place. As for the perceptible miracle, it ends with the ending of its time and place.

Or they sought the signs they proposed, as in their saying: ﴿They said: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush for us from the earth, (90) or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly, (91) or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claim, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee, (92) or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky; and we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book we can read.…"(93)﴾ [al-Isra'].

So they sought signs they proposed themselves, and signs are not by the proposal of those to whom the messenger is sent, but by the bounty of the One who sends.

Someone may say: why did the Truth, glory be to Him, not send them a perceptible miraculous sign as they said? We say: the Truth, glory be to Him, has said: ﴿Nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them…(59)﴾ [al-Isra'].

On this basis their demand for signs is refuted, because the Truth, glory be to Him, sent signs before and the former peoples denied them. Or they sought signs they proposed. The Truth, glory be to Him, relates what was on their tongues: ﴿Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ and in this is an acknowledgement from them that Muhammad (ﷺ) has a Lord, and he (ﷺ) conveys from Him; so how then do they deny that he is a messenger?!

We know that they said earlier: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him" when the revelation paused from him (ﷺ), but the Truth, glory be to Him, answered them: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]﴾ [al-Duha] (3).

Thus they have contradicted themselves: in one state they denied that he has a Lord at all, and in another state they affirmed that he has a Lord. This is a contradiction in one matter, a kind of contradiction that leads to disorder of judgment, and disorder of judgment indicates the domination of desire (hawa).

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says in reply to their request for a perceptible sign: ﴿Say: "The unseen belongs only to Allah"﴾. Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches His Messenger (ﷺ) a cautious answer: it is possible that the Truth, glory be to Him, sends down the perceptible sign, and it is possible that He does not send it down. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not pass judgment on his Lord, because the unseen is a matter specific to Him, glory be to Him; if He wills, He makes what is in the unseen manifest, and if He wills, He keeps the unseen wholly unseen. You have nothing but to wait, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) declares that he is with them among those who wait: ﴿So wait; I am with you among those who wait (20)﴾ [Yunus].

(1) "Lawlā" is used as a particle of offer and urging, like "halā", and it is specific to entering upon the present tense, as in His saying: ﴿Lawlā tastaghfirūna Allāh…﴾ (46) [al-Naml]; and it enters upon a past form in the sense of the present, as in His saying: ﴿Lawlā akhkhartanī ilā ajalin qarīb…﴾ (10) [al-Munafiqun], meaning: "Lawlā tu'akhkhirnī" (had you not delayed me). "Lawlā" is also used for reproach and regret, and then it is specific to the past, as in His saying: ﴿Lawlā jā'ū ʿalayhi bi-arbaʿati shuhadā'…﴾ (13) [al-Nur]. It has other uses, to which one may refer in the books of linguistics [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/208, 207].

(2) This is among what Allah specially granted to His Messenger (ﷺ) and his community, and it is indicated by the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I have been given five things which no one before me was given: I was made victorious by terror over a distance of a month's journey; the earth was made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification, so whichever man of my community is overtaken by prayer, let him pray; spoils were made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given intercession; and every prophet was sent to his own people specifically, while I was sent to mankind generally." From the hadith of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (335) and Muslim (521).

(3) "Lawlā" is a conditional particle that does not govern, and it denotes the prevention of the response due to the existence of the condition. The conditional clause is a nominal clause (subject and predicate), and the predicate is obligatorily omitted if it is a general existential verb; and if a pronoun follows it, it is a separate nominative pronoun, as in: ﴿Lawlā antum lakunnā mu'minīn…﴾ (31) [Saba']. The response clause is verbal and is usually joined with the lam if affirmative, and is bare of it if negative. Allah said: ﴿Lawlā faḍl Allāh ʿalaykum wa-raḥmatuh mā zakkā minkum min aḥadin abadan…﴾ (21) [al-Nur]. The response may also be omitted if a sign indicates it, as in His saying: ﴿Lawlā faḍl Allāh ʿalaykum wa-raḥmatuhu wa-anna Allāh raʾūfun raḥīm﴾ (20) [al-Nur]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, vol. 2, p. 207].

(4) Al-yanbuʿ: the flowing spring and the abundant-watered stream; the plural is yanabiʿ. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root n-b-ʿ].

(5) Kisafan: plural of kisfah, meaning a piece; the intended meaning is punishment. Allah said: ﴿If We wish, We cause the earth to swallow them, or We cause to fall upon them pieces (kisafan) from the sky…﴾ (9) [Saba']. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root k-s-f].

(6) Al-qabil: a group of anything.

(7) Zukhruf: decoration, adornment, and gilding with gold. Al-zukhruf also means gold mixed with other things. Allah said: ﴿Until, when the earth takes on its adornment (zukhrufahā) and becomes beautiful, and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes upon it by night or by day…﴾ (24) [Yunus]. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root z-kh-r-f].

(8) Tarqā: to ascend; al-ruqiy means ascent. In the hadith: "I was a climber (ruqqa') upon the mountains," meaning one who ascends them; the form fa''āl is for intensification. Allah said: ﴿Nay, when it reaches the collarbones (al-taraqi) (26), and it is said: "Who is a charmer (rāq)?" (27)﴾ [al-Qiyamah].

(9) Al-dahḍ: repulsion and invalidation. From it is His saying: ﴿Their argument is dāḥiḍah…﴾ (16) [al-Shura], meaning: false, void.

(10) Qalāhu: he hated him, abandoned him, and forsook him. On the authority of Jundub al-Bajali, who said: Jibril was delayed in coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the polytheists said: "Muhammad has been forsaken." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness (1), and by the night when it is still (2), your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you] (3)﴾ [al-Duha]. Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1797) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (3345), and he said: a hasan sahih hadith. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (4/522) cited it through the route related by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi to Jundub with the wording: "The polytheists said: Muhammad has been forsaken by his Lord."

(11) Fatara al-wahy: it ceased.

(12) That is: he (the disbeliever) lets his desire rule all his conduct and the directions of his thinking; that is, he takes his desire as his god, obeys its command, and stops at its prohibition; therefore contradiction arises. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god, and Allah has led him astray despite knowledge, and sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a covering? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not be mindful?﴾ (23) [al-Jathiyah].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 10, verse 21:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity had touched them, behold, they have a scheme against Our signs. Say: "Allah is swifter in scheming. Indeed, Our messengers record what you scheme."﴾

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was distressed by the disbelievers, the chieftains of Quraysh, he prayed against them that they be struck with years of drought like the years that befell Egypt, which Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) was able to manage. So Allah, glorified is He, sent upon Quraysh drought and famine (٢), and then brought them mercy after that. It was incumbent upon them to return to Allah and to believe in the message of His Messenger (ﷺ), after they knew that the famine and drought that touched them were caused by the supplication of the Messenger (ﷺ): "O Allah, make it upon them years like the years of Yusuf" (٣).

The seven years ended, and mercy came to them in the form of rain. But they did not turn their attention to the necessity of thanking Allah and believing in His Messenger (ﷺ). Instead they kept searching for the causes of the rain. Some of them said: "Our rain came as a result of the rising (nawʾ) of such-and-such star (٤), and because the winds blew over such-and-such regions." They did this without paying any attention to the end of the supplication of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They were like someone who sits searching for the causes of victory in war and makes its causes material, in equipment and arms (٥). No one denies the importance of preparing for battle and its benefit, but the success granted by Allah, glorified and exalted is He, remains above every consideration; for the believers in Allah who prepared for battle and entered the battles found miracles manifest through the victory of Allah, because the Truthful, glorified is He, supports whoever supports Him.

As for those who confine the causes of victory to martial preparation alone, the fighters who waged war after serious training know that training alone does not create the spirit of the fighter; rather, his spirit is polished (٦) by his desire to fight, to attain martyrdom, and to enter Paradise.

Thus: the reinforcement of heaven has its entry point. Whoever among the fighters sees a sign contrary to the laws of the cosmos should know with certainty that the hand of Allah was above the hands of the believing fighters. Whoever claims that any victory is the result of civilization will find the answer from the fighters themselves: civilization without faith is merely a material advancement, weak (٧), that produces no victory (٨), and victory does not come through matter alone. Allah has commanded us to prepare well materially, but victory comes through faith above matter.

Therefore we find that those who fought our victorious war on the 10th of Ramadan 1393 AH know that the reinforcement of Allah was with them after they had prepared well. None of the fighters believes that material preparation alone can suffice for victory; it is a necessity, but victory comes through faith and the good use of weapons. Therefore the fighters do not believe those who attribute victory to matter alone, and this disbelief extends to everything said by those who deny the role of faith in victory.

Thus we find that whoever strips victory of the value of faith is in fact serving faith, because denying faith diminishes the value of material opinion. In this way Allah supports His religion until He establishes it in the hearts of His soldiers, and diminishes the value and standing of those who deny the worth of faith.

An example of this in the history of Islam: the Jews who used to seek victory over the people of Madinah from the Aws and the Khazraj, saying that a Prophet would appear, and that they—that is, the Jews—would follow him, and would kill the Arabs of the Aws and the Khazraj with the killing of ʿAd and Iram.

When the time came for the appearance of Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah, the Aws and the Khazraj hastened to believe in him, and they said: "He is the Prophet with whom the Jews have threatened us, so let us hasten to him before they outpace us."

Thus the word of the Jews was the motive that led the Aws and the Khazraj to faith.

Therefore: Allah supports His religion through the wicked man, despite the wicked man's presumption that he is scheming against the religion.

Likewise, when mercy came to them after the famine, they were thrown into agitation (٩), and kept analysing the cause of the falling of rain by limited scientific causes confined to matter, not by faith which is above matter.

For this reason the Truthful, glorified is He, says here, in the verse about which we are presenting our reflections:

﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity had touched them, behold, they have a scheme against Our signs. Say: "Allah is swifter in scheming. Indeed, Our messengers record what you scheme."﴾ [Yunus].

Scheming (al-makr) is crooked speech that refuses to acknowledge the mercy of Allah, and the claim that such-and-such a star-rising is the cause of the falling of rain, or such-and-such a constellation is the cause of the falling of rain.

As for His saying: ﴿a scheme against Our signs﴾: scheming (al-makr) is hidden plotting, and what is meant here is an attempt at circumvention, to strip the wonders of their being the creation of Allah. Even knowledge and its laws are a gift from Allah; the Truthful is the One able to suspend causes, to do what He wills, to break laws. He, glorified is He, is the Lord of the laws, so do not attribute any event except to Him, glorified is He, lest we go astray with the error of the philosophers who said that God exists and created the cosmos and created the laws so that the cosmos would be governed by laws.

We say: if the Truthful, glorified is He, had created the laws and the regularities and left them to govern, nothing would have deviated from those laws. Miracles accompanying the messengers—by way of example—were a departure from the laws. Allah retained in His hand the governance of the laws. True, He, glorified is He, has set them free, but He remains the Sustainer over them: He suspends the law whenever He wills, manifests it whenever He wills, and directs it as He wills.

Scheming, as we know, is derived from the intertwining of the branches of a tree like a braid, so that one cannot recognise the origin of a leaf or from which branch it came, for the origins of the leaves have become mixed until they are hidden from you. From this comes the sense of hidden plotting. You may plot against your equals, but you will not be able to plot against one who is above you. If you scheme, then Allah is swifter in scheming, and the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿Allah is swifter in scheming﴾. This is called "correspondence of expression" (٣ mushākalah) (١٣).

That is: you must take that in its counterpart regarding the doer and the act, but do not take from this saying a name for Allah. Beware of saying that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is "a schemer," because scheming is hidden plotting that you carry out against your equals, but you cannot do that with one who is aware of your plotting, and you do not perceive what He wills for you.

Look at any group that plots for any matter, and you will find among them someone who reports them to the authorities and security services. If the scheming of humans against humans is exposed by those among them who inform on others, and there are even humans who are not schemers who can, by their insight, deduce and uncover those who scheme against them.

There are also contemporary devices that can record people's calls and eavesdrop (١٤) on them; all of this is human scheming against humans. What then of us, if Allah schemes against someone, when there is no one with Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to report His scheme to us, and no one can spy upon Him?!

The scheming of Allah, glorified is He, is therefore stronger than any human scheming, because the scheming of humans may expose some schemers or be discovered through spying on them; but if Allah schemes against them, do they know anything of His scheme? Of course they do not know.

The phrase ﴿swifter in scheming﴾ draws your attention to there being two contestants in a race. When you say, "So-and-so is swifter than so-and-so," it means that each of them is trying to reach the same goal, but one of them is swifter than the other in reaching the goal.

Your human scheming is something that occurs anew, but Allah, glorified is He, is eternal in existence, knowing everything before it happens and arranging every matter before it occurs. Therefore He is the swiftest in responding to your scheming, if you scheme.

Here the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity had touched them (١٥), behold, they have a scheme against Our signs﴾. The first "idha" is a temporal adverb, while the second is "idha" of suddenness, like your saying: "I went out, and behold, the lion is at the door."

When the Truthful sends down rain to them as mercy from Him, they do not calm down and enjoy and taste the mercy of Allah the Exalted upon them, in the water that came to them after drought; instead they suddenly devise a scheme. Then the words of the Truthful, glorified is He, come: ﴿Say: "Allah is swifter in scheming. Indeed, Our messengers record what you scheme."﴾

Thus you see that what nullifies the schemes of human schemers occurs by one of these means: either by the informing of one of the schemers, or by the power of espionage from others, or by the messengers of the Most High, the angels, who record everything human beings do. So glorified is He who said: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble recorders, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar].

And read also the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your soul against you today as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra'].

The Truthful, glorified is He, brought all that has preceded because He willed to give Quraysh an opportunity to retract from their obstinacy against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)—the obstinacy about which they said: "We follow what we found our fathers upon." This is a mistaken statement, for the fathers were originally believers, but misguidance came to them as an accidental matter. The idols they worshipped were foreign to them, brought from Rome by a man who had travelled in the lands of Rome: "ʿAmr ibn Luhay" (١٦). So if you return to faith after your obstinacy, this is the straight path upon which your fathers were, by nature and by the primordial covenant.

١ Here "the messengers" means the guardian angels. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay, but you deny the Recompense. And indeed, over you are guardians, noble recorders, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar].
٢ Al-jadb: the opposite of fertility, i.e., dryness and cessation of rain. In the hadith on seeking rain: "The livestock perished and the lands became barren," i.e., they suffered drought and prices rose. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root j-d-b]
Al-qahṭ: withholding of rain; al-qahṭ is also drought, because it results from it. In the hadith on seeking rain: "The rain was withheld and the trees turned red" is of this kind. Qahṭ may be extended to anything whose good has diminished, though its original sense concerns rain. Qahṭ in anything means the lack of its good. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root q-h-ṭ]
٣ From Abu Hurayrah: that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he raised his head from the last rak'ah, would say: "O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar; O Allah, make it upon them years like the years of Yusuf…" The hadith is related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1006) and Ahmad in his Musnad (2/521, 502, 470).
٤ Nāʾa yanūʾu, from the door of qāla, means: rose up. From it comes al-nawʾ for rain, plural anwāʾ. [al-Misbah 2/151]
٥ Al-ʿatād: equipment; plural aʿtidah and ʿutud. al-Layth said: al-ʿatād is that which you prepare and make ready for a matter. In the hadith describing the Prophet (ﷺ): "For every situation he had ʿatād," i.e., what suits every event that occurs. Here ʿatād means weapons and instruments of war. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blazing fire﴾ [al-Insan]. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root ʿ-t-d]
٦ Al-ṣaql: polishing and sharpening; here it means religious zeal and the psychological and moral mobilisation of the fighters. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root ṣ-q-l, adapted]
٧ Al-hashsh and al-hashīsh of anything: that which has softness and pliancy; here it means weakness.
٨ Allah the Exalted says: ﴿…And victory is not but from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Al ʿImran 126].
٩ Allah has related this to us in His Book, saying of the Jews: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them—and they had been, before, seeking victory over those who disbelieved—but when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 89]. And from some elders of the Ansar who said: "We had dominated them by force for ages in the Jahiliyyah, and we were people of polytheism while they were people of the Book. They used to say: 'A Prophet is about to be sent now; we shall follow him, his time has drawn near, and we shall kill you with him, the killing of ʿAd and Iram.' When Allah sent His Messenger from Quraysh and we followed him, they disbelieved in him." Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (1/124), citing Ibn Ishaq.
١٠ This has been reported in a hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). From Abu Hurayrah who said: We witnessed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the battle of Hunayn. He said to a man who claimed Islam: "This man is of the people of the Fire." When the fighting came, the man fought fiercely and was wounded. It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, the man you said a moment ago was of the people of the Fire fought fiercely today, and he has died." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "To the Fire." Some of the Muslims almost doubted. While they were in that state, it was said that he had not died, but had a severe wound. When night came, he could not bear the wound and killed himself. The Prophet (ﷺ) was informed of this and said: "Allahu akbar, I bear witness that I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger." Then he commanded Bilal, who proclaimed among the people: "None enters Paradise except a Muslim soul, and Allah strengthens this religion through the wicked man." Sahih hadith, agreed upon, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3062) and Muslim (111).
١١ Arjafū: they were thrown into severe agitation. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root r-j-f]
١٢ Al-makr: contrivance in secret. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they schemed a scheme, and We schemed a scheme, while they perceived not﴾ [al-Naml 50]. The people of exegesis said: the scheming from Allah the Exalted is a recompense named after scheming by way of figurative usage, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it…﴾ [al-Shura 40]; the second is not truly an evil, but is called so for the sake of parallelism of speech. Likewise His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him…﴾ [al-Baqarah 194]; the first is injustice, the second is not injustice, but is named by the name of sin to show that it is a punishment for it and a requital for it. Ibn al-Athir said: the scheming of Allah is the infliction of His affliction upon His enemies and not upon His friends. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root m-k-r]
١٣ Mushākalah: a rhetorical term frequent in the Qur'an, meaning mentioning a thing by the wording of another, because it occurs in its company, actually or by implication. Such as His saying: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed…﴾ [Al ʿImran 54]; the application of makr to the Creator is only for the correspondence with what is with it. (al-Itqan fi ʿUlum al-Qur'an, 3/281)
١٤ Tanaṣṣut: here meaning espionage. Anṣata al-rajul inṣātan: he listened attentively. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent…﴾ [al-Aʿraf 204]. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root n-ṣ-t, adapted]
١٥ "Idha" comes with two meanings: conditional and sudden (fujā'iyyah). The conditional idha is a noun of condition for future time; it specifically precedes verbal sentences, and it is inflected, and sometimes precedes nominal nouns in the nominative, the following word then being the subject of an elided verb explained by the verb that follows, such as Allah's saying: ﴿And when the heaven is stripped away﴾ [al-Takwir 11]. "Idha" may also be sudden and specifically precedes nominal sentences, such as His saying: ﴿So he threw it, and behold, it was a snake, moving swiftly﴾ [Ta-Ha 20]. The conditional and the sudden are combined in His saying: ﴿Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, behold, you will come out﴾ [al-Rum 25]. And as in the verse: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity had touched them, behold, they have a scheme against Our signs…﴾ [Yunus 21].
١٦ Ibn Hisham mentioned in the Sirah (1/77) that ʿAmr ibn Luhay went out from Makkah to Syria on some of his affairs. When he arrived at Ma'ab in the land of al-Balqa', where the ʿAmaliqah then lived, he saw them worshipping idols. He said to them: "What are these idols that I see you worshipping?" They said: "These are idols we worship; we seek rain from them and they give us rain, and we seek victory from them and they grant us victory." He said: "Will you not give me one of them, so that I may carry it to the land of the Arabs and they may worship it?" So they gave him an idol called Hubal, and he came with it to Makkah, set it up, and commanded the people to worship it and venerate it.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 10, verse 22 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, a violent wind comes upon them and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they are encompassed. Then they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him: "If You save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾ (22):

This noble verse comes as a stage in Allah the Exalted's account of those who opposed the call of Islam. The Truth, glory be to Him, began it by saying that He had shown them mercy by delaying the answer to their prayers against themselves for evil. Had He answered them in what they asked against themselves of evil, in their saying: ﴿If this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ (32) [al-Anfal], He would have settled their affair. So it is part of Allah's mercy that He did not respond to their supplication.

Since Allah, glory be to Him, delayed the answer to their prayers against themselves for evil out of mercy towards them, they must know that delaying the answer to their prayers for good is also mercy towards them. For they may pray for evil while thinking they are praying for good. After that, He showed that they were lying in their prayers against themselves for evil, by saying that when harm touches them they call upon Allah lying down(1), sitting and standing.

If they truly loved evil for themselves, they would remain in the trial they are in until Allah decides a matter concerning them.

Then He, glory be to Him, presented another issue: when He touches them with harm, it is so that they may take heed, and Allah, glory be to Him, brings His mercy to rescue them from this harm. How well would it have been if they had thanked Allah's blessing in the mercy after the harm. But they pass on as though they had never called upon Allah, glory be to Him, against a harm that had touched them.

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, the Truth, glory be to Him, depicts for us another situation, the situation of travel on land and sea. He says: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾ (22) [Yunus]. The phrase ﴿enables you﴾ indicates that the one who causes the travel is Allah. But the Qur'an contains verses establishing that travel is attributed to human beings, when He says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth﴾ (69) [al-Naml].

And when the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then when Moses had fulfilled the term and set out with his family﴾ (29) [al-Qasas].

And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Travel therein by night and day in security﴾ (18) [Saba']. So it is as if this verse we are reflecting on attributes the causing of travel to Allah, glory be to Him, while some other verses attribute travel to the human soul.
