We say to those who imagined that there is a contradiction in this: If you had understood the definition of the agent (fa'il, the grammatical subject) according to the grammarians(2) and how they put it in the nominative case, you would know that the realization of any act returns to the will of Allah, glory be to Him. When we say: "So-and-so succeeded," is it he who succeeded, or is it someone else who allowed him to succeed? The examiner and the corrector are the ones who allowed him to succeed, in appreciation of his answers which show that he exerted effort in study.

Likewise we say: "So-and-so died." Did so-and-so cause death himself? Especially since we parse "died" as a past-tense verb, and parse the word "so-and-so" as the agent, or we say that death has befallen him and he has been characterized by it. For the definition of the agent is: the one who performs the action, or is characterized by it.

If we want to attribute things to their direct causes, we say: "The man walked."

If we want to trace a man's walking back through causes, and go back with it into the past, we will find that the one who caused him to walk is Allah, exalted is He.

All the causes of existence, if you look at them directly, you find them attributed to the one who is their agent. But if you follow them through their chain of causes, you find them traced back to Allah, glory be to Him.

For example: if you are asked, "Who made the chair?" you answer, "The carpenter." If you ask the carpenter, "Where did you get the wood?" he will answer, "From the merchant." And the merchant will tell you that he imported it from the forest lands, and so on.

So: if you want to trace every movement in existence back in sequence, it must end with Allah, exalted is He(3).

When the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then when Moses had fulfilled the term(4) and set out with his family﴾ (29) [al-Qasas].

We understand from this that Moses, peace be upon him, set out with his family, because the causing of travel in all its elements is from Allah, exalted is He.

Another example: we read in the Qur'an His saying, the Truth: ﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾ (43) [al-Najm]. He, glory be to Him, is the one who created laughter and created weeping.

Then someone says: "How can Allah, glory be to Him, say that He created laughter and weeping, when He says in the Qur'an: ﴿So let them laugh a little and weep much﴾ (82) [al-Tawbah]?"

We say: If you look at the one who performs the laughing, he is the human being who laughed. But if you look at the one who created the instinct of laughter in the human being, you find it is Allah, glory be to Him.

The instinct of laughter exists by universal agreement among all kinds of existing beings, and likewise weeping. There is no "Arabic laughter" and "English laughter," nor "French weeping" or "Russian weeping."

So: Allah, glory be to Him, is the one who created laughter and weeping.

The words of the Truth are confirmed: ﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾ (43) [al-Najm]. But the one who laughs and the one who weeps is the one characterized by the attribute. Likewise His saying, the Truth: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ (17) [al-Anfal].

Allah, glory be to Him, willed that His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as a human being, should throw the pebbles, but the delivery of the pebbles to every individual in the opposing army was the will of Allah(5).

So: the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾ does not contradict that they are the ones who travel. And if you consider travel on land or at sea, you will find that travel is the movement of the traveler from one place to another, and he determines the purpose of the travel with his mind. The land or the sea on which he travels, by his feet or by car or by ship: this mind was created by Allah, exalted is He, and the land likewise, and the sea too. They are all creatures created by Allah, glory be to Him. And when you move your legs to walk, you do not know how you began to walk or how many muscles moved in your body. The one who subjected all the energies of your body to the purpose of your mind is Allah, exalted is He.

So: every matter ultimately goes back to Allah, glory be to Him.

Here is a point about travel on land and at sea: the two differ. A person, while traveling on dry land, may be cut off from his way, and he can cry out for help to some passer-by, or wait for some passers-by to pass and assist him.

As for crossing the sea, there are no many passers-by or travelers on it, so that a person can call out to them for help(6).

So: crossing the sea is more precise than crossing the land. For this reason, in this verse we are reflecting on, the Truth, glory be to Him, says about travel on the sea: ﴿until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, a violent wind comes upon them and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they are encompassed. Then they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him: "If You save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾ (22) [Yunus].

Thus we do not find in this same verse any talk of travel on land, because the Truth, glory be to Him, since He has spoken about removing danger from the one in distress at sea, this includes removing it from one who travels on land, all the more so. When a stronger proof comes, the weaker proof is necessarily included within it.

An example of this is the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ (15) [al-Ahqaf].

Then all the reasons (for kindness) are given afterwards concerning the mother, and no reason is given for the father, when He says: ﴿His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning is thirty months﴾ (15) [al-Ahqaf].

Allah willed this, because the mother's reason is based on weakness, so He wants to soften the heart of her son towards her. The father is a man who may be able to struggle in this world, and the father's favor upon the child is something the child perceives. But his mother's favor upon him while he was in her womb, he is not aware of it, and in his earliest childhood he is not aware of this favor either. But afterwards he realizes that his father provides for all the necessities of his life, food and clothing, and the mother's role in the child's eyes remains a faint memory.

So: the mother's reason is the one that is emphasized, because her exhaustion in pregnancy and nursing was not perceived by the child.

Likewise here, in this verse we are reflecting on, the Truth, glory be to Him, left out the reason of the land and explained in detail the reason of the sea: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until, when you are in ships(10)﴾ (22) [Yunus]. The word (al-fulk, ships) comes once in the singular and once in the plural, and its form is the same in both cases. An example of this is that when Allah, exalted is He, wanted to save Noah, peace be upon him, and drown the disbelievers in him, He said to our master Noah: ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes﴾ (37) [Hud]. So: it is used for the singular and for the plural, and it has parallels in the language in both cases. In the singular it is like qufl (lock) and qurt (earring), and in the plural it is like asad (lions).

The Truth, glory be to Him, describes the wind here as "good." The noble Qur'an, by the nature of its style, when it speaks of wind in the singular form, it intends by it punishment, like His saying, the Truth: ﴿And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said: This is a cloud bringing us rain. Rather, it is what you were hastening: a wind in which is a painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾ (24-25) [al-Ahqaf]. But when He speaks of it in the plural, it is for mercy, and He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We sent the fertilizing winds﴾ (22) [al-Hijr].

He also says, glory be to Him: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, until, when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land and send down water therewith, and bring forth with it all kinds of fruits﴾ (57) [al-A'raf].

Here the winds came in the plural form. The reason for the existence of a wind of evil(12), and winds of good, you can infer by looking at all of existence. This observation makes clear to you that air has stages: the air of ease is the one that passes gently, like a soft breeze. Sometimes the air stops and not a single breath passes, but we breathe still, hot air during the heat of the weather. Then the air sometimes intensifies and becomes somewhat strong winds, then turns into whirlwinds.

Air, as we know, is the fundamental sustainer of every living being, and of every non-living stable thing. So if air is the fundamental sustainer of the human soul, then massive buildings, like skyscrapers, remain stable in their place only as a result of the balance of air currents around them. And if air is removed from one side of them, the building collapses.

So: it is air that achieves balance in the whole universe.

For this reason we find that the noble Qur'an has detailed the matter of the winds and clarified their function. Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind﴾. It is as if He, glory be to Him, is speaking here about sailing ships that move by the air gathered in their sails. And if the advancement in shipbuilding has passed beyond the sail to steam, and then to electricity, the words of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿a good wind﴾ encompass all stages of advancement, especially since the word "wind" has come in the noble Qur'an with the meaning of power, whatever it is: air, or an engine moving by any energy. And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your power depart﴾ (46) [al-Anfal].

Thus we understand that the meaning of "wind" goes to power. Also the word "wind" is in harmony with all the facilitations of the sea.

The saying of the Truth: ﴿until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it﴾. This noble statement includes three events: being in the ship, the ship sailing with a good wind, and their rejoicing at that. These are three things mentioned in the conditional clause, and then the answer to the condition also contains three things:

The first: ﴿a violent wind comes upon them﴾. The second: ﴿and the waves come at them from every place﴾. The third: ﴿and they think they are encompassed﴾.

As for the violent wind: it is the destroying one. It is said: "So-and-so sweeps away such-and-such," and in the Qur'an: ﴿like a field eaten (stripped)﴾ (5) [al-Fil]. So: ﴿a violent wind﴾ is the destructive, drowning wind. His saying, the Truth: ﴿and the waves come at them from every place﴾.

The waves come from below, and the wind comes from above, and raise a

1 Al-idtijae: lying down, and placing the side on the ground. Ibn al-Muzaffar said: this ṭā' was originally a tā', but they found it ugly to say (iḍtajaʿa), so they changed the tā' to ṭā'. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾ (16) [al-Sajdah] [Lisan al-Arab: root ḍ-j-ʿ].

2 Because the definition of the agent according to the grammarians is: every nominative noun preceded by a verb, transitive or intransitive, and this noun is the one who performed the action, or established it, or was characterized by it, like: "Muhammad read the book," "Muhammad succeeded," and "the tree bore fruit."

3 He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿He arranges the affair, explaining the signs that you may be certain of meeting your Lord﴾ (2) [al-Ra'd]. And He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter is returned﴾ (123) [Hud].

4 That is because Shu'ayb said to Moses: ﴿I intend to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it is from your own choice﴾ (27) [al-Qasas]. Moses said to him: ﴿That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me; and Allah is Guardian over what we say﴾ (28) [al-Qasas]. It is established in a hadith that Moses, peace be upon him, fulfilled the more complete and perfect term, which is ten years [Ibn Kathir: 3/384-387].

5 From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: on the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, and said: "O Lord, if this band perishes, You will not be worshipped on earth ever." Then Jibril said to him: "Take a handful of dust and throw it in their faces." So he took a handful of dust and threw it in their faces, and there was not one of the polytheists but that dust from that handful struck his eye, his nostrils and his mouth, and they turned back fleeing. Narrated by Abu Nu'aym (p. 404) and al-Bayhaqi (3/79), both in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, and mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (2/294).

6 Yastaṣrikh: to cry out seeking help. Al-ṣarkhah: a loud shout at the time of terror or calamity. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So the one who had sought his help the day before seeks his help again﴾ (18) [al-Qasas]. And He said: ﴿And if We willed, We would drown them, and there would be no one to cry out for them, nor would they be rescued﴾ (43) [Ya-Sin]. Al-ṣarīkh: the one who gives relief [Lisan al-Arab: root ṣ-r-kh, adapted].

7 Sabil sabilah: a path that is travelled. Al-sabilah: the people of the road, those who wander on the roads about their needs; the plural is al-sawabil. Al-sulūk: the verbal noun of "salaka a road," and those who travel a road are sālikah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He who made the earth for you a cradle and made for you therein roads﴾ (53) [Ta-Ha] [Lisan al-Arab: roots s-b-l, s-l-k].

8 Ḍawā ilayhi: joined and took refuge. Yanḍawī fī al-shay': enters into it and falls under it [Lisan al-Arab: root ḍ-w-y, adapted].

9 Al-fiṣāl: weaning. The meaning: the period of a woman's carrying until the time the child is separated from her nursing is thirty months, and a woman weaned her child, i.e., she weaned him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿His mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years﴾ (14) [Luqman]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And mothers suckle their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ (233) [al-Baqarah] [Lisan al-Arab: root f-ṣ-l, adapted]. The scholars have derived from this that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months. It once happened that a woman's case was brought to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, as she had carried for six months, and her husband accused her of adultery, and he acquitted her, relying on the combination of these verses. This is the view of the majority [Fiqh al-Sunnah: 3/367].

10 Al-fulk: a ship, for the masculine and feminine, the singular and the plural. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then We saved him and those with him in the laden ship﴾ (119) [al-Shu'ara'], where He made it singular and masculine, meaning the vessel. And He said: ﴿And you see the ships ploughing through it﴾ (14) [al-Nahl], where He made al-fulk plural and described it with (mawākhir), meaning ships [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 2/89].

11 Lawāqiḥ: bearers, because they carry the water and the clouds, turn them and direct them. Then they milk them, so they impregnate the clouds with water, and the clouds pour out water and rain falls, and they fertilize plants so they yield their produce [Lisan al-Arab: root l-q-ḥ] and Ibn Kathir (2/549).

12 Among the winds are those that Allah subjects and makes into winds of good, like His saying about Solomon, peace be upon him: ﴿So We subjected the wind to him, flowing gently by his command wherever he directed﴾ (36) [Sad]. The gentle wind (al-rīḥ al-rakhā') is the soft, swift wind that does not shake anything from its place [see Lisan al-Arab: root r-kh-w].

١٣ That is, their strength. Here *al-rih* (ريح) means strength, and *dhahab al-rih* (ذهاب الريح) means the loss of strength and prestige. Strength is balance in life. When it is exercised with good character, it returns benefit and peace to humanity. When it is stripped of character, it becomes tyranny and corruption on earth, as history has recorded and as we witness in the reality of the world, which is the greatest proof. It may also be used for scent, as in His saying: ﴿And when the caravan set out, their father said, "Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph..."﴾ [Yusuf: 94]. This also serves the meaning of strength, since whoever loses his scent from existence is evidence that his strength has departed.

١٤ *Al-'asf al-ma'kul* (العصف المأكول) means chaff. *Al-'asf* (العصف) has two meanings:
- That He made the people of the elephant like leaves whose grain has been taken, leaving only the husk with no grain in it.
- Or He meant that He made them like chaff that cattle have eaten. [Lisan al-'Arab, root ʿ-ṣ-f (عصف)]

Then Allah, glory be to Him, brings their words of supplication: ﴿If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.﴾ Did they fulfil the covenant? No. For Allah, glory be to Him, says after that: ﴿But when He delivered them, they at once committed injustice in the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves—[it is] the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ (10:23):

Immediately after Allah has delivered them, the sudden "idha" (إذا الفجائية, the "suddenly" particle) comes to make clear to us that they did not wait until they had recovered themselves, or until a period of time had passed between them and the supplication and the result of their humble entreaty was realised. No, rather they transgressed (بغوا)(1) immediately in the earth: ﴿But when He delivered them, they at once committed injustice in the earth without right.﴾

Al-baghy: it is exceeding the limit in wrongdoing, and it is corruption. For when a person takes anything out of its soundness, it is said: "baghā 'alayhi" (he transgressed against him). If you dig a well-levelled road, this is corruption; if you throw refuse(2) into a well from which people drink, this is corruption and transgression; and anything that stands upon soundness, which you take out of its function and affect with something that corrupts it, this is transgression.

Al-baghy is the highest rank of injustice, for the Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he oppressed them (fa-baghā ʿalayhim)...﴾ (28:76).

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives us the image of transgression represented in aggression through corruption against what is good, and he (ﷺ) says: "The quickest of good in reward is righteousness and maintaining the ties of kinship, and the quickest of evil in punishment is transgression and severing the ties of kinship."(3)

Allah, the Exalted, does not postpone the punishment for transgression and severing the ties of kinship until the Hereafter, but punishes for them in this world, so that society may be kept in balance. For if you see a wrongdoer living in contentment and ease and then dying in goodness, everyone who sees him and knows his injustice, and finds no punishment for him in this world, will go on to spread injustice.

Therefore you find that Allah's punishment for such a wrongdoer in this world, and that people see his evil end, and when people see that, they take warning and do not commit injustice; and this is what achieves balance in society.

Otherwise, if Allah, glory be to Him, left the matter to the recompense of the Hereafter, society would be made miserable by those who do not believe in the Hereafter and who make a profession of transgression. Therefore people see their torment in this world, and then they will have their place in the Fire in the Hereafter.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said, warning: "Do not transgress, and do not be a transgressor."(4) So the transgressor is merely creating a disturbance in the balance of society. The one who transgresses takes the right of another, so that he may enjoy a gain not earned by his own effort and work, and he turns into a person who makes a profession of imposing levies(5) on people, and who is idle from any other work. You see this in the simplest of places and quarters, when some who are deluded by their physical strength make a profession of it, and they have become "fityan" (thugs)(6) whom some hire to harm others; and one of these has adopted eating without exerting effort in honourable work.

So transgression is the work of one who corrupts the movement of life for people, for those upon whom the injustice of transgression falls become averse to toil and honourable, pure work. And when people become averse to toil and honourable work, the movement of life is disrupted and the interests of mankind are disrupted, and indeed the interests of the wrongdoer himself are disrupted. This is why the Truthful, glory be to Him, said: ﴿when they committed injustice in the earth without right...﴾ (10:23). And one may ask: is there transgression that is with right?

I say: yes, for transgression is aggression against what is good through corruption. When you see a person corrupting something good, you ask him: "Why do you do that?" and he may answer you that his purpose is reform, and he enumerates for you reasons for this transgression; this is transgression with right. But whoever is a transgressor without a lawful cause, this is transgression, indeed its very summit.

As an example of transgression with right, I say: Did the Prophet (ﷺ) not seize the land of the Banu Qurayza, burn their crops, cut down the trees on their lands, and demolish their houses? Is there not in that an aggression against what is good?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did that because he was responding to an aggression harsher than that. Thus we see that there is transgression with right and transgression without right. Therefore Allah calls the recompense of an evil "an evil like it"(7), and He says: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in like manner.﴾ (2:194). And He, glory be to Him, calls it "aggression", although it is not aggression but the repelling of aggression.

Allah, the Exalted, states it as a principle that remains for ever after what has preceded, saying: ﴿O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves—[it is] the enjoyment of worldly life.﴾ (10:23). Here Allah, glory be to Him, makes clear, as though addressing the transgressor: O you who wish to take the right of another, know that the utmost(8) that taking this right will give you is some portion of the enjoyment of this world, and then after that you will be recompensed with an everlasting Fire.(9)

If you compare the period of the usurped enjoyment resulting from transgression with the period of punishment for it, you will find that the enjoyment is cheap and trivial compared with the punishment you will receive for it, and it does not even take up your life in this world measured against the life of the world itself; for Allah, glory be to Him, may will to make the life of the world twenty million years, but your life in it is limited.

So be wary(10) for your souls, and understand that the enjoyment of this world is small, if this enjoyment is the result of your injustice to yourselves; for the consequence of this injustice falls upon you, since what this injustice gives you of enjoyment and blessing is a matter limited to your life in this world, and your life in it is limited. Let no one think that his lifespan is the lifespan of mankind in the world; rather let each of you measure his lifespan in the world, and it is limited.

Therefore the Truthful, glory be to Him, says in another verse: ﴿Say: the enjoyment of this world is little...﴾ (4:77). Here Allah, glory be to Him, affirms: ﴿Your transgression is only against yourselves﴾ (10:23).

The recompense of transgression may take the form that Allah, glory be to Him, wills that the wrongdoer shall not die until he sees his victim in a state better than what was taken from him; therefore I always say: if the wrongdoer knew what Allah has stored up for the one wronged of good, he would begrudge himself the injustice.

Even supposing that the wrongdoer enjoys his injustice, which is the little enjoyment of this world, we find the Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then to Us is your return...﴾ (10:23).

When we return to Allah, the Exalted, there is no injustice at all; for none of you will be wronged or will wrong, and each of you will meet what Allah, glory be to Him, informs him of, whether reward or punishment, confirming His true word: ﴿Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you(11) of what you used to do﴾ (10:23). The report of the recompense has come before it occurs, so that all may know that for every deed there is a corresponding reward or punishment; and also, mentioning the report in advance is a rebuke to those who wrong themselves through transgression.

1 Al-baghy: injustice, corruption, arrogance, overbearing over people, harming, and oppression; and the root of al-baghy is exceeding the limit. Allah says: ﴿And if Allah had extended provision to His servants, they would have transgressed upon the earth...﴾ (42:27). And He says: ﴿But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the one that transgresses...﴾ (49:9). [Lisan al-'Arab: root (b-gh-y), adapted]

2 Nafayah of a thing: its remainder and its worst part. Al-nafayah: what you discard from a thing because of its badness. What is meant here by nafayah: refuse, and everything that would soil and corrupt the thing. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (n-f-y), adapted]

3 Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4212), and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (4/70), ed. Dar al-Fikr, and al-Dhahabi in Mizan al-I'tidal (no. 3831), from the hadith of 'A'isha; both in the biography of Salih ibn Musa al-Talhi, who is Kufan and weak. Ibn 'Adi said: he does not deliberately lie, and the wording of the hadith is acted upon.

4 Narrated by al-Hakim in his al-Mustadrak 'ala al-Sahihayn (2/338) from Abu Bakra, and he said: its isnad is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it. Al-Dhahabi concurred.

5 Ita'at (plural of ita'a): a sum of money extracted by force and compulsion, without any lawful right, by those with power and domination. It resembles the makus (unlawful tolls).

6 This is a term people use for every deviant person who uses his strength as a threat to security, robbery of people's property, and intimidation of people. In Arabic: al-fata is the strong young man, and al-fata is also the slave; its plural for paucity is fityah, and for abundance fityan. The feminine is fatah, plural fataat. Futuwwa was known among the Arabs as the people of valour, help and seeking reward, but this word was applied to every deviant who practises corruption as a trade.

7 This is in the like of His saying: ﴿And the recompense of an evil is an evil like it...﴾ (42:40). This is by way of mushakala, a rhetorical term meaning naming a thing by the name of something else because it occurs in its company; so the recompense here is a right and is not described as an evil, but it is named thus because of its correspondence with what accompanies it. See (al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an 3/281).

8 Qasara al-shay': its end and its limit, and it derives from the meaning of qasr, i.e. restraint; because when you reach the limit, it holds you. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (q-s-r), adapted]

9 Among examples of usurpation and transgression without right is what Ibn Mas'ud narrated: I said: O Messenger of Allah, which injustice is greatest? He said: a cubit of land which a Muslim man takes from his brother's right; for no one takes a pebble of the earth but it will be hung around his neck to the bottom of the earth on the Day of Resurrection, and none knows its depth except the One who created it. Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/396) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/266). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/174): "The isnad of Ahmad is hasan."

10 Irba' 'ala anfusikum: guard them and keep them far from everything that would bring them punishment in the Hereafter. And in the hadith: "My likeness and your likeness is that of a man who went to watch over his family" (yarba' ahlahu), i.e. protects them from their enemy. [Lisan al-'Arab, root (r-b-')]

11 Al-anba': important reports. Allah says: ﴿Those are the cities; We relate to you some of their news...﴾ (7:101), and He says: ﴿For every news there is a fixed time...﴾ (6:67), i.e. for every report there is a time or place in which it occurs, in the future or the past. Its nabba' (the intensive form) means to inform; doubling the letter conveys emphasis and repetition. Allah says: ﴿And Allah will inform them of what they used to do...﴾ (5:14). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, vol. 2, pp. 250–251]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 24 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:
﴿Indeed, the example of the life of this world is like water which We send down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it, from which men and livestock eat, until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified(1), and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it into stubble, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who reflect.﴾ (10:24)

The water that descends from the sky is the water fit for irrigation and watering, because the waters found in existence are stores of life; they are often salty, like the waters of seas and oceans. The Truth, glory be to Him, willed this in order to protect them from rot and corruption. Then the process of distilling the waters is completed by the rays of the sun, which turn the water into vapour; the vapour gathers like a cloud, then falls as sweet, distilled water fit for drinking and irrigation.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿like water which We sent down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it (10:24)﴾ [Yunus]. Ikhtilat (mingling) is the gathering of two things or several things in such a way that they remain separate, so that one can be isolated from the other. If you mix some broad beans with some lupin seeds, you can separate each from the other. But there is another kind of gathering of things, in the form of blending, like when you squeeze a lemon into water sweetened with sugar, and this results in each particle of the lemon and the sugar dissolving into the particles of the water.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿like water which We sent down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it﴾. It may be understood from this that the water and the plants have mixed together; but the plant, as we know, is a living being created from water, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And We made from water every living thing.. (21:30)﴾ [al-Anbiya'].

Here we must note the difference between the "ba'" of mixing (ba' al-khalt) and the "ba'" of causation (ba' al-sababiyya)(2). The ba' here in this verse is the ba' of causation, and so the meaning is: the plants of the earth mingled by its means. And you see that after the rain falls on the earth, the waters cover the earth, and then after days or weeks you find the surface of the earth covered with crops, all intermingled and interlaced; and whenever the crops intertwine with one another, this is evidence that irrigation is present and the fertility of this land is high, and this is the result of the interaction of the water with the soil.

As for when the land is not fertile, you find a plant in one area of the land and another far from it. This is what the people of the Egyptian countryside call, when planting maize, for example: "the maize is going bankrupt" (tufallis), meaning that each stalk of maize is distant from the other as a result of the land's infertility.

So then: the fertility of the land has an important basis in germination, and water exists to dissolve the nutritive elements for the plant, so that the roots of the plant spread through it.

If circumstances allow you to visit the scientific agricultural centres in Tokyo or California, you will see that they grow plants on fine threads, watered with water containing the nutritive elements necessary for germination, because they found that any plant takes from the earth the materials necessary for its growth to no more than five percent of its weight, and takes from the air ninety-five percent of its weight.

So then: the rain that descends from the sky through the air is what dissolves the elements of the earth, so that the plant may absorb them.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, here wished to strike for us a parable. A parable (mathal) is a saying whose likeness is drawn from its origin: whatever thing we want to liken to another thing must be known, and the thing used as the likeness must be known, and the thing taken as a likeness is what we want to clarify in its form. Therefore it is not valid to liken an unknown to an unknown; rather we liken an unknown to a known.

You find someone who says to you: "Do you not know so-and-so?" You say: "I do not know him." Your companion replies: "He is like so-and-so in appearance." Thus you have known the unknown by the known.

Some of those who try to object to the Qur'an entered through this aspect and said: If the thing is unknown and we want to make it known, should we not make it known by something known? Then why does Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, say about the tree of zaqqum(3):
﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs from the root of Hellfire. Its emerging fruit is like the heads of devils.(4)﴾ [al-Saffat] (37:64-65).

Why does Allah, glory be to Him, describe the tree of zaqqum, which is a tree in the Fire that we do not know, so that He makes it known to the believers in Him by saying that its spathe resembles the heads of devils? Thus He would have likened an unknown to an unknown. Those who said this overlooked that the One speaking is God, exalted be He. The Truth, glory be to Him, wished to liken for us the tree of zaqqum to something hideous that is known to us, and the known hideous thing is the devil.

The Truth, glory be to Him, willed not to specify the hideousness, so that the comparison would not be limited; for a thing may be hideous in your eyes and not hideous in the eyes of another. Allah, glory be to Him, wants to make the spathe of the tree of zaqqum repulsive, so He chose the thing whose hideousness is agreed upon, namely the heads of devils, and let every person imagine the form of the devil, with what repels and disgusts him. Thus the greatness of the Truth, glory be to Him, is manifest in that He made the form of the devil obscure(5).

As for the parable we are concerned with here, which is the likening of the life of this world to the water which the Truth, glory be to Him, sent down from the sky, so that the plants of the earth mingle with it, the life of this world: we perceive a part of it, and each of us perceives a period of it, and has not perceived its beginning, and may not perceive its end. So the Truth, glory be to Him, brought a parable which each of us sees, namely the crop that is watered by rain. Allah, glory be to Him, wished to gather for us the image of the world in a parable well known to all of us, which we perceive; so we perceive what has preceded and what follows. Every thing takes its share of flourishing and beauty, then it ends; so too is the world.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿like water which We sent down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it, from which men and livestock eat, until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it into stubble, as if it had not flourished yesterday (10:24)﴾ [Yunus]:

Zukhruf is the beautiful thing that pleases the soul and delights you when you see it; the world adorns itself with diverse colours in wondrous arrangement, then all of that becomes stubble(6). This is what we see in our lives. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has gathered the parable of life from its beginning to its end in a form visible to every person, so that no one is deceived by the adornment of the world or its beauty.

The Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who says: ﴿So let man look at his food (24). That We pour down water in torrents (25). Then We split the earth in splitting (26). And We cause to grow therein grain (27), and grapes and clover (28), and olives and palm trees (29), and gardens of dense trees (30), and fruit and pasture (31), as a provision for you and your livestock (32). But when the Deafening Blast comes (33), on the day a man flees from his brother (34), and his mother and his father (35), and his wife and his children (36), each man of them on that day will have a matter that occupies him (37).﴾ [Abasa] (80:24-37).

So then: the world with all its beauty that you see is only withering, and whatever brilliance of colour you see is only wilting, and however the world adorns itself it is headed for extinction. So beware of transgression, for in transgression lies the enjoyment of the world, and the whole world is headed for extinction, like the extinction of the garden upon which rain falls, so the earth brings forth flowers, then all of that withers.

The Truth, glory be to Him, has said: ﴿We tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit at dawn (17). And they did not make an exception (18). Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord while they slept (19). So it became like the black, harvested night (20).﴾ [al-Qalam] So then: the world is in this form and in this state.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified (10:24)﴾ [Yunus]:

The earth adorns itself by the command of its Lord, and the Truth, glory be to Him, attributes perceptions to what we do not know to have intellect or will. Did the Truth, glory be to Him, not say in the story of the righteous servant: ﴿So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. And they found therein a wall about to collapse.. (18:77)﴾ [al-Kahf]. Does the wall possess a will to collapse? If we examine the matter well, we will find that the Truth, glory be to Him, gave every being in existence a life suited to it, a will suited to it, and an affect suited to it. And the Truth, glory be to Him, has struck for us in this various images, and we find that the thing which our minds find difficult to grasp is made manifest to us by a clarification from God, exalted be He.

An example of this: the hoopoe's knowledge of monotheism in the story of Solomon, peace be upon him, and how this hoopoe informed our master Solomon, peace be upon him, about the kingdom of Sheba where the people prostrate to the sun instead of God, so the hoopoe seems to have known who deserves to be prostrated to when it said: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth.. (27:25)﴾ [al-Naml].

Who would have thought that the hoopoe, being a bird, would have such insight into beliefs in their purest form? Because the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to show us that this bird has no desire that corrupts its creed, and that it is our desires that corrupt beliefs; and whoever Allah has given alternatives is the one who corrupts choice, so long as he does not guard his choice with faith, and choose in the light of the method of Allah, exalted be He.

We see that whatever is below man, whether bird or animal, corrupts nothing, because its instinct leads it. We do not find an animal eating beyond its capacity, but we find a man bringing on himself indigestion; and we do not find a donkey leaping over a canal of water which it cannot cross, rather we see it drawing back from it; but we find a man rolling up his sleeves to leap over a water channel, and so he falls into it(7).

So then: by our desires, which dominate our instincts, we throw ourselves into what harms us, unless we guard ourselves with the method of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted. And in the example of the hoopoe we find doctrinal purity in monotheism, as pure as the purest of Sufis could be, and it brings what concerns it: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth﴾: because al-khab' is the hoopoe's sustenance; it does not eat from what is apparent on the surface of the earth, but strikes the earth with its beak to bring itself what it feeds on.

The Truth, glory be to Him, gives us another example in the ant that said: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his hosts crush you while they do not perceive (27:18)﴾ [al-Naml]. This is a precision of justice from this ant: it did not say that Solomon and his hosts would crush our fellow ants wrongfully, rather it said: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾, because you do not appear beneath their feet.

So then: every being in existence has a life suited to it, but the calamity is that we want to imagine life in every being as we imagine it in the highest being, which is man.

We must know that plants have a life suited to them, animals have a life suited to them, and inanimate things have a life suited to them, and everything in life has a kind of life suited to it.

We have previously explained that the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿that whoever perishes might perish by clear proof, and whoever lives might live by clear proof.. (8:42)﴾ [al-Anfal]. Perishing is the opposite of living, and living is the opposite of dying, and perishing is equivalent to dying. And the Truth, glory be to Him, depicts the state on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Everything is perishing except His face.. (28:88)﴾ [al-Qasas]. So then: the inanimate perishes, but it enjoys a kind of life that we do not know; and likewise every being has a life suited to it, and the calamity is that man wants to know the life that is in the inanimate as he knows life in man.

Look at the precision of Qur'anic expression in His word, the Truth: ﴿until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day (10:24)﴾ [Yunus]:

This statement came before science advanced and established that the earth resembles a sphere, that it revolves, and that every night corresponds to a day. Likewise came the word of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they sleep? (97) Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the forenoon while they play?.. (98)﴾ [al-A'raf] (7:97-98). So then: the command of Allah, glory be to Him, is realised when He wills, and it is one command for those who are in the forenoon or at night.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So We made it into stubble (18), as if it had not been (19) yesterday (24)﴾ [Yunus]: That is, as though it had never had existence.

The Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the verse with His word: {Thus

---

1. Zukhruf: adornment. Ibn Sayyidah said: zukhruf is gold; this is the origin, then every gilded or ornamented thing was called zukhruf. A "muzakhraf" house is an adorned house. Zakhrafa the house: he adorned and perfected it. In the hadith: the Prophet (ﷺ) did not enter the Ka'bah until he ordered the zukhruf to be removed. His word, exalted be He: "when the earth takes on its zukhruf" (10:24): the intended meaning of zukhruf here is the adornment of worldly life and its fleeting enjoyment, whose glitter deceives the eyes of those heedless of the Hereafter and its lasting bliss. [Lisan al-'Arab, root z-kh-r-f, adapted]. Al-Qurtubi said: zakhrafaha, that is, its beauty and its adornment. Zukhruf is the perfect beauty of a thing, and from it gold is called zukhruf. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/3254). Ibn Kathir said: zakhrafaha, that is, its transient adornment; wazzayyanat, that is, it became beautiful with the bright flowers of diverse shapes and colours that emerged upon its growth (Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/413).

2. Ba': a particle that governs the noun, apparent or pronominal, arising either originally or as an extra particle, and carrying a number of meanings, the best known of which are fifteen: adhesion (ilsaq), help (isti'anah), causation (sababiyya), transitivity (ta'diyya), locative (zarfiyya), exchange ('iwad), accompaniment (musahaba), partitive (tab'id), passing beyond (mujawaza), elevation (isti'la'), emphasis (tawkid), and meaning "instead of" (badal), and meaning "to" (ila). See the detail in al-Nahw al-Wafi (2/490-497).

3. The tree of zaqqum is the cursed tree in the Qur'an. The Almighty said: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and the cursed tree in the Qur'an.. (17:60)﴾ [al-Isra']. Allah, exalted be He, informed in His noble Book that it springs from the root of Hellfire. Its fruit is zaqqum, which is the food of the people of the Fire. [Lisan al-'Arab, root z-q-m, adapted].

4. Al-tal': a sheath resembling a jug, which opens to reveal a layered seed, containing the fertilising material of the palm tree [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root t-l-'].

5. Mubham: hidden, obscure. Istubham al-amr means the matter became closed. Al-mubham is so called because it is withheld from clarification, so no evidence is placed upon it. From this comes the name "bahima" for what does not speak. [Lisan al-'Arab, root b-h-m].

6. Hasidan: reaped, cut down, with nothing left in it. Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-hasid is the uprooted. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 4/3254].

7. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: al-qadb is the fodder that animals eat [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/472, adapted].

13. *Yurid an yanqud* (he wants to collapse): *al-infiqad* means falling quickly. Attributing the wish to collapse to the wall is a metaphor (*majaz*) for how close its fall is, by way of likening it to one who intends an action. In the Book of God is His saying: ﴿And when the anger subsided from Moses...﴾ (154) [al-A'raf], and His saying: ﴿But when the matter was resolved upon...﴾ (21) [Muhammad]. [Tafsir Surat al-Kahf by Shaykh Muhammad Muhammad al-Madani, adapted]..

14. *Al-khabʾ* (that which is hidden): that which has been hidden. The *khabʾ* in the heavens is rain, and the *khabʾ* in the earth is plant growth. It was also said that *al-khabʾ* is everything that is absent or unseen, so the meaning is: He knows the unseen in the heavens and the earth. [Lisan al-Arab, root kh-b-a]..

15. *Al-takhama* (indigestion): what befalls a person from food when he finds it unwholesome (*istawkhamahu*), that is, finds it heavy. The term *takhama* may also be applied to an excess of food and to overdoing eating and drinking, to the point that digesting the food becomes heavy on the body, so the person suffers from *al-wakhm* (heaviness and sluggishness), and loses the ability to move. [Lisan al-Arab, root w-kh-m]..

16. *Al-sa'id* (forearm): the place where the two forearm bones meet, from the elbow to the wrist. *Al-sa'id* also means the forearm of the arm, which is the part between the two bones and the elbow. It was named *sa'id* because it assists (*musa'adah*) the palm. Its plural is *sawa'id*. [Lisan al-Arab, root s-'-d]..

17. This is the fulfillment (*misdaq*) of His saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was ever unjust and ignorant.﴾ (72) [al-Ahzab]..

18. *Al-hasid* and *al-hasd*: the crop that has been harvested after it is reaped. The intended meaning of *al-hasid* here is a simile and depiction of God's destruction of the earth at the end of the world, by means of what happens when plants are harvested, namely uprooting and cutting them down. [Lisan al-Arab, root h-s-d, adapted]..

19. ﴿As if it had not flourished yesterday﴾: that is, it had not been inhabited. *Al-maghani* in the language means the dwellings that people inhabit. Qatadah said: "As if it had not been prosperous." Qatadah also read *yaghni* with a *ya*, taking it back to *al-zukhruf* (adornment, الزخرف), meaning: just as the crop perishes, so likewise is the world. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/3254]..

Dar al-Salam (the Abode of Peace): this is the Hereafter, which differs from the world-abode (dar al-dunya) full of hardships, this world which adorns itself and beautifies itself, and ends in crumbling debris. Therefore God, exalted is He, calls to another abode, the Abode of Peace; because among the troubles for the people of this world is that one of them may take his share of status, wealth, health and well-being, but he lives in the shadow of one of two anxieties: the first is fear that this bounty will be taken from him while he is alive, and the second is that he himself will pass away from the bounty.

As for the Hereafter, a person lives in it in lasting bliss; therefore God, glorified is He, says: ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace﴾.

In this Hereafter, no one will quarrel with another, and you will not find anyone consuming another's sweat, whereas such things happen in this world (1). And if we live in the world by the means of God, then in the Hereafter we live by God, glorified and exalted is He; so whatever occurs to your mind, you will find it.

If in the world the means vary and people's capacities differ despite their taking the means, then in the Hereafter they live with the bounty of God, glorified is He, without effort or means; because the Abode of Peace is the abode of God, exalted is He, for God is the Peace.

And to God belongs the Highest Example. If your ruler invites you to his abode, he prepares for your invitation according to his own standing and what befits his station; so what of when your Creator, glorified is He, invites you, provided you have followed His method? It is He, glorified is He, who said: ﴿Indeed, the companions of the Garden today are busy in enjoyment, they and their spouses, in shade, reclining on couches. For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they call for. [It is] a word of peace from a Lord Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin] (2)(3)(4). This peace is not from humans; for among humans there are those who give you peace while harboring for you nothing but peace, or who give you peace while intending harm to you; but he is of the changing (4), so he changes and cannot give you this peace. But when peace comes from God, exalted is He, it is peace from a Lord whom nothing can overcome, nothing can lack, and to whom no change applies. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured"﴾ [Ar-Ra'd] (23-24). The angels, when they say this, have taken their peace only from the inner reality of God's peace. Even the people of the Heights (5), who have not entered the Garden but see the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire, greet the people of the Garden with peace. Thus the people of the Garden live in a comprehensive, encompassing and tranquil peace, because the One who calls is God, glorified is He, and no one can compel Him to annul His peace.

God's call is His method, which He sent the messengers with, to govern the movement of life as a faith-based movement, in which people coexist in accordance with the method of God, so that this world becomes like the Garden. But what burdens people in this world is that some people neglect a part or parts of God's method (6), glorified is He.

And if you see a society suffering some kind of misery in any direction, know that a part of God's method has been neglected.

And if people had followed the method of God, glorified and exalted is He, there would not exist in existence a single flaw; for what reveals the flaws of existence is the heedlessness of some people toward the method of God, glorified is He.

And if you see poor people who cannot find what to eat, know that there is someone who has neglected the method of God, exalted is He: either the poor themselves, among whom some have grown accustomed to laziness (7), or the rich have been stingy in fulfilling God's right regarding those poor; and thus God's method, glorified is He, is neglected.

But if God's method dominates life, life becomes like the Garden.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And God guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾. We know that guidance is of two kinds: guidance of indication through the method, so whoever takes the method, God facilitates for him the path of the straight way; and thereby the servant moves from the stage of guidance by indication to guidance by assistance. And when the Resurrection occurs, God, glorified is He, guides them with light to the Garden: ﴿Their Lord guides them by their faith﴾ [Yunus] (9). So: whoever takes God's guidance by indication, which is the method, and follows this method, then the Truth, glorified is He, makes for him a light running before him: ﴿Their light runs before them and on their right﴾ [At-Tahrim] (8).

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And God guides whom He wills﴾ [Yunus] (25), because everything in this existence does not go beyond His will, glorified is He; laws do not govern Him, rather He is the One who governs everything.

And if God has made clear whom He wills to guide, He has also made clear to us whom He wills to lead astray, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And God does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [At-Tawbah] (37), and His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [At-Tawbah] (24). So: the Truth, glorified is He, has made clear to us whom He guides to the Garden and whom He does not guide. Let no one say: "And what is the sin of the disbelievers and the defiantly disobedient?" For the Truth, glorified is He, has made His method clear; whoever takes it, He makes for him a light running before him, and He admits him into the Garden.

(1) On this, the Lord of Might says concerning the people of the Garden: ﴿They hear therein no ill speech nor sinful utterance (25), but only the word "Peace, peace" (26)﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah]. They hear therein no vain or ugly speech; rather their saying to one another is "Peace, peace," meaning their greeting one another with peace; thus it is the Abode of Peace.
(2) ﴿Busy in enjoyment﴾: pampered, luxuriating in the bliss of the Garden. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Enjoying what their Lord has given them (18)﴾ [At-Tur]. [Lisan al-'Arab: root f-k-h, adapted].
(3) ﴿Reclining on couches﴾: The exegetes said: the arā'ik are couches within canopies; it was said they are furnishings. It was also said: the arīkah is a decorated, cushioned couch in a dome or chamber. It was also said: the arīkah is whatever one reclines upon, whether a couch, a bed, or a platform. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Reclining therein on couches; excellent is the reward (31)﴾ [Al-Kahf]. [Lisan al-'Arab: root '-r-k, adapted].
(4) The peace of the people of change varies according to interests, whereas God's peace is not subject to alteration or substitution; for His promise is true, His word is truthful, and He is Peace, and from Him is peace.
(5) The people of the Heights are a group whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal; they stand between the Garden and the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, looking at the people of this and the people of that, awaiting God's pardon. Concerning them God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And upon the Heights are men who recognize each by his mark; and they call out to the companions of the Garden, "Peace be upon you." They have not entered it, but they aspire [to] (46). And when their sight is turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people" (47)﴾ [Al-A'raf].
(6) The method of God: His path and His law. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a method﴾ [Al-Ma'idah] (48). He has laid down a method for the spirit, sublimity; for the heart, love; for the soul, tranquility; for the intellect, thought and contemplation; and for the body, movement. The method of these faculties establishes a society of lordship with a creed that unifies it, worship that loves and fears God, and transactions with morals. If one of these faculties becomes disordered through forgetfulness or heedlessness, the progress along the method toward God, majestic is His name, is disrupted.
(7) Istamra'a: he found a thing pleasing and became accustomed to it. [Lisan al-'Arab: root m-r-', adapted].
(8) The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind (124). He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, and I was [once] seeing?" (125) He will say, "Thus came to you Our verses, but you forgot them; and similarly, this Day, you are forgotten" (126)﴾ [Ta-Ha].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 26:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿For those who did good is the best (reward) and more. Neither darkness nor shame will cover their faces. Those are the companions of the Garden; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ (10:26)

The word ﴿al-husna﴾ (al-husna) is like our saying: "a superior woman" (imra'a fadla). We also say: "a greater woman" (imra'a kubra). It is an elative form (af'al al-tafdil, the comparative/superlative form), meaning hyperbole in excellence(1).

What is meant by His words, glorified is He, ﴿for those who did good, the best﴾ is: they strove to the utmost in performing good deeds. And a good deed, as we know, is rewarded tenfold. Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿for those who did good, the best and more.﴾ So what is this "more"?

We say: it is an additional gift over the good deeds. There is a "scale" (kadir) of reward for good deeds, beginning with ten times the good deed and reaching seven hundred-fold, whereas an evil deed is recompensed with one(2). This "scale" does not limit the bounty of God, the Exalted; rather, the Truth, glorified is He, increases His bounty for whomever He wills.

For this reason we must not distinguish between the justice of God, glorified is He, in that a thing equals a thing, and the bounty of God, the Exalted, in that a good deed is rewarded many times over beyond what we imagine.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: In the bounty of God and His mercy, in that let them rejoice...﴾ (10:58).

Some of the knowers of God said: the intended increase is in the tenfold and the seven-hundredfold, and the bounty (fadl) is what exceeds that.

Thus the degrees of reward are many: there is the tenfold, the seven-hundredfold, the "best" (husna), and the "more than the best" (ziyada). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding this: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, He says: 'Do you want anything more that I should give you?' They say: 'Did You not whiten our faces? Did You not admit us into Paradise and save us from the Fire?' He said: 'Then the veil is lifted, and they are given nothing more beloved to them than gazing upon their Lord, mighty and majestic'"(3).

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Neither darkness nor shame will cover their faces﴾, that is: no dust will cover their faces. He, glorified is He, also says: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ (75:22-23), and He says: ﴿And faces that day will be upon them dust (ghabara), covered by darkness (qatara)﴾ (80:40-41). "Tarhaquha" means: covers them. "Qatara" means: dust. It is derived from "al-qatar," which is the vapor filled with the smoke of rendered fat from roasted meat; its smell may be enticing and make the mouth water, but whoever has this vapor placed on his face acquires a black layer.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Neither darkness nor shame will cover their faces﴾ (10:26): because they feared God, glorified is He, and loved His method. And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿On the day when some faces will be whitened and some faces will be blackened...﴾ (3:106): the intended meaning is not the color of the face in this world, for you may find a person black of complexion whose face has been illuminated by faith, and his features are encompassed by a halo of splendor. And there is one who is white of face but, from the excess of disobedience to God, his face has become without light.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Those are the companions of the Garden; they will abide therein eternally﴾ (10:26): that is, they are constant in the Garden as a companion is constant with his companion; or "companions of the Garden" means: those who possess it.

1 Elative form (af'al al-tafdil): a derived noun on the pattern (af'al) that generally indicates that two things share a quality, one of them exceeding the other in it, such as (ahsan, afdal, akbar), as in our saying: the bliss of the Hereafter is better, more excellent and greater than the enjoyments of this world. In the feminine it is formed on the pattern (fa'la), such as (husna, fadla, kubra). See the detailed treatment in (al-Nahw al-Wafi: 3/394-415).
2 On the authority of Abu Hurayra that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, mighty and majestic, said: "When My servant intends a good deed and does not do it, I record it for him as a good deed; if he does it, I record it as ten good deeds up to seven hundredfold. And when he intends an evil deed and does not do it, I do not record it against him; if he does it, I record it as one evil deed." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (128), and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6491) with a different wording, from Ibn 'Abbas.
3 Related by Muslim (181), Ahmad in his Musnad (4/332), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2552), from the hadith of Suhayb al-Rumi.
4 Qatr: plural of qatara, which is ghabara (dust). In Tahdhib: qatara is dust overlaid with a blackness of smoke; al-qatar is the smell of a cooking pot, and it may come from roasting and burnt bone, and the smell of roasted meat. In the hadith of Jabir, may God be pleased with him: "Do not harm your neighbor with the smell of your pot." [Lisan al-'Arab: root q-t-r].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 27:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Those who have earned evil deeds—the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent, and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah. It is as if their faces had been covered with pieces of the darkest night. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ (10:27):

Since the Truth, glory be to Him, has mentioned those who were called to the Abode of Peace and given Paradise as a reward for good deeds, mentioning the opposite of a thing makes it stick more firmly in the mind. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So let them laugh a little, and let them weep much...﴾ (9:82) [at-Tawbah]. Also, among the examples of muqabalah (antithesis) in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾ (82:13-14) [al-Infitar]. So, the presentation of the opposite of a thing indeed fixes it in the mind. And because the Truth, glory be to Him, has spoken of the call to the Abode of Peace, and of whoever enters this call, for him is Paradise, abiding therein, no darkness or humiliation covering his face, it was necessary that the opposite be presented, and that the rejection of the call to the Abode of Peace be made to look ugly, while the matter is made to look fair to those who accept the call.

Therefore, it is necessary that the believer rejoice, because he will not be among the people of the Fire. It is also necessary that some of those who went astray come out of heedlessness, so that they may flee the fate of the Fire and turn to faith.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And those who have earned evil deeds...﴾ (10:27). We know that "kasb" (earning, acquiring) occurs in matters that are natural to human nature and suit acts of obedience, because obedience is a matter that is suited and congenial to the fitrah (innate human nature). No one is ashamed to pray, to give charity, to fast, or to perform Hajj; but among people there are those who are ashamed to be known as a liar, a usurer, or a drinker of wine.

When a person commits an evil deed, he goes through conflicting reactions. The one who steals from his father's cupboard while he sleeps, you find him tiptoeing on the tips of his fingers, being careful not to bump into anything that would expose his act; likewise the one who looks at the forbidden women of others.

All this indicates that committing what is contrary (to the good) involves contrivance (iftiʿal), i.e., it needs acquisition (iktisab). But the calamity is that a person continues to commit sins until they become a habit, and their practice becomes easy; so he commits sin professionally, and thus it turns from acquisition (iktisab) into earning (kasb).

Or the wicked among these people may reach a stage of settled dissolute conduct, so that he recounts what he does of sins and transgressions with pride, as when he says: "Last night we had a gathering that bewitched the mind, and we did such-and-such," and he relates it as if he had earned that gathering with all its sins and transgressions.

It is from Allah's mercy toward creation that He recompenses the perpetrator of an evil deed with an equivalent evil, so He says: ﴿the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent﴾. And the mercy of the Truth, glory be to Him, also becomes manifest when He grants a rank to the one who does not commit evil; so he becomes among those of whom the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿no darkness or humiliation will cover their faces﴾. But as for those who were not guided among them, of whom the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿they will have no protector from Allah﴾, meaning: no one will grant them protection before Allah, the Exalted, and no one will say to Allah, glory be to Him: "Do not punish them." Or the meaning of "no protector for them" is: Allah, the Exalted, will not then command that they not be punished.

Their situation is not limited to that alone; rather the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿It is as if their faces had been covered with pieces of the darkest night﴾, meaning: as if pieces of the dark night had covered their faces, and their abode will be the Fire ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾.

This is the state of those who denied the signs of Allah, Exalted, and denied the messengers, and refused the call of Allah, glory be to Him, to the Abode of Peace, followed their desires, and took partners besides Allah, Exalted.

The Truth, glory be to Him, willed to make all of this manifest to us in this world, so that the whole universe may have insight into what will happen to them in the Hereafter, because it is the inevitable result of what occurred from these people in this world.

(1) Muqabalah is a type of tibaq (antithesis, or positive-negative pairing), and it means combining two opposites within a sentence. Muqabalah is when two or more words are mentioned, then their opposites are mentioned in the same order. Among its examples also is the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿He enjoins them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things﴾ (7:157) [al-A'raf]. See: al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an by al-Suyuti (3/284-287).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 28:

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And on the Day We gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated partners with Allah: "Stay in your place, you and your partners." Then We will separate them, and their partners will say: "You did not use to worship us."﴾ (28)

Al-hashr (the gathering): it is the bringing of people from many places onto one place. These many places will eject those among them who are disbelievers, so that they arrive at the place which Allah, glory be to Him, has willed for them.

Whenever people draw near to this place, they crowd together. This is the nature of a circle with its circumference, and the inner circumferences within it which all converge at the centre. So when you look at a wide circumference of a circle, and then take the individuals from this wide circumference in order to cast them into the centre, there is no doubt that the closer you get to the centre, the more the circles narrow, and the gathering takes place.

It is as if we shall be crowded together in a severe crush, and this crowding has its hardships; but people will be occupied from it by what they are in of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection.(1)

His saying, the Truthful: ﴿And on the Day We gather them all together﴾ indicates the emphatic collecting of the states of those who did not respond to the method of Allah, the Exalted, nor to the call of Allah, glory be to Him, to the Abode of Peace, who denied their messengers and took rivals (andad) besides Allah, the Exalted.(2) Allah, glory be to Him, gathers the one who took rivals and the one taken as a rival, and confronts them, so that the disgrace may be complete and general: between the worshipper who worshipped falsehood, and the worshipped who did not ask his worshipper to worship him, or the worshipped who did ask his worshipper to worship him.

Therefore the Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then We will say to those who associated partners with Allah: "Stay in your place, you and your partners..."﴾ (28) [Yunus]. Thus there meet those who worshipped the angels with the angels, and those who worshipped a messenger and made him a god, and those who worshipped an idol, or worshipped the sun, or worshipped the moon, or jinn, or a devil from among the devils of mankind or the devils of the jinn.

So then: the worshipped are many, and each of these worshipped has a role in that gathering, and the confrontation will be open and exposed.

When we look at the worshipper who took a false god, whether he was of the angels or a messenger who was sent to them to lead them to the worship of one God, Allah, the Exalted, and they were tempted by the messenger and worshipped him, or they worshipped things that have no knowledge of those who worship them: such as idols, the sun, the moon, and trees.

As for the worshipped who has knowledge, and who has a call that others should worship him, he is concentrated in the devils of mankind, the devils of the jinn, and Iblis.

As for the angels, Allah, the Exalted, confronts them with those who worshipped them, and asks them: "Did you command these people to take you as gods?" They will say: "Glory be to You! You are our Protector," and they will disown these people, confirming the saying of the Truthful, glory be to Him: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed...﴾ (166) [al-Baqarah].

The angels have no knowledge of him who took them as gods. When we move to humankind, at whose head are the messengers, peace be upon them, there comes our master Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, and the Truthful, glory be to Him, says to him: ﴿Did you say to people: "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"...﴾ (116) [al-Ma'idah].

Our master Jesus, peace be upon him, says what came upon his tongue in the noble Qur'an: ﴿Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it...﴾ (116) [al-Ma'idah].

So these people had worshipped one who had no knowledge of this deification, and was not called to it.

Likewise the idols have no knowledge of him who claimed their divinity. But the one who has knowledge of that call is Iblis, because when it was grievous to him that he had disobeyed Allah, he led Adam astray; then Adam, peace be upon him, repented and Allah, the Exalted, accepted his repentance. As for Iblis, the Truthful did not accept his repentance, because he rejected the command of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to prostrate to Adam, and became arrogant, and considered himself of higher rank.(3) As for Adam, peace be upon him, he did not reject the command of Allah, the Exalted.

The Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We created you, then We fashioned you, then We said to the angels: "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated. He said: "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?" He said: "I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay."﴾ (11-12) [al-A'raf]. From this we take a brief article of faith: those who cannot master themselves in submitting to the method of Allah, the Exalted, it is better for them to say: the method of Allah, glory be to Him, is truth, and His judgment, glory be to Him, is right, but we were not able to submit ourselves to the judgment; and thus they leave the circle of returning the matter to the one who commands, and they are able to repent with the intention of not returning to disobedience.

So then: the contention and disputation(4) directed by Iblis at the offspring of Adam, for Iblis swore by the might of Allah, glory be to Him, that he would lead astray all the children of Adam except those whom Allah has chosen for His worship, glory be to Him, the Exalted, for Iblis knew that he was unable to lead them astray.(5)

Thus it is the might of Allah, glory be to Him, that enables Iblis and his offspring among the devils to lead astray, or not to lead astray, the creation of Allah, glory be to Him, the Exalted.

The devils are the disobedient jinn, because we know that the jinn are a kind corresponding to the kind of mankind; among the jinn there are the righteous and obedient, and among them are the disobedient, who are called devils, and who serve Iblis in leading mankind astray, so that he gains power over a person in what he knows to be a point of weakness in him.

So whoever loves wealth, the devil enters to him through wealth; whoever loves beauty, the devil enters to him through beauty; and whoever loves status finds the devil adorning for him reaching status by any means that conflict with noble morals and the method of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Every person has a point of weakness in his life which the devil knows, and creeps into him through it. Iblis and his offspring may recruit people from mankind who work with the aim of leading a person astray and corrupting him.

So there are, then, three who seek to turn people away from the method of Allah, the Exalted, and the call of truth: these three are Iblis, the disobedient jinn (that is, the devils), and then the humans who share with Iblis in leading astray, namely the devils of mankind who do deeds that oppose the method of the messengers.

Will the dialogue on the Day of Resurrection be between the angels and those among mankind who worshipped them? Will the dialogue be between the idols and those who worshipped them without their knowledge? Will the dialogue be between Jesus, peace be upon him, and those who took him as a god without his knowledge? Here we find a knower of Allah saying on the tongue of the idols: "They worshipped us, and we are more worshipful of Allah than those who stand in the pre-dawn hours.(6)" Because the Truthful, glory be to Him, is the One who says: ﴿And there is not a thing but it exalts Him with His praise...﴾ (44) [al-Isra']. And the knower of Allah continues: "They took our silence as proof against us, so we became fuel of the Fire for them," and the Truthful, glory be to Him, is the One who says: ﴿Then guard yourselves against the Fire whose fuel is people and stones...﴾ (24) [al-Baqarah]. The knower of Allah continues: "They have transgressed in ignorance, as they transgressed against the son of Mary and the disciples.(7)" So what is the position of Allah, glory be to Him, regarding these and those? We say: for the one who exaggerates there is his recompense, and the one exaggerated about is saved by the mercy of the All-Forgiving."

Thus the position of everyone who worships other than Allah, glory be to Him, or associates partners with Him is made clear: these are those whom the saying of the Truthful, glory be to Him, encompasses: ﴿And on the Day We gather them all together...﴾ (28)(8) [Yunus]. Thus will be gathered those who worshipped idols, or stars, or associated partners with Allah, and likewise the devils of the jinn and of mankind; all of them will be gathered in the place on the Day of Gathering. Let everyone remember in this world that on the Gathering matters will be uncovered, and every person who associated another with Allah will be exposed therein, glory be to Him, and there will be a confrontation with the one he associated in worship with Allah, glory be to Him, without the knowledge of the angels, the messengers, the stars, or the stones concerning the matter of these people. The command of the Truthful, glory be to Him, will come to them all: ﴿Then We will say to those who associated partners: "Stay in your place..."﴾ (28) [Yunus]. When you hear the command "Stay in your place," it means: "Keep to your place," and it is not said as a greeting; rather it carries threat and warning, and waiting for the outcome of a situation which will not be in favour of the one to whom it is said. We know that the angels, the messengers, the stars, and the stones have no knowledge of the matter of these people whom they were worshipped.

So then: those to whom this command applies are these polytheists who thought they could escape accountability, but they hear the command ﴿Stay in your place, you and your partners﴾. Does that mean they will come together with the angels and those among the messengers, stars, and stones who were worshipped, in one procession? No; because these servants agreed on a false position, and Allah, glory be to Him, wills to separate truth from falsehood.

Therefore the Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then We will separate them, and their partners will say: "You did not use to worship us."﴾ (28)(9) [Yunus]. That is: He made the polytheists one group, and made those who were worshipped without their knowledge another group, and the group of those who were worshipped without their knowledge declared: ﴿You did not use to worship us...﴾ (28) [Yunus].

That is: you did not worship us with our knowledge.

Look at the shameful position of those who worshipped other than Allah, glory be to Him, or associated partners with Him. Each one of them has worshipped a worshipped without the worshipped knowing of him, although the essence of worship is the worshipper's commitment to the command of the worshipped. This matter applies to the angels and to our master Jesus, peace be upon him, and it applies also to the stars and the stones; for Allah, glory be to Him, who makes the parts of a person speak on the Day of Resurrection so that they testify against their owner, is able to make the stones speak.
