The Truthful, glory be to Him, is the One who says: ﴿And on the Day the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in ranks. Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do. And they will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?" They will say: "Allah has made us speak, who made everything speak..."﴾ (19-21) [Fussilat]. The idol is found on the Day of Resurrection cursing him who worshipped it, just as the skin disowns its owner if he disobeys Allah, the Exalted. The Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿On the Day their tongues and their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ (24) [al-Nur].

But do not let your mind imagine how the idol speaks. You have believed that the limbs of a person, of hand, foot and skin, will speak on the Day of Resurrection. Have you reasoned how the hand speaks, how the skin speaks, and how the foot speaks in the Hereafter? You believe the report of the Hereafter, so do not look at the realities of the matters of the Hereafter through the laws of this world, for everything changes in the Hereafter. Has not the report told you that you will eat in Paradise and will not excrete waste?(10) This is not logical by the laws of this world, yet we believe it. And if the Truthful, glory be to Him, informs us of things that will happen in Paradise, were we to measure them by our minds against what we know in this world, we would stand helpless before them; but the believing heart reasons about the matters of the Resurrection and the Hereafter on the basis that they are unseen, and the measures differ regarding them, for man is a vessel(11) between heaven and earth. Does this world have an earth and a heaven, and does the Hereafter also have an earth and a heaven?

The Truthful, glory be to Him, says: ﴿On the Day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens...﴾ (48) [Ibrahim].

So then: everything changes on the Day of Resurrection. If it happens that the idols speak, denouncing being worshipped besides Allah, the Exalted, and the angels curse those who worshipped them besides Allah, glory be to Him, then do not be astonished.

(1) On the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, men and women together, looking at one another?" He ﷺ said: "O ʿĀʾishah, the matter is too severe for them to look at one another." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2859) and al-Bukhari (6527). So the terror of the Day of Resurrection is a severe terror, to the extent that people wish that the Day of Reckoning would end, even if their destination were the Fire.

(2) The nid (rival): the like and the equal; its plural is andad. The Exalted said: ﴿And they set up rivals to Allah...﴾ (30) [Ibrahim], that is, opposites and likenesses. The Exalted also said: ﴿And among people are those who take rivals besides Allah, loving them as they love Allah﴾ (165) [al-Baqarah]. [Lisan al-Arab: root n-d-d].

(3) On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the son of Adam recites the prostration verse and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping, saying: 'Woe is me! The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and he prostrated, so for him is Paradise; and I was commanded to prostrate and I refused, so for me is the Fire.'" Related by Muslim in his Sahih (81).

(4) The nid (contention): al-muhajjah is contention, striving and disputation. Al-hujjah is proof and evidence. Hajjahu and haajahu: he overcame him in his argument. The Exalted said: ﴿And if they dispute with you, say: I have submitted my face to Allah...﴾ (20) [Ali 'Imran]. Al-Azhari said: the argument was so named because it is aimed at (tahuj), that is, intended; for the intention is toward it and for it; likewise the road-way (mahajjat al-tariq) is the destination and the path. [Lisan al-Arab: root h-j-j].

(5) The Exalted said of Iblis: ﴿He said: "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them."﴾ (82-83) [Sad]. These chosen ones are the servants of the All-Merciful whose attributes Allah mentioned in Surah al-Furqan, verses (63-74). On the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, in a hadith that Iblis said: "My Lord, by Your might and Your majesty, I will not cease to mislead them as long as their souls are in their bodies." Allah the Exalted said: "By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they ask My forgiveness." Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/29) and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (4/261), and he authenticated it, and al-Dhahabi agreed.

(6) Al-asmar: plural of al-sahar, which is the last part of the night before dawn. [Lisan al-Arab: root s-h-r]. Those who stand in the pre-dawn hours are those who worship and pray in the night.

(7) That is, the disciples (al-hawariyyun), who were the companions and helpers of Jesus, peace be upon him, who were purified of every defect, like white flour that is sifted of its bran. [Lisan al-Arab: root h-w-r].

(8) Nahshuruhum: we gather them for reckoning; from it comes the Day of Gathering (yawm al-mahshar). Al-hashr: the gathering of people on the Day of Resurrection. The Exalted said: ﴿And fear Allah, and know that you will be gathered to Him﴾ (203) [al-Baqarah].

(9) The nid (rival): zayyalna baynahum: We separated between them. Al-tazayyul: divergence. The Exalted said: ﴿Had they been separated, We would have punished those among them who disbelieved with a painful punishment﴾ (25) [Lisan al-Arab: root z-y-l].

(10) On the authority of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "The people of Paradise eat and drink therein, and they do not spit, nor urinate, nor defecate, nor blow their noses." They said: "Then what of the food?" He said: "Belching and perspiration like the perspiration of musk; they are inspired to glorify and praise (Allah)." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2835), and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/364).

(11) That is: man is a place for the conditions of time and place, between the earth of this world and its heaven, and the earth of the Hereafter and its heaven; the laws of life differ between them in each of them.

Then Allah, exalted is He, says after that:

﴿So Allah is sufficient as a witness between us and you; indeed, we were unaware of your worship.﴾

So, the created beings that were worshipped besides Allah, exalted is He, declare their rejection of being worshipped. If the bird, represented by the hoopoe, had earlier expressed its astonishment that some of mankind worship other than Allah, exalted is He (1),

the hoopoe also inferred, as evidence of the power of Allah, exalted is He, from what concerns its own provision, knowing that Allah, exalted is He, has knowledge of the hidden thing (al-khabʾ) in the heavens and the earth. If the hoopoe knew this, then the denial is a logical matter from others among the creatures, whether they were angels, or Jesus, peace be upon him, or the idols, the trees, and the stars.

For this reason, we find Allah, exalted is He, giving the example of His question to the angels: ﴿Did these used to worship you?﴾ [Saba' 34:40]. The angels answer with their words: ﴿Glory be to You; You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn...﴾ [Saba' 34:41]. Allah, exalted and sublime is He, presents these positions in the surahs of the Noble Qur'an in a scattered manner (2), repeated in a way that leaves no room for heedlessness to afflict a person. For example, Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the day He will gather them all, [and say], "O company of jinn, you have taken much (3) from mankind..."﴾ [al-Anʿam 6:128], and He says, in the words of those who took the devils as allies: ﴿And their allies from mankind will say, "Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us..."﴾ [al-Anʿam 6:128]. Their saying this includes speech about themselves and speech about the jinn.

And one may ask: how do the jinn take many from mankind?

We say: Allah, exalted is He, created the jinn in a form different from the form of mankind, and He gave the jinn properties different from the properties of mankind. Among these properties is what Allah, exalted is He, said about: ﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe (4), from where you cannot see them...﴾ [al-Aʿraf 7:27]. Allah, exalted is He, gave the jinn more strength than He gave mankind, and gave them the ability to pass through iron barriers, walls, and other things. This is a logical matter given the original constitution of the jinn: the jinn are created from fire, and man is created from clay. There is a difference between the nature of fire and the nature of clay: what comes out of clay is qarr (5), meaning it does not radiate, whereas what comes out of fire has radiation and heat.

The meaning is this: if you were sitting in a room, and behind your back in the other room there was a lit fire, then the barrier, whatever it is, would convey to you some of the fire's heat, unless it were a heat insulator.

But if there were an apple, which is created from clay, in the other room, its taste or smell would not reach you.

So, fire has its law, and clay has its law. The law of a material created from clay does not move unless you move the body (6) to the place where it is located.

We glimpse this matter of regulation in the story of Prophet Solomon, peace be upon him, when he learned that the Queen of Sheba was traveling toward him to declare her Islam, and Prophet Solomon, peace be upon him, wanted to bring her throne from its place before she arrived.

He said to those in his assembly: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ [al-Naml 27:38].

This indicates that there were different kinds in his assembly, and each kind among them had abilities different from the abilities of the other kind. Moving the throne from Yemen to the place of Prophet Solomon, peace be upon him, requires time and strength. If they had been equal in their abilities, he would not have said: ﴿Which of you will bring me...﴾ [al-Naml 27:38].

The first to come forward to carry out what Solomon wanted was an ʿifrit of the jinn, not an ordinary jinni. Among the jinn there is one who is dull and of little intelligence, and one who is clever; although they are of one kind, they are also varied. The ʿifrit of the jinn was the first to speak, and said: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place...﴾ [al-Naml 27:39]. But Solomon's session might continue for an hour or several hours (7). The one speaking was an ʿifrit of the jinn who knows that he has attributes stronger than those of mankind. As for ordinary humans among those present at Solomon's assembly, they did not speak, because what was required was not within their ability. But the one among mankind who spoke was one who had knowledge from the Book, and he said: ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you...﴾ [al-Naml 27:40] (8), and it did not take any time at all. Therefore, the Qur'an then used a quick expression, saying: ﴿So when he saw it settled beside him, he said, "This is from the bounty of my Lord..."﴾ [al-Naml 27:40].

So: the jinn have power over things that mankind cannot match (9). The jinni did not acquire his properties of lightness, power, and the skill of shrinking time from his own constitution, but by the will of the Creator, exalted is He. For this reason, the Truth willed to mention that the jinn acquired those special qualities by His will, exalted is He. The Truth is the One able to make mankind, who is the lesser in power, capable of subjugating the jinn. For this reason, a person tries to take from the subjugation of the jinn a strength for himself, so that he may overpower his peer among mankind.

But Allah, exalted is He, has issued a judgment against whoever attempts that: subjugating the jinn increases one in distress (10). Consider the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and that which was sent down upon the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But they teach no one until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve."﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:102]. So, teaching magic to mankind by the jinn is evidence of the superiority of the jinn's abilities and their distinction from the abilities of mankind.

But the two angels Harut and Marut (11), when they taught man magic, first warned him not to take from it an additional opportunity that would make him tyrannical over his own kind and wrong them with it. The matter is entirely a test: if you learn it, let it be to protect yourself from evil, not to inflict it upon others. Then, O human, you may, from the perspective of changing circumstances, guarantee yourself at the time of undertaking (the trust), but what about the time of fulfilling it?

It is like when a person comes to deposit a thousand pounds with you as a trust. Will you remain faithful to the trust, or might you deny the money entirely when its owner demands it from you, or might a financial crisis befall you so that you dispose of this money?

For this reason, you find the wise man is the one who says to the one depositing this money: "Keep your money safe for yourself, because I am one of the changeable ones."

This is the original faith issue in the whole universe, because Allah, exalted is He, is the One who said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust (12) to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and were apprehensive of it; but man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:72]. The trust is what remains in the responsibility of the trustee, and the trustee has no proof against it except his conscience. There are no witnesses to it, and there is no receipt for that trust; rather, it is a deposit with no documentation, except the trustee's conscience. He may acknowledge it, or he may deny it.

Accordingly, the right of the trustee over the trustee is subject to the choice of the trustee. For this reason, we found that the heavens, the earth, and the mountains said: "O Lord, we do not want to put ourselves into this test. Do with us as You wish and make us subjugated, with no choice for us, and we do not want to bear the trust."

As for man, Allah distinguished him with reason and the ability to choose between alternatives. Therefore, man accepted to bear the trust, and when the time came to fulfill it, he did not find himself trustworthy in matters as he had thought of himself at the time of undertaking it.

Likewise, those who learn magic: one of them says to himself, "I will learn it to repel harm from myself." We say to him: "You cannot guarantee yourself, because you are one of the changeable ones. A person may anger you or irritate your nerves, so you use magic and thus afflict yourself with distress."

So, when Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O company of jinn, you have taken much from mankind...﴾ [al-Anʿam 6:128], the meaning is: you took much from mankind by giving them a weapon that grants them an opportunity and strength over other humans.

Allah, exalted and sublime is He, has told us that some of mankind who responded to the jinn said: ﴿We benefited from one another...﴾ [al-Anʿam 6:128]. Mankind's benefit from the jinn stems from humans gaining a strength above other humans, and the jinn's benefit from humans stems from the jinn helping that human in his disobedience, in fulfillment of the oath of the accursed Iblis: ﴿So by Your might, I will mislead them all﴾ [Sad 38:82]. But this benefit ultimately does not give anything beyond what is decreed for each kind. For this reason, you find that everyone who practices magic and subjugates the jinn is in suffering, confirming the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And they increased them in distress﴾ [al-Jinn 72:6].

You find that the provision of one who practices magic or subjugates the jinn comes from the hand of one who does not know magic. Had there been any advantage over mankind in learning this, He would have made his provision come from another source other than those who do not know magic or subjugate the jinn.

When you see one of these people, you find dust on his features, and in his offspring there is a defect or flaw. Among them is one who is one-eyed, or with withered hand, or lame, because he wanted to take an opportunity in life greater than other humans through the jinn. This opportunity increases his distress. Therefore, every person should adhere to his proper conduct and the measure Allah, exalted is He, has willed for him, and not think of taking an opportunity that increases his distress.

We see among people one who uses a person of physical strength or accuracy with a weapon to intimidate others, and he may succeed in that once or more, but then this "champion" or this hired killer turns against the one who hired him.

So: every person must respect the decree of Allah, exalted and sublime is He, regarding himself, and not take an opportunity from another kind that he thinks will add anything to his worldly life, but in reality it will add to his fatigue and increase his distress. For this reason, we find that Allah, exalted and sublime is He, says about them: ﴿Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us." He will say, "The Fire is your residence..."﴾ [al-Anʿam 6:128]. Thus we see that the outcome of benefiting from the strength of the jinn is the Fire, for the human who used the jinn and for the jinn who misled the human.

Then the Truth, exalted and sublime is He, presents to us another issue in this matter, saying: ﴿Intimate friends that day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:67].

The intimate friends (al-akhilla') are the group whose members are united by companionship and affection, and each of them permeates the life of the other. You find people in two categories: people who have taken friendship (al-khullah) (17) for the sake of Allah, exalted is He, who go to the mosques, study knowledge, eat only what is lawful, recite the Qur'an, and if one of them intends a sin, he finds in his friend what turns him back from sin; they make pilgrimage to the Sacred House of Allah and perform 'umrah, and their lives revolve around the saying of the Chosen Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Two men who love each other for Allah's sake, they gather for His sake and separate for His sake" (18). This is one kind of friendship.

The other kind includes people who help one another in disobedience, who drink wine, gamble, and commit every sin. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they meet the judgment of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿There is no trade therein, nor friendship﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:254]. So there is no friendship except the friendship of meeting for the sake of Allah, exalted is He. When friends who met for Allah's sake meet, they rejoice in one another, because each of them protected his brother from sin. But as for those who gathered in this world for sin, each of them curses the other, and the judgment of Allah, exalted is He, is fulfilled: ﴿Intimate friends that day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:67]. For this reason, we find the dialogue between those who were oppressed and those who were arrogant, and we find the Truth, exalted is He, bringing us this dialogue in the Qur'an: ﴿The weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so will you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?"﴾ [Ibrahim 14:21]. The others will answer: ﴿If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It is equal for us whether we are impatient or patient; for us there is no escape.﴾ [Ibrahim 14:21]. Then comes the confession of Satan, of whom the Truth, exalted is He, says: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and betrayed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot be your deliverer, and you cannot be my deliverer..."﴾ [Ibrahim 14:22]. This dialogue reveals to us what will happen on the Day of Resurrection.

1 This is in the story of the hoopoe with Solomon: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling them, and she has been given of everything, and she has a great throne. I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appear fair to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided.﴾ [al-Naml 27:23-24].

2 Scattered (manthur): a thing thrown here and there in scattered form, like grain and other things. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root n-th-r].

3 That is: you misled many of them, and most of them were misled by you.

4 The qabil (tribe): a group of people who form three or more from different peoples, such as the Arabs, the Romans, and the Zanj; or it may be from one origin, and a qabil may be from one father, like a tribe. Every generation of jinn and humans is a qabil. Allah says: ﴿Or you bring Allah and the angels as a qabil (in front of us)﴾ [al-Isra' 17:92]. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root q-b-l].

5 Qarr: that is, settled in its place; nothing moves from it unless you move it. One says: so-and-so is qarr, meaning still and firm. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root q-r-r].

6 Al-jirm: the body. Its plural is al-ajram.

7 Solomon, peace be upon him, used to sit to judge between people in their grievances from the beginning of the day until the sun declined.

8 Al-tarf: the eyelid of the eye; it also refers to closing the eyelid over the other eyelid. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root t-r-f].

9 The Imam says: the jinn have a strength according to their fiery constitution that surpasses the strength of humans. Then he pours upon us that man, through Allah's method, has a supplied strength from Allah when he lives by the method and understands the secrets of the Book. This is manifested in the fact that the devil said to Solomon: ﴿An ʿifrit of the jinn said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. And indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it." One who had knowledge from the Book said, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when he saw it settled beside him, he said, "This is from the bounty of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful is grateful only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous."﴾ [al-Naml 27:39-40]. So: the one connected to Allah is stronger than all others, this from the perspective of divine giving; but from the perspective of constitution, man is from clay, and clay is not like fire.

10 This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, but they increased them in distress﴾ [al-Jinn 72:6], meaning: humiliation and weakness. Al-Suddi said: a man would take his family out, come to a land, and camp there, and say: "I seek refuge in the lord of this valley from the jinn, that I or my wealth or my children or my livestock be harmed." Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (4/428).

11 Harut and Marut were two angels from the heaven who were sent down to the earth. It was said that they were displeased with the judgments of the children of Adam regarding the worshippers. So they were sent down to judge between people, and they taught people magic. It was stipulated upon them that they should not teach anyone until they said: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve."

12 The scholars differed in interpreting "the Trust" in the verse, but the most agreed-upon view is that it is obedience by choice. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is obedience. He presented it to them before presenting it to Adam, but they could not bear it. He then said to Adam: "Indeed, I have offered the Trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, but they could not bear it. Will you take what is in it?" He said: "O Lord, and what is in it?" He said: "If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished." So Adam took it and bore it. See Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/522).

13 Al-ighwa': misguidance. Allah says: ﴿So We misled you, for indeed, we were misguided﴾ [al-Saffat 37:32]. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root gh-w-y].

14 Al-akta': one whose fingers have drawn back into his palm, and the joints of the roots of his fingers have become visible. "Akta'" is used in emphasis as a follower, so one says: the army came, all of it, withered (akta'). [al-Muʿjam al-Waseet: root k-t-ʿ].

15 Al-mathwa: the place of residence and settlement. Its plural is al-mathawi. Allah says: ﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers﴾ [Al ʿImran 3:151]. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root th-w-y].

16 Al-akhilla' is the plural of khalil, meaning close friend. Allah says: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as a khalil﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:125], and Allah says, quoting the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Woe to me! I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend﴾ [al-Furqan 25:28]. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root kh-l-l].

17 Al-khullah: friendship and love. Al-khull: affection and a friend. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root kh-l-l].

18 This is a hadith with the same wording in the sense of the saying in the transmitted sources; it is transmitted with a chain of narrators in the collections of hadith.

١٨ On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Seven whom Allah will shade in His shadow on a day when there is no shade but His shadow: a just ruler; a young man who grew up in the worship of Allah; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who loved each other for the sake of Allah, came together for His sake and parted for His sake; a man who was called by a woman of rank and beauty and said, 'I fear Allah'; a man who gave charity and concealed it, so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives; and a man who remembered Allah in solitude and his eyes overflowed." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1031) and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (660).

١٩ Al-jaza' (anxiety, impatience): the opposite of patience (al-sabr). Allah the Exalted says of man: ﴿When evil touches him, he is distressed (jazu'an)﴾ [al-Ma'arij 70:20]. [Lisan al-Arab, the Arabic lexicon of Ibn Manzur, entry: jazi'a].

٢٠ Mahis: a place of escape. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those, their abode is Hell, and they will find no escape (mahis) from it﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:121]. [Lisan al-Arab, entry: haysa].

٢١ Al-sultan: the authority of domination, in subduing his followers. The word sultan is also applied to proof and evidence. Allah the Exalted says, of Solomon threatening the hoopoe: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority (sultan mubin)﴾ [al-Naml 27:21].

٢٢ Musrikhakum: one who gives you aid. Al-sarikh: the one who gives aid. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So when the one who had sought his help the day before called to him for help...﴾ [al-Qasas 28:18]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no one to cry for help for them, nor are they rescued﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:43]. [Lisan al-Arab, entry: sarakha].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 30:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿There, every soul will test what it has sent before (1), and they will be returned to God, their true Master, and what they used to invent will have deserted them.﴾ (30):

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿There﴾ means: at this time, or in this place. Time and place are the two containers of an event, because every act necessarily has a time and a place. If time is the dominant element, the adverb of time is used; if place is the dominant element, the adverb of place is used.

﴿There﴾ also occurs in the story of our master Zakariyya, peace be upon him, where the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord...﴾ (38) [Al 'Imran]: that is, at that time when Maryam, may God be pleased with her, uttered a saying which led to a matter of creedal faith for her guardian, who was our master Zakariyya, peace be upon him, and who used to bring her food. God, glorified and exalted is He, willed that she should inform him herself. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision...﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran]. Provision is that by which one benefits. Zakariyya, peace be upon him, was her guardian for everything she needed, yet he was surprised to find provision which he had not brought himself, as shown by his saying: ﴿Where has this come to you from?﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran]. This is the alertness and vigilance of a guardian when he finds his ward enjoying what he did not provide. This is the matter of "Where did you get this from?", which is the matter of the general guardian of society when he sees someone enjoying what his activity in life does not qualify him for; by this, the one who misappropriates benefit from what belongs to others is discovered, without his guardian knowing. Had his guardian insisted on knowing where the sources of his income came from, he would have protected society from corruption.

Consider the reply of Maryam, peace be upon her, to the saying of Zakariyya, peace be upon him, which the Lord of Might, glorified is He, mentioned: ﴿Where has this come to you from?﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran]. Maryam said: ﴿It is from God...﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran], then she gave a reason for the answer: ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account.﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran]. She said that because he found with her things that are not found at such a time of the year, so our master Zakariyya, peace be upon him, was amazed. So there were two things: something he had not brought himself, and something contrary to the season he was in, as if he found grapes out of their season, or found oranges out of their season (4). His question was evidence of the guardian's alertness, and her answer was a matter of creedal faith: ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account.﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran]. Since it is ﴿from God﴾, glorified and exalted is He, your own reckoning does not apply to things in the light of this matter.

But did our master Zakariyya, peace be upon him, neglect the matter of faith that God provides for whom He wills without account? We say: No, he did not neglect it, but it was not at the focus of his awareness at that moment; so the saying of Lady Maryam came with it to remind him of this matter, and here Zakariyya remembered himself, as a man who had reached old age (5), and whose wife was barren. Since God, glorified is He, provides for whom He wills without account, it is not necessary for him to be young or for his wife to be young in order to bear a child. So the Truth came expressing Zakariyya's thought in His saying: ﴿There Zakariyya called upon his Lord...﴾ (38) [Al 'Imran]: that is, at this time or that place, or both together in time and place. Here the answer came to him from his Lord, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿He said: "So (it will be). Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing.'"﴾ (9) [Maryam]. The Truth brought this matter in order to prevent anyone from suspecting ill of the chastity of Maryam, peace be upon her, because she was in a position of seeking refuge; so the Truth made her speak with His saying: ﴿He provides for whom He wills without account.﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran]. Since provision is without account, at a time other than its time, in a place other than its place, without a cause and without the knowledge of her guardian, then the seeking of refuge in God was realized through the good acceptance with which the wife of 'Imran prayed: ﴿And indeed, I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the expelled.﴾ (36) ﴿So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance (6) and caused her to grow in a good growth, and He entrusted her to Zakariyya...﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran].

Zakariyya, peace be upon him, applied it to himself; then she herself was subjected to it, when the Truthful, glorified is He, gave her the good news of a boy named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon them both.

She would bear him without a man touching her, and she knew that the causes operate such that there is no procreation except with a male and a female. God, glorified is He, willed to decree for her that she bear without this process, so He brought that premise upon her tongue: ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account.﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran].

When she asked: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?﴾ (47) [Al 'Imran], the answer came to her that his name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, God gives you good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary.﴾ (45) [Al 'Imran]. By her faithful alertness she perceived that this child would be attributed to his mother; so she knew that his father was nullified, and she realised that this boy would not come as the result of a marriage, even later. Thus she had to return to the matter of faith she had mentioned: ﴿Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account.﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran]. And here, in the verse about which our reflections are concerned, the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿There, every soul will test what it has sent before.﴾ (30) [Yunus]: that is, at that time every soul is tested, and sees whether the recompense is good or not. If it has done evil, it will find the recompense to be evil.

So, at the time of outcomes, a person tests himself by what he did.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿and they will be returned to God, their Master (7), the True.﴾ (30) [Yunus]. It is as if they were in this world with a master other than God, the True, glorified is He; and the master other than the True is the partner or partners whom some people took as their masters. Here, on the Last Day, they are returned to the True God and the True Master, glorified is He.

The expression "returned to such-and-such" does not indicate that they were with the opposite and came to Him; rather it indicates that they were with Him first, then went to the opposite, then were returned to Him a second time, like His saying, glorified is He, about Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿So We returned him to his mother...﴾ (13) [Al-Qasas]. It indicates that he was with his mother, then he separated from her, then he was returned to her.

His saying, the Truthful, glorified is He, here: ﴿and they will be returned to God, their true Master (8).﴾ (30) [Yunus]: that is, they were with God first, then the partners took them, and on this Last Day they return to their Lord, glorified is He.

A person is first with his Lord by the original, creative, believing nature, then his parents steer him toward Zoroastrianism or any other religion carrying shirk with God (9), and in the shade of those polytheistic religions they were with a master, lord, commander and legislator, but it is a master who is not true, because the Truth is the constant which the changing cannot grasp.

﴿There, every soul will test what it has sent before.﴾ (30) [Yunus]: that is, every soul will know what it did, and each person will be exposed in the particulars of his own self, and likewise the general exposure of every person who associated partners with God, glorified is He.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿and what they used to invent will have deserted them.﴾ (30) [Yunus]: that is, the gods they worshipped will not know their places and positions, and that they are in danger, so that they would take them by the hand; because these gods have no knowledge of them. Had these gods they worshipped besides God, glorified is He, possessed any truth, and had they found them in a predicament, they would have been obliged to defend them; but they did not know their places. ﴿and what they used to invent will have deserted them.﴾ (30) [Yunus]: that is, what they used to lie about with deliberate falsehood.

1 ﴿Tabluu kullu nafsin ma aslafat...﴾ (30) [Yunus]: it means it will taste the recompense of what it did and sent forward. It was said: it will test. It was said: it will follow, i.e., every soul will follow what it sent forward in the world. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "tatlu," meaning every soul will recite its book which was written for it. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 4/3261] and Ibn Kathir [2/416].
2 "Anna laka hadha?": how, and from where, is this for you?
3 For God in His giving there is provision by account, and provision without account. Provision by account is in proportion to the good and righteous deed you offer; giving is measured by the scale of divine justice. As for provision without account, it is the provision of those who have given their whole selves to the Absolute Whole: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (162) [Al-An'am]. So, that provision here is without limit is in confirmation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Adorned for those who disbelieve is the worldly life, and they mock those who believe; but those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And God provides for whom He wills without account.﴾ (212) [Al-Baqarah], because the knowing imam said: whoever approaches God with an account, He gives him by an account, and whoever approaches Him without account, He gives him without account.
4 ﴿Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision...﴾ (37) [Al 'Imran]. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and others said: that means he found with her summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer. This indicates the miracles (karamat) of the saints [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/360].
5 Shaykh "'ataa," "'utiyyan," "'ataiyan": became old and advanced in years. [Lisan al-'Arab: root ('-t-a)].
6 Accepting a thing and receiving it is evidence of taking the thing willingly; you may take it unwillingly or reluctantly, but if you receive it, then that taking is with acceptance and pleasure. As for good acceptance, it is an increase in pleasure.
7 Al-mawla: the helper and the friend who takes charge of your affairs, and only one who is near you takes charge of you; he is the supporter and helper to whom you turn in your hardships.
8 God says here: ﴿and they will be returned to God, their true Master...﴾ (30) [Yunus], affirming that God is their true Master, and He says in another verse: ﴿and that the disbelievers have no master.﴾ (11) [Muhammad]. He, glorified is He, is not a master to them in support and aid, but He is a master to them in provision and the abundance of blessings.
9 Narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah; then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?" Then he recited: ﴿The nature of God upon which He created people; there is no alteration to the creation of God. That is the correct religion...﴾ (30) [Al-Rum]. Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4775) and Muslim (2658).

Once Allah, glorified is He, had made the matter clear, and had shown what will happen in the Hereafter, and had frightened them and described to them the destiny that awaits them if they persist in disbelief, in the hope that they would be deterred(١) and would remember the necessity of returning to the worship of the true God, glorified is He, the Exalted, the Real, brings forth what restores to them the right guidance of faith in their souls. So He says: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who owns hearing and sight? And who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living? And who arranges the affair?" They will say, "Allah." So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ (10:31)

That is: Allah, the Real, glorified is He, says to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: Ask them this question. No one asks this question except one who is confident that the one questioned, even if he were to consider all the possible answers in his mind, would find no answer other than what the questioner already has.

An example of this from our own lives, and Allah has the highest example: if someone comes to you and says, "My father neglects me," you hold him and ask him, "Who brought you these clothes and that pen, and feeds you and teaches you?" He will say to you, "My father."

You ask this question only while you are confident that if he were to consider all the answers, he would find no answer except the one you expect from him, for he has no other answer. For if you knew that he would answer you with a different answer, you would not have asked him. It is as if you have accepted his judgment in the matter.

The Real, glorified is He, said at the beginning of this noble verse: ﴿Say﴾, just as He sent down similar verses that begin with His saying: ﴿Say﴾, such as His saying: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One(١)﴾ [al-Samad]. This is what the address of the Real, glorified is He, to creation has always required, and it differs from the address of created beings to one another. When you say to your son, "Go to your uncle and say to him such-and-such," the son goes to the uncle and says to him the content of his father's message, without saying to him: ﴿Say﴾. But the address of the Real, glorified is He, to creation, He willed that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, convey it to us exactly as it was revealed, ﴿Say﴾. The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is trustworthy in conveying from Allah, the Exalted. He does not leave out a single word of the revelation without conveying it to mankind. And since the Real, glorified is He, is the one who commanded him, he conveys what he was commanded, so that the ears of Allah's creation are not deprived of any word that came from Allah, glorified is He.

Likewise, the Real, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, here to say: ﴿Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth...(٣١)﴾ [Yunus]. We know that provision (rizq) is what one benefits from, and the first benefit establishes life, while the second is luxury or the extras of life. The provision that is the basis of life is water that descends from the sky and plants that come forth from the earth.(٣)

Thus the Real, glorified is He, said it, and the answer is known in advance. He did not say to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, "Answer yourself," but left it to them to answer by themselves.

Likewise, the Real, glorified is He, brought another question: ﴿Or who owns hearing and sight...(٣١)﴾ [Yunus].

Hearing and sight are the two masters of the faculties of perception, because the perception of knowledge(٤) has many means. If you want to perceive a smell, it is through your nose; if you want to perceive softness, it is through your touch and your skin; if you want to perceive the taste of something, it is through your tongue; if you want to speak, it is through the organs of speech, whose chief is the tongue; and if you want to hear, it is through your ear.

Likewise, the appearances(٥) become manifest to you through your eye, and then come many perceptions from the senses, which become things we call the "leaven" (al-khamira), from which the final rational proposition arises. A child before a fire finds its sight beautiful and attractive, but as soon as he touches it, it burns him, and he never approaches it again after that, because he has tested it with his senses, so the rational proposition became fixed in him, namely that this is a burning fire, and this became settled in him as a certainty.

Thus sensory perceptions are many perceptions that create a "leaven" in the soul, from which the immaterial perceptions are formed.

Therefore: the means of knowledge for a living being are the senses, and these senses give the intellect data that become impressed upon it, to settle afterward in the conscience, and then they become beliefs.

Therefore: the stages of perception are: sensory perception, then rational reflection, then a final binding of belief. That is why we call religion "aqida" (creed). That is: you have tied (ʿaqadta) the thing in your certainty in such a way that you cannot untie it again to dissolve it. This is called ʿaqida.

Therefore, when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wanted to relate to us the stages of perception in the human soul, so as to educate man and his knowledge, the Real, glorified is He, said: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts, that you might be grateful.(٧٨)﴾ [al-Nahl]. Therefore it is said: "As his mother bore him," meaning he was not yet given the ability to use his senses. Then the Real, glorified is He, gives him the senses and makes him capable of using them.

He did not mention the rest of the senses, but mentioned the two masters, hearing and sight, because the signs of the universe require seeing, and conveying the messengers requires hearing, and these are the two most important instruments of conveyance. You see with your eye the signs of the universe and the miracles of the messengers, and you hear the message of Allah's way from the messengers.

Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, drew our attention to the wonders when he said: "Marvel at this human being: he sees with a fat(ʿ) piece, speaks with a flesh, hears with a bone, and breathes through a hole."(٦)

The sound strikes the bone of the ear and resonates on its eardrum, and we see with the fleshy part(٧) of the eye, and we speak with the flesh of the tongue.

Some have added: "And we smell with cartilage, and touch with skin, and think with dough." The human being is born as though his brain were a piece of dough that works to receive information from the universe and store it within, and it will be the foundation for forming the heart afterward.

The Real's saying here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, came with two of the means of perception, and He left out the other three apparent means, although modern science, when it spoke about the functions of the organs, was cautious about the matter and determined that these senses are the five apparent senses.

This means that there are other senses beyond these that will be revealed, senses that the ancients did not know, such as the sense of "between-between" (al-bayn bayn), by which we distinguish between types of cloth and paper and other things, and the density of this kind from that. This sense exists between two touches of two closely placed fingers.(٨)

Likewise, the muscular sense, which weighs the heaviness of things, and when you carry a certain weight you know how much strain it causes you and whether it differs from the strain of carrying another weight.

When the scholars considered the meanings of the terms, they said: "Similar things, when they differ, there must be a reason for the difference." Hearing is an instrument of perception, and sight is an instrument of perception. So why did the Real, glorified is He, say of the first instrument of perception "hearing (al-sam)," and say of the second "sight (al-absar)"? And why did hearing come in the singular while sight came in the plural, and not both in one pattern(٩)?

We say: the speaker is Allah, the Exalted, and every word from Him has wisdom and is placed in a balance. When you hear, you hear any sound coming from any place, but with the eye you see from one direction. If you want to see what is on your right, you turn your eyes to the right; if you want to see what is behind you, you change your position. The ear hears without any action on your part, but sight requires several operations in order for you to see what you want.

Also, hearing is not a matter of your choice: you cannot block your ear from hearing something. But sight, you control it by movement or by closing the eye.

The Real, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned hearing first, because the ear is the first means of perception to carry out its task in a human being, while the eye does not begin to carry out its task until after three to ten days, generally. Here the Real, glorified is He, says: ﴿Who owns hearing and sight...(٣١)﴾ [Yunus]. The Real, glorified is He, owns them because He created them, and He is able to preserve them, and He is able, glorified is He, to disable them. Allah has given us an example of this in the Qur'an, when He spoke of the People of the Cave: ﴿So We struck upon their ears in the cave for a number of years(١١)﴾ [al-Kahf]. Allah, glorified is He, disabled their hearing by striking upon their ears, and they went into a sleep that lasted three centuries and increased by nine.

How did this happen? The longest a typical person sleeps is a night. Therefore, when Allah raised them, they asked one another: ﴿A speaker among them said, "How long have you remained?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day..(١٩)"﴾ [al-Kahf]. But their appearance did not indicate this, for their hair had grown very long, and its black color had changed, and they had become gray and elderly. Therefore the Real, glorified is He, said: ﴿Had you looked at them, you would have turned away from them in flight, and been filled with terror of them..(١٧)﴾ [al-Kahf].

We note here a point that must be noticed. In this noble verse the Real, glorified is He, says: ﴿Who owns hearing and sight..(٣١)﴾ [Yunus], while in another verse, in Surat al-Sajda, He says: ﴿And made for you hearing and sight..(٩)﴾ [al-Sajda]. We must be mindful of the difference between "creating" (khalq), "making/placing" (jaʿl), and "owning" (mulk). The Real's ownership of everything is a matter that is binding in creed and well known. As for "making" (jaʿl), it is directing what was created toward its function.

You make clay into a jug and cloth into a robe; that is at the human level. But as for the Real, glorified and exalted is He, He created the matter first, then made from the matter hearing and sight, and then added ﴿who owns﴿. So the one who created is Allah, the one who made is Allah, and the one who owns is Allah.

He, glorified is He, draws our attention to this: the beneficial things for the children of Adam He creates, and makes them, and then owns them for him.

As for the essence of a human being and his parts, such as hearing, sight, and others, although they were created in the human being and made for him to benefit from, they will remain Allah's possession: He keeps them in their state, or snatches them away, or afflicts them with a calamity, or disables them.(١٠)

Therefore: they were created by Allah, made by Allah, and remain Allah's possession, and He changes them as He wills. The beatings of the heart, love and hatred, and the involuntary matters that work for the benefit of the human being, these are the dominion of Allah.

The Real, glorified is He, for example, made every animal's skin something we benefit from and tan, except two skins: the skin of a human being and the skin of a pig. The use of human skin was forbidden because of his dignity before his Creator, and the use of pig skin was forbidden to show its prohibition and impurity.

We must notice that the Real, glorified is He, has created, made, and owned. The evidence of the Real's ownership, glorified and exalted is He, is that He forbade Paradise to the one who takes his own life,(١١) because no one takes life except the Giver of life. You, O human being, are not the owner of yourself. There is no excuse for anyone once this message has reached him, and he must understand it. As for the one who does not understand, he will meet his fate.

Therefore He, glorified is He, is the one who provides, and He is the one who owns.

Then the Real, glorified is He, says: ﴿And who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living..(٣١)﴾ [Yunus]. We know that every being in existence has a life suited to it, as the Real, glorified is He, says: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face..(٨٨)﴾ [al-Qasas]. Since everything will have a time in which it perishes, this means that everything has a life, except that our life, outwardly, is only sensation and movement. A human being eats vegetables, bread, and fruit, and from these foods and others the body is formed: the sperm in the man and the ova in the woman, and from them the human being comes. Likewise the chick emerges from the fertilized egg, because the unfertilized egg does not produce a chick; it has no life, and therefore no embryo forms from it. There is a difference between the capacity for life and life itself.

Likewise the date pit: if it is thrown without being placed in the earth, it will never become a palm tree, but if it is planted in the earth and finds the suitable environment, a palm tree comes forth.

Then the Real, glorified is He, says: ﴿And who arranges the affair..(٣١)﴾ [Yunus]. Management (tadbir) is the process of administering anything so that it carries out its function. By Allah, who directs your heart? Who directs the movement of your intestines? So that you may extract from...

١ Irtidaʿ: refraining from something. Tara daʿa al-qawm: some of them deterred others, rebuking them and restraining them from sins and harming people. [See Lisan al-Arab, root r-d-ʿ.]
٢ The verse contains the logic of innate nature (fitra) toward monotheism. When the disbeliever is asked about the creation of the universe, about the management of the affair, and about the wonders of the signs, he cannot answer except by innate impulse: the Creator is Allah, and the Manager is Allah.
٣ This provision is what the Lord of Majesty mentioned in His saying: ﴿Then let man look at his food. That We pour down water in torrents, then We split the earth in splitting, and We make grow therein grain, and grapes and herbage, and olives and palm trees, and enclosed gardens of dense trees, and fruit and pasture, as enjoyment for you and your cattle.﴾ [ʿAbasa]
٤ Perception gives rise to feeling (wijdan), feeling gives rise to choice, and choice gives rise to thought and contemplation, and through reflective thought comes the affirmation of God's oneness.
٥ Ra'a yara fa-huwa ra'in; what sight falls upon is marʾi, and the plural is marai.
٦ Recorded by al-Sharif al-Radi in his book "Nahj al-Balagha" (4/4), published by Mu'assasat al-A'lami li-l-Matbu'at, Beirut.
٧ From shahmat al-ʿayn: its pupil, and it is said: its iris, or what lies beneath the iris. As for shahmat al-udhn (the earlobe), it is the soft part at its bottom, where the earring hangs. [Lisan: root sh-h-m]
٨ This is other than the sense of touch by which we perceive the smoothness or roughness of this cloth or that; the latter is perceived by the sense of touch, usually by passing the palm of the hand over the cloth, whereas perceiving the thickness (takhana) of this cloth or that is done by this other sense.
٩ Al-wateera: the manner. From al-tawatur, meaning succession. Things proceeded in one wateera: that is, in the same quality and manner. [Lisan: root w-t-r]
١٠ Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿The lightning nearly snatches away their sight. Every time it lights for them, they walk in it, and when it darkens over them, they stand still. And if Allah willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.(٢٠)﴾ [al-Baqara]
١١ From Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever kills himself with an iron implement, his implement will be in his hand, stabbing himself in the belly in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever. Whoever drinks poison and kills himself, he will sip it in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever. And whoever throws himself from a mountain and kills himself, he will be throwing himself in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever." Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (5778) and Muslim (109), and the wording is Muslim's.

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿So that is Allah, your true Lord. Then what is there after the truth except error? So how are you turned away?﴾ (32)

Almighty Allah's words ﴿So that﴾ are a pointing (ishara) by Him to what He mentioned earlier: provision, ownership of hearing and sight, the power to bring the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, and the management of affairs.

So His words ﴿So that﴾ point to many and varied things and blessings, which He indicates with a single expression, because they all proceed from one God. ﴿So that is Allah, your true Lord...﴾ (32) [Yunus]. There are not two truths in existence, but one truth; whatever is other than it is error. Therefore Almighty Allah says: ﴿Then what is there after the truth except error...﴾ (32) [Yunus]. So, if you direct lordship to other than Him, you have certainly lost the way. Error is when you have an aim you want to reach, but you set out on a road that does not lead to it. If you turn away from the true God, then you arrive at error.

For this reason Almighty Allah concludes the verse with what shows that there is nothing but truth or error, saying: ﴿So how are you turned away...﴾ (32) [Yunus]. That is: if you turn away from Almighty and Exalted Allah, then it is toward error, while the truth is one, fixed and unchanging.

Whoever worships the angels, the stars, or the planets, or some of the messengers of Allah (peace be upon them), or an idol among idols, has fallen into error.

And if you wish that we debate with you by reason, then let us read together the words of Almighty Allah after this:

﴿Thus has the word of your Lord been justified against those who defiantly disobey; they will not believe.﴾ (33)

¹ "So how are you turned away": that is, how do they turn their minds away toward worshipping what neither provides, nor gives life, nor causes death. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 4/3267].

² The truth is one not according to human reasoning but according to the method of the Truth itself; for the realities of things are fixed, and knowledge of them is attainable, unlike the Sophists, and unlike those who believe that falsehood is truth and truth is falsehood. Truth is not subject to the distortions of minds or the distortion of thought aimed at opposition and sophistry.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 33:

His words, "Thus" (﴿kadhalika﴾), point back to what was mentioned before: God's provision to all of mankind, His control over hearing and sight, His management of the whole affair, and His bringing the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living. That is the true God, glory be to Him. This has been established by His question, glory be to Him and exalted, a question whose answer He knew in advance could only be acknowledgment of Him as the true God: ﴿So what is there after the truth but error?﴾ (32).

Exactly like this matter is the word of the True One, glory be to Him: ﴿Thus the word of your Lord has come true against those who defied, that they will not believe﴾ [Yunus] (33). This is because they misunderstood oneness and belief, and they deserved to be punished, since they diverted the truth away from its rightful owner.

This address was directed to those present in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), yet some of them believed in God, Exalted is He; therefore punishment only befalls those who do not believe.

This statement applies to those who, in God's eternal knowledge, were already known not to believe. Likewise, the word of your Lord has come true against these who defied, who do not desist from their defiance and disbelief, and who persist in deviating from worship of God Most High and the true Lord, glory be to Him and exalted.

The proof of God's eternal knowledge is what we read in Surat al-Baqara: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqara] (6).(1) So God knows who will believe and who will not, and whoever persists and insists upon his disbelief is the one who meets the punishment, and God knows concerning him that he will never believe.

Then the Truth mentions, after this, what can be used to argue with the disbelievers on the basis of their own circumstances. Within the souls of those who do not believe in a God there exists an innate inclination to do good and to guide others to it, and this is found even among non-believing nations. Every people are guided toward good according to their beliefs. Among the non-believing peoples we find wise men, physicians and scholars, and these guide people to some of the good they see.

We also see a small child acquiring beliefs, customs and attitudes from his parents and from what he hears of their guidance. You find him keeping away from fire or electricity, for example, because the guidance and advice of others has taken root in his mind. Indeed, he learns how to deal with these things without being harmed by them.

So there is guidance from creatures to creatures toward the paths of good. Do we not find, in non-believing countries, someone who directs people to the roads on which they may travel in two directions, and the roads on which they must travel in one direction only?

Is there not someone who warns people of the dangerous bends on roads, and likewise directs them to the necessity of reducing the speed of cars in front of children's schools? Yes, there are in non-believing lands those who do this.

So thinking about what is good for the benefit of nations is a natural, instinctive matter found in all societies. And if guidance toward good comes from a human being who is equal to another human being, is it not that God, glory be to Him, is more worthy of guiding toward good? He is the One who created man and created for him what sustains his life on earth. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say: Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it? Say: God originates creation and then repeats it, so how are you deluded?﴾ (34).

(1) The verse alludes to the society of hypocrisy, and the society of hypocrisy lives between two societies: the society of faith, confirming His words: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful﴾ [al-Baqara] (5), and the society of disbelief, confirming His words: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and he finds God with him, so He pays him in full his account; and God is swift in account﴾ [al-Nur] (39). The society of hypocrisy is more dangerous than the society of disbelief, since disbelief is declared openly and I am alert to it, whereas hypocrisy is deception..

(2) Al-Ifk: falsehood and sin. "Anna tu'fakun": how are you lying? [Lisan al-'Arab, root (a-f-k)]. Al-ifk is more dangerous than ordinary lying, since al-ifk consists of invented fabrication and baseless exaggeration that has a harmful effect on societies and individuals. For this reason the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every man among them is what he earned of sin, and he who undertook most of it among them will have a great punishment﴾ [al-Nur] (11). He did not say "with falsehood" even though it was falsehood, but He expressed it as ifk, because it involves fabrication against people's dignity and the values of society.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 34:

Here Allah, glorified is He, commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to ask them: ﴿Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?﴾ [Yunus 34]. The meaning of Allah asking the people this question is that the answer must be as He wills it, glorified is He. If someone says: how can He trust them with such an answer? Could they not have attributed it to other than Allah?

We say: this question is only posed by one who knows that it has a single answer. The one asked will find no answer except to say: the One who does that is Allah, glorified is He. They cannot say that the idol does that, because they know that they themselves made the idols, and the idols have no power to perform such an act.

So the answer is known in advance: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, alone is capable of that. This shows that falsehood is confused (lajlaj) and truth is clear (ablaj)(1), and truth has a leap and force (sawlah)(2). When you utter a word of truth on some matter, you find it has done its work in the one who is upon falsehood, and it takes him a long time until he finds words with which to refute what you said. Rather, he is struck with dazzlement and astonishment, and his argument is cut off(3).

For this reason Allah, glorified is He, did not say here as He had said before: ﴿They will say, "Allah."﴾ [Yunus 31].

Rather He said: ﴿Say, "Allah originates creation and then repeats it."﴾ [Yunus 34]. Allah, glorified is He, phrased it thus because when they were asked this question, the truth overwhelmed them, seized their tongues and their thoughts, so they were unable to say anything at all.

An example of this—and to Allah belongs the highest similitude—is that we see the public prosecutor squeezing the accused with many questions until he puts to him a question that dazzles the accused by its exceeding precision, and he has only one answer, which his nature refuses to give, so the accused answers, confessing.

Man, as Allah created him, is fit to believe and fit to disbelieve, so his will intervenes here. But his parts are believing, worshipping, glorifying. The tongue, which may utter disbelief, is in reality believing, glorifying, praising, thankful. But the human will, which Allah willed to be distinguished by choice, may choose disbelief—and we seek refuge with Allah—so the tongue utters disbelief.

The hand may obey the command of its owner and stretch out to steal, or the feet may walk—for example—to a place where wine is drunk. But are these acts willing with those deeds? No, they are not willing(4); they are only subject to the will of the doer.

When the question is asked: Who originates creation and then repeats it? The tongue, by its believing natural constitution, wants to speak; but it does not possess the will to speak. So Allah, glorified is He, makes clear to the Prophet (ﷺ) that he should answer on behalf of the believing parts, and He says, glorified is He: ﴿Say, "Allah originates creation and then repeats it."﴾ [Yunus 34]. By this He affirms the wording, and it suffices that Muhammad (ﷺ) say this statement as one conveying from his Lord, and this statement receives the honour of being from Him: ﴿Say, "Allah originates creation and then repeats it; so where are you deluded?"﴾ [Yunus 34].

Al-ifk (إفك) is deliberate lying, and it is fabrication (iftira'). There is a difference between unintentional lying and deliberate lying. Unintentional lying is one who transmits what reached him from another as he understood and believed it; it is a kind of lying that does not coincide with the truth, and its speaker retracts it if he comes to know the truth.

As for fabrication, it is deliberate lying, meaning that a person knows the reality and yet rejects it(5). For this reason the scholars paused here: some said there is truth and there is falsehood, but other scholars said: No, there is an intermediate position between truth and falsehood.

An example of this: a son enters upon his father, having heard from people that there is a fire in the house of so-and-so, and the son says to his father: there is a fire in the house of so-and-so. The father goes to inspect the matter. If he finds a fire, the son's statement is true; if there is no fire, the report is false, but the one who conveyed the report conveyed it as he heard it.

So there is a difference between the truth of a report and the truthfulness of the reporter: sometimes the report is true and the reporter is true; sometimes the report is true and the reporter is not true; and sometimes the reporter is true and the report is not true.

Here there are four positions. Those who said there is an intermediate position between truth and falsehood are those who said: truth requires correspondence between reality and the report, whereas falsehood is when the report does not correspond to reality.

Therefore we must distinguish between the truth of the report in itself and the truthfulness of the reporter, in that he says what he believes. As for the truth of the report, it is that it must be the reality.

The words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿so where are you deluded?﴾ mean: how are you turned away from the realities? For you know the reality and deny it with deliberate lying? We all know the words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ [al-Najm 53]. The overturned cities (al-mu'tafikah) are the towns that were overturned upon their people, meaning turned upside down; so the liar likewise overturns the reality.

1 Al-lajlajah: the mixing of voices. Abu Zayd said: it is said, "The truth is clear (alladd), and falsehood is confused (lajlaj)." Al-ablaj is that which is bright and straight. As for al-lajlaj, it is that which is mixed, crooked, and wavering, not stable. [Lisan al-'Arab: root l-j-j, adapted]
2 Al-sawlah: the leap, and the force to destroy falsehood.
3 This is what happened to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) with Nimrod, which Allah, mighty and majestic, related in His Book: ﴿Ibrahim said, "Indeed Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." And the one who disbelieved was overwhelmed﴾ [al-Baqarah 258]. Fa-buhit means he was taken by surprise by the argument and its logic, was bewildered in his answer, and found no rebuttal.
4 Evidence: they will come on the Day of Resurrection and become witnesses against the human being. Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿On the day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur 24].
5 Al-mu'tafikah: the town that was overturned with its people, i.e., turned over. Al-i'tifak: overturning. [Lisan al-'Arab: root a-f-k]. Ibn Kathir said regarding ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ [al-Najm 53]: it means the cities of the people of Lut, which Allah overturned upon them, making their upper part their lower part. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/259, adapted]

6 This is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended in his saying: "Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie and seek out lying until he is written with Allah as a liar." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2607) and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6094).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 35:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say: "Is there any of your associates who guides to the truth?" Say: "God guides to the truth. Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who cannot find guidance unless he is guided? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?"﴾

This is a command to the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, to put to them a new question, to which there is no answer except what reality imposes. And reality confirms that guidance belongs only to the Truth, because every created being exists for a purpose, and nothing is created in vain(1).

With our limited power we manufacture the microphone, the television, the refrigerator, the bed and others. Each of them has a purpose, and each has its own rules of maintenance. The one who determines the purpose of this factory or that is its maker, and he sets down the rules for its maintenance so that it may fulfil its purpose. The purpose of anything exists before the thing itself, so that the thing may come into being in accordance with its purpose.

The affliction of the world today is that they know that Allah, glory be to Him, created man, yet they devise from themselves laws to maintain man and to regulate man's movement. This is stupidity and heedlessness on the part of those who do it. They should have left the matter of maintaining man to the laws laid down by the Creator of man, glory be to Him.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has determined the purpose of creating man and has determined the rules for his maintenance. The evil that exists now is due to ignorance of man's purpose and to deviation from the path man must follow. So the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Say: "Is there any of your associates who guides to the truth..."﴾ (35). That is: is there among these associates anyone who guides man to his purpose? Did the sun, for example, declare its purpose? Did the angels declare their purpose? Did the trees, the stones, or the messengers you worshipped say anything other than what Allah, exalted be He, wills? They are gods who do not know the purpose of the one who worships them, nor do they know the path that leads to that purpose.

Therefore comes the decisive word: ﴿Say: "God guides to the truth..."﴾ (35). So God has guided you, O man, to the truth in every movement you make, by the method that Allah, glory be to Him, sent down complete upon His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, from the beginning of "There is no god but Allah" to removing harm from the road(2). It is a method that encompasses and fully covers all of man's movements.

The answer came from Allah, exalted be He, on the tongue of His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, because they were stunned by the question and became confused, and none of them had any ability to contradict it. The purpose of the creation of man and of others is summed up in the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat] (56). Worship is not only the pillars of Islam; rather it is the building up of the universe as a living structure for Islam. The one who determined the purpose is the Creator, glory be to Him, and He is the one who determines the way to reach it.

When we wish to reach a place in the desert, for example, we first determine the place and choose the route of arrival. If the straight route is full of obstacles and mountains, you will be forced to deviate from that route in order to reach your goal. Thus this crooked route is the straight route, because it is the route that keeps us away from obstacles.

An example of this: the torrents that descend upon the highlands of Abyssinia chose for themselves the easy channel, which became the Nile. No one dug the Nile as we dug the canals or the Suez Canal. Rather the torrent descended and chose for itself the easy path, and it flowed along it, winding between the bends, sands and rocks.

Therefore you find that everything in which humanity has no part may wind its way in order to pass through, whereas what man has made cannot do that.

Every creation must have a purpose. Therefore we find our master Abraham, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, saying: ﴿Who created me, and He guides me﴾ [al-Shu'ara] (78). So the one who creates is the one who determines the purpose, because this purpose exists with Him first, before He creates. The precision of the Qur'an's words on the tongue of our master Abraham, peace be upon him, is evident: he did not say "Who created me guides me," but said ﴿Who created me, and He guides me﴾, which indicates that this matter will be opposed, and that after man is created some people will, to protect their own interests, set up other paths that contradict the purpose, and so lead to misguidance.

As for the Truth, glory be to Him, He has sent down the Qur'an in which is the true guidance. The one who created is the one who legislates. Therefore the Qur'an mentions on the tongue of our master Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿And who feeds me and gives me drink﴾ (79) [al-Shu'ara]. By this saying, Abraham, peace be upon him, reached the conclusion that the One who provided fathers with the ability to derive sustenance, as food and drink, is Allah, glory be to Him.

The Qur'an also mentions on the tongue of our master Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿And who causes me to die, then gives me life﴾ (81) [al-Shu'ara]. Causing death and giving life belong to the Truth, glory be to Him, so no one asks who possesses the power to cause death and give life. As for the cure of illness, he said: ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ (80) [al-Shu'ara](3). You may go to the doctor and think that he is the one who cures you; rather he treats, but it is Allah who cures.

Thus we know that the saying of our master Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿Who created me, and He guides me﴾ (78) [al-Shu'ara] puts guidance first, then creation, then the clarification of the path that leads to that purpose. If any of that is opposed, then the world will never be set right.

And in the Qur'an, on the tongue of our master Moses, peace be upon him, you find: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it﴾ (50) [Ta-Ha]. Since the Truth, glory be to Him, has created, He guides to the way that leads to the purpose. The Qur'an also says: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (1), who created and proportioned (2), and who determined and guided (3)﴾ [al-A'la] (4). Thus it becomes certain for us that, since there is a purpose, there must be a path to which the One who created us guides us.

And here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿God guides to the truth...﴾ (35). Because He, glory be to Him, is the Creator, it is logical that after this there comes the question: ﴿Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who cannot find guidance unless he is guided...?﴾ (35).

The reason for the presence of the lam in His saying ﴿guides to the truth (li-l-haqq)﴾ is the consideration of the purpose, and the reason for the presence of ﴿to the truth (ila l-haqq)﴾ is to draw attention to the fact that reaching the purpose requires a path. So the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to combine both expressions in a single verse.

We know that this verse was revealed concerning those who took associates with God. They acknowledge God, but they associate others with Him. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is singular in divinity through His lordship over creation, because He created from nothing, provided sustenance from nothing, created for us the means of knowledge, arranged our affairs, brought the living out of the dead, brought the dead out of the living, and guided to the truth.

So where, then, are these associates whom you have taken alongside God? Has any one of them, or all of them together, made any one of those things(5)?

Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Is there any of your associates who guides to the truth...﴾ (35) [Yunus].
