So then: the one who guides is the one who created, and those who associated others with God have acknowledged God as Creator by their own testimony, when the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "God..."﴾ (87) [al-Zukhruf].

So then: those who associated others have committed a great sin. These associates are either angels, or prophets and messengers by whom some people were tested. And there are those who took other intermediaries, such as the sun, the moon and the stars; these are heavenly things. Some people took lowly intermediaries, such as trees and stones. So is any of these things a guide to the truth? And what is the method of any of them, then? And how did they convey it to you?

All these people know that none of them is able to guide; rather each is guided by Allah, glory be to Him and exalted. So from where did you say that the angels would guide you? Or from where did those who were tempted by their messenger, and took him as a god, come? And from where did this messenger bring his method?

Every being is not guided unless it is first guided by Allah. Even if the things taken as associates have no guidance, no method, no intellect and no thought, like the sun, moon and stars among the heavenly things, and the trees and stones among the lowly things, what did these things say? They said nothing.

Thus the taking of associates with God does not stand upright, even the angels, for God is the One who chooses from among them the angel who conveys from Allah, glory be to Him; and likewise the messengers, peace be upon them: ﴿Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who cannot find guidance unless he is guided...?﴾ (35) [Yunus].

﴿Cannot find guidance﴾ is read in this way, and in the language there is a process of easing the sound for ease of pronunciation and the soundness of the Arabic language. We know that ﴿yahdi﴾ means "yahtadi" (he is guided). Its original form is yahtadi, in which there is a silent ha', a ta', a dal and a ya'. There is a closeness of articulation points among these letters, and this closeness makes the meaning hazy and the pronunciation heavy, so the language performs a process of substitution and assimilation and frees itself from the meeting of two unvocalised letters, so that it reaches our ears as God revealed it, for the soundness of pronunciation and the beauty of meaning. For the Qur'an refined the language with the speech of heaven, so that its wording and meaning would endure. So if you are on a path of guidance, then the origin of guidance is God, exalted be He.

The Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ (35) [Yunus].

That is: what has befallen your minds that you pass this judgment, so that you associate with God what has no method, or has a method but it is connected to God, which came to convey it to them?

When you hear ﴿kayfa﴾ ("how"), it is used to inquire about a strange action which, in the understanding of a reasonable person, should not have happened. Like saying: "How did you hit your father?" or "How did you insult your mother?" All of these are things that the natural disposition rejects and that nature and religion reject.

His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ is as if it were a strange matter that should not have occurred, because the Truth, glory be to Him, alone is the God, and the Truth is that which is fixed and unchanging in purpose and in path. God, glory be to Him alone, is the One who determined for us the purpose and the path that leads to it, and He, glory be to Him, is the One who said: ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace...﴾ (25) [Yunus]. The method is the path that leads to the Abode of Peace away from the affliction of change(6), because the whole world is change. You may be strong and then grow weak, or healthy and then be struck by illness, or rich and then become poor, or sighted and then lose your sight, or sound of hearing and then become deaf afterwards(7).

So: this is a world of change. Suppose a person took from his world all his share: health, security, safety, wealth and everything. We would still find him in anxiety from two directions. The first is that he fears that all this blessing will leave him, or he fears that he himself will leave this blessing. This is what we see in our lives.

So: the world with all its changes has no security. We should understand that all the gifts of the created are only a bestowal from the Creator, glory be to Him and exalted, because if they were from your own self, you would be able to preserve them. But they are gifts from the Most High, glory be to Him. A thing that was given may become taken away.

(1) Allah, exalted be He, says in Surat al-Mu'minun: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ (115) [al-Mu'minun]. And He, glory be to Him, said in al-Dhariyat: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ (56) [al-Dhariyat]. So the Truth has a purpose and wisdom, and it is worship in its absolute sense, that is, obedience.

(2) On the authority of Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Faith has seventy-some or sixty-some branches. The best of them is the saying 'There is no god but Allah,' and the lowest of them is removing harm from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (9) and Muslim in his Sahih (35).

(3) On the authority of Abu Ramtha, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I set out with my father toward the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He had thick hair, with traces of henna, and wore two green garments. My father said to him: "Show me this that is on your back, for I am a physician man." He said: "Allah is the Physician. Rather, you are a gentle man. Its physician is the One who created it."

(4) ﴿Who created and proportioned﴾ (2) [al-A'la]: that is, He created the human being and proportioned every creature in the best forms. And His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And who determined and guided﴾ (3) [al-A'la]. Mujahid said: He guided man to misery and happiness, and guided livestock to their pasture. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/500].

(5) And He, glory be to Him, says in Surat al-Rum: ﴿Allah is He who created you, then provided for you, then causes you to die, then gives you life. Is there any of your associates who does any of that? Glory be to Him, exalted above what they associate (40)﴾ [al-Rum].

(6) That is: the conditions of the world change and transform, and do not remain in one state.

(7) Because the world is a world of change, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, advised a man admonishing him: "Seize five before five: your youth before your old age, your health before your sickness, your wealth before your poverty, your leisure before your preoccupation, and your life before your death." Related by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (4/306), who declared it sound according to the condition of Shaykh [Muslim], from Ibn Abbas, and al-Dhahabi affirmed it.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ (36)

The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture...﴾ (36) indicates that some of them were following certainty, because the opposite of conjecture (ẓann) is certainty (yaqīn). The relations (nisab) that occur between things connect the subject (mawḍū') and the predicate (maḥmūl), or the judged (maḥkūm) and the judged-upon (maḥkūm 'alayhi). These are relations we have mentioned before, and we mention them again: there is something you affirm with conviction, and something you do not affirm with conviction. What you affirm with conviction and can demonstrate is knowledge of certainty (ʿilm yaqīn). What you cannot demonstrate is not knowledge of certainty, but rather imitation (taqlīd), as when a child says: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ (al-Ikhlas) — this is true, but the child cannot demonstrate it, and what is said by one who affirms it with conviction while it is not an established fact is ignorance (jahl).

Knowledge ('ilm) is a proposition affirmed with conviction, which is established and supported by evidence, in contrast to ignorance (jahl), which is a proposition affirmed with conviction without any evidence for it.

Conjecture (ẓann) is the equality of two relations in affirmation and negation, such that you cannot affirm either of them with conviction; for if one side prevails, it becomes a weaker proposition, and a weaker proposition is doubt (shakk), conjecture, or delusion (wahm). Thus conjecture is the preponderance of one relation over the other. Doubt (shakk) is the equality of the two sides.

The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture...﴾ (36) shows us that those who opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did so either out of obstinacy (ʿinād) despite their knowledge of the truth of what he conveyed, or they were obstinate without knowledge, confirming the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge...﴾ (39) [Yunus]. Each of them, when he reflected upon the message from Allah, the Exalted, and the proofs for it, would declare faith; but among them were those who reflected on the proofs and remained in their obstinacy. Those who followed conjecture only followed what avails nothing against the truth.

Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear to them that He is Knowing of the hidden depths of their souls, and He knows that all their denial of faith stems from obstinacy or from inability to grasp the matter of faith. Hence the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do...﴾ (36) [Yunus]. So: Allah, glory be to Him, has known from eternity that some of them, in the depths of their souls, were certain of the value of faith, yet they denied it, confirming the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿We already know that what they say saddens you. But it is not you they deny; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah﴾ (33) [al-An'am]. So: the Truth, glory be to Him, is Knowing, and nothing is hidden from Him: they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge, some of them did not grasp the value of faith, and whoever among them knew its value denied it out of obstinacy and arrogance.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance...﴾ (14) [al-Naml].

(1) Conjecture, just as it is doubt, is also a kind of certainty, but not certainty of direct observation; it is certainty of reflection. Certainty of direct observation is called only knowledge ('ilm). It is used as both a noun and a verbal noun, and its plural is ẓunūn. The Exalted said: ﴿And you assume about Allah assumptions﴾ (10) [al-Ahzab]. [Lisan al-'Arab, root ẓ-n-n.]

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And this Qur'an could not have been fabricated apart from Allah; but it is a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the Book, there being no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds.(37)﴾:

When you listen to the Qur'an and to what it contains of the secret of numbers and of reports of the unseen, which are not subject to the logic of time or the logic of place, sound human nature yearns to affirm that this Qur'an cannot be fabricated, and that its speaker and its sender must be All-Knowing, All-Aware. This is because the Qur'an came confirming what was before it of earlier books.

That is: what is present with it is always before the people, or confronts them. It is a Book that confirms the earlier books before their distortion, such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms(1), which preceded the Qur'an in revelation, not in reality, so the Qur'an came confirming them.

That is: they confirm it, and it confirms them, before their distortion. These are the books that gave good tidings of Muhammad (ﷺ) as a Messenger, just as the Qur'an mentions concerning the confirmation by Jesus (peace be upon him) of the coming of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him): ﴿And a messenger giving good tidings of one who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad..(6)﴾ [al-Saff]. So when Ahmad (Muhammad (ﷺ)) came and the Qur'an was revealed to him, it confirmed the Gospel in this statement of his. And what the Qur'an contains of authentic creeds, which are creeds that all the heavenly Books brought, is likewise confirmed. The Almighty says: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms.(163)﴾ [al-Nisa']. And the Almighty says: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: to establish the religion and not be divided therein..(13)﴾ [al-Shura]. So there are principles that all the heavenly Books brought, and there are also reports that the heavenly Books related the occurrence of, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conveyed to us the Qur'an containing those reports. So from where did Muhammad (ﷺ) obtain those correct creeds and those reports found in the earlier books, when he (ﷺ) was not among the People of the Book and had learned nothing from them?(2)

Therefore, when Muhammad (ﷺ) says what was mentioned in the books preceding the Qur'an, those books confirm what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, because these reports have come to pass, and this is confirmation of his truthfulness. For by the testimony of the people of his time, he did not sit with a teacher, nor did he read a book; his history and biography are well known, for he is "from among yourselves", and it is not known of him that he ever practised eloquent speech, or delivered a sermon to a people before the Prophethood, or recited poetry.

Then, after that, he was surprised, just as you were surprised, by the coming of this wondrous exposition. From where did it come?

You say that he himself brought it, but he (ﷺ) attributes the elevation to its Owner and declares that he (ﷺ) is only a conveyer, so he says what Allah commanded him to say: ﴿Say: "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. Indeed, I dwelt among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?"(16)﴾ [Yunus].

The noble Qur'an urges the Prophet (ﷺ) to ask them: did you notice in his words, before this, any eloquence, rhetoric, or poetry?!

Let us consider the "mā kuntu" (3) verses of the Qur'an, which are the verses in which the Almighty says ﴿wa-mā kunta (and you were not)﴾, such as His saying: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you; and you were not with them when they cast their pens (4) to determine which of them would be the guardian of Mary..(44)﴾ [Al 'Imran]. This is a fact established in the reports. And the Almighty says: ﴿And you were not at the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses.(44)﴾ [al-Qasas]. The revelation to Moses (peace be upon him), and the place where that revelation descended, is a fact established in the reports.

And the Almighty says: ﴿But We produced generations, and the age grew long for them. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but it is We who were sending (the messengers).(45)﴾ [al-Qasas]. Many of these verses make Muhammad (ﷺ) as though he were asking his contemporaries: how did I report events and reports at whose time or place I was not present?

It must then be that Allah, the True, the Almighty, is the One who informed me of what agrees with what you have of reports.

Then the noble Qur'an came confirming what was before it: ﴿For he has brought it down upon your heart by permission of Allah, confirming what was before it..(97)﴾ [al-Baqara]. That is: it is the Book which contains the truth of every event to come, for the Qur'an broke through the veils and barriers of the past and the future.

We know that unseen matters occur through two causes. The first: that one speaks of something that preceded the time in which he was sent down, so he speaks of a past which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), not being one of those who had the means of observation and learning, could not have known or been taught.

Likewise, the noble Qur'an broke through the veil of the present that was contemporary with its revelation, a present that may be veiled by place.

Let me give this example—and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: an event may occur in Alexandria at the same time as you are present in Cairo, and you do not know of this event because it is hidden from you by distance of place. The barrier of place is typically represented in present matters, whereas future matters are veiled from us by both time and place together.

When the Qur'an informs us of a past event which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not witness, did not learn, and did not read about, then the Qur'an is breaking open, before us, the veil of past time. And when the Qur'an informs of a present event in a place we do not visit, upon our Master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this is a breaking of the veil of place, such as the saying of the Almighty: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"..(8)﴾ [al-Mujadila]. When the hypocrites and disbelievers heard this noble statement, they did not deny that they had said to themselves what the Qur'an brought, and thus the Qur'an broke through the barrier of place within themselves.

Therefore, the reports of the unseen in the Qur'an are either a breaking through of past time, or a breaking through of the time of the present, or a breaking through of the time and place of the future.

We know that the Qur'an was being revealed while the Muslims were weak, unable to protect themselves, and no one could grant protection to another. The Prophet (ﷺ) set out for Ta'if to present Islam to its people, perhaps seeking from the people of Ta'if a protector for them; but he (ﷺ) found only harm and aversion (6), and he advised some of his Companions to emigrate to Abyssinia (7). In the midst of all these crises, the Qur'an's words descended: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs..(45)﴾ [al-Qamar]. So much so that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) wondered: which multitude is this that will be routed, when we are unable to protect ourselves? Then the Battle of Badr came, and 'Umar witnessed the defeat and flight of the fighters of Quraysh; thus he saw with his own eyes the truth of what the revelation had brought earlier (8).

Thus everyone was assured that the noble Qur'an is not fabricated, so how could the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) be accused of having fabricated it?

And if this Qur'an were fabricated, why would you not fabricate something like it? Among you are poets, eloquent speakers and orators! Muhammad (ﷺ) never claimed to be eloquent, an orator or a poet, and the noble Qur'an did not ask them to bring someone like Muhammad (ﷺ), who has no connection with eloquence or rhetoric; rather, it asks them to bring all the eloquent people together, and challenges them to produce even one verse like the Qur'an.

And if they say: what he brought is sorcery, and Muhammad is a sorcerer who has bewitched the slaves and the weak and brought them into Islam, then why has Muhammad not bewitched you?

Your remaining without being bewitched indicates that your application of the word "sorcery" to what he brought is a false claim.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book, there being no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds..(37)﴾ [Yunus]. The Qur'an contains the detailed explanation of all the rulings suitable until the Hour arrives, whereas the books preceding the Qur'an contained the rulings suited to their time and to the places of their revelation.

It is a Book ﴿in which there is no doubt (la yarība fīhi)﴾, that is: there is no uncertainty in it. It exposes the disbelievers and lays bare their doubt and their lying, for they have acknowledged the greatness of the Qur'an and said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two cities?(31)﴾ [al-Zukhruf]. Thus they knew that there is no defect in the Qur'an and no doubt, even among those who disbelieve in it. The response to their claim of fabrication comes in the Almighty's saying:

﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."(38)﴾:

1 Al-Zabur (the Psalms): the book of David (peace be upon him). Its origin is: every book that is zabūr, i.e. written. The Almighty says: ﴿And We have favoured some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms..(55)﴾ [al-Isra'].
2 On this the Almighty says: ﴿And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you write it with your right hand; for then the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt.(48)﴾ [al-'Ankabut].
3 The "mā kuntu" verses of the Qur'an are the verses in which the phrase ﴿mā kunta﴾ occurs, in eleven verses: [Al 'Imran: 44], [Hud: 49], [Yusuf: 103], [al-Qasas: 44, 45, 46, 86], [al-'Ankabut: 48], [al-Shura: 58].
4 Al-aqlām here means the arrows (al-qidāh), which were marked with signs by which they would know who would be the guardian of Mary, by way of lottery. The arrow was called qalam (pen) because it is pared (yuqallam), i.e. trimmed. [Lisan al-'Arab, root q-l-m].
5 Thāwiyan: dwelling; Madyan: the town of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him).
6 This was after the death of his uncle Abu Talib, who had been defending him and protecting him from the harm of the polytheists. But the people of Ta'if lined up in two rows on his path, and whenever he lifted or set down his feet they struck them with stones until they drew blood from his feet. [Dala'il al-Nubuwwa of al-Bayhaqi, 2/415]. At that he (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, I complain to You of the weakness of my strength and the scarcity of my resources." Allah granted him the Night Journey beyond human reason, and the Ascension beyond even that; this was for His protection of him and His care for his religion.
7 On the authority of Umm Salama, who said: "When Mecca became too narrow for us, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were harmed, tested, and saw the affliction and trial in their religion that befell them, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could not repel that from them—while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was under protection from his people and his uncle, so that nothing he disliked which reached his Companions could reach him—the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: 'In the land of Abyssinia there is a king under whom no one is wronged; so join his land until Allah grants you relief and a way out of what you are in.'" A lengthy hadith related by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (2/301), and Ibn Hisham cited it in his Sira in similar wording (1/321).
8 On the authority of 'Ikrima, who said: When "The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs" (al-Qamar 45) was revealed, 'Umar said: "Which multitude will be routed?" That is: which multitude will be overcome? 'Umar said: "When the day of Badr came, I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) leaping in his armour while saying: 'The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs' (al-Qamar 45), and I understood its interpretation on that day." Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (4/266), attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 38:

The challenge (tahaddi) that came before has already explained the reasons for their inability to succeed in meeting it, because the preceding verse establishes that the earlier heavenly scriptures confirm the revelation of the Noble Qur'an, and between it and the Qur'an there is mutual confirmation.

So they are defeated in it before it was ever revealed.

The Truthful, Glorified One says: ﴿Say: Then bring a surah like it...﴾ (10:38). The challenge also came once with the Book, in His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants.﴾ (17:88). They were unable to do so, so the level of the challenge was lowered, and He challenged them to bring: ﴿ten surahs like it, fabricated...﴾ (11:13). When they could not bring ten surahs, He challenged them to bring a surah that would come close, even from afar, to the style of the Qur'an, and they could not do that either: ﴿So bring a surah like it...﴾ (2:23). How, then, after all of that, do they claim that Muhammad (ﷺ) fabricated the Qur'an, when he (ﷺ) had no connection with rhetorical styles or eloquence?!

He has called you to bring all the eloquent and skilled speakers to fabricate, even a single surah like it, and He made a condition, saying: ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides Allah...﴾ (10:38). This is because Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, is the only one capable of sending down a Qur'an. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told them to call upon the partners, so that the disbelievers, and some of them people of stubborn contention (lajaja) (1), would not say: "We will call upon Allah." For this reason the Qur'an brings the exception: ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.﴾ (10:38). By their very nature they are not truthful in this challenge.

When Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, sends a messenger to a people to teach them His method for the movement of life, He wants the movement of life to achieve the goal required of man as God's vicegerent on earth. Therefore the messenger comes from the same kind as those he is sent to, so that he may be an example for them, because if the messenger came as an angel, the example would not be valid; rather he must be a human being (2).

The Truthful One does not send any messenger except with him a clear proof (bayyinah) and evidence of truthfulness that he is a messenger conveying from Allah, Exalted is He.

The clear proof must be of the same kind as the eloquence (nubugh) (3) of the people, so no miracle comes to them in a matter they have not known or become accustomed to, lest they say: "Had we been taught this, we would have brought the like of what came."

The Qur'an came to establish their inability in that in which they excelled, namely the craft of speech: poetry, prose, and oratory.

The Qur'an was the miracle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among an eloquent people who would set up markets for poetry, and who would hang the winning poem of these on the walls of the Ka'bah as a sign of its fame and testimony to it.

So they were people of expertise in the craft of speech, and the miracle came with the Messenger (ﷺ) from the same kind of thing in which they excelled, in order to challenge them. A challenge calls for gathering the full strength of the opponent so that he may answer this challenger; if he is unable despite the challenge, the inability becomes binding.

The Truthful One challenged all the Arabs with the entire Qur'an: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants (4).﴾ (17:88). They could not produce its like, so the Qur'an descended to them gradually in the challenge, asking of them something less than that, which is to bring ten surahs like it, in His saying: ﴿Say: Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated...﴾ (11:13). Then He challenged them to bring something like a single surah of the Qur'an. On reflection we find that the expression asking for a surah came in two forms: once He says ﴿a surah like it﴾ (10:38), and once He says ﴿a surah from its like﴾ (2:23). Each of the two forms is eloquent in its place. In ﴿a surah like it﴾ (10:38) it shows that the likeness here is absolute, i.e., like what came of the surahs of the Qur'an. His saying ﴿a surah from its like﴾ (2:23) means: a surah from the likeness of Muhammad (ﷺ), in that he did not sit with a teacher, did not read, and it was not known of him that he spoke with eloquence at any stage of his life before the mission (5).

The Truthful, Glorified One said: ﴿Say: Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. Indeed I dwelt among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?﴾ (10:16). So: ﴿a surah from its like﴾ (2:23) means: like Muhammad (ﷺ), who had not been taught and was unlettered. But why does this kind of challenge come? Because they said the Qur'an is ﴿tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, so they are dictated to him morning and evening﴾ (25:5). Indeed, in the height of their heedlessness they accused him of learning from a man who was in Makkah, so the Qur'an draws their attention to the fact that the man, whom they claimed was the teacher of the Messenger (ﷺ), was a non-Arab foreigner: ﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ (16:103). The Truthful One further distinguishes them...

1 Lajaja: persisting excessively in dispute and contention.
2 For this reason the Lord of Might said: ﴿Say: Had there been angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ (17:95). So the messenger is of the kind of those to whom he is sent. ﴿And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered for them what they cover.﴾ (6:9).
3 Nubugh: excellence and mastery in a particular science or art. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit]
4 Zahir: helper and supporter. Allah said: ﴿So do not be a supporter of the disbelievers.﴾ (28:86). Some scholars held that the challenge was addressed to mankind only, not the jinn, because the jinn are not among the people of the Arabic language; Allah mentioned them in the verse to magnify the inimitability of the Qur'an, since their joint inability to bring its like is evidence that a single group of them is even less able. [See al-Burhan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an by al-Zarkashi, 2/111]
5 In the interpretation of this verse there is a third opinion, mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (1/277), who said: "﴿from its like﴾ (2:23), i.e., from the like of the Torah and the Gospel. The meaning is: bring a surah from a book like it, for it confirms what is in it." Each of these opinions is correct and admissible.
6 Asatir: plural of uswurah, i.e., what the ancients wrote down. Asatir also means falsehoods, baseless tales the ancients inscribed and composed. [Lisan al-Arab, root s-t-r]
7 Iktatabaha: he asked scribes to copy it for him.
8 Yulhidun ilayhi: they incline towards it. The exegetes differed on naming this man whom the polytheists claimed Muhammad (ﷺ) learned from, but the important thing is not searching for his name; rather it is that he was a foreigner, so how could he teach Muhammad (ﷺ) this Arabic Qur'an?

Then he says after that:

﴿Nay, they denied that of which they did not grasp the knowledge, and its interpretation (ta'wil) had not yet come to them. Thus did those before them deny; so see how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ (10:39)

This kind of people, those who ﴿denied that of which they did not grasp the knowledge..﴾ (10:39), are those who were seized by surprise when they heard something they did not know. People are enemies of what they do not know. So they denied what Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought of the Qur'an before they had discerned the beauty of its expression and the order of its lofty values. When an opportunity presents itself for them to discern the beauty of its expression and the precision of its inimitability, they turn towards faith.

An example of this is ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). He was a disbeliever, then he learned that his sister and her husband had embraced Islam. So he went to her house and struck her, and her blood flowed. The flow of blood from a sister by the blow of her brother stirs the emotion of tenderness, and this is what happened with ʿUmar. The wave of his obstinacy subsided, so he received the Qur'an with a spirit free of obstinacy. He then went and believed in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (1). Before that he was among those who ﴿denied that of which they did not grasp the knowledge, and its interpretation had not yet come to them..﴾ (10:39), meaning they did not know its aims. As soon as they heard of his (ﷺ) message suddenly, they accused him of lying, and Allah forbid.

Therefore read the word of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until when they go out from your presence they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he say just now?" (2)..﴾ (47:16). This shows that they did not understand what was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of the Qur'an. The answer comes from Allah, glorified and exalted: ﴿Say, "It is for those who believe a guidance and healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness (3), and it is upon them blindness..﴾ (41:44). So the Qur'an is guidance for those whose hearts open to faith. As for hearts filled with hatred for its speaker and for Islam, such people cannot have a sound judgment.

If any of them wants a sound judgment, let him expel from his heart what contradicts what he hears, then he should receive both matters; and surely his heart will be entered by the stronger proof, which is Islam.

So: whoever his heart is filled with a false creed cannot be guided. ﴿Nay, they denied that of which they did not grasp the knowledge, and its interpretation had not yet come to them..﴾ (10:39). Ta'wil (4) is that to which a thing returns. This shows us that there are matters in the Qur'an whose explanation has not yet come; events will explain them. The Noble Qur'an may state a matter of the unseen, then time comes to confirm that matter; here we know that its ta'wil has come.

These people denied before the ta'wil came to them, and the non-arrival of the ta'wil was the reason for the delay in the clarification of the truth on the matter, because its time had not yet come.

As an example: here is ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when the battle broke out between Muʿawiya ibn Abi Sufyan and Imam ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), and ʿAmmar fought in ʿAli's ranks and was killed. Here the Companions became aware of the ta'wil of a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) where he said: "Woe to ʿAmmar! The rebellious group will kill him" (5).

Thus the ta'wil of the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to pass when it was realized in reality, and this was the reason for some Companions turning away from the army of Muʿawiya.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿and its interpretation had not yet come to them..﴾ (10:39): meaning the ta'wil had not yet appeared to them.

Among the particles of negation is "lam" as in our saying "lam yajii fulan" (Fulan did not come), and we also say "lamma yajii fulan" (Fulan has not yet come). The negation with the first is a definite negation not connected to the present, as if he did not come yesterday.

As for negation with "lamma", it means that the coming is negated up to the moment of speech, that is, the present, and it may come after that; because "lamma" conveys negation and conveys expectation of affirmation.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'..﴾ (49:14). These Bedouins said ﴿We have believed﴾ although they had seen the Muslims and imitated them falsely and hypocritically (6), and faith had not yet entered their hearts. When they heard the Truth's word, glorified is He: ﴿and faith has not yet entered your hearts..﴾ (49:14), they said: "Praise be to Allah," because that meant faith would enter their hearts.

Likewise the word of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿Or do you think you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who fought and known the patient? (3:142). When they heard that, they said: "Then we are assured that Allah's knowledge of us as strivers and patient ones will come." Thus we know that ﴿lamma﴾ means that what is negated by it is expected to occur. And ta'wil, as we know, is the return of a thing.

The Qur'an contains many reports that were not expected at the time they were mentioned, or thought likely to occur. When they occurred, with no human agency in their occurrence, this means the speaker of these words took them from One who is able to bring them into being, as in the report of the victory of the Romans over the Persians despite the Romans' defeat.

The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿The Romans have been defeated (2) in the nearest land; but they, after their defeat, will overcome (3) within a few years. To Allah belongs the command before and after; and that day the believers will rejoice (4) in the victory of Allah..﴾ (30:2-5). This report came and the Muslims awaited its ta'wil, and its ta'wil came according to what the Qur'an had reported. Or the ta'wil will come in the Hereafter, and what the matter of denial returns to they will know after that.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for a people who believe (52). Do they await but its ta'wil..﴾ (7:52-53). They are waiting for what the Qur'an returns to and what they return to: if in this world, then the victory of the people of the Qur'an; and if in the Hereafter, then the word of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿The Day its ta'wil comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had come with the truth. Do we have any intercessors to intercede for us, or could we be returned so we might do other than what we used to do?"..﴾ (7:53). This is the ta'wil that some denied before.

So: the ta'wil is either for whoever of the disbelievers remains, who sees what the Qur'an reported coming according to what a Prophet reported, who cannot control the destinies of things, yet it comes in accordance with what he said.

So it is as if Muhammad (ﷺ) were gambling by saying words that might not come true, whereupon those who believed in him would turn away. But he (ﷺ) said only what he was confident and certain would occur, because the report of it came from the Presence of the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.

And the other possibility is that the ta'wil also comes in the Hereafter.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿Nay, they denied that of which they did not grasp the knowledge, and its interpretation had not yet come to them..﴾ (10:39). The Truth, glorified is He, draws the attention of His Messenger (ﷺ) to the fact that what happened to him had happened to messengers before him, so He said in the same verse: ﴿Thus did those before them deny; so see how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ (10:39). Meaning: look at the procession of all the messengers from the beginning of the sending of messengers: did Allah send a messenger and grant the disbelievers against him victory over him? No. Victory has always been for the messengers of the Truth, Mighty and Majestic, in confirmation of His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Allah has decreed, "I will surely overcome, I and My messengers.."﴾ (58:21). We know what befell the wrongdoers: some of them Allah drowned, some of them the earth swallowed, and some of them He seized with the Cry (8).

So the ta'wil is clear in every procession of messengers that preceded the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). And if every people of wrongdoers received what fits the message of their messenger, then the wrongdoing disbelievers in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) will receive what fits the universality of his message (ﷺ).

When the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿So see how was the end of the wrongdoers..﴾ (10:39), we must know the meaning of wrongdoing: it is placing the truth in other than its rightful place, and rights differ in their station: there is a higher right, a middle right, and a lower right.

If you come to the lower right, by attributing divinity to other than Allah, glorified is He, this is the pinnacle of wrongdoing, and the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is great wrongdoing (9)..﴾ (31:13). Because in this there is a transfer of divinity from Allah, glorified is He, to another. Would that the other were a claimant with a call between him and Allah, but no: that one to whom divinity is transferred is not a claimant at all; rather the wrongdoer volunteers this of himself, taking partners with Allah besides Him, and in this is volunteering wrongdoing without any claimant.

Suppose Allah, the Exalted, said: "There is no god but Me." Then either the matter is true, or it is not. If someone supposes—God forbid—that it is not true, then the second god should have declared himself, and not left another to listen for him and announce him; otherwise he would be a deaf, heedless god. But no one has announced divinity other than Allah, glorified is He; therefore the unity of divinity is established for the true God, glorified and exalted. Allah has declared to us: "There is no god but Me; I am the Creator, I am the Provider." No one else has ever claimed those works; thus the claim is confirmed that there is no god but Allah.

The next degree of wrongdoing is wrongdoing in judgments. If someone judges that usury is permissible, this is wrongdoing in a major matter; but if a judge rules that a debtor must return only the debt, this is justice. Likewise the judge who wrongs in his rulings is transferring people's rights to others. Thus wrongdoing has degrees according to the thing in which the wrong occurs.

(1) The account of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab's conversion is mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (1/343-346).
(2) Ānifan: just now, previously. This verse was revealed about the hypocrites who used to listen to the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when they left his presence they asked the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mockingly, and to make known that they had paid no heed to what he said: ﴿What did he say just now?..﴾ (47:16), meaning: what did he say a moment ago and before? [Lisan al-ʿArab, root ʾ-n-f, adapted].
(3) al-Waqr: weakness of hearing. It is said: deafness. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root w-q-r].
(4) Ta'wil, meaning and tafsir are one. Its origin is what a thing returns to. The Exalted says: ﴿Do they await but its ta'wil, the day its ta'wil comes..﴾ (7:53), meaning: they await the realization and occurrence of the punishment.
(5) Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (447) and Muslim in his Sahih (2915) in similar wording, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. Its completion is that at the building of the Prophet's Mosque, Abu Sa'id said: "We were carrying one brick at a time, while ʿAmmar carried two bricks at a time. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, shook the dust off him, and said: 'Woe to ʿAmmar! The rebellious group will kill him; he calls them to Paradise and they call him to the Fire.'"
(6) Al-Bukhari went to the view that these Bedouins were hypocrites, but some scholars took exception to this, saying they were Muslims, but when they first entered the religion of Islam they claimed for themselves the station of faith, while faith had not yet taken root in their hearts. See Ibn Kathir's tafsir (4/218-219).
(7) Al-Bid': what is fewer than ten. The nearest land: between Adhri'at and Busra in Syria, the nearest of the lands of Syria to the Arabian Peninsula. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/422-424].
(8) Allah said: ﴿Then of them We sent a storm of stones upon, and of them was he who was seized by the Cry, and of them We caused the earth to swallow, and of them We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (29:40). Al-Hasib is a violently cold, strongly blowing wind that carries pebbles of the earth and throws them on people and uproots them from the ground; with it Allah punished the people of ʿAd. The Cry punished the people of Thamud; Qarun was punished by the earth swallowing him; Pharaoh and his soldiers were punished by drowning.
(9) Grandeur for a deviant value is debasement, and for a sound value is elevation.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 40:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord knows best the corrupters.﴾ (40)

The discussion here concerns those who denied, so how does Allah divide the deniers, who by their denial do not believe, into two groups: a group that believes and a group that does not believe?

We know that faith is an action of the heart, not an action of the senses, so we do not have access to hearts, and the Truth, glory be to Him, knows which of these deniers conceals faith in his heart.

So, among them are those who profess denial with their tongues while concealing faith in their hearts, and among them are those whose tongues agree with their denial because their hearts are empty of faith. Among those who said, "This Qur'an is nothing but a fabrication," there are those who believe in their hearts that Muhammad is the messenger of God and truthful in conveying the message from God, but stubbornness, arrogance and malice push them to declare their unbelief. Likewise, among them is another group that does not believe and declares that openly.

So, what is divided is not the faith that proceeds from the heart and is expressed by the tongue, but the faith that is in the heart, unexpressed, which has not reached the level of verbal affirmation. What confined the faith of some of them to the heart, unexpressed by the tongue, is malice, envy, hatred, and an inability of the soul to submit to what the method requires.

When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, announced to some of the Arabs that they should say: "There is no god but God," it would secure for them sovereignty over the whole world (1). They refused to say the word, because they knew that it is not a word merely to be uttered; rather, they understood the content and demand of the word, and knew that "There is no god but God" means equality among human beings, and they disliked that they would not have leadership and dominance over their peoples.

This also indicates that the Truth, glory be to Him, willed that Islam begin in Mecca, where the people openly declare their opinion. For this reason we find that hypocrisy arose only in "Medina." In Mecca, they were a people consistent with themselves: when they declared disbelief, they did not suffer from a divided disposition. But the hypocrites in Medina and elsewhere were the ones who suffered from a divided disposition, and among them were those who played both sides, saying with their tongues what was not in their hearts.

Therefore, the Truth consoles His noble Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and comforts him (2), and makes clear to him: Beware of grieving because they deny you, for you are beloved and revered among them. So the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿We certainly know that what they say grieves you, but it is not you they deny...﴾ (33) [al-An'am]: that is, you, O Muhammad, are free from lying.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿But it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of God...﴾ (33) [al-An'am] (3). That is, He bears it on behalf of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the Truth, glory be to Him, knows that His Messenger was trusted among his people, and even in the midst of their conflict with him, one of them would entrust him with his precious possessions (4).

As for those who believed in his message, may God bless him and grant him peace, but did not declare their faith, and those who did not believe, their affair is entrusted to God, the Exalted, so that each may receive his reckoning from the Creator, glory be to Him, for He is the most knowing of those who deny out of obstinacy and those who deny out of rejection.

The Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who punishes and holds to account, and each one of them will receive according to the measure of his corruption. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿And your Lord knows best the corrupters...﴾ (40) [Yunus]. The corrupter, as we know, is one who comes to a righteous thing and spoils it (5), because the world was created before human intervention in a sound form, and God's handiwork, glory be to Him and exalted, was not touched by corruption except through the deliberate act of man, while God's handiwork performs its function as it should.

And you, O human, if you wish that every matter in existence be set right for you, then look at the higher cosmos in which you have no part, and you will find everything in it upright, confirming the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And the heaven He raised high and set up the balance, that you not transgress within the balance, and establish weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance﴾ (7–9) [ar-Rahman]: that is, perfect the discharge of the responsibility for what is in your hands and do it well, as God, glory be to Him, has done well in what He created for you beyond your hands. Thus what is required of a person is to leave the righteous in its righteousness, if he cannot increase it in righteousness, so that he does not enter the circle of the corrupters.

1 His paternal uncle Abu Talib said to him: "O son of my brother, what do you want from your people?" He said: "I want from them one word, by which the Arabs will submit to them, and the non-Arabs will pay them the jizya." He said: "One word?" He said: "One word." He said: "O uncle, let them say: There is no god but God." Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/227) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (3232), who said it is a hasan hadith.
2 Yusri 'anhu: he removes from him worry and grief. [Lisan al-'Arab, root s-r-y]
3 al-Juhud: the opposite of affirmation. al-Jawhari said: al-juhud is denial with knowledge. God the Exalted says: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance...﴾ (14) [an-Naml]. [Lisan al-'Arab, root j-h-d]
4 Mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (2/485), quoting Ibn Ishaq, then said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had in Mecca no one who had anything they feared for that he did not deposit with him, because of what they knew of his truthfulness and trustworthiness, may God bless him and grant him peace."
5 al-'Atab: corruption and destruction.
6 Tatghu: from tughyan, meaning injustice; that is, be just in all your affairs, weigh matters and things by the balance of justice, and let none of you wrong another. al-Qist: justice. [Lisan al-'Arab, root q-s-t, adapted]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 41:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my work, and for you is your work. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do."﴾ (41)

This is a verse that places reassurance in the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah, glorified is He, did not say, "If they deny you," but said: ﴿if they deny you…﴾ (41). Allah, glorified is He, willed to bring the denial in the context of doubt, and He followed it with His saying to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿say: "For me is my work and for you is your work…"﴾ (41). That is, convey to them: I do not want to compel you to do what I do. I only want good for you, in that you should do good. If you do not do good, this will not affect the reckoning of my own work.

Thus it becomes clear to us that the Messenger (ﷺ) is not held accountable for the number of those who believe in him, but for performing the delivery (al-balagh) as Allah willed it.

Allah, glorified is He, willed that Muhammad (ﷺ) convey good to his nation. If they remain upon evil, this evil will not reach him, because the goodness of delivering the methodology gives the Prophet (ﷺ) goodness, since he applies it to himself. The evil of those who do not follow him returns only upon them, because those who refuse to respond to any caller only think that the caller will benefit.(2)

Delivery from Allah is something the Messenger (ﷺ) applies as a method and a conduct, and he is rewarded for it.(3) So it is not permissible to confuse these matters: ﴿For me is my work and for you is your work…﴾ (41).

Then Allah, glorified is He, says on the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do…﴾ (41) [Yunus]. The word ﴿free (bari')﴾ implies that there is a sin, and this true statement is a concession to the opponents. Allah, glorified is He, willed to teach His Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers the etiquette of dialogue and debate, so He says: ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ (24) [Saba']. That is: we—the Messenger and the believers with him—and you, O disbelievers, are either upon guidance or in error. The Messenger (ﷺ) is certain that he is upon guidance and that the disbelievers are upon error, but he concedes to them out of his justice (ﷺ) and in order to engage them.

Likewise his Lord, glorified is He, teaches him to say: ﴿Say: "You will not be asked about what we have committed, nor will we be asked about what you do."﴾ (25) [Saba']. That is: he clarifies to them: suppose I had committed a crime, you would not be asked about my crime. And from the etiquette of the Messenger (ﷺ), Allah, glorified is He, willed for him to say: ﴿nor will we be asked about what you do﴾ (25) [Saba'].

He did not say: "nor will we be asked about what you commit as crimes." Likewise, Allah, glorified is He, willed that here, in this verse about which we are reflecting: ﴿You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do…﴾ (41) [Yunus].

(1) Evidence for this is that Noah remained among his people calling them for a thousand years less fifty years, and despite this the Lord of Honour said of him: ﴿and none believed with him except a few…﴾ (40) [Hud]. They differed about the number of those who believed with him, between ten persons and eighty persons, among them his sons. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/445).

(2) Therefore Noah said to his people: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return; my reward is only from Allah…﴾ (29) [Hud]. Hud said to his people 'Ad: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from He who originated me. Will you not reason?﴾ (51) [Hud]. Likewise Salih said to his people Thamud: ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (145) [al-Shu'ara']. Lot said to his people: ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (164) [al-Shu'ara']. And Shu'ayb said to his people, the people of Madyan: ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (180) [al-Shu'ara'].

(3) The Messenger is charged with delivering what he was sent with, neither adding nor subtracting. Therefore the Lord of Honour says about His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and not one of you could have prevented Us from him﴾ (44–47) [al-Haqqah].

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not use their reason?﴾ (10:42)

The word "min" (من, "those among whom") may be used to refer to a singular, a dual, or a plural, and it may be used to refer to a single [person] or a plurality. Sometimes the wording agrees with it, as when Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿And among them is one who listens to you...﴾ (6:25), and sometimes the meaning is intended, as when He says: ﴿And among them are those who listen...﴾ (10:42). This is because "min" is suitable for both.

Hearing, as we know, is the ear's reception of sound. If the sound is ambiguous, like the sounds of animals or the sounds of musical instruments (a'wad), then these sounds convey nothing beyond what a tune produces in the body of vibration or tremor.

As for sound that has a conventional meaning, like the different languages in which people in different lands converse, if you speak English in a country whose people speak that language, they understand you and you understand them. This is the meaning of convention in language, that is, the speaker and the listener are on the same level of agreement about the language.

The Prophet (ﷺ) was an Arab who spoke in clear Arabic to a people of Arabs. So what, then, is the obstacle to hearing? The obstacle to hearing is turning the ear away from what comes from the opponent. Hearing, as we know, is the addressee's readiness (istishraf) to understand what the speaker says. If the addressee has no readiness to hear, then the speech is uttered but does not arrive.

Therefore, the listener must be in a state of readiness to understand what the speaker says. As the proverb says: "One ear is full of clay and the other of dough." Or as the joke goes, a man leaned toward the ear of a friend of his and said: "I want to tell you a secret," so the friend drew near, ready to hear the secret. The man said: "I want a hundred pounds as a loan." The friend said: "As if I had not heard this secret."

Thus, speech is not merely a sound that reaches the ear; there must be a psychological readiness to receive it. They do not possess this readiness, so Almighty Allah said: ﴿But can you make the deaf hear...?﴾ (10:42), meaning: as if their hearing does not hear.

An example of this: we find a teacher explaining the lesson to pupils, and among the pupils there is one who is ready to listen, so he understands the lesson, while the one who is not ready is as if he had not heard the lesson.

They are worse than the deaf, because the deaf may understand through movement, gesture, or the language of the eyes, but these people neither hear nor reason: ﴿But can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not use their reason?﴾ (10:42).

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And among them are those who look at you. Can you then make the blind to see, even though they do not perceive?﴾ (10:43)

Visions too require anticipation, and that a person turn toward what he wishes to see. Sometimes the one who sees is not anticipating, because his heart is not inclined to seeing.

It was said to a man: "You say, 'Whoever sees so-and-so, the righteous one, Allah will guide him.'" The listener responded, questioning: "How can you say that?!" The speaker replied: "Abu Jahl saw something better than this, and yet he remained a disbeliever." The listener responded: "Abu Jahl did not see Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but he saw the orphan of Abu Talib."(2)

Thus the man explained that Abu Jahl did not look at Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger, because if he had looked at him with this perception, the tranquility of faith would have crept into him, along with the awe of humility and the majesty of piety. We may meet a righteous man whose complexion is dark-tanned or swarthy, yet his righteousness shines around him, and he has a bearing (asr)(4) of piety and the attraction of scrupulousness.

Had Abu Jahl seen Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger, his state would have changed.

Here is Fadalah(5) recounting a moment in which he intended to kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was circumambulating the House in the year of the Conquest. When he drew near to him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "What were you saying to yourself?" He said: "Nothing, I was remembering Allah." He said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed, then said: 'Seek forgiveness from Allah,' and then placed his hand on Fadalah's chest."

When Fadalah heard this, and saw Muhammad (ﷺ) saying that speech, he said: "Nothing was more hateful to me than his face, but I turned to him, and nothing was more beloved to me in the whole earth than his face."(6)

This is hearing, and this is sight, and both hearing and sight are the noblest and most honored of the faculties, because hearing is the means of listening to what Allah conveys from Him, and a person, before he reads, must first have heard. What is meant here by blindness in the words of the Almighty ﴿Can you then make the blind to see, even though they do not perceive?﴾ is blindness of insight.

(1) The sight of the righteous carries a pull toward faith, because the one who sees perceives the light of faith calling him, so he meets it and is met by it.
As for the sight of Abu Jahl, it was a vision of faith's severance, because his receptivity to faith was cut off. He saw no light and did not sense it; his seeing was through the rancor that made him see in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only an orphan of Ibn Abi Talib. This is unlike the stance of Fadalah, who sensed the light and so loved him.

(2) Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir (4/3232) that the polytheists said: "Allah could find no one to send except the orphan of Abu Talib."

(3) Adma among people: intense swarthiness. It was also said: it is from the adma of the earth, which is its color, and the Father of Mankind, peace be upon him. [Lisan al-Arab, root (a-d-m)]

(4) Asr: the bearing that overcomes the feelings of those around him.

(5) He is Fadalah ibn Umayr ibn al-Mulawwih al-Laythi.

(6) Ibn Hisham mentioned it in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (4/417) with the wording: "By Allah, he did not remove his hand from my chest until there was nothing in Allah's creation more beloved to me than him."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 44:

And the Truth, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who wrong themselves.﴾ (10:44)

The word "Allah" is a proper name for the Necessarily Existent One (wajib al-wujud), who is characterised by all the perfect attributes that we know from the Most Beautiful Names, the ninety-nine. Although Allah, exalted is He, has perfections that have no end, because the names or attributes carried by the ninety-nine names are not sufficient to contain all of Allah's perfections, for His perfections, glorified is He, are endless.

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I ask You by every name You have named Yourself with, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept hidden in the knowledge of the unseen with You" (1).

If someone asks: why does Allah, glorified is He, keep some of His names hidden in the knowledge of the unseen? I say: so that Allah, glorified is He, may give us in the Hereafter further perfections that we did not know; for this reason we find that the Truth, glorified is He, will open to His Messenger (ﷺ) "praises of Him and good commendation of Him, the like of which He has not opened to anyone before him" (2).

This is a portion of an unending overflow from the horizons of the name "Allah" as the Necessarily Existent One, and of the attributes of the Necessarily Existent One. The ninety-nine names that we know (3) are those required for our life in this world, but in the Hereafter we will find other attributes of perfection. The word "Allah" comprises all these names, both what we know of them and what we do not.

When any of us sets about a task, that task requires the combination of many attributes: it requires power, knowledge, wisdom, gentleness, mercy, and other attributes. If you say, "In the name of the Strong," you need strength; if you say, "In the name of the Capable," you need capability; if you say, "In the name of the Forbearing," you need forbearance; if you say, "In the name of the Wise," you need wisdom. But if you say, "Bismillah" ("In the name of Allah"), it suffices you for all of this and more besides. For this reason the beginning of actions (4) is with "Bismillah." So when you need power, you find it; if you need sufficiency, you find it; and if you need expansiveness (5), you find it.

All the attributes of perfection, the Truth, glorified is He, has summarised for us in our saying: "Bismillah." When you begin your work with the name of Allah, you acknowledge that all strength (6) you have is bestowed by Allah, that the things which are subdued to you are subdued only by the name of Allah, and that everything is made subservient to you by the name of Allah. He is the One who says:

﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, so that they are their owners? And We have subdued them for them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat.﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:71-72). Had Allah not subdued the cattle and things for us, we would not have been able to own them, as is shown by the fact that Allah, exalted is He, has left some things unsubdued for us, so that we learn that we cannot do so, neither by our knowledge nor by our power; rather, it is the Truth, glorified is He, who subdues.

You see a child in the countryside leading a camel and commanding it to kneel, and it kneels; commanding it to rise, and it rises. But if we see a serpent, many of us run away to flee, and none confronts it except one who has skill in killing it. A tiny little flea may come to bite you at night, and you do not know how to catch it, because Allah has not subdued it for you.

Likewise, if you pick fruit from a tree before it ripens, it is unpalatable; but if you pick it after it ripens, you enjoy its taste, then you take its seed to replant it, and so ensure the continuation of the species. Indeed, the fruit falls from the tree when it ripens, as though calling to whoever will eat it.

Likewise, when a person reaches puberty, that is, becomes able to beget others, Allah then imposes upon him the obligations of faith; for if He had imposed them before that, and then the troubles of adolescence came upon him, he might not be able to bear the obligation.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, willed to create from nothing, and to rear until the human being is complete, then He set the obligation from the moment of puberty, and made a condition the completion of reason and maturity, and that there be no defect or madness.

No one is stronger than Allah, glorified is He, such that He could impose on you what would make you do other than what Allah wills. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, willed that maturity be complete for the human being at the moment of obligation. As for the insane, Allah, glorified is He, has not obligated him; and likewise the obligation is lifted from the one who is compelled, because obligation in its essence is a choice between alternatives, and this is the utmost justice in legislation.

When you receive the obligation, you should not look at what the acts of worship take from you, for they do not take from your freedom; rather, you too respect the freedom of others, and they respect your freedom. If He has forbidden you to steal, then He, glorified is He, has protected you by forbidding all creation to steal from you (8). So the restriction has come for your benefit.

Suppose you let your hand loose among people: what would you do if they let their hands loose upon what you own?

And when the obligation has forbidden you to look upon the unlawful (mahārim) of others, He has forbidden others to look upon your unlawful.

And when He has commanded you to give zakat, He has taken from you so that He may give to the poor from the wealth in which Allah has made you His vicegerent.

So do not look at what is taken from you; rather, look at what may return to you if fate afflicts you with poverty. As for the thing you feel is being taken from you, Allah, glorified is He, gives you reward many times over (9).

After that, look at the movement of life, and look at what Allah, exalted is He, has forbidden you of things, and what He has made lawful for you otherwise; you will find that what is permitted to you is more than what He has prohibited you from.

So the obligation is for your benefit. Then, after all this: does anything of what you do in the way of obligations return to the Truth, glorified is He? No. Does it give Him an attribute He did not have? No; for the Truth, glorified is He, has created us with all His attributes of perfection, and there is nothing in our action that adds anything to Him.

So it is in your interest to carry out the obligations, because they return to you yourself with good.

Consider, for example, the farmer in the field: he ploughs the land, carries the manure, sows, waters, and toils, and after that he rests awaiting the fruits.

When you carry out the obligations of the Truth (10), glorified is He, you find the return; and you see in your life that the lazy farmer is afflicted with regret on the day of harvest, so what of the reckoning of the Hereafter?

And the farmer who takes from his store an ardab (11) to sow it, and in this case his store is not diminished, because after a period he will return with fifteen ardabs.

Thus whoever carries out the obligations, every good returns to him. For this reason I say: look at what the method of Allah, exalted is He, gives you, not at what it takes from you.

Thus you see that there is no injustice, for we are the handiwork of Allah. Have you ever seen a craftsman spoil his own handiwork?

So the Supreme Craftsman does not wrong His handiwork, nor does He ever spoil it; rather He perfects it and gives it beauty and splendour (11). For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who wrong themselves.﴾ (10:44). That is: it is the people who wrong themselves. Among wrongdoing is the denial of the truth, and this is the greatest wrong; and among wrongdoing is that a person gives himself a hasty desire, so that he afterwards tastes a deferred punishment, and by that he deprives himself of lasting bliss. And when he wrongs himself, he has lost the ability to measure his life in this world: life, however long, is short, and whatever has an end is short.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, addresses people, He has set up enduring signs until the Hour comes, in which all are partners: these are the cosmic signs (12). Then He singled out each messenger with a sign and a miracle, and sent down a method of "do" and "do not do," and He explained in the verses of the Book what is required to be done and what is required to be refrained from (13), and He left the remaining matters permitted to you.

The example I always give is the pupil who fails at the end of the year. This pupil has not been wronged by the school, as is shown by the fact that others have passed. So it is not correct to say: the school failed so-and-so; rather the correct statement is: so-and-so has failed himself, and his classmate has passed himself, and the school's role in that is to announce the result.

Among wrongdoing too is that the wrongdoer regards a blessing in the possession of the wronged as excessive, so he wants to take it from him. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, cannot be a wrongdoer who begrudges the blessings of His servants, for He is exalted above that; moreover, His creatures have no blessings that He wants, for it is He who gave them these. Therefore no injustice comes from Him, glorified is He; and if injustice occurs, it comes from the human being to himself.

(1) Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/452, 391) and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (1/509), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, and he declared it sahih according to the conditions of Muslim, free of interruption (irsal).
(2) This takes place on the Day of Resurrection, at the station of the intercession of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), after his brethren among the prophets have delayed from it. On the authority of Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) comes beneath the Throne and falls down in prostration; then Allah opens upon him praises of Him and good commendation of Him, the like of which He has not opened upon anyone before him. Then it is said: O Muhammad, raise your head, ask and it shall be given, intercede and your intercession shall be accepted; so the Messenger (ﷺ) raises his head and says: 'O Lord, my ummah, my ummah.'" From a long hadith narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4712), and Muslim in his Sahih (194).
(3) On the authority of Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever counts them enters Paradise." Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7392) and Muslim (2677). The mention of the Most Beautiful Names in detail occurs in another narration from Abu Hurayra, recorded by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (3507) and Ibn Majah (3861), and the route of al-Tirmidhi is more sound.
(4) Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad (2/359) from Abu Hurayra that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every speech or matter of importance that does not begin with the mention of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is abtar (deficient) — or he said: cut off."
(5) That is, that He expands your provision; He is al-Basit (the Expander). He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it...﴾ (13:26).
(6) Al-hawl: strength, stratagem, and the capability to manage your affairs in life.
(7) That is, he would not be able to carry out what he was charged with, because he is not yet mature; for this reason the obligation accompanies puberty, so that there is an educational balance that trains the soul to the desires of Allah. Yet if the child performs the obligations, he has reward.
(8) On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (41). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) thus made safety from harming, whether by tongue or hand, a sign of the goodness of a servant's Islam.
(9) Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says in His Noble Book: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.﴾ (4:40). And He, the Mighty and Majestic, has said: ﴿And those who are observant of zakat (23:4)﴾; ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase, and invoke blessings upon them; indeed, your invocation is a comfort for them (9:103)﴾; ﴿And those in whose wealth is a known right, for the beggar and the deprived (70:24-25)﴾.
(10) The obligations of the Truth, glorified is He, are His commands and prohibitions, which Allah imposes upon whoever believes in Him. Similar is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, and do not kill your children out of poverty — We provide for you and for them — and do not approach immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. This He has instructed you that you may reason. And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in the best manner, until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice; We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it should be [against] a near relative; and the covenant of Allah fulfill. This has He instructed you that you may remember. And [He says], "Indeed, this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path. This has He instructed you that you may fear Him (6:151-153).﴾
(11) On this the Lord of Honour says: ﴿[He is] the One who perfected everything He created and began the creation of man from clay (32:7)﴾, and He says in another verse: ﴿Allah is the One who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a ceiling, and formed you and perfected your forms (40:64)﴾.
(12) Allah has placed in the universe signs by which He addresses all people, that they may reflect upon them and thereby conclude that this universe has one Creator. Allah has gathered them in His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah sends down from the sky of water, giving life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and dispersing therein every creature, and the variation of the winds and the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who reason (2:164).﴾
(13) As in His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you...﴾ (6:151).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 45:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿On the Day He gathers them, [it will be as though they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day, recognizing one another. Those will have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not [rightly] guided.]﴾ (45)

This worldly life, for which a person longs and from which he takes his share, and of which he sometimes forgets the Hereafter, when the Resurrection occurs you will feel as though you had not remained in the world except an hour. The "hour" here is the all-encompassing Hour in which the Resurrection takes place. But the hour in the world is a part of time, and we know that the day is divided into twenty-four hours. The word "sā'ah" (hour) is also applied to that instrument hung on the wall or worn by a person on his wrist, which indicates the time.

Timekeeping is fixed, in terms of the hour, minute and second, from Adam, peace be upon him, until those who will come after us. However, the timekeeping differs from place to place. For example, the clock in Cairo may show two in the afternoon, while in New York it is seven in the morning, and in another country it shows three after midnight. The clock is not unified for all creation except on the Day of Resurrection.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour.﴾ [Ar-Rum] (55). They will be surprised that their long and broad worldly life has all passed as though it were merely an hour, and thus they discover how brief the life they lived was. The matter is not limited to that; rather, they did not benefit from it either, for it is a span of time that had no value.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿As if they, on the Day they see what they were promised, had not remained but an hour of a day, [a notification]. So will be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ [Al-Ahqaf] (35). That is: the world passes over them in amusement, play and preoccupations, and they did not take life with the seriousness it deserves; so it was lost from them as though it were an hour.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says here: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them, as if they had not remained but an hour of a day.﴾ [Yunus] (45). On the Day of Gathering people are divided into two groups: a group who used to recognize one another in righteousness, and a group who used to recognize one another in sin.
