Those who knew one another in the worldly life in righteousness rejoice with one another, while those who knew one another in the worldly life in sin repel one another with enmity. The Truth, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿Intimate friends that Day will be, some of them to others, enemies, except the righteous.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf] (67).

Likewise He said about those who knew one another in sin: ﴿When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed.﴾ [Al-Baqarah] (166). They will recognize one another, but this recognition will not last; it turns into disavowal. Each one of them does not want to see the one who was the cause of his arriving at this fate, and their recognition is a recognition of reproach.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah.﴾ (45) [Yunus]. Whenever you hear the word "khasira" (to lose), know that the matter concerns some trade, and loss means that the merchant loses either part of his capital or all of it.

The stages of trade, as we know, are either a gain that increases the capital invested, or the merchant neither gains nor loses, but he feels that the price of his effort and his time in this trade has been wasted. All of this happens in transactions.

We find the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, describing the process of faith in the world by saying: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? [It is that] you believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ [As-Saff] (10-11). And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, hope for a transaction that will never perish.﴾ [Fatir] (29). Trade depends on the fact that you do not enter into a deal unless it is strongly probable to you that this deal will bring you more than what you paid in it.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says about losing transactions: ﴿Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance, so their transaction has not profited, and they were not [rightly] guided.﴾ [Al-Baqarah] (16).

He also says: ﴿And when they see a transaction or amusement, they rush to it and leave you standing.﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah] (11).

Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, willed that the meaning of trade be clear and expressive of many situations, because trade represents the sum of all the movement of life. One person moves in one field and benefits others, and another works in a different field and benefits himself and others.

Thus a person benefits from his own movement and the movement of others, and he benefits from the movement of others more than from his own. It is in the interest of every person that each person perform his movement well, so that he himself is at ease, because what reaches him from the activity of people will be of good quality.

Trade also carries the role of intermediary between producer and consumer.

For this reason, when Allah, glorified is He, wanted us to respond to the call to Friday prayer, He said: ﴿O you who have believed, when [the call] is proclaimed to prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ (9) [Al-Jumu'ah]. Allah, glorified is He, did not say: "Leave farming," or "leave industry," or "leave teaching." Rather, He chose from all the movements of life the movement of selling, because in it is trade, and trade is what encompasses all the movements of life.

The merchant is an intermediary between producer and consumer, and trade requires buying and selling. In buying, the merchant pays a price; in selling, he takes the price. The purpose of everything is that a person acquire wealth.

Therefore selling is preferable to the merchant over buying. You may buy something while disliking it, due to your need for it, but when you sell the goods you feel happiness and radiance, because buying involves taking, while selling involves giving, and giving always pleases the soul, because the fruit of the transaction comes to you in its very moment.

If you are a farmer, you prepare the land, plough it, sow the seeds, water them, trim the plants, and wait until the crop ripens. Likewise, if you are a craftsman, you spend much time perfecting the craft. But selling in trade brings you gain quickly. Thus the example of trade was drawn from the fundamentals of commerce by way of selling, and not by way of buying.

So: it is necessary for us to consider that your entry into the transaction of faith is a trade, from which you take more than your capital and profit. But if you abandon some of the religion, you lose in proportion to what you have left, and even many times over.

In any transaction you may compensate for what you lost later on. If the loss continues, its effect does not exceed the world, and you may profit afterwards. And if you do not profit, your effort will merely be wasted. Since the world is limited in time, its loss is bearable. But loss in time that is not limited, the enduring time, is a great loss, because the Hereafter has no changes like the world does. In the Hereafter you are either in a Garden of enduring bliss, and in this is great profit and gain, or in the Fire, and this is the true loss.

True loss is for a person to deny not only the bounty of Allah, but also the meeting with Allah.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah.﴾ (45) [Yunus]. That is: Allah, glorified is He, was not in their minds, and when the Resurrection occurs they will find Allah, glorified and exalted is He, before them. For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert plain which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing.﴾ [An-Nur] (39). The mirage, as we know, is seen by the traveller in the desert; it is an reflection of light, so he thinks there is water before him, but if he goes to it he finds no water. Thus the Truth, glorified is He, likened the deed of the disbeliever to one who walks in a vast desert and sees the mirage and thinks it is water, but it is a mirage; as soon as he reaches it, the words of the Truth, glorified is He, apply to him: ﴿Until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, but he finds Allah with him, and He pays him in full his account.﴾ [An-Nur] (39). That is: he is surprised by the presence of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and Allah settles his account with him.

For this reason, whoever disbelieves in Allah and does what benefits mankind, he takes his reckoning from those for whom he worked, and that will not be counted for him in the Hereafter. You find people honouring him, erecting statues for him, or granting him prizes, and the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) apply to him: "He did it so that it would be said, and it has been said."

And here the Truth, glorified is He, says about those who denied the meeting with Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they were not [rightly] guided.﴾ (45) [Yunus]. That is: they were not walking on the path that their Creator, glorified is He, set for them. This path represents the law of preservation for the creation of Allah, the Exalted, and Allah, glorified is He, created man for a task, and Allah, glorified is He, preserves man through the methodology so that he may fulfil this task.

Guidance is the path which, if a person follows it, leads him to achieving the task required of him, because the Truth, glorified is He, has made him vicegerent on earth.

And whoever does not believe in the Lord of the methodology, glorified and exalted is He, and does not apply the methodology, he is headed toward manifest loss, that is, all-encompassing loss.

1 "Labitha": to remain, to stay.
2 "Sā'ah": its origin is a part of time, not specifically defined, in which scarcity is noticed. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿The criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour...﴾ (55) [Ar-Rum], meaning a short period; and His saying: ﴿And for every nation is a term; when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor precede [it]﴾ (34) [Al-A'raf], meaning they will not delay for a moment. The "Hour" (as-sā'ah) is the Day of Resurrection, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the Day the Hour is established...﴾ (55) [Ar-Rum], meaning the Resurrection.
3 For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due effort while he is a believer—those are the ones whose effort is appreciated﴾ (19) [Al-Isra'], so striving for the Hereafter must be in proportion to the greatness of that final Day.
4 "Khasira": the man lost in his trade, khasran, khasaran, khasarah and khusran; he was cheated in it, did not profit, and suffered deficiency. "Khasira al-rajul" also means he went astray; so he is khasir and khasir. The Almighty says: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah﴾ (31) [Al-An'am]. "Khasira nafsahu" means he destroyed himself through misguidance. And the Almighty's saying: ﴿He has lost the world and the Hereafter﴾ (11) [Al-Hajj]. From the intransitive form is the Almighty's saying: ﴿Then he has certainly lost a clear loss﴾ (119) [An-Nisa'], and it may come transitive, like the Almighty's saying: ﴿Say, indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (15) [Az-Zumar] [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].
5 "Tajara" (from the pattern of nasara): tajran, tijaratan: he bought and sold seeking profit. "Tijarah" is applied to the wealth in which the merchant trades, and is applied figuratively to work that results in good, as reward is profit and deprivation of it is loss. The Almighty says: ﴿Except that it be a present trade which you conduct among yourselves﴾ (282) [Al-Baqarah]; here "tijarah" is the object traded in. His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, hope for a transaction that will never perish﴾ (29) [Fatir] refers to righteous deeds; and His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ (10) [As-Saff] refers to trade in the figurative sense, i.e., righteous work [Al-Qamus al-Qawim].
6 "As-sarab": what is seen at midday when the heat intensifies, like water in the desert, clinging to the ground. It is a deception of sight. It was named "sarab" because it "yasrub" (flows) flowing, i.e., it moves in a way that deceives the viewer from afar, so he thinks it is water while it is not water, but an optical and visual illusion arising from the psychological state of the person when he is extremely thirsty and in a barren desert; so any movement from afar he thinks is water, and he runs toward it, only to be surprised that there is nothing.
"Al-qay'ah": a wide, level land that does not grow trees. Al-Farra' said: "Al-qay'ah" is the plural of "al-qa'," and "al-qa'" is what is spread out of the earth. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And leave it a level plain﴾ (106) [Ta-Ha].
7 On the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first of people to be judged on the Day of Resurrection will be a man who was martyred. He will be brought forward and his blessings will be made known to him, and he will recognize them. He [Allah] will say: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I fought for You until I was martyred.' He will say: 'You lie; rather you fought so that it would be said, "He is brave," and it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is thrown into the Fire. And a man who learned knowledge and taught it and recited the Qur'an, he will be brought and his blessings will be made known to him, and he will recognize them. He will say: 'What did you do with them?' He will say: 'I learned knowledge and taught it, and I recited the Qur'an for Your sake.' He will say: 'You lie; rather you learned knowledge so that it would be said, "He is a scholar," and you recited the Qur'an so that it would be said, "He is a reciter." And it has been said.' Then he will be ordered, and he will be dragged on his face until he is thrown into the Fire..." The hadith was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1905) and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/23), Dar al-Kutub al-'Ilmiyyah edition, Beirut.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We cause you to die, to Us is their return; then Allah is Witness over what they do.﴾ (46)

The Almighty's words ﴿وإما﴾ (wa-immā) are composed of "in" (إن) and "mā" (ما), assimilated into one another. Here the Almighty makes clear to us that He promises those who denied His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, punishment, humiliation, retribution and disgrace. That is: O Muhammad, either you will see what We have said about them of abasement and humiliation, or We will cause you to die before you see this in this world, but you will see it in the Hereafter, when you witness the everlasting humiliation that befalls them on the Last Day.

In this there is consolation for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The words of the Almighty ﴿وإما نرينك.. (46)﴾ mean: that We show you what We promised them of abasement and humiliation in this life. And even if you do not see it in the life of this world, you will surely see their humiliation in the Hereafter, where the return is to Allah the Exalted; for He, glorified is He, will afflict them in themselves with things beyond the humiliation seen among people, such as anguish in the soul and suppressed grief when they see the victory of the believers.

As for what is seen, it is the outward matter, namely the abandonment, the defeat, the grief, the killing, the seizing of wealth, the taking captive of women and children, or other things that you will see of them—after your soul has departed to its Creator—so you will see in them what Allah has promised you.

You will not need anyone's testimony against them, for He, glorified is He, is ﴿Witness over what they do (46)﴾, and Allah suffices as a witness: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness (79)﴾ [An-Nisa].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 47:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿For every nation there is a messenger. When their messenger comes, judgment will be passed between them with justice, and they will not be wronged.﴾

The Truth, glory be to Him, does not wrong anyone, and He does not punish a people except after they have disbelieved in the messenger He sent to them. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them﴾ [Fatir 35:24], and He, glory be to Him, also says: ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the cities wrongfully while their people were unaware﴾ [al-An'am 6:131]. Thus there is no criminalization and no punishment except by a text and a clarification of the prohibition of this act or that, through the sending of messengers, so that no one may argue that nothing reached him by which he could be held accountable.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, explains that for every nation there is a messenger who takes charge of it with the affairs of the method (manhaj).

God, glory be to Him, created all creation, and they were monotheists from the time of the offspring of Adam, peace be upon him. Then events required that they spread apart and scattered across the earth, meetings became distant, and so did means of travel, and afflictions multiplied with the multiplicity of environments.

But when meetings draw close and travel becomes easy, what happens in the East you see at that very moment while you are in the West, and this means that afflictions become unified or nearly one. For this reason the Seal of the Messengers, may God bless him and grant him peace, was necessary. In ancient times, however, there was an age of isolation, each community living far from the others; therefore a messenger was necessary for each community, to treat the ailments of its environment. Now that the environments have met, the Seal of the Messengers treats all ailments.(3) Hence the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿For every nation there is a messenger. When their messenger comes, judgment will be passed between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Yunus 10:47]. History has related this to us: every messenger who came was believed in by some and disbelieved by others, and those who believed in him were victorious, while those who disbelieved in him were defeated. Or the verse is general: ﴿For every nation there is a messenger﴾, meaning that on the Day of Resurrection every nation will be called by the name of its messenger: "O nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace! O nation of Moses! O nation of Jesus!" and so on.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these?(4) (41) On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from God any word.﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:41-42].

So, the Truth, glory be to Him, here explains that for every nation there is a messenger who came to it with the delivery of the message from God. Some believed in him and some disbelieved. Since belief has occurred, and likewise disbelief, there must be a judgment between the believers and the disbelievers.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿When their messenger comes, judgment will be passed between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Yunus 10:47]. And since there is a judgment, the believer must regard the disbeliever as a disputant against him, and the disbeliever must regard the believer as a disputant against him, and the matter becomes a case requiring a ruling. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Judgment will be passed between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Yunus 10:47].

That is: judgment will be passed between them with justice. The believers, God the Truth searches out their good deeds and increases them for them, while the disbelievers have no good deeds, because they disbelieved in the true God; so He casts them into the Fire. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had informed them that a day would come on which they would be questioned about everything. They considered this unlikely and said: ﴿When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised up? And our forefathers of old?﴾ [al-Saffat 37:16-17]. They were astonished by resurrection and denied it, yet they will find it certainly and truly.

God, glory be to Him, wills to address this matter to them in a manner of faith, saying: ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation?﴾ [Qaf 50:15]. That is: when you die and dissolve into the dust, would God be unable to create you anew? No; He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record﴾ [Qaf 50:4]. That is: He, glory be to Him, commands the particular elements of each human being to be gathered together entirely, and this is not difficult for God who created them at first.

They denied, rejected and mocked the coming of the Day of Resurrection and the resurrection, and their mockery reached the point that they hastened(5) this Day. This is evidence of their ignorance, for each of them should have fled from the terror of that Day.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says afterwards, on their tongues: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ [Yunus 10:48].

Notes:
1. Qasata (قسط), yaqsitu, in the form of daraba, qasatan and qusuwwan; and qasata, yaqsitu, in the form of nasara, qasatan: to wrong or to act justly; it is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-adداd), understood through context. The Qur'an uses it in the sense of wronging in His words: ﴿And as for the unjust (al-qasitun), they will be fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Jinn 72:15], and aqsata means to act justly and remove injustice; the Qur'an uses it in the sense of justice in His words: ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice﴾ [al-A'raf 7:29]. Al-qistas means the balance and justice (Al-Qamus al-Qawim).
2. Khala (خلا): passed and elapsed. From it His words: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the bygone days﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:24], i.e., the past (Al-Qamus al-Qawim).
3. This is because the message of Islam is the summation of the values of every previous religion, confirming His words: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you should establish the religion and not be divided therein...﴾ [al-Shura 42:13].
4. On the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: "Recite to me." I said: O Messenger of God, shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you? He said: "Yes, I love to hear it from someone other than myself." So I recited Surat al-Nisa' until I came to this verse: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you as a witness against these?﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:41]. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "That is enough for now," and his eyes were overflowing with tears. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (5050) and Ahmad in his Musnad (1/380).
   Linguistically: al-shahid is an intensive form of al-shahid (witness), and al-Shahid is among the Beautiful Names of God: ﴿Indeed God is ever Witness over all things﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:33]. His words ﴿Let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:282] mean a witness. Al-shahid also means one who is killed in the way of God; al-shahadah means a decisive report; al-shahid is the active participle, its plural being shuhud and shuhud (Al-Qamus al-Qawim).
5. The Lord of Glory has said of them: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, but God will not fail His promise﴾ [al-Hajj 22:47], and He says in another verse: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and had it not been for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them﴾ [al-Ankabut 29:53].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 48:

This denial, rejection and mockery is the discourse of the polytheists and the atheists (ملحدون)(1) in every era and place. In the recent age, the Communists said it when they carried out their false revolution and slaughtered the upper class of society under the pretext of lifting injustice from the poor.

If they had believed in the necessity of reward and punishment, then who is it that judges this? Does the oppressor judge an oppressor, so that the result is that the oppressor will be destroyed by the oppressor? That has happened. So where are the Communists now?

Why did they not notice that this universe has a Creator who punishes those who oppressed in the past, or who will oppress in the future?

They did not notice, because they took matter as a god, and said: there is no god, and life is matter. So where are they now?

And if you have gained dominance over your contemporaries, and claimed that you spread justice among them, then what of those who came before and those who came after?

They, therefore, did not notice that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has willed that no oppressor dies until Allah has taken vengeance upon him.(2)

Nor did they notice that behind this abode there is another abode in which the good-doer is recompensed for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil.

Logic required that these people believe that this universe has a just God, and that the day must come when every person is recompensed for what he did. But they mocked, just as those who disbelieved before them mocked, and their account came in the saying of Allah, glorified, on their tongues: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"﴾ [Yunus: 48].

But the promise of Allah is true, and the promise of Allah is coming, and Muhammad (ﷺ) is a messenger from Allah, conveying what came from Allah, exalted is He. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not possess anything for himself.

Therefore the Qur'an says after that:

﴿Say, "I do not possess for myself any harm or benefit, except what Allah wills. For every nation is an appointed term; when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it."﴾ [Yunus: 49]:

1 Mulhidun (ملحدون): plural of mulhid, one who attacks religion and turns away from it. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses are not hidden from Us...﴾ [Fussilat: 40]. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root (ل ح د)].
2 The Truth says: ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly, [They will be] racing, with raised heads, their glances not returning to them, and their hearts void.﴾ [Ibrahim: 42-43]. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 49:

The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, disclaims for himself any power or strength (ḥawl wa-ṭawl)¹, and proclaims what Allah, glory be to Him, has commanded him to proclaim. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, does not possess for himself any benefit or harm, because benefit or harm is in the hand of its Creator, glory be to Him, and He, glory be to Him and exalted, is your Creator, and every matter is by His will, glory be to Him.

This verse came in response to their question which Allah, glory be to Him, related in the preceding verse: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"﴾ [Yunus 48]. They asked about this promise of punishment with mockery, as if they were hastening the descent of the punishment in derision. This shows that the word of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, the matter will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Yunus 47], was not revealed for the Day of Resurrection, but rather was revealed to clarify the stance of those who disbelieved in the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and who then said: ﴿When is this promise, if you should be truthful?﴾ [Yunus 48]. This means that they said this statement before the Hour was established. The verse that clarifies that for every nation there is a messenger is supported by many verses, such as His, glory be to Him: ﴿And We would not punish until We sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra' 15], and likewise the word of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while its people are unaware﴾ [al-An'am 131], and likewise the word of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger..."﴾ [Ta-Ha 134]. All of this confirms that the messenger sent to a nation is the one who came with the methodology of Allah, exalted be He; some people believed in him, and others denied him, and Allah judged between the believers and the disbelievers by humiliating the disbelievers and granting victory to the believers.

And if the disbelievers hasten the humiliation, they will surely see it. Therefore, Allah, glory be to Him, commanded His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿Say, "I do not possess for myself any harm or benefit..."﴾ [Yunus 49]. That is: if you ask Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about harm and benefit, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is a conveyor from Allah, exalted be He, and he does not possess for himself any harm or benefit, let alone possess for them harm or benefit. All of this matter is in the hand of Allah, exalted be He, and for every nation there is a term² by which the disbelievers are struck with punishment, and the decisive word is pronounced therein.

And the word of Allah, glory be to Him: ﴿Except what Allah wills. For every nation is a term...﴾ [Yunus 49], indicates that the will of Allah is the decisive factor, and it shows that the Prophet and people do not possess for themselves harm or benefit, because man is created with compulsion³ in some matters and with choice in other matters. Choice is in the matters of obligation, confirming His, glory be to Him, word: ﴿So whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve...﴾ [al-Kahf 29]. You are free to obey or to disobey, and all of this falls within the scope of your choice. If a person performs an act of obedience, he is producing benefit for himself, and if he performs an act of disobedience, he is producing harm for himself.

Thus, in matters of choice there is harm and benefit. An example of that: one who commits suicide by hanging himself has brought harm upon himself, and his relatives may rescue him, and that is by the will of Allah, glory be to Him. So, in matters of choice, a person—by the will of Allah—possesses harm or benefit for himself, and Allah, glory be to Him, shows us that for every nation there is a term, so do not you set the terms of nations, because their terms—whether annihilation or punishment—are from Allah, glory be to Him and exalted.

The servants are always hasty, but Allah is not hasty with the haste of the servants, until matters reach what He, glory be to Him, wills. Allah, exalted be He, is free from being an employee of creation; rather, He is the Supreme Creator, glory be to Him and exalted.

He, glory be to Him, is the One who said: ﴿He will show you His signs, so do not ask Me to hasten﴾ [al-Anbiya' 37], and He, glory be to Him, is the One who said: ﴿And man supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good, and man is ever hasty﴾ [al-Isra' 11].

So, Allah, glory be to Him, delays His desired outcomes out of mercy to creation, and when the term comes, it does not delay from its appointed time, nor does it advance from its appointed time.

Therefore, the Almighty says: ﴿And when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ [Yunus 49]. And His, glory be to Him, word: ﴿nor can they advance it﴾ is not part of the answer to the conditional ﴿when their term comes...﴾ [Yunus 49]⁵, because the answer is: ﴿they cannot delay it﴾. They do not advance before the term arrives.

¹ Ḥawl: skill, quality of insight, and ability to act precisely in matters. Ṭawl: grace, wealth, and ease. Allah says: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford the means to marry free, believing women...﴾ [al-Nisa' 25]. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit]..
² Ajal: the duration of a thing, the limit of a time, and the time of life, or the time of a debt or the time of a work. Al-ajal is the very time for which a matter is appointed: ﴿So when Moses fulfilled the term...﴾ [al-Qasas 29], i.e., completed the period set for it. Ajjala al-shay': set a future term for it: ﴿For what day has it been postponed?﴾ [al-Mursalat 12], i.e., the limit of death or old age. His word: ﴿Then He decreed a specified term with Him...﴾ [al-An'am 2]: the first is the duration of remaining in this world, and the second is the duration of remaining in the graves until the Day of Resurrection, or the duration of the Hereafter. And His word: ﴿And when they have reached their term...﴾ [al-Baqarah 234], i.e., the end of the period of waiting ('idda). Al-ājil is the opposite of al-'ājil, and al-ājila is the opposite of al-'ājila. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]..
³ Qasr: compulsion and coercion..
⁴ 'Ajūlan: an intensive form, to be hasty in matters. Ista'jala al-amr: to seek it quickly and speedily. Allah says: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them...﴾ [Yunus 11]. Al-'ājil: the swift, the opposite of al-ājil; al-'ājila is the worldly life, and al-ājila is the Hereafter. The Almighty says: ﴿No! But you love the immediate﴾ [al-Qiyamah 20], i.e., the worldly life. 'Ajjala al-amr: sought it before its time out of impulse of desire; 'ajjala al-amr: preceded it. Allah, exalted be He, says: ﴿Moses returned to his people angry and grieved. He said, "Evil is that which you have done after me. Did you hasten the command of your Lord?"﴾ [al-A'raf 150]..
⁵ Idha: comes in two senses, conditional and sudden. Idha as a conditional particle is a noun of condition for future time; it takes a verbal sentence, and idha is parsed as an adverb of future time governing its condition in the genitive and governed in the accusative by its answer. Allah says: ﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say, "Peace be upon you..."﴾ [al-An'am 54]. It sometimes precedes nominal nouns in the nominative, in which case the noun after it is the subject of a deleted verb explained by the verb that follows, as in: ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 1], i.e., when the sky splits. Idha may also be a particle of surprise, and it governs a nominal sentence. Allah says: ﴿So he threw it, and suddenly it was a moving serpent﴾ [Ta-Ha 20]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 50:

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿Say: Tell me, if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals seek to hasten?﴾ (10:50)

This is a conclusive reply to their urgency for the punishment. If the punishment comes to you, let us see what their position will be?

By hastening the punishment, they demonstrate their own foolishness in asking about its occurrence.

The words of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Tell me﴾. That is: inform me of what will happen to you.

The Truth, glory be to Him, willed that the time of the punishment's coming be left vague here, so He said, glory be to Him:

﴿If His punishment comes upon you by night or by day...﴾ (10:50). By "bayat" (overnight attack) is meant the night, since the night is the time of lodging (al-baytutah), and the day is the time of being visible. The daily time is divided into two parts: night and day.

The Truth, glory be to Him, willed the vagueness of the day and the time, for if it comes at night, a person at that time is generally heedless and asleep, and if it comes by day, a person during the day is occupied with the movement of life.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says in another place: ﴿Did the people of the towns feel secure that Our might would come upon them by night while they were sleeping?﴾ (7:97), and He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Or did the people of the towns feel secure that Our might would come upon them in the morning while they were playing?﴾ (7:98). If you look at reality, you will find that the punishment comes both at night and by day together, because there are lands where it is night, and at the same time it is day in other lands.

And when the punishment comes suddenly, and they try to declare faith, that faith will not benefit them, because the Truth, glory be to Him, says of one who takes this position: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters?﴾ (10:91). So if the punishment comes to you now, when you have hastened toward it, because declaring faith will not benefit you, and God will not accept it from you, then the punishment will befall you in this world, in addition to the punishment of the Hereafter. This hastening on your part toward the punishment doubles the punishment for you twice: in this world, and then the lasting punishment in the Hereafter.

¹ "Ba's" (bi's, might): Our punishment. And "al-ba's" means strength, as God says: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might...﴾ (57:25), that is, strength and firmness. His words: ﴿that God may restrain the might of those who disbelieve...﴾ (4:84), their severity and strength, so that it turns them away from you. His words, the Truth: ﴿and at the time of battle...﴾ (2:177), that is, at the time of fierce war. The Truth says: ﴿and coats of mail that protect you from your might...﴾ (16:81), that is, your severity and strength in war, so that armor protects you from the dangers of war. And "al-ba'saa'" means poverty and hardship, and the Truth says: ﴿and the patient in misfortune and adversity...﴾ (2:177), at the time of poverty and need.

Then the Truthful Lord (Allah, glorified is He) says after that:

﴿Is it only now, when it has already come to pass, that you believe in it, while you used to seek to hasten it?﴾

That is: when the punishment comes to pass, will you then believe?

The declaration of your faith at this time will not benefit you, and your punishment will be without any ransom.

So, your hastening of the punishment will not benefit you in any state, because faith at the moment the punishment descends does not benefit. An example of this is Pharaoh (1) when drowning overtook him: ﴿He said: "I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of those who submit."﴾ [Yunus: 90].

(1) This is because Pharaoh set out with a great army, estimated at one hundred thousand, and caught up with Moses at the edge of the sea at sunrise. Allah revealed to Moses that he should strike the sea with his staff: ﴿So We revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff." And it parted, and each part was like a great mountain.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 63]. Then Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in rebellion and enmity, until, when drowning overtook him, he said: "I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of those who submit."﴾ [Yunus: 90].

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Allah drowned Pharaoh, he said: 'I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe.' Jibril said: 'O Muhammad, if only you had seen me as I took mud from the bottom of the sea (i.e., the clay of the sea) and pushed it into his mouth (i.e., his mouth), for fear that mercy would overtake him.'" Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, and he said: this is a hasan (good) hadith. See the tafsirs of Ibn Kathir (2/430) and al-Qurtubi (4/3305).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 52:

The Truthful, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Then it will be said to those who did wrong, "Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?"﴾ (10:52)

This is information about the punishment that awaits those who disbelieved, which they will encounter on the Last Day. By their disbelief they have wronged themselves in the world, and they will encounter the punishment in the Hereafter, and it is ﴿the punishment of eternity﴾, meaning a punishment that does not end.

The Truthful, glorified is He, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?﴾ That is, the Truthful, glorified is He, did not wrong them. He conveyed to them the message of faith through a Messenger with a miracle, with a clear and supported method, and He gave them a long respite, but they did not benefit from it, because they did not believe.

So, ﴿they will encounter the punishment of eternity﴾. He, glorified is He, mentioned here the news of the punishment of eternity because the punishment of this world is limited in time; it contains disgrace and humiliation, but its being bounded within life makes it a small punishment compared with the everlasting punishment of the Hereafter.

The Truthful, glorified is He, mentioned the matter of the punishment of eternity as a matter of what they earned, and earning is an addition beyond the principal. Whoever trades with ten pounds may earn five pounds.

Here is a question: does the one who commits a sin gain beyond the principal? Yes, because Allah, glorified is He, forbade him something and he made it lawful for himself, so he takes an addition in the lawful and diminishes from the forbidden, while he thinks he has gained, by his imaginary understanding that the desire of the commanding self adorned for him. This means that he looks at the reality of the pleasure in itself and does not look at the consequences of that pleasure, and he thinks he has gained, although in reality he is a loser.

1 Al-khuld (eternity): permanence; the intended meaning is that it is a lasting punishment. [Lisan al-'Arab, root kh-l-d]
2 Allah the Exalted says: ﴿For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has earned.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:286]. So whoever makes the forbidden lawful and brings it upon himself must bear the consequences that follow from this; for him, by his righteous deed, is the gain, and against him, by his deed, is the thing that is the recompense of what he has earned.
3 Tab'at al-shay' (the consequence of a thing): its result, its outcome, and the effect that follows from it. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root t-b-']

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 53:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿They ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you cannot escape (Allah's power)."(53)﴾:

They had already said earlier: ﴿When is this promise...(48)﴾ [Yunus]: and here they have returned to questioning. ﴿They ask you﴾ means they seek from you the news (naba'). The naba' is the report concerning something great, and they seek the report from you, O Messenger of Allah, asking: "Is it true?" The word "true" (haqq) here carries many implications, because the pronoun ﴿it﴾ may refer to the origin of the religion: the Qur'an, prophethood, and legislation. It is a word that carries affirmation that the Qur'an is true, the legislation is true, prophethood for Muhammad (ﷺ) is true, the Resurrection and the Resurrection-after-death are true, and the speech about punishment in this world, through their humiliation and the victory of the believers over them, is true.

So their saying: ﴿They ask you, "Is it true?"(35)﴾ has more than one referent, as if they asked: "Is the Qur'an you have brought true? Is the prophethood you claim true? Is the legislation, which you say God sent down as a method governing human conduct, true? Are the Resurrection and the Resurrection-after-death true? Is punishment in this world true?" It is a comprehensive word that can be interpreted in more than one meaning.

The answer comes from God, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true"(35)﴾ [Yunus]. When someone asks you, "Is Zayd present?", you say, "Yes, he is present," and you do not say to him, "By God, Zayd is present," because you do not emphasize your speech to one who asks you, since he does not deny Zayd's presence.

So you do not emphasize an answer unless there is in the question a suspicion of denial. Thus you deduce from the words of the Truth, glory be to Him, ﴿They ask you, "Is it true?"(35)﴾ that their question carried meanings of denial and mockery; for this reason the answer came with "ay" (4), which is a particle of response meaning "yes," and "ay" always comes with an oath.

Each particle of response has its place: there is "balā," which comes in answer to a negative question, as in His saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord? They said, "Yes indeed."(172)﴾ [al-A'raf], and the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, here: ﴿Yes, by my Lord...(53)﴾ [Yunus]: meaning, "Yes, and I swear by my Lord that it is true." You do not swear to anything unless the questioner has a suspicion of denial, and you use "inna" for further emphasis.

An example of this is His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And set forth for them a parable: the people of the city (5), when the messengers came to it, (13) when We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We reinforced (6) them with a third, and they said, "Indeed we are messengers to you."(14)﴾ [Ya-Sin]. And what was the response of those to whom the three were sent?

﴿They said, "You are only human like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are only lying."(15)﴾ [Ya-Sin]: thus the deniers' denial of the three messengers was severe. The messengers said to them:

﴿Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you.(16)﴾ [Ya-Sin]: their saying was thus suited to the severe denial of the disbelievers.

So the emphasis in the speech of one addressed comes in proportion to the denial; if there is no denial, there is no need for emphasis.

If the speech meets with slight denial, the emphasis comes once. If the speech meets with obstinacy in denial, the emphasis comes twice. If the speech meets with arrogant denial, the emphasis comes three times.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, taught His Messenger (ﷺ) to answer their asking by saying: ﴿Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true...(53)﴾ [Yunus]. Here the Messenger (ﷺ) swears by the Lord, because the Lord is the One who charged him; then he emphasizes ﴿it is indeed true﴾ because their question contained denial and mockery.

Since He has said, ﴿Yes, by my Lord, it is true,﴾ if they do not believe, they will surely meet punishment, for there is no escape from God, and you cannot escape God by flight, nor can you escape Him through intercession from anyone, nor through ransom, nor through a friend who comes forward to intercede for you.

Then His saying, glory be to Him, at the end of the verse: ﴿And you cannot escape (Allah's power).(53)﴾ [Yunus]: the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to explain a glimpse of His inimitable power, for God, glory be to Him and exalted, may accept the intercession of intercessors, and may accept ransom; therefore the clarification came in the following verse, where He says:

﴿And if every soul that wronged had all that is on the earth, it would surely offer it for ransom. And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment. And they will be judged with justice, and they will not be wronged.(54)﴾:

1 ay: yes. A particle of response...
2 i.e., that you will not escape God in that He will restore you after your death, gather you, and punish you for what you used to earn...
3 The naba' is news, or news of great importance. God says: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news (1-2)﴾ [al-Naba'], and this news is the Resurrection. Anba'ahu bi-l-shay' and banna'ahu bihi: informed him of it. Anba' takes one direct object, as in ﴿Inform them of their names (33)﴾ [al-Baqarah]; it takes two objects, as in ﴿She said, "Who informed you of this?"(3)﴾ [al-Tahrim]; and it may take the preposition "'an," as in ﴿And inform them about the guests of Abraham (51)﴾ [al-Hijr], meaning: tell them. Istanba'ahu: asked that he inform him, as in God's saying: ﴿They ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true..."(53)﴾ [Yunus].
4 ay: a particle of response, like "na'am" (yes). It occurs after an oath, as in God's saying: ﴿They ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true..."(53)﴾ [Yunus].
5 It is said to be Antioch, between Syria and Turkey, and it may be another village. Its king worshipped idols, so God sent to him three messengers, and he denied them. From Tafsir Ibn Kathir (3/568), with adaptation.
6 'Azzazna: strengthened and reinforced.
7 al-fida': what is offered of wealth or the like to free the one ransomed. God says: ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice (107)﴾ [al-Saffat]. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root f-d-y]
8 He regretted what he did, regrets, and regret (nadama, nadam, nadamah), and in the pattern of fariḥa: he felt sorrow and grief and wished he had not done it. God says: ﴿And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment (54)﴾ [Yunus]. And nadim is the active participle; the Truth says: ﴿and he became among the regretful (31)﴾ [al-Ma'idah].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 54:

When the punishment comes, man desires to flee from it, even by ransom.

See how a person tries to free himself by giving up everything he owns as a ransom for his soul, even if he possessed everything in the heavens and the earth(1).

But could anyone other than God, glory be to Him, possess the heavens and the earth? Of course not.

So evil cannot come about. Suppose it did come about: ransom by possessing what is in the heavens and the earth would still not avail, because the wrongdoer in this world has taken the right of another, and that other person has earned by a lawful way what the wrongdoer took from him. The wrongdoer is only taking the fruit of someone else's work. If that were valid, some people would turn into usurpers of others' rights, and would seize the sweat and toil of others, and the movement of life would come to a halt.

For this reason, if God, glory be to Him and exalted, does not restrain the wrongdoer in this world before the Hereafter, oppression would spread. When oppression spreads in a society, unemployment spreads in it, and every person tries to take from the blood and sweat of others, and thereby the balance of justice is disturbed and the whole movement of life is corrupted.

Suppose the wrongdoer took the whole kingdom of this world and wished to ransom himself with it at the hour the punishment comes, and then discovers that his earnings from what is unlawful are not accepted as ransom. Is this not the great loss? This is a phenomenon found in people's worlds.

Suppose someone took bribes, embezzled, or stole, and the law catches him by the collar(2), and he says: "Take what I have and leave me." The authorities of the law will not accept that. Even if such a concession happens in customs, where we see someone give up smuggled goods in exchange for his release, this is what happens in this world, but it will not happen in the Hereafter.

In Surat al-Baqarah the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And beware of a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:48].

And the Truth, glory be to Him, said in another verse: ﴿And beware of a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:123].

Some skeptics claimed that the two verses are identical, and they did not notice that each verse differs from the other in placing compensation first and intercession later.

True eloquence is manifest in the two verses, because the reader of the beginning of each of them, and the one who understands the Arabic linguistic faculty, knows that the end of each verse fits its beginning.

Whoever reads the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And beware of a Day when no soul will avail another soul...(48)﴾ [al-Baqarah],

sees that he is before two souls: the first soul is the one that offers intercession, and the second soul is the one for whom intercession is made. Here, intercession is not accepted from the first soul, and likewise compensation is not accepted.

In the second verse, neither intercession nor compensation is accepted from the soul for whom intercession is made; it tries first to offer compensation, then when that does not benefit it, it brings the intercessor.

Thus the advancing and delaying in the two verses come appropriately to the situation in each of them.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And if every soul that had wronged had all that is in the earth, it would surely ransom itself with it...(54)﴾ [Yunus]. In this statement, a single soul is shown to be incapable of possessing all that is in the earth; and even if we supposed this soul possessed it, it would not be able to ransom itself with it. The result is what the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And they will conceal regret when they see the punishment...(54)﴾ [Yunus]. That is: they will hide the grief that comes to the soul, having no outward sign of verbal or physical distress.

Indeed each of them keeps his anxiety in his heart, because at the moment he sees the punishment he is astonished, struck senseless and speechless(5) by the terror of the punishment, so his blood freezes and he cannot even cry out. In this way he suppresses his pain within himself, because the terror of the situation freezes every drop of blood in their veins and silences their tongues, and he cannot speak, because he is unable to express himself physically through screaming or pain.

We know that physical expression is a form of bodily release, and when a person cannot do it, he suffers more.

They, therefore, conceal their regret when they see the frightening, agonizing punishment. The speech here is about the wrongdoers, and despite their wrongdoing, the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And it will be judged between them with justice(6), and they will not be wronged(54)﴾ [Yunus]. These people, despite their disbelief and their deserving of punishment, receive justice from God. Suppose a disbeliever, far removed from religion, wronged another disbeliever: would God, glory be to Him, stand toward this matter in a neutral position?

No, because the right of God's creature, the wronged disbeliever, requires that God, glory be to Him, exact retribution for him from his disbelieving wrongdoing brother, since the disbelieving wrongdoer wronged a creature of God, even if the wronged party was a disbeliever.

For this reason God judges between them with truth, meaning He lightens for the wronged some of the punishment to the degree that it burdens the wrongdoer.

This is the meaning of ﴿And it will be judged between them﴾, because it requires a judgment, that is, lack of partiality, and requires separating two disputes.

From this judgment follows a ruling; therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, shows us that they, although they disbelieved in Him, if one of them wrongs another, the Truth is the Lord of all and the Creator of all, just as He gave them, by the law of lordship, every good as He gave the believers. He, glory be to Him, is the One who gave the sun, the water, the air, and all means of provision and sustenance to all people, believers and disbelievers. So if wrong happens between people of the same religion, or non-religious people, the Truth, glory be to Him, must judge it with separation and rule with justice.

1 He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The guilty one would wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his children(11), and his spouse and his brother(12), and his family that shelters him(13), and everyone on earth, then that it would save him(14)﴾ [al-Ma'arij]..
2 Al-talabib: the gathered parts of a man's garment. And talbib: gathering the garment that one wears at the chest, throat and pulling it.[Lisan, root l-b-b]..
3 Al-'adl: an equivalent ransom. God, exalted, says: ﴿Nor will compensation be taken from it(48)﴾ [al-Baqarah], meaning: it will not be saved from the punishment by paying an equivalent ransom, nor will it be accepted from it. 'Adl al-shay' and 'adalahu: he set it up and made it even; the Truth says: ﴿Who created you and proportioned you and balanced you(7)﴾ [al-Infitar]. 'Adala al-mushrik bi-rabbihi: he made a rival equal to Him. God, exalted, says: ﴿Then those who disbelieve, in their Lord they ascribe equals(1)﴾ [al-An'am], and what is negated is that they make equal to Him anything else, for there is nothing like Him. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Rather, they are a people who ascribe equals (to Him)(60)﴾ [al-Naml], meaning they make a co-equal partner for Him. As for His saying: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by truth and by it act justly(181)﴾ [al-A'raf], meaning they judge with justice [al-Qamus al-Qawim]..
4 That is: the first verse speaks of the non-acceptance from the interceding soul, and the second verse speaks of the non-acceptance of compensation first and intercession second from the soul for whom intercession is made; this is what is understood from the intended meanings of the Shaykh, may God be pleased with him..
5 Yabhat: that is, the terror of what is happening overcomes him, so he stops speaking or doing anything else..
6 Al-qist: what is meant here is justice.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.﴾ (10:55)

"Ala" (ألا), in the language, is described as "an particle of alerting" (أداة تنبيه) — it alerts the listener that the speaker is about to say, after it, something of the utmost importance. The speaker, as we know, controls his own tongue by virtue of his position as speaker, but the listener is in a state of being taken by surprise.

A speaker may utter what has passed through his mind in order to bring it out on his tongue to the addressee, but the addressee is caught off guard, and until he pays attention he may miss a word or two of what the speaker says.

Allah, glorified and exalted, wants no word of His to be missed by the listener, so He brought an alerting particle that draws attention to the statement that follows it, which is the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth..﴾ (10:55). Thus the Truth, glorified be He, willed that the alerting particle precede the universal matter, which is that He, glorified be He, is the Owner of everything. He is the One who created the universe and created man as the vicegerent (khalifah), and subjected the universe to the vicegerent man, and ordained that causes submit to what their agents bring about; so whoever strives and brings about the causes, they give to him, whether he is a believer or a disbeliever.

When causes serve a man, and this man is heedless of his Lord or of belief in Him, and thinks that causes have submitted to him by his own strength, and is seduced by those causes, and says as Qarun said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I possess.﴾ (28:78)

So whoever forgets the Causer of causes and attaches himself directly to causes, he will receive punishment, and if not in this world then in the Hereafter. It is as if the Truth, glorified be He, is alerting them: "Be alert, O ignorant ones, and understand this great matter: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth..﴾ (10:55)."

So beware, O man, of being deceived by causes, or thinking that by your means you have taken other than what Allah wills for you; for He, glorified be He, is the One who gave you and decreed for you, and all causes interact for you by the giving and decree of Allah, mighty and majestic.

The changes of the universe are evidence of this: your mind with which you plan may be struck by the affliction of madness, and the limbs such as the hand, the foot, the tongue, the eye, or the ear may be afflicted with some illness, so you do not know how to act.

Everything in which changes occur is not from your essence, and everything you possess is a gift to you from the Causer of causes.

So beware of looking at causes and forgetting the Causer, for Allah is the owner of the things you possess and of the tools by which you possess them; the proof is that He, glorified be He, when He wills, takes them away from you. So be alert, O heedless one, and beware of thinking that causes are the doers; the proof is that Allah, glorified and exalted, creates causes, then wills that they not bring about their results, like one who plants cotton seeds, for example, and plows the land, and waters it at its appointed times, then the cotton worm comes and eats the crop. Thus the return of everything owned is to Allah, exalted.

Know that there is ownership (mulk) and there is ownership. The "milk" (ملك) is what you possess: a robe, or a house, or a donkey, and so on. As for "mulk" (الملك), it is that you possess the one who has ownership and control over it, so the summit, then, is in mulk.

Consider the saying of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will..﴾ (3:26). So, sovereignty in this world belongs entirely to Allah, glorified be He.

The word "ala" came at the beginning of the verse under our present reflections to alert the one heedless of the Truth, because the causes responded to him and gave him results, so he was deceived by them; therefore Allah, glorified be He, makes causes differ in some things, so that man remains tied to the Causer.

The Truth, glorified be He, says in the same verse: ﴿Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is true..﴾ (10:55). A promise, if it concerns good, is good tidings of good that will occur, and if it concerns evil, it is a warning of evil that will occur; and the word "wa'id" (وعيد) predominates for it. So, for the most part, the word "wa'd" (وعد) comes for both good and evil, whereas the word "wa'id" comes only for evil.

A promise is: information about something that will happen from one who has the power to make it happen. Carrying out a promise has elements: first, the doer; second, the object; third, the time; fourth, the place; then the cause.

An event requires capacity. If you say, "I will come to you tomorrow at such-and-such place to speak with you about such-and-such matter," what do you possess of the elements of this event? You cannot guarantee your life until tomorrow, and the one listening to you does not own his life; likewise the place you specify for the meeting may be struck by something that destroys it, and the subject you want to speak about may occur to you as a thought that you should not speak about it before the meeting takes place.

Suppose all the elements came together: what do you or anyone else possess of the elements of the promise? Nothing at all.

For this reason Allah, glorified be He, teaches His creatures the courtesy of not giving promises they do not possess, so He says: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," (23) unless [You add], "If Allah wills."(24)﴾ (18:23-24). When you put forward the will of Allah, then if something happens that prevents carrying out the promise, you will not be a liar.

Thus our Lord teaches us to safeguard our reports from falsehood, and made us speak within the scope of our capacities; and our capacities contain no element of the event. But when Allah, glorified be He, speaks and promises, there is no repeller of what He has promised, glorified be He, because He is exempt from breaking the appointment; for the elements of all events submit to His will, glorified be He, and do not refuse Him, and His promise is true and firm. As for you, the changes that the Truth, glorified be He, causes to run upon you control you.

Suppose you wanted to build a house, and told the engineer the specific specifications you want in this house, but the engineer was unable to buy from the markets some of the materials you specified; so you wanted what the engineer does not have the power to dispose of.

But the matter differs with respect to the Supreme Creator, glorified be He; for He is the One who owns everything, and when He promises, His promise becomes certain to be carried out, but the disbelievers deny this; therefore Allah, glorified be He, said: ﴿But most of them do not know (10:55)﴾, meaning: they do not know this reality, for they had already said: ﴿When is this promise..﴾ (10:48). Or that ﴿most of them do not know﴾ means: man must not commit himself to an appointment without making the will (of Allah) a condition, for he possesses none of the elements of any promise except what Allah, exalted be He, wills.

1 "Wa'ada" (وعده) — he promised something, promises it, a promise (wa'd) and a promise (ida): he informed him that he would bring it about for him or give it to him; it takes two objects, and one of the two sayings may be omitted because it is known. Allah said: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best..(95)﴾ (4:95): "kullan" is the first object placed first, and "al-husna" is the second object; i.e., Allah informed them that He would give them the best of ranks. The promise comes often for good and sometimes for evil, as in His saying: ﴿Satan threatens you with poverty..(268)﴾ (2:268), i.e., he warns you and frightens you with evil; the verb takes two objects: "kum" is the first, and "al-faqr" is the second. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted]

2 Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Moses, but he oppressed them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would surely burden a band of strong men. When his people said to him, "Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not like the exultant."(76)﴾ (28:76). Qarun was the cousin of Moses, peace be upon him. Allah gave him wealth deposited in treasuries, so that its keys could not be carried by a group of people because of their abundance and weight; so Allah destroyed him for his oppression, his exultation in his wealth, and his arrogance toward people. His saying ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I possess..(78)﴾ (28:78)... and his recompense was: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And he did not have any company to help him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.(81)﴾ (28:81).

3 Mulk (الملك): in concrete, perceptible things it is literal, and in meanings it is figurative. From the literal sense Allah said: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling them..(23)﴾ (27:23), and from the figurative sense His saying: ﴿Or who owns hearing and sight..(31)﴾ (10:31). "Malik" is an active participle, its plural "malikun," Allah said: ﴿So they are to it masters..(71)﴾ (36:71). "Mamluk" is a passive participle, as in His saying: ﴿Allah presents an example: a slave owned..(75)﴾ (16:75). "Mulk" is a verbal noun, Allah said: ﴿They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our own choice..(87)﴾ (20:87), i.e., by our will and choice. "Mulk" as a verbal noun in the sense of authority, Allah said: ﴿...upon the kingdom of Solomon..(102)﴾ (2:102), i.e., in the time of the kingdom of Solomon. "Al-malik" means the ruler, Allah said: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will select him for myself..(54)﴾ (12:54), who was Pharaoh. It was also read "Malik Yawm al-Din" and "Malik Yawm al-Din." "Al-Malik," "al-Malik," and "al-Malik" are among the Beautiful Names of Allah. "Al-Malakut" means the great kingdom, which belongs to Allah alone; Allah said: ﴿...in whose hand is the realm of all things..(83)﴾ (36:83). "Al-malik" is the singular of "al-mala'ikah" (angels). [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted]

4 Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned that a delegation of the Quraysh disbelievers went to rabbis of the Jews asking them about the description of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying to them: "You are the People of the First Book, and you have knowledge of the prophets that we do not have." So the Jews instructed the Quraysh disbelievers to ask Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about three matters, among them: "Ask him about the youths of the former age, what was their affair, for they had a remarkable story." They asked him, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "I will inform you tomorrow of what you asked about," and he did not add an exception, i.e., he did not say, "If Allah wills." So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained fifteen nights without revelation coming to him about that, and then this verse was revealed. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (3/71).

5 Ta'abbi (التأبى): it is refusal and non-submission. Ibaa' (الإباء): is stronger refusal. [Al-Lisan: root abā]

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ (56)

We know that the movement of life, and dominion and sovereignty, are branches from the living, and He, glorified is He, is Living, because He is the Owner of the origin; and He is capable of causing death. Everything that proceeds from life, Allah, glorified is He, strips it away through death. He is the Owner of things and of the causes that produce things, and nothing escapes Him of promise or threat. We live by His will, glorified is He, and we die by His will, glorified is He, so we will not escape from Him. Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and to Him you will be returned.﴾ So whoever does not take warning from the matter of living things, let him be restrained by the fear of the return.

(1) Salaba al-shay' yuslubuhu, from the pattern of nasara, salban: he took it from him by force, or snatched it away. The Truth says: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it...﴾ (73) [al-Hajj], i.e., it pulls out from them something. It is a verb that takes two objects (al-Qamus al-Qawim).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 10, verse 57:

The Truthful (al-Haqq) subhanahu then says:

﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a cure for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.(57)﴾

The address here is to all of mankind, because when the Truthful subhanahu addresses the believers with His words, Exalted is He, ﴿O you who have believed...(104)﴾ [al-Baqarah], this is an address to those who have believed in the method (al-manhaj).

The Truthful subhanahu addresses mankind in general with the fundamentals of belief, such as the words of the Truthful subhanahu: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord...(1)﴾ [al-Nisa']. As for the believers, He, subhanahu, charges them with address directed to them, such as His words: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you...(183)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

And like the words of the Truthful: ﴿O you who have believed, prescribed for you is retribution (al-qisas)(1) for the murdered...(178)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. That is: His address subhanahu to the believers is always in the rulings by which the believers are addressed, whereas in the fundamentals of belief and the highest faith in the One who brings into existence, it is an address to mankind in general.

The Truthful subhanahu says here: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition...(57)﴾ [Yunus]. The verse here depicts the admonition as though it had taken on a body and had come, although the admonition is words; and God, exalted is He, intended by this to give the admonition the image of movement that influences and urges toward faith.

The admonition (al-maw'itha)(2) is advising toward good and distancing from evil with an affecting expression. It is said: so-and-so is a distinguished preacher (wa'iz mutamayyiz), meaning that his speech wins hearts and his style is affecting and beautiful. The one being admonished is always weaker than the admonisher, and the soul of the one being admonished is heavy, so it does not accept admonition with ease except from one who excels at influence through beauty of word and sincerity of delivery(3); because the one being admonished may say to himself: "You have seen me in a position below you, and you want to raise me, while you are higher than me." So if the admonisher takes this circumstance of the one being admonished into account, he wins over his soul.

Let us recall the saying of wisdom: "Counsel is heavy, so do not make it a debate, nor send it as a mountain; and borrow for it lightness of expression." This is so that you win the hearing ear to you, and bring to him an eloquent, convincing, pleasing style that delights him, and touch in his soul the core of what you wish to reach it.

The admonition differs from the bequest (al-wasiyya), because the bequest usually comes only as the essence of the wisdom of things. Suppose a man is ill and has children, and death is upon him; he writes his bequest and enjoins them with the essentials of matters (`uyun al-masa'il)(4).

The Truthful subhanahu says here: ﴿there has certainly come to you an admonition...(57)﴾ [Yunus]. The admonition is either something you hear or you reject it. And because it is an admonition that has come ﴿from your Lord﴾, there must be attentiveness and awareness. Note that the Truthful subhanahu has singled out the admonition as being from the Lord (Rabb), not from the God (Ilah); because the God (Ilah) wants you to be a worshipper, but the Lord (Rabb) is the Nurturer and Guarantor, even if you disbelieve in Him.

This admonition comes from the Lord, that is, it is from the perfections of nurturing (tarbiya). We know that the matters pertaining to lordship (rububiyya) are distributed between two categories: The first category is the necessities of life which God, the Truthful, gives, of sustenance and provision, and these necessities are for the believer and for the disbeliever. The other category is the necessities of values that outline the method of life's movement, and these are for the believer only.

Therefore, the admonition is a kind of nurturing that has come from your Lord, the trustworthy over you; because He is the one who created from non-existence and sustained from non-existence, and His blessing of lordship has not been reserved for believers only, but His grace has embraced all creation.

Therefore, the admonition comes from One who gives and does not expect anything from you, for He, subhanahu, is exempt from purpose, because He will gain nothing from you(5); you have no power over anything with His power, subhanahu.

The admonition that comes with the method is specific to rational, rightly-guided people, because the movement of the rational, rightly-guided person passes through his intellect first, and he chooses among alternatives; whereas the movement of the insane is disordered and unarranged, and does not pass through his intellect, because his perception is deranged and he lacks the capacity to choose among alternatives.

But why does a rational person's choice among alternatives become corrupted? What corrupts the rational person's choosing is desire (hawa), and desire arises only from what is in the soul and the heart. Therefore the Truthful subhanahu and exalted, in the verse about which we are reflecting, says: ﴿there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a cure for what is in the breasts...(57)﴾ [Yunus]. That is: He, subhanahu, has sent down to you what cures your breasts of rancor that affects your judgments, and of hatred, envy and deceit, and purifies the inner self of the human being; because every movement of a human being has an emotional source, and the emotional source must be healed so that it may be sound; so that the movements that come out of the limbs emerge from a pure, refined and sound conscience; and thus the movements issuing from the human being are sound(7).

For this reason the Truthful subhanahu said: ﴿and a cure for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers(57)﴾ [Yunus]. The word "cure" (shifa') came first, to show that true guidance to the straight path requires expelling from the heart what desires it contains, and then directing it to the straight method.

If someone asks about the difference between cure and mercy, we answer: cure is the removal of what sickens the breasts, whereas mercy is the following of guidance with what does not bring sickness back again. Read, if you wish, the words of the Truthful subhanahu: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a cure and a mercy for the believers...(82)﴾ [al-Isra']. Thus the effect of the admonition becomes clear to us: cure, guidance and mercy; it treats not only the surface symptoms of illness but treats the roots of illness.

Therefore, the cure of the breasts must occur first; for this reason we find that the skilled physician is the one who does not look only at the surface symptoms in order to treat them, but seeks what lies behind those symptoms, unlike the untrained, hasty physician who treats surface symptoms without treating the roots of the illness.

An example of this: the unskilled dermatologist, when he sees pustules, treats them with what hides and temporarily removes them, but they return after a little while; whereas the trained, understanding physician treats the causes that produce the pustules and removes them with effective treatment, thus eliminating the causes of their appearance.

In the Noble Qur'an we find the story of the trial of our master Ayyub, peace be upon him. The Truthful subhanahu said to him: ﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool washing-place and a drink(42)﴾ [Sad]. That is: strike the ground with your foot at that place, and cool water will come out for you from it; wash in it, and it removes the apparent symptoms, and drink from it to treat the root of the disease.

Therefore, the admonition is as though it had taken on a body, so it came from your Lord, the trustworthy over you, as a cure, to treat the inner states (mawajid) from which actions issue, so that they become sound and upright inner states, without corruption in them; and guidance to the path that leads to the true goal; and mercy, for whoever follows it the human being is not afflicted by any disease. This admonition leads to righteous deeds acceptable to God subhanahu.

But if the four fruits that issue from the admonition are sound for you: the cure, the guidance, the mercy, and righteous action, beware of rejoicing in them; for above all that is God's grace upon you. Therefore the Truthful subhanahu says:

﴿Say: "In the bounty of God and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."(58)﴾

1 Qisas: is the imposition of punishment for one who killed or wounded another, by the like of what he did; it is a law that the Torah brought and that the law of Islam upheld. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein: life for life, eye for eye, nose for nose, ear for ear, tooth for tooth, and for wounds is retribution...(45)﴾ [al-Ma'ida].
2 Wa'aza, ya'izuhu, wa'zan wa 'iza: he advised him to obedience and righteous action, and guided him to good. God, the Exalted, said depicting the obstinacy of the disbelievers: ﴿They said, "It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers"(136)﴾ [al-Shu'ara'], for in their obstinacy both matters are alike to them. The admonition (al-maw'itha) is what one is admonished with, of speech or deed, as in His words: ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing(66)﴾ [al-Baqara], and He said: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition...(125)﴾ [al-Nahl]. The admonition has rhetorical preliminaries from a faithful logic. Root w-‘-z, adapted. From "al-Qamus al-Qawim".
3 The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the good example and the highest model in wise admonition. It is related from al-'Irbad ibn Sariya who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood among us one day and admonished us with an eloquent admonition, by which hearts trembled and eyes shed tears... The hadith was related by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (42), al-Tirmidhi (2676), and Ahmad in his Musnad (4/126, 127).
4 In "'uyun al-masa'il": that is, its roots and what is important in it; and the "eye" (ayn) of every thing is its best part. [Lisan al-'Arab: root '-y-n]
