5 The Qur'an has given us an example of this in the sacrificial animals brought by pilgrims, where He, subhanahu, says: ﴿Their meat does not reach God, nor their blood, but what reaches Him is piety from you. Thus He has subjected them to you that you may glorify God for having guided you; and give good tidings to the good-doers(37)﴾ [al-Hajj].
6 Badala: to replace a thing with another; and badala al-kalam: to change and distort speech. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿But those who did wrong substituted a word other than that which had been said to them, so We sent upon those who did wrong a punishment from the sky because they were defiantly disobedient(59)﴾ [al-Baqara], that is, they changed it into other speech. And the Truthful said: ﴿except for one who wrongs and then substitutes good after evil; indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful(11)﴾ [al-Naml], that is, he does good and righteousness after doing evil. And one thing may be substituted for another: abdala al-shay' ja'alahu badalan minhu, and tabaddala al-shay' bi-al-shay' wa min al-shay' ja'alahu badalan minhu, as in His words: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses; and God is ever Watchful over all things(52)﴾ [al-Ahzab].
7 It is related from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (52) and Muslim in his Sahih (1599).
8 God, subhanahu, tested His servant and prophet Ayyub, peace be upon him, with illness in his body and the loss of his wealth and children. This trial continued for eighteen years, which he lived patient with God's decree, and none remained with him except his wife, who was forced to work serving people until she secured food for herself and her husband. When Ayyub called upon his Lord: ﴿And Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful"(83)﴾ [al-Anbiya'], God responded to him and removed the harm from him, when He said to him: ﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool washing-place and a drink(42)﴾ [Sad]. God commanded him to stand and strike the earth with his foot, and he did so, and God caused a spring to gush forth from the earth, and commanded him to wash in it, and he removed all the affliction that was on his body; then He commanded him to strike the earth in another place, and he did so, and God caused another spring to gush forth for him, and commanded him to drink from it; so all the evil that was within him was removed, and his well-being was completed outwardly and inwardly. [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 4/39, 40.] And He, subhanahu, said of him: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant; indeed, he was one who turned back in repentance(44)﴾ [Sad].
9 Al-mawajid: what is meant by them are the actions of the heart, which if they are upright, the limbs become upright.

You and all the believers, however much you act to apply God's method, we will never, through our acts of worship, render the due of the blessings we already possess before we were charged with obligations. We must reflect on the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God covers me with His mercy." So if a person boasts of his obedience to God, that obedience returns to the servant's benefit in this world, and he will not, by his obedience, render the due of all the blessings God has bestowed upon him.

An example of this: the servant is not charged with obligations until he reaches puberty, that is, at around the age of fifteen. If he considers the blessings God Almighty has bestowed upon him until he reached this age, he will not be able to count them. How much more so the blessings that surround us throughout our whole lives. And when the Truth (al-Haqq) recompenses us in the Hereafter, He does not recompense us with justice, but treats us with grace (fadl).

So, beware of saying: "I gave charity such-and-such, or I prayed such-and-such," lest your compliance with God's method give you conceit in your worship. Remember the well-known saying: "A sin that produces humility and brokenness is better than an obedience that produces pride and arrogance."

1 Taghammadahu Allah bi-rahmatihi (God covered him with His mercy): He entered him into it and immersed him in it. Abu 'Ubayd said: the saying "yataghammadani" means: He clothes me, envelops me, and covers me. [Lisan al-'Arab, root gh-m-d]
2 Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6463) and Muslim in his Sahih (2816) from Abu Hurayrah.
3 And the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿And if you should count the favor of God, you could not enumerate it﴾ [an-Nahl: 18]. He, glorified is He, used the singular "favor" here, because every blessing of God upon you, even if you regard it as one in your view, contains blessings that cannot be counted or enumerated. How much more so when the blessings are taken together.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 59:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say: "Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you have made some of it forbidden and some lawful?" Say: "Has God permitted you, or do you invent against God?"﴾ (59)

The enjoyment a person has in life, whether through dominion (mulk) or possession (milk), all of it requires the preservation of life by the provision that the Truth, glory be to Him, gives us, and likewise the preservation of the species by the pairing of male and female.

But the provision that preserves life must be lawful (halal). For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has defined for us the prohibited things, so do not approach them, and it is incumbent upon you to abide by what God has specified. Do not go beyond what God has made lawful in order to make it forbidden, for the Truth, glory be to Him, has specified for you from among the food what will preserve your life and give you fuel for the movement of life. So treat yourself as you treat the machine you make: you give every machine the appropriate fuel so that it can perform its task. Likewise, God, glory be to Him, has made for you the specifications that benefit you, from which you derive benefit and by whose energy you carry out the movements of life, through what God has made lawful for you. And likewise God has forbidden you what harms you.

Beware of saying: "Since these things harm me, why did God create them?" For you must know that there is a difference between direct provision and indirect provision. Everything in the universe is provision, but it is divided into direct provision, from which you benefit immediately, and indirect provision. An example of this is fire: you do not eat fire, but it cooks your food for you. Thus there is something created for a task that helps in producing what benefits you.

The Truth, glory be to Him, has made lawful for you, for example, the flesh of sheep and goats, and camels and cattle and others, and has forbidden you the flesh of swine (2). So do not ask: "Why did God create the swine?" For He created it for another task: it gathers up and consumes the filth of existence. This is indirect provision, so leave it to the task for which God intended it.

Some people have forbidden to themselves things that God the Exalted has made lawful (3), and by doing so they constrict themselves. Some think that when they make lawful what God has forbidden, they widen things for themselves. So the Truth, glory be to Him, commands His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say: ﴿Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision...﴾ (59) [Yunus]: that is, tell me what God has sent down to you of provision, which is everything from which you benefit, either directly or through intermediaries. How then do you interfere with declaring things lawful and unlawful, when the One who sent down the provision has already made clear to you the lawful and the unlawful?

The word ﴿sent down﴾ indicates that all provision comes from above (4), and everything you see around you is provision, from which you benefit directly or indirectly. The money with which you buy most provisions is not eaten by a person; rather, it is with it that one buys what one eats.

The word ﴿sent down﴾ means: brought into existence, and created from above. Since everything has come into being by His will, from One who is above all existence, then everything is for your benefit, directly or through intermediaries.

Do not take the word ﴿sent down﴾ in the sense of sensory height; take it in the sense of immaterial height. Rain, for example, descends from above in the sensory sense, and mingles with the earth, so that plants take their nourishment from it; provision by rain and from the earth is determined by the One who created, and He is the Most High, glory be to Him.

The Truth, glory be to Him, has said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance that people may uphold justice, and We sent down iron, wherein is mighty violence and benefits for people (5)...﴾ (25) [al-Hadid].

Yes, the Truth, glory be to Him, sent down His methodology upon the messengers, peace be upon them, so that people's lives might be set right, and He also sent down iron, which we extract from the mountains and the earth.

So the meaning of "sending down" here is bringing into existence, from One who is higher than you, for your benefit, O human being.

Since the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who sent down provision and explained the lawful and the unlawful, why do you thrust your noses into the lawful and the unlawful, making some of the lawful unlawful, and some of the unlawful, or all of the unlawful, lawful? Why do you not leave the determining to the One who created, He who knows better what is in your interest?

﴿Has God permitted you...﴾ (59): that is, has God given you authorization to make the lawful unlawful and the unlawful lawful? ﴿Or do you invent against God?﴾ (59): that is, do you deliberately lie against God?

The Truth, glory be to Him, brought the lawful and the unlawful in order to show us how ugly is the conduct of forbidding what God has made lawful and permitting what God has forbidden.

The Truth, glory be to Him, in summarizing this verse, points to other verses that detailed the unlawful, which we have previously discussed in our reflections, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God did not ordain any bahira, sa'iba, wasila, or ham, but those who disbelieve invent lies against God, and most of them do not reason (103)﴾ [al-Ma'ida]. The bahira, as we have mentioned, is the she-camel that has borne five litters, the last of which was a male; they would slit her ear, announce that she had fulfilled her duty, and leave her free-pasturing (6), unowned, no one riding her, no one loading her with any load, no one milking her, no one shearing her wool; then the attendants of the idols they worshipped would slaughter her. They named her "bahira" (7) because they slit her ears as a sign that she had discharged her task.

As for the sa'iba, it is the one that is not tied, because tying indicates ownership. A man, if he recovered from an illness, or wished for something (8), would vow to make a she-camel for the attendants of the idols, named sa'iba; it likewise was not ridden, not milked, not loaded, and no one would touch it.

The wasila is the female that the she-camel bears in a single litter together with a male, so they say: "She has joined her brother," and so they would not slaughter the male for the idols, for the sake of his sister.

﴿Nor ham﴾: the ham is the stallion that protects his back by fathering ten litters; after that no one rides him, no one loads him, and he is left for the attendants of the idols.

These are the permitted livestock which they forbade to themselves, while the attendants of the idols would eat them; and in mentioning the non-prohibition of those livestock there is a mercy toward them. There is also His saying, the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Eight mates: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say: "Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful (143). And of the camels two, and of the cattle two. Say: "Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you? Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against God to lead people astray without knowledge? Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people (144)﴾ [al-An'am]. So they had forbidden some of what God had made lawful to them, and they said what the Qur'an reports: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created (9) of the tilth and the livestock, and they say: "This is for God, by their claim (10), and this is for our partners." But what is for their partners does not reach God, and what is for God reaches their partners. Evil is what they judge (136)﴾ [al-An'am].

The Truth, glory be to Him, summarized all of that in His true saying: ﴿Say: "Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you have made some of it forbidden and some lawful?" Say: "Has God permitted you, or do you invent against God?"﴾ (59). Thus they intervened in forbidding some of the lawful and making lawful some of the unlawful, and in this there is an transgression of what they ought to have refrained from committing (11); for the Truth, glory be to Him, is their Creator and the Creator of their provision, and in this there is a deliberate lie against God, glory be to Him.

(1) Says the Lord of Honour, glory be to Him: ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and what has been dedicated to other than God...(115)﴾ [al-Nahl].
(2) Says the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress; indeed God does not love transgressors (87). And eat of what God has provided for you, lawful and good, and fear God, in whom you are believers (88)﴾ [al-Ma'ida].
(3) Says the Truth, glory be to Him, concerning Ya'qub, peace be upon him: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was sent down. Say: "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful" (93)﴾ [Al 'Imran].
(4) Says the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised (22)﴾ [al-Dhariyat]. So the descent of rain from the sky is a provision that God sends down, by which the dead earth is made to live and produces crops, from which every living creature on the earth eats, whether human or animal. ﴿Indeed, the likeness of the life of this world is like water which We send down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it, of which men and livestock eat...(24)﴾ [Yunus].
(5) Al-bayyinat: the clear signs. Al-qist here: justice. Al-ba's: strength. [Lisan al-'Arab].
(6) Al-sa'iba: sheep and livestock that graze wherever they wish. Al-sa'im: one that goes off in whatever direction it wishes. [Lisan, root s-w-m].
(7) The reason for the name "bahira" is that the slit in its ear is wide, resembling the sea in its breadth (adapted from Ahkam al-Qur'an of al-Jassas, 2/608). On the precise referent of the bahira, whether it is the she-camel that bore five litters or her daughter who bore in the last litter, there is difference of opinion; see Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/107-108) and likewise Ahkam al-Qur'an of al-Jassas. For this reason some say that the sa'iba is the mother of the bahira.
(8) In the pre-Islamic era, a man who returned from a long journey, or from an illness, or whom a beast had saved from hardship or war, would say: "My she-camel is sa'iba," meaning she is set loose, so that her back is not used, she is not kept from water, not prevented from pasture, and not ridden. [Mentioned by Ibn Manzur in Lisan, root s-y-b].
(9) Dhara'a: created. Al-harth: the crops and fruits.
(10) Bi-za'mihim: that is, by their false saying.
(11) The Truth, glory be to Him, has summarized the forbidden foods in His saying: ﴿Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, unless it be carrion, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine, for it is impure, or a transgression dedicated to other than God. But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor exceeding, indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful (145)﴾ [al-An'am].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 60:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And what will those who invent lies against Allah think on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of them do not give thanks.﴾ (60)

This verse makes clear that every matter is subject to reckoning. Those who invent lies against Allah will find their reckoning on the Day of Resurrection to be severe. The Truth, glorified is He, is far above heedlessness, even if they supposed that there is no Hereafter and no reckoning; they are mistaken in their supposition. Had they kept in mind what Allah has prepared for them of punishment and retribution(1) on the Day of Resurrection, they would not have done this. But they are like one who supposes that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is unaware of their actions, as if these were deeds without any accounting for them, without any record of them, and without any watcher who reckons them.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of them do not give thanks.﴾ (60) [Yunus]: Allah, glorified is He, bestows favour upon all His creation, and you(2) are among them, with many things. Why, then, do you deprive yourselves of this bounty?! Had you given thanks to Allah, exalted is He, for this favour, He would have increased His giving to you, but you forget gratitude.

(1) Nakal: inflicting a punishment and torment in a manner that makes whoever does such a deed an example to others. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, a deterrent punishment from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾ (38) [al-Ma'idah].

(2) They are the people of Makkah. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure while people are being snatched from around them? Then in falsehood do they believe, and in the favour of Allah do they deny?﴾ (67) [al-'Ankabut], and He also said: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.﴾ (57) [al-Qasas].

Al-Sha'rawi, *Tafsir al-Sha'rawi* (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 10, verse 61:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair, nor recite from it any part of the Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, but We are witnesses over you when you are immersed in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register.﴾ (Yunus: 61)

The address here is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning: "You are not, O Muhammad, engaged in any affair." *Sha'n* (affair, matter) is a great, distinguished state that befalls a matter.

In our daily lives we say: "What is your affair today?" or "What is your state?" The listener answers with the important thing that happened to him or that he did, and overlooks trivial matters. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, describes Himself saying: ﴿Every day He is in an affair.﴾ (al-Rahman: 29). That is: do not think that our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, created the laws and regulations and then said to them, "Act, you," no. He, glorified is He, is in an affair every day.

For this reason, when one of the scholars was asked: "What is your Lord's affair now, since it is established that the pen has dried?" he said: "Affairs He manifests, not affairs He initiates." That is, He, glorified is He, has inscribed everything and assigned it a time to appear. He, glorified is He, is *Qayyum* (the Self-Subsisting Sustainer), meaning He is most diligent in standing over your welfare. For this reason He, glorified is He, reassures us, having made the night for our sleep and rest, that He is *Qayyum*, neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him, and He watches over us.

So the discourse in the verse we are concerned with is directed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair...﴾ (Yunus: 61). The affair of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that concerns him is not food or drink; rather, what matters to him is conveying the message through the method of "do" and "do not do." ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair and recite from it any part of the Qur'an...﴾ (Yunus: 61).

Here "*minhu*" (from it) carries the meaning of *al-lam* (for), meaning: "what you recite for it" (footnote 3), and it signifies a specific focus on the verses of the Qur'an. Elsewhere in the Qur'an the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned﴾ (Nuh: 25), meaning: they were drowned because of their sins.

So here, in the verse we are reflecting upon, we understand: "you are not engaged in any affair and recite, for the sake of this affair, any part of the Qur'an." The Prophet (ﷺ) is engaged in an important affair, which is the message, and he recites from the Qur'an, focusing on this affair, which is conveying the message through the method. Included in this affair is what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was entrusted with, according to the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and what he forbids you, refrain from.﴾ (al-Hashr: 7). An example of this is determining how to perform the *salah* (ritual prayer, the prescribed prayer) and the number of *rak'ahs* (units) of each prayer, and likewise the *nisab* (threshold) of *zakat* (obligatory almsgiving). These are matters the Qur'an did not come with in detail, but the prophetic traditions came with them.

So: there is a delegation from the Truth to the Messenger (ﷺ), so that the message of Allah's method is completed, through the texts of the Qur'an, and through Allah's delegation to him to legislate.

Therefore: every affair of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is either a message from Allah through the Qur'anic text, or a practical application of the Qur'anic text through the prophetic tradition (*hadith*), and through the exemplary conduct he left us in his *sunnah* (the Prophet's normative practice, his way).

The proof for any ruling comes from the Qur'an. If the rulings are not issued directly by Allah, it suffices that they were issued by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by Allah's delegation to legislate.

By this we refute the hypocrites who, when some of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) words are related to them, say: "Between us and you is the Book of Allah" (footnote 7). Their aim is to reject the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) words, whether in action, speech, or tacit approval.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, shifts the address from the singular to the plural, saying, exalted is His majesty: ﴿...nor do you do any deed, but We are witnesses over you...﴾ (Yunus: 61). Here there is a transition to the listeners of the Qur'an, to whom this method is conveyed, for every deed is witnessed by the Truthful, glorified is He.

A deed (*'amal*) is the collection of actions that proceed from a person. Every action that proceeds from a person, even if only in the intention of the heart, is called a deed, because the deed of the hearts is intention. But if the action proceeds from the tongue, it is speech, and if it proceeds from the rest of the limbs, it is action.

Thus deed is divided into two types: speech and action. The action of the tongue has been specifically named speech, because the root of all the sources of obligation (*taklif*) is verbal.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿when you are immersed in it﴾, meaning: you hasten to the deed with energy, vitality, and eagerness, which indicates a good response to the method as soon as the Messenger (ﷺ) conveys it.

Engagement in the obligatory deed with this longing, this eagerness, this good reception, and this sincere performance, all these meanings are what the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He, ﴿when you are immersed in it﴾ leads to, just as the water of a vessel overflows when it is full and pours out. That is: you turn to the deeds of obligation quickly, with outpouring and spilling. The Truthful, glorified is He, has said: ﴿And when you pour forth from ʿArafat...﴾ (al-Baqarah: 198).

That is: you began to depart hastily, because you performed a rite from which you took energy, and you turn with it to a second rite (footnote 8/9). So Allah, glorified is He, witnesses every deed of yours. But what about intentions, and the thoughts that are hatched within them?

Here is the Truthful, glorified is He, informing us that everything, however small and hidden, is known and reckoned. The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register.﴾ (Yunus: 61). That is: all your affairs, the affairs of creation, and all created things are known to Allah, exalted is He, and written in a clear, evident register. No one is able to steal away the movement of a heart or the movement of a conscience. The word *ya'zub* means: to be absent and hidden.

The Truthful, glorified is He, informs us that the reward of any deed or intention is not lost before Him, however minor the deed or intention may be in its lowest degree of insignificance.

The Arabs had nothing to give as an example of a small weight except the *dharrah* (the atom, mote), which is the tiny ant, extremely small. Then *dharrah* was applied to the floating motes that are common in the air. You can see these motes if you sit in a dark, closed room and a ray of light enters it. Here you see this light passing through the hole like an arrow, and you see the components of this arrow from the moving particles of dust present in the air. These particles you do not see when you are only in the light or only in the dark, but the contrast between light and darkness makes them visible.

You do not perceive a thing or sense it for one of two reasons: either because it is so extremely small, or because it is so extremely large, so you cannot encompass it. When applied science advanced, they invented microscopes that magnify extremely small things thousands or millions of times.

If you place your skin under a microscope lens, you will see crevices like wells that you had not seen or sensed before, because they are so fine and tiny that your eyes cannot perceive them. If you see them through a microscope they become magnified, so you see crevices, creases, and elevations and depressions, no matter how smooth the skin you see looks under the microscope.

Likewise, you cannot perceive a huge thing, and a distance may separate you from a large object so that you see it smaller than its size. The farther it is, the smaller it appears. For example, if you see a tall man at a great distance, you see him as if he were a small child, and the closer you get to him, the taller he becomes in your eyes. Thus neither bigness, nor distance, nor smallness prevents the knowledge of the Truthful, glorified is He, of any thing.

The Truthful, glorified is He, addressed the Arabs with the smallest thing they knew, which is the *dharrah*, that is, the tiny ant.

If you step on an ant in sandy ground, it does not die; rather, it enters the crevices of the sand and finds for itself a path back to the surface of the earth.

The Truthful, glorified is He, has clarified this matter when He spoke of Sulayman (peace be upon him) in the Valley of the Ants, saying: ﴿...A small ant said, "O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush you while they do not perceive."﴾ (al-Naml: 18). That is: they do not see them, because of the extreme smallness of their size.

Thus the Truthful, glorified is He, gives us an explanation about every nation in life, and that among them are soldiers who guard with vigilance. The ant warned its people about Sulayman and his soldiers, because they would not see the small ants (footnote 10). So the *dharr* is either the tiny ant, or the particles of dust. Allah, glorified is He, wanted to give us an example of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, that not even an atom's weight is absent from Him. The verb *ya'zub* means: to be absent, to be hidden. It is said, "This well's water is *'azib*," meaning it comes from a far depth and its extraction requires a bucket and long ropes. We call a man who is far from his family *'azab* (a bachelor/one far from home).

The Truthful, glorified is He, says: "*wa ma ya'zub*" (and not absent), meaning: nothing, small or great, is far from Him or hidden from Him. He, glorified is He, says this to reassure us that every thought of a human being is witnessed by Allah, known by Him, and He is the one who will recompense for it.

If a person can conceal himself from the judgment of the earth, he will not be able to conceal himself from the judgment of the heaven (footnote 11). The matter of the atom and smallness, the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ (al-Zalzalah: 7-8). This refers to what is equal in weight and measure. As for what is smaller than the atom, the Truthful, glorified is He, mentioned it here in the verse we are reflecting on, saying: ﴿nor anything smaller than that or greater...﴾ (Yunus: 61).

At the time of the revelation of the Noble Qur'an, no one knew that there was anything smaller than the atom. Until before the First World War, we all did not know that there was anything smaller than the atom, and scientists believed that the atom was the indivisible part, because it was the smallest thing the eye could fall upon. So Allah gave as an example the least thing known at the time the Qur'an was revealed.

When science advanced after the First World War, and Germany invented a machine to break the atom, it was said of it: it is a machine that breaks the *al-jawhar al-fard* (the indivisible particle, the atom). That is, the thing that cannot be divided. This machine consisted of two cylinders like the two cylinders of a sugarcane press, and the distance between the two cylinders was barely visible. When Germany broke what was called "the indivisible particle," it turned into something even smaller, and the atom was shattered. Allah, glorified is He, made the measure of smallness the atom.

When Germany invented that machine, those connected with religion became anxious and feared that it would be said that the Truthful, glorified is He, had not mentioned anything smaller than the atom. But they turned to the verse we are reflecting on and read the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is [any part] of an atom's weight...﴾ (Yunus: 61). The word *ya'zub* means: does not get far or become hidden, ﴿from your Lord﴾, meaning: from His knowledge, ﴿[any part] of an atom's weight﴾, meaning: the weight of an atom.

We said long ago that some say that *min* (from) may be a superfluous particle in the language, as in our saying: *ma ja'ani min rajul* ("no man came to me"). The word *min* is parsed as a superfluous preposition (*harf jarr za'id*, a superfluous preposition), and *rajul* is a subject in the nominative case marked by the apparent *damma*, which was prevented from appearing by the occupation of the position by the *lam*, with the vowel of the superfluous preposition.

But in the speech of Allah there is no superfluous particle (footnote 12). So *min* in His saying ﴿min mithqal dharrah﴾ ("[any part] of an atom's weight") is from the beginning of what is called *mithqal* (weight).

The Truthful, glorified is He, says in another verse: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you — the Knower of the unseen. Not absent from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth..."﴾ (Saba': 3). The word ﴿my Lord﴾ is an oath, and the *waw* (the letter "and," here of oath) is the preposition of oath. It did not come here with *al-shahadah* (the witnessed, the visible), but came with *al-ghayb* (the unseen), and did not come with "the knowledge of the unseen" as in the verse we are reflecting on.

"The Knower of the witnessed" means: He knows everything that is witnessed. Humans think that it is not encompassed because of its greatness, or because Allah is unseen and sees only the unseen. But the Truthful, glorified is He, sees and knows both the unseen and the witnessed.

The Truthful, glorified is He, has said the phrase "*mithqal dharrah*" (an atom's weight) three times: once when He said, glorified is He: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good...﴾ (al-Zalzalah: 7); and once when He said here: ﴿[any part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven...﴾ (Yunus: 61). He brought "*min*" here to make clear that nothing is absent from...

There is another example that our esteemed Shaykh often mentions in his sayings, giving these examples, because a particle, as long as it has a function, is not superfluous. Then the Exalted says after that:
﴿Surely the friends of God—no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ (10:62)

This verse came after His statement about Himself, glorified is He, that He is the Knower of the unseen (al-ghayb), and nothing is hidden from Him. God, glorified is He, willed by this to teach us that He may pour upon some of His creatures outpourings of support in proportion to the spiritual discipline of those who undertake it. Suppose God has bestowed upon you a gift (nafha), then beware of saying that it comes from you. Rather, it comes from the Knower of the unseen, glorified is He, from whom nothing is hidden on earth or in heaven.

Accordingly, one should not say, "So-and-so knew the unseen, so he is a friend of God." Rather, let us say, "So-and-so is one who has been taught the unseen (mu'allam ghayb)," because the unseen is what is hidden from people. What is hidden from you but not from others is not absolute unseen.

An example of this: a man has had something stolen from him and does not know where the stolen item is, but the thief knows. Likewise, whoever helped the thief and concealed him and hid the stolen goods for him—all of these know. Also, the jinn who were in the same place as the theft know. This is not absolute unseen.

Also, the secrets of the cosmos which were once unseen for a limited time, such as the gravity of the earth, the negative and positive in electricity, and the pollination of winds for the clouds(1) so that water descends—all of this was unseen at a certain time. Then God, glorified is He, willed and set for each of these a time of disclosure, and they became well-known matters.

God, glorified is He, willed this so that man would work and strive to uncover the secrets of the cosmos.

Strangely, the researcher may work to uncover a specific thing and happen upon another discovery, because God, exalted is He, has permitted that discovery, which was unseen, to come into being, even if the people of the earth did not search for it.

Whoever discovered "penicillin" saw green mold around some organic materials, so he investigated the secrets of that and discovered "penicillin."

And Archimedes, who discovered the law of buoyancy, from which the shipbuilding and submarine industries and everything that moves on the sea have benefited. The law of buoyancy was discovered by chance.

So, in the cosmos there is unseen that may become visible: either through preliminary causes that God's creation follows through research, or it comes by chance during some search for another thing.

An example of this: the age of steam, which began with a man who saw a covered vessel in which water was boiling, and the lid kept rising to release some steam. The man realized that steam could be transformed into energy that pulls carriages moving on wheels, and thus the age of steam came.

So, the appearance of some secrets of the cosmos was a reminder from God, exalted is He, to one of His servants so that he would reflect and uncover one of those secrets.(2)

Most secrets of the cosmos were discovered by chance, so that we understand that God's bestowal of their emergence—without preliminary causes from creation—is greater than what is reached through the bestowal that comes from preliminary causes of creation.

For this reason, you find the Qur'anic expression concerning the two aspects of the unseen to be a precise expression, so that we understand that there is an unseen hidden from all creation, which has no preliminary causes, and God does not will its emergence, and God has kept its knowledge exclusive to Himself, so no one knows it except Him, glorified is He.

The Exalted says: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills…﴾ (2:255). This is the unseen that God, glorified is He, reveals to them, either through preliminary causes or by chance. He attributed the willing to Himself, glorified is He, and the encompassing to humans. This is the unseen of innovations.

As for the other unseen, which no one knows except Him, glorified is He, and which none reveals except the Messenger (ﷺ), the Exalted says about it:
﴿Knower of the unseen, so He does not reveal His unseen to anyone, except to one of the messengers whom He has approved…﴾ (72:26–27).

So, God, exalted is He, pours from His essential unseen upon some of His creatures, and the Noble Qur'an contains much of the unseen, which God, exalted is He, poured upon His Messenger (ﷺ), and the events came to pass as they were mentioned in the Qur'an.

The Exalted grants some of His creatures some of His outpourings, and God, glorified is He, gave His Messenger (ﷺ) some gifts and specified to whom He would give some of the unseen:
﴿except to one of the messengers whom He has approved…﴾ (72:27). This is not an exclusive limitation, because the Messenger (ﷺ) is an exemplar(3), and the Exalted says of him:
﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of God you have a good example for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God often.﴾ (33:21). Whoever acts according to the deeds of the Messenger (ﷺ) and follows his example, God, exalted is He, grants him a gift that people see, so they know that whoever follows the Messenger (ﷺ) as a model, God, glorified is He, gives him luminous gifts. But this gift is not a job, nor is it a "shop" (dukkan) for the unseen; rather, it is from God's bestowals, exalted is He.

Look at the precision of the Qur'an when He says:
﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him…﴾ (6:59). That is: He, glorified is He, has not given the key of the unseen to anyone. The friend of God takes the gift only from Him, glorified is He, but the key of the unseen is with God alone.

When we reflect on the words of the Exalted:
﴿Surely the friends of God—no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ (10:62), we find that the word "wali" (friend/protector) derives from "walaha, yaliyhi," meaning "close to him." He is the first refuge to which one resorts if a matter arises in which one needs assistance from another. If he needs support, he supports him, and his goodness flows to those who befriend him.

Whoever draws close to a scholar takes some knowledge; whoever draws close to a strong person takes some strength; and whoever draws close to a wealthy person, if he is in need, the wealthy person gives him, even as a loan.

Accordingly, the wali is the close one, the helper, the supporter, the ally. The word "wali" is applied sometimes to God, glorified is He, and the Qur'an said: ﴿So God is the Wali…﴾ (42:9). This is because He, glorified is He, is close to all His creatures, unlike creatures who draw near to one another or distance themselves according to their capabilities. As for God, glorified is He, He is the absolute Wali. His nearness to one creature does not distance Him from another creature, and nothing preoccupies Him from anything else. He is the true Wali, and He, glorified is He, says: ﴿There, the guardianship belongs to God, the Truth…﴾ (18:44). So whoever needs true guardianship should resort to God, and He, glorified is He, pours guardianship upon those faithful to His method.

We find the precise Qur'anic expression: ﴿God is the Wali of those who believe﴾ (2:257). He, glorified is He, draws near to His believing servants, and the believers draw near to God, exalted is He, in the words of the Exalted:
﴿Surely the friends of God…﴾ (10:62). Accordingly, absolute guardianship belongs to God, and even if it is restricted by something added and an added-to, it is sometimes from the believers to God, and sometimes from God to the believers.

The Exalted is not governed by laws. By the freedom of His power, glorified is He, when He sees in a person some good trait, He honors him first, and that servant then becomes obedient afterward.

You hear someone say, "So-and-so was snatched from sin," meaning that he was a sinner, then God, exalted is He, loved a good trait in him, and guided him.

An example of this: a man who gave a dog water—rather, he devised a way to give it water by filling his leather sock (khuff) from the well to quench the dog's thirst—so God, glorified and exalted is He, forgave his sins.(7)

This man did not give the dog water out of hypocrisy toward the dog, but because the man felt compassion toward a living creature with a moist liver.

Accordingly, matters with God, exalted is He, are not mechanical or automatic. Rather, the freedom of His power decrees each situation just as He decreed the diversity of creation. For this reason He, glorified is He, said:
﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages(8) and your colors…﴾ (30:22). God does not have a mold into which He places creatures; rather, He, glorified is He, creates the tall and the short, the fat and the thin, the fair and the black. This is part of the freedom of His power, glorified is He. And by His mercy, glorified is He, He drew near to His creatures who believed first, and His nearness to them: ﴿He brings them out from darkness into light…﴾ (2:257).

Whoever follows the method takes the light. When God, glorified is He, knows of his action according to His method, He draws him near still more, and gives him an elect gift that those around him see, and they may follow his example.

The Exalted wants the believer to have courtesy with God's creation. If he knows of a person's bad deed, he should conceal it, because the Exalted loves concealment and loves those who conceal.

You may dislike a person about whom you know of some wrongdoing, and you may dislike every good deed of his. God wants you not to be deprived of the good deeds of one who has a bad deed, so He conceals it from you so that you may take some of his good deeds. And the Truth commands you not to belittle this wrongdoer, because he may possess one good trait, and God, glorified is He, honors him first for its sake, and then this servant obeys Him second.

The Exalted says in a sacred hadith (hadith qudsi): "O son of Adam, I love you, so by My right over you, love Me." And God, glorified is He, says in a sacred hadith: "I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs."

In this saying, He places the responsibility for drawing near to God in the hands of the creatures, and the Exalted adds: "And if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running."(9)

Whoever wants God to come to him running, let him go to God walking. Accordingly, faith in God delivers to the believer the key to nearness to God.

Whoever is one of the creatures committed to the method, God draws him closer and closer.

Accordingly, some people reach God's honor through obedience to God, and knock on the door of the Truth, and the door opens for them. And some people reach obedience to God through God's honor first.

And to God belongs the highest example: you, as one of mankind, may have someone knock on your door who needs a morsel of food or charity, and you give him. And there is another person whom you yourself love to give to, and when you give him, he obeys you out of the logic of kindness to him. So what of God's giving to His servants?

Accordingly, some people reach obedience to God through God's honor, and some reach God's honor through obedience to God. When a person reaches nearness to God, and God draws near to the servant, then the servant is in God's companionship (ma'iyya), and this companionship showers him abundantly.

Abu al-'Ala' al-Ma'arri said to his beloved:(10) "You are the beloved, but I seek refuge in Him from being a lover who is not loved." That is: he seeks refuge in God from being a lover of one who rejects his love. But God's love differs from the love of humans, and He does not treat His lovers that way. When you love God, He draws you closer and closer, and this is called "al-musafa" (intimate closeness). When God, glorified is He, pours upon some of His creatures gifts of honors, then the servants whom the Truth, glorified is He, has singled out with that should show good courtesy toward God, and none of them should flaunt himself boastfully over God's gift to him.

Boasting about honors destroys them, and the Truth, glorified is He, takes them away from the one who shows off, boasts, and vaunts himself. Whoever feigns honor has no honor.

Accordingly, the Truth, glorified is He, wants the servant to always be in His companionship. He is the One who began and clarified by the clear verse that He, glorified is He, is the Wali of the believers, and so He will bring them out from darkness into light.(11) He said: ﴿God is the Wali of those who believe; He brings them out from the darknesses into the light…﴾ (2:257). We know that He, glorified is He, brings sensory things to clarify spiritual meanings, because human familiarity first comes through sensory things, and they are closer to bringing the meaning near. When the Truth, glorified is He, strikes for us the example of disbelief and faith, He describes disbelief as darkness and faith as light. The Truth only wants to make the meaning clear to you and connected to your understanding.

If we avoid the perils of sensory darkness, is it not more fitting for us also to avoid the perils of spiritual darkness? Sensory darkness hides things so that we do not see them, and we may collide with the weakest thing and break it, or bump into the strongest thing and be crushed by it.

Accordingly, the veils of the hypocrites cause disasters. But when light comes, it shows the features of things, so they proceed in guidance while you are at peace.

Suppose you are in a dark place and there is another thing in a bright place. You, in darkness, can see whoever is in the light. This is a matter whose interpretation has not been understood.

The Qur'an expresses darknesses to mean disbelief and light to mean faith, and this is the eloquence of inimitability in the Book of God.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 10, verse 63:

Allah, glory be to Him, explains to us the conditions of walāya (divine friendship), saying: ﴿Those who believed and used to be God-fearing (63).﴾

Faith (īmān) is the first doctrinal matter on which every action is built. It requires the implementation of Allah's method: the command where there is a command, the prohibition where there is a prohibition, and the permission where there is a permission.

Taqwa (God-consciousness, piety), as we have learned, is guarding oneself against the attributes of majesty of Allah, the Exalted, and also guarding oneself against the Fire. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) added to the attributes of one from whom taqwa proceeds, because it consists of stages. He (ﷺ) said, describing the God-fearing: "They are a people who love one another through the Spirit of Allah, without blood ties between them and without wealth that they exchange. By Allah, their faces will indeed be radiant, and they will indeed be upon light." (1)

ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about the God-fearing and said: "The one of them whose sight makes you draw nearer to Allah." It is as if he, may Allah be pleased with him, were explaining to us the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Their mark is on their faces, from the traces of prostration... (29)﴾ [al-Fath]. When you see a God-fearing person, you are delighted and rejoice in him, and you do not know the source of that joy until it is said to you that he is committed to the taqwa of Allah. This joy draws you to imitate him, because seeing him reminds you of khushūʿ (humility) (3), of khuḍūʿ (submission), of tranquility (4), of gentleness of bearing, and of an open countenance.

One of these people looks at the universe and finds in it no defect at all; rather, he sees everything in its exact place and sees no ugliness in existence. Even when he encounters ugliness, he says: this ugliness shows us the beautiful, and were it not for the existence of falsehood and its hardships, people would not have loved the truth. Thus falsehood becomes one of the soldiers of truth. The existence of evil drives people toward good. For this reason it is said: "Be beautiful in your religion, and you will see existence as beautiful," because when you see things and accept the decree of Allah concerning them, Allah then pours upon you gifts from the Supreme Overflow, and the more you draw near to Allah, the more Allah, glory be to Him, draws near to you, and He pours upon you wisdom and the secrets of creation (5).

An example of this is the righteous servant upon whom Allah bestowed mercy from Him and taught him knowledge from His presence. This servant taught Mūsā, peace be upon him (6). When he compared the servant's damaging of a sound ship, while he (Mūsā) did not know that there was a tyrannical king who seizes every ship by force, Mūsā therefore debated with the righteous servant and asked: how can a sound ship be damaged? Then the righteous servant explained to him that when the unjust king finds the ship damaged, he will not take it, and it belongs to poor people (7).

When the righteous servant killed a boy, this act appeared to Sayyidunā Mūsā to be a crime, and Sayyidunā Mūsā did not know what the righteous servant knew: that this boy would bring harm upon his parents. Allah commanded the righteous servant to kill him before puberty, lest he tempt his parents (8), and this boy would enter Paradise and become one of the daʿāmīṣ (little ones) of Paradise (9).

It is said that whoever dies before puberty has no fixed dwelling in Paradise, but goes wherever he wishes; he is like a small child who enters a palace and cannot bear to stay in one place, but goes here and there, and he may go to where Sayyidunā Muḥammad (ﷺ) is, or Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, or to a noble companion.

Also, when Sayyidunā Mūsā, peace be upon him, together with the righteous servant, came to a town and asked its people for food, and they refused to feed them — and asking for food is the most truthful form of request — the people of the town refused to feed them, and this is evidence of meanness and baseness. So the righteous servant set up the wall that was about to collapse in that town.

Sayyidunā Mūsā, peace be upon him, had not known what the righteous servant knew: that a righteous man had died and left a treasure for his children beneath this wall, and he had built it to be stable until the children reached the age of maturity. The wall would fall so that the children would find the treasure their father had left them, and the base people of the town would not dare to plunder it (10).

So then: these are gifts from the overflow of the Truth, glory be to Him, upon His righteous servants. He, glory be to Him and exalted, makes such servants like the masts set up to guide people, or like the lighthouse that guides ships in darkness.

1 Narrated by Abū Dāwūd in his Sunan (3527), from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and its complete form: "Indeed among the servants of Allah are people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whom the prophets and martyrs will envy on the Day of Resurrection because of their station with Allah, the Exalted." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us: who are they?" He said: "They are a people who love one another through the Spirit of Allah, without blood ties between them and without wealth that they exchange. By Allah, their faces are indeed light, and they are indeed upon light. They do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve when people grieve." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, the friends of Allah — no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve (62).﴾ [Yunus].
2 Sīmāhum: the signs of taqwa and faith; it is that light in their faces.
3 Khasha'a (khushūʿan): humbled himself; khasha'a in his prayer and supplication. It was said: with the heart. It is derived from "khasha'at" the earth, when it became still and settled (al-Miṣbāḥ al-Munīr).
4 Khaḍaʿa to his creditor (yakhḍaʿu, khuḍūʿan): he was abased and submissive; he is khāḍiʿ, and poverty humbled him (akhḍaʿahu). Khuḍūʿ is close to khushūʿ, except that khushūʿ is used most often for the voice, as in ﴿and voices are hushed before the Most Merciful (108)﴾ [Ṭā-Hā], while khuḍūʿ is used for the necks, as in al-Farazdaq's saying: "Humbled are the necks, lowered are the gazes." (al-Miṣbāḥ al-Munīr).
5 The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him, and My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely grant him refuge." Narrated by al-Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ (6502) and Aḥmad in his Musnad (6/256), from Abū Hurayra.
6 Allah, glory be to Him, said about Mūsā and his servant at their meeting with al-Khiḍr, peace be upon him: ﴿So they found a servant of Ours, to whom We had given mercy from Us and whom We had taught knowledge from Our presence (65). Mūsā said to him: "May I follow you on condition that you teach me something of what you have been taught of right guidance?" (66) He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me (67). And how can you be patient about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?" (68) He said: "You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter." (69) He said: "If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you." (70)﴾ [al-Kahf].
7 Al-Qisṭ (the matter): Mūsā disapproved of his act and said: ﴿Have you damaged it to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing (71)﴾ [al-Kahf]. Later his answer to him was: ﴿As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working in the sea, so I wanted to damage it, for behind them was a king who seizes every ship by force (79)﴾ [al-Kahf].
8 Mūsā said: ﴿Have you killed a pure soul without its having killed anyone? You have certainly done a deplorable thing (74)﴾ [al-Kahf]. Then al-Khiḍr informed him of the interpretation of what he could not understand or grasp, saying to him: ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief (80). So we wanted their Lord to replace him for them with one better than him in purity and nearer in mercy (81)﴾ [al-Kahf].
9 Daʿāmīṣ: they are small children; it was explained as the little creature found in stagnant water. He said: al-daʿmūṣ is one who intrudes into matters, i.e., they are wanderers in Paradise, intruding into its dwellings, not barred from any place, just as children in this world are not barred from entering the women's quarters, and none of them is veiled from anyone. (Lisān al-ʿArab, root d-ʿ-m-ṣ).
10 This is a matter that the Lord of Might mentioned in His Book, saying about Mūsā and al-Khiḍr: ﴿So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to entertain them. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he (al-Khiḍr) set it up straight. [Mūsā] said: "If you had wished, you could have taken a payment for it" (77)﴾ [al-Kahf]. Then al-Khiḍr said to him later: ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord wished that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it by my own command... (82)﴾ [al-Kahf].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 64:

Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no alteration in the words of Allah. That is the great triumph.﴾ (64)

Al-bushra(1): from bashar, bishara and tabshir, all of which derive from al-bashra, which is the skin, because any emotion within the human soul shows itself upon the skin. When you bring a person a pleasing matter, you see the effect of that joy on his features, and when you bring a person bad news, you see the gloom appear on his skin. The skin is thus the first thing to be affected by joyful or painful events.

When it is said "bushra", this means words which, when the hearer hears them, brighten his skin and gladden him, because they are words announcing good.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about al-bushra, he said: "It is the good dream seen by the believer, or seen for him." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is a part of forty-six parts of prophethood."(2)

The Revelation came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in dreams for six months, and it came to him while awake for twenty-three years. If you compare the six months with the twenty-three years, you will find that the six months represent a part of forty-six parts.

The ru'ya (true vision) is not the same as the hulm (dream), because the ru'ya is something that did not occupy your mind during the day, and Satan has no part in it.

The colloquial proverb says: "The hungry one dreams of a market of bread." So if what a person sees during sleep is related to a matter that preoccupies him, this is a hulm and not a ru'ya. And if what a person sees during sleep is something that contradicts the way of Allah, this is an inspiration (qadhfa) from Satan.(3) Thus there is a difference between the ru'ya and the hulm, and between adghath al-ahlam (confused dreams).(4)

So al-bushra is the good ru'ya, or it is the preliminary signs that make the creatures of Allah feel for them, so that people's hearts turn towards these friends (awliya'). You may find that Allah, the Exalted, loves someone in heaven, and Allah, glorified and exalted, says to Jibril, peace be upon him: "I love so-and-so, so love him." He said: "So Jibril loves him. Then Jibril calls out in heaven: 'Indeed Allah loves so-and-so, so love him,' and the inhabitants of heaven love him. He said: Then acceptance is placed for him on earth."(5)

When you see him written as accepted, everyone agrees that in seeing this beloved one there is a good aura, and this is al-bushra.

Or al-bushra comes at the moment the Angel of Death comes, and he greets him, peace be upon him, and he feels that death is a natural matter, confirming the saying of the True One, glorified is He: ﴿Those whom the angels take in a good state, saying: Peace be upon you; enter the Garden for what you used to do.﴾ (An-Nahl: 32)

Or at the moment when the face becomes bright, when a person takes his book in his right hand. This is good news in this world and in the Hereafter.

The True One, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, those who say "Our Lord is Allah" and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them: "Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good news of the Garden which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter..."﴾ (Fussilat: 30-31). So these friends of Allah receive from the outpourings (fuyudat) of Allah upon them through the angels, and they are distinguished from others, because one of them may impose upon himself voluntary acts beyond the obligatory ones, since the obligatory acts are the least of the duties.

And one of them may see that performing the obligations does not match his love for Allah, so he increases in their kind beyond what Allah has prescribed, and he prays ten more units of voluntary prayer besides the five obligatory ones, or he fasts a month or two in addition to Ramadan, or he fasts on Monday and Thursday of every week.

This is evidence that he finds the obligations few in comparison with the degree of his love for Allah, and that Allah deserves more than that. This means that such a servant has entered the station of mutual affection (wudd) with Allah, and here Allah, glorified and exalted, pours upon him what He wills, and he attains from the good pleasure of Allah what came in the hadith qudsi: "Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely grant him refuge. I do not hesitate about anything I am going to do as I hesitate about the soul of the believer, who dislikes death, and I dislike to harm him."(9)

Thus the measures differ between a servant who loves Allah and performs beyond what is incumbent upon him, and another servant who performs only the obligations.

The True One, glorified is He, concludes the verse about which our reflections are: ﴿There is no alteration in the words of Allah. That is the great triumph.﴾ (Yunus: 64). Since the True One, glorified is He, has said: ﴿There is no alteration in the words of Allah..﴾, you will not find anyone able to do that, just as all creatures will be subdued on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever Allah permitted to possess something in this world will no longer possess anything, as evidenced by everyone hearing the saying of the True One, glorified is He: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (Ghafir: 16). Since the True One, glorified is He, has promised the good news of this world and the good news of the Hereafter, there is no alteration of what Allah has decreed, and nothing resists the judgment of Allah, glorified is He. The promise of glad tidings in this world and in the Hereafter is a certain great triumph.

(1) Bashara bi-kadha, yubashiru, like faraha in pattern and meaning, means istibshar (to be glad). The verbal noun is al-bushur; the active participle of the form with the doubled-less stem is bashir, which is the bearer of good more than of evil. Al-bushr: radiance of the face. Al-bashra: the outer surface of the skin. Between al-bushra in the sense of joy and al-bashra as the outer skin, there is a connection: it is a reaction that appears visibly in joy and otherwise. [Al-Misbah al-Munir, adapted]

(2) Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6973) and Muslim (2264) from Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The good dream of the righteous man is a part of forty-six parts of prophethood."

(3) Similar was narrated by Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said to a Bedouin who came to him and said: "I dreamt that my head was cut off and I am following it." The Prophet (ﷺ) rebuked him and said: "Do not inform Satan's plaything about you in a dream." Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih (2268).

(4) Adghath al-ahlam: a vision that cannot be interpreted because of its confusion and mixing. Al-dughth: a dream that has no interpretation and no good in it. In the revealed text: ﴿They said: "Confused dreams."﴾ (Yusuf: 44), meaning your vision is a mixture, not a clear vision, and ﴿We are not learned in the interpretation of dreams.﴾ (Yusuf: 44), meaning there is no interpretation for a confused vision with us. They said this because of their inability to interpret it, but Yusuf explained it to the king, so it was not adghath al-ahlam. [Lisan al-'Arab, root dh-gh-th]

(5) Agreed upon. Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3209) and Muslim (6237) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. The wording is Muslim's, and its completion in his version is: "And when He hates a servant, He calls Jibril and says: 'I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: So Jibril hates him. Then he calls out among the people of heaven: 'Indeed Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: So they hate him. Then hatred is placed for him on earth."

(6) These are the friends who have abandoned sins and adorned themselves with acts of obedience, so Allah, glorified is He, manifests Himself to them through outpourings, and from this outpouring is acceptance and the good dream.

(7) Among the gifts of acceptance are the rest of the verses in His saying: ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and for you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you ask for. A hospitable gift from the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ (Fussilat: 31-32). There are gifts and supports which we do not know, but Allah knows them, and He is the Knower of the unseen.

(8) Wadda: to love. The noun is al-mawadda. Wadud means loving; it applies equally to male and female.

(9) Sima-hum: al-masa'a (evil) is the opposite of al-masarra (joy); its root is masw'a, and so the waw returns in the plural, so one says al-masawi, but the plural is used in a lightened form, and badat masawihi, meaning its faults appeared. Al-sau'a: the private parts; the plural is sawat, and it was called sau'a because when it is exposed it distresses its owner. [Al-Misbah al-Munir]. The hadith was recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6502) and Ahmad in his Musnad (6/256) from Abu Hurayrah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 10, verse 65:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And let not their saying grieve you. Indeed, all might belongs to Allah. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (65)

This verse comes after Allah, exalted is He, has made clear to us the objections of the disbelievers, their harm to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), their denial of him, and what they said about him. Some of what they said grieved him (ﷺ). Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, asked him not to be affected by what they said as a grieving person would be. They said: "A sorcerer," "a liar," "a fabricator," "a madman." Allah, glorified is He, negated all that they said. If Muhammad (ﷺ) were a sorcerer, why did he not bewitch them too? And does the bewitched have any will alongside the sorcerer?!

Thus He refuted their claim that he (ﷺ) had bewitched their slaves and children.

They also said: "A madman," yet there was no trace of madness in his (ﷺ) conduct. He refuted these claims with His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed, you are of a great moral character.﴾ [al-Qalam] (1–4)

A madman does not have a great moral character, ever.

When they said that he had fabricated the Qur'an, He challenged them to produce a surah like it, and they were unable to do so, although they were trained in poetry, literature, and eloquent expression.

As for the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And let not their saying grieve you...﴾ (65), it is because their sayings have no effect in standing against the call, because ﴿...all might belongs to Allah...﴾ (65). "Might" (ʿizzah) is power and dominance, and it is said: "This thing is ʿazīz," meaning there is nothing like it. He, glorified is He, is the Absolutely Mighty, for there is no god but Him, He is not overcome and not subdued.

When you recite this verse you will notice the letter "mīm" (a pause sign) above the word ﴿qawluhum﴾ (their saying), and it means that a pause is necessary here.

Someone may ask: how is a pause required here, when the Qur'an is built on continuity (waṣl), and the last letter of every surah is tanwīn, and there is nothing in the Qur'an that obliges the reader to pause?

My answer to this question is: when the scholars noticed the weakness of linguistic faculty, they introduced this pause so that the reader, who has no knowledge of Arabic eloquence, understands how to read this verse. Suppose someone does not possess the discernment of delivery; he would attach ﴿...indeed, all might belongs to Allah...﴾ (65) to ﴿And let not their saying grieve you...﴾ (65), and misunderstand, and think—God forbid—that the might of Allah is a matter that grieves the Prophet (ﷺ). Therefore the scholars placed the pause here so that we may read precisely and understand well.

Hence we must read ﴿...And let not their saying grieve you...﴾ (65), then pause before continuing with ﴿indeed, all might belongs to Allah...﴾ (65). In this way we understand the meaning: "Do not grieve, O Muhammad, for their sayings will not change the course of the certainty of your victory over them."

Here the Truth, glorified is He, wishes to reassure His Messenger (ﷺ) on a specific matter: that his duty is only to convey, and he is not obliged to compel them to believe in his message and submit to his method.

Allah, glorified is He, made clear to him: if they turn away after your delivery, do not grieve over what they say; for their sayings have no proof upon which they rest, and no argument to support them. Concerning them the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿and they denied them while their souls were convinced of them...﴾ [an-Naml] (14). Their sayings will not stand in the way of your call; Allah will complete His light, and there is no one mightier than Allah, glorified and exalted is He. No one can give protection against Allah to anyone; He grants protection and none can be given protection against Him.

If might is coercion and dominance, it may be the might of argument, it may be the might of alliance, it may be the might of wisdom, and each of Allah's creatures may have some might in a particular field or sphere. But might belongs to Allah, glorified is He, comprehensively and absolutely, in every sphere and every field, encompassing everything and anything.

Why did the Truth, glorified is He, not use the restrictive construction (qaṣr) (6) in this verse? That is, that the attribute is attached to the qualified and negated from anything else, as when we say: "Zayd has property that no one else has." If we place the prepositional phrase first, which is the complement, and say: "Fulān has such-and-such," this means that others than Fulān do not have such-and-such.

If we say: "Fulān has such-and-such," it is correct to say: "And Fulān has such-and-such, and Fulān has such-and-such, and Fulān has such-and-such."

But if you say: "Fulān has such-and-such," its meaning is: it is impossible that anyone other than Fulān has anything like what you mentioned.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿...indeed, all might belongs to Allah...﴾ (65). He used emphasis, and did not use for it the restrictive construction which would give might to Allah, glorified is He, and negate it from others; because there is no opponent to this verse, and it is an initial statement by which Allah, glorified is He, informs of a cosmic fact that all might belongs to Allah.

Since the Truth, glorified is He, is the One who says this—and He is the Creator of creation—no cosmic fact will come to contradict it. And if—God forbid—a cosmic fact were to contradict it, the verse would not be true. This has never happened and will never happen with the verses of the Truth, glorified is He; for He is the Creator of the universe and the One who sent down the verses; so there can never be contradiction between the cosmos and the words of the Creator of the cosmos, glorified and exalted is He.

It has happened that some claimed might (7) for themselves, and they said: ﴿If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner﴾ [al-Munafiqun] (8). The purport of their saying was claiming might for themselves and claiming lowliness for the believers. So might was claimed; and since it was claimed, why was it not expressed with the restrictive construction? We say: No; Allah, glorified is He, willed to say: ﴿But might belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun] (8). So the might of Allah does not exceed Him; but He, glorified is He, willed that the might of His Messenger (ﷺ) and the might of the believers be from within the might of Allah, exalted is He.

His saying here, glorified is He: ﴿...indeed, all might belongs to Allah...﴾, that is: in all its forms it belongs to Allah, glorified and exalted is He. If it is the might of wisdom, He is the All-Wise; if it is the might of grasping matters, He is the Mighty; if it is the might of forbearance, He is the Forbearing; if it is the might of anger and retribution, He is the Avenger, the Compeller; and all forms of might belong to Allah, exalted is He: ﴿...He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (65)﴾ [Yunus]. Since might is dominance and subjugation, Allah, glorified is He, hears whoever deserves to be subdued by Him; and since the matter involves speech, He comes with the attribute of hearing, and if it involves action, He comes with the attribute of the All-Knowing; He is the All-Hearing of what is said and the All-Knowing of what is done.

We know that the thing forbidden here is: ﴿And let not their saying grieve you...﴾ (65) [Yunus]. Therefore it was fitting that it be said first: ﴿He is the All-Hearing...﴾.

The Truth, glorified is He, wishes to demonstrate this matter by a cosmic proof in the signs of Allah in the cosmos, and there is nothing in existence or in the cosmos that can stand before Him, glorified is He. Therefore we must note that the law "all might belongs to Allah" is governed by the fact that to Allah, exalted is He, belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And those who invoke other than Allah do not follow partners; they follow only assumption, and they are only guessing (66)﴾.

1. "Man" (mann) on him with manumission and other things: from the root qatala. "Amnun ʿalayhi bihi" means bestow upon him with it. The noun is "minnah," and the plural "minan." "Minnah" with a dammah means strength, and it is among the words with opposite meanings. "Mantu ʿalayhi": I enumerated to him what I had done for him of favours. In this there is annoyance and change that breaks hearts. For this reason the Lawgiver forbade it in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like that of a smooth stone with dust on it; a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They are unable to do anything with what they have earned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah] (264).
Also "mannantu al-shay'" means I cut it, so it is "mamnun." And "al-manna" is something that falls from the sky, and is gathered. [al-Misbah, adapted]
2. That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say: "Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful"﴾ [Yunus] (38).
3. "Murtadun lil-shi'r": that is, they have practice in composing and arranging poetry.
4. This is the necessary stance, and like it is His saying: ﴿Only those who hear will respond; and the dead, Allah will raise them﴾ [al-An'am] (36).
5. "Al-juhud": denial despite knowledge. "Istayqana al-amr": he knew the matter with certainty. [Lisan al-Arab: root (y q n)]
6. "Uslub al-qasr" (or al-hasr): is restricting one matter to another by a specific means, namely establishing the judgement for the mentioned and negating it from what is other than it. It is divided into: restriction of the qualified to the attribute, and restriction of the attribute to the qualified; each of them is either real (haqiqi) or figurative (majazi). [al-Itqan fi ʿUlum al-Qur'an, by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti, 3/149]
7. Ubayy: this is ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, head of hypocrisy in Medina. This occurred in the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq in the month of Sha'ban in the sixth year after the Hijrah. He described Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, saying: "They have competed with us and outnumbered us in our land; by Allah, our case and the case of the Quraysh's pack animals is only as the first said: 'Fatten your dog and it will eat you.' By Allah, if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner." Then he turned to those of his people present and said to them: "This is what you have done to yourselves: you have let them settle in your land and shared your wealth with them. By Allah, if you withheld from them what is in your hands, they would move to other than your dwelling." Ibn Hisham related it in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (3/290, 291).
8. Yakhrusun: they follow their assumptions, their lies and their falsehood. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/424)]

Therefore, Allah the Exalted—so to speak—will not let anyone at all escape from His dominion.

Whenever you find Allah the Exalted clarifying a thing and its opposite, He brings the principle and the framework: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:284]. An example of this: when the people of Pharaoh pursued Musa (peace be upon him) and his people, the companions of Musa said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken.﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:61]

They said this because they saw the sea before them. Allah the Exalted willed to show them that the sea would not hinder His will, and the sea did not escape the power of Allah the Exalted, because to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and the sea is among them.
