Therefore the sea split apart, and every part became like a great mountain (1).

Nothing escapes His dominion, the Exalted. Therefore Allah the Exalted brings the opposite: after He made a path for them through the sea, and every part was like a great mountain, the sea remained split and the people of Pharaoh entered into it.

And Allah the Exalted says to Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿And leave the sea parted; indeed, they are an army to be drowned.﴾ [al-Dukhan 44:24]. So Allah the Exalted commands the sea to return to what it was, and the people of Pharaoh are drowned, after Allah—glorified and exalted be He—had saved Musa (peace be upon him) and those with him. Thus with one thing He destroys and He saves, because to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; and so that Allah the Exalted may show us that nothing in the creation of Allah the Exalted ever stands in the place of His might, the Exalted, at all.

There is another example: when Nuh (peace be upon him) says to his son: ﴿O my son, board with us.﴾ [Hud 11:42], the son replies, saying: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water.﴾ [Hud 11:43]. This is a sound statement in that the mountain's height is above the level of the waters, but the son of Nuh forgot that Allah the Exalted has another soldier, which is the wave; so he was among the drowned.

It is true that the son of Nuh perceived that the ship would come to rest on "al-Judi" (3), and that whoever boards it will not drown, and likewise whoever takes refuge in a high mountain; but he did not perceive the wave that came between him and the mountain, so he was among the drowned.

Therefore: every existent is subject to the command of Allah the Exalted, and since might belongs to Allah entirely, its proof is that to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; and there is no being in existence that refuses to be one of the soldiers of Allah the Exalted, so that it is a soldier for destruction and a soldier for deliverance at the same time (4).

The statement of Allah the Exalted here: ﴿Alā﴾ ("Indeed/Look"). From it we know that ﴿alā﴾ is a particle of alerting the listener, so that he is not taken unawares, does not miss a wisdom of the wisdoms of speech, and pays attention that there is an address which requires him to gather his whole mind in order to receive well what follows. In this, the address is not...

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth...﴾ [Yunus 10:66]

One might say: there are many non-rational beings, and His saying here "man" (من) is intended for rational beings?

To refute this speaker we may ask: Is there anything in existence that does not understand from Allah? Of course not, and Allah the Exalted Himself says about the earth: ﴿That Day, it will report its news. Because your Lord has inspired it.﴾ [al-Zalzalah 99:4-5].

Therefore: all beings, in the usage of reception from Allah the Exalted, are equal whether described by "man" or by "ma", and everything in existence understands from Allah.

We observe that Allah the Exalted says once: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly...﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:83], and once He says: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth...﴾ [Yunus 10:66], as occurs in this verse that we are discussing now.

﴿Allah the Exalted willed that⦆ because there is a kind of being that exists in the heavens and exists on the earth, namely the angels who arrange the affair (5). These are the ones intended by "to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and the earth."

Allah the Exalted also has a kind in the heavens that does not exist on the earth, namely the angels "al-muhayminun" (6), the exalted, and they have no existence on the earth; just as Allah has soldiers on the earth who have no existence in the heavens. If we consider the angels who arrange the affair, we find that the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth...﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:284] is fitting for them.

And if we consider that Allah has angels "muhayminun" in the heavens and soldiers on the earth unrelated to the heavens, the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth...﴾ [Yunus 10:66] is fitting for that. And since everything in the cosmos is owned by Allah the Exalted, nothing escapes His will, the Exalted. For example, there is no cave that a creature may enter in flight from Allah, because He is able to seal the cave; and if Allah the Exalted wills to help the one who entered the cave, He, the Exalted, blinds the sight of whoever watches the cave (7).

Therefore nothing can grant protection against Allah the Exalted, and His attribute of might remains, which no one's scratch can harm from the existence of God in the cosmos.

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners...﴾ [Yunus 10:66]

The meaning of their following "partners" is as if there were partners, although the principle and the reality is that He has no partners, the Exalted.

Therefore they follow other than a thing; the evidence for that is present within the matter itself: they worship them besides Allah the Exalted, and the meaning of worship is that a command is obeyed and a prohibition is observed; but what they worship of things has no commands and no prohibitions, so there is no method they brought.

Therefore there is no divinity for them. Therefore the principle is that Allah the Exalted has no partners; and if He had partners they would have sent down a method and established commands, and there would be prohibitions from Him; because the one who says "worship Me" is the one who determines the manner and style of worship. Bring one of those you follow and call upon, who has a method—and they will not be able to do so. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: If there were with Him other gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:42]. That is: if we supposed there were gods having an appearance of power, like the sun that shines and the moon that gives light, and the rain that descends from the sky, and the angels who arrange the affair, and if we accepted that all these were gods, they would seek the One, the Unique; to take from Him the power you thought belonged to them.

Therefore Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And there was not with Him any god; otherwise each god would have took away what he created, and some would have overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe.﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:91]. For if this matter were true, there would be divine domains.

Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek means of access to their Lord.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:57]. They claimed they worship the angels, but they should know that the angels themselves worship Allah the Exalted; and since there are no partners of Allah for you to follow, then you are following conjecture.

Therefore came the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They follow not except assumption, and they do not but guess.﴾ [Yunus 10:66]

Those who are fond of finding apparent contradictions in the Qur'an in order to cast doubt upon it say: this verse is an example of that. They say: at the beginning of the verse He says: ﴿And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners...﴾ [Yunus 10:66]

So He denies that the polytheists follow partners of Allah; then at the end of the verse He says they follow conjecture and guessing. In its beginning He negates following, and at its end He affirms it.

This is the ignorance of the one who said this and claimed there is a contradiction in the verse. Allah the Exalted denies that what these polytheists call upon are partners of Allah in His dominion; to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth; but He affirms that they follow conjecture, guessing and speculation.

We say: what is conjecture? And what is guessing?

Conjecture (zann) is a judgment of the more probable, as we explained before regarding ratios: there is a ratio which, if not present, is doubted; or a probable ratio; or a ratio in which doubt equals affirmation. If doubt equals affirmation, this is doubt (shakk). If the probable side prevails, this is conjecture (zann). As for the less probable, we call it delusion (wahm).

Conjecture, then, is a judgment of the probable. And guessing (khars) is speculation, saying without a foundation or evidence.

Allah the Exalted says here: ﴿They follow not except assumption, and they do not but guess.﴾ [Yunus 10:66].

When the Qur'an addresses an audience, it brings an address that encompasses every possibility, and He, the Exalted, has judged them here that they follow conjecture and guessing.

We know that the disbelievers are of two kinds: a kind who knows the reality of the matter but alters the reality into falsehood (ifk) and guessing; and another kind who does not know the reality of the matter, but listens to someone they believe does know.

Therefore there is one who follows (with a kasra on the ba') and one who follows (with a fatha on the ba'). The one who follows (with fatha) knows that what he says is crooked speech that distorts the reality and adorns it; but the one who follows (with kasra) supposes that he follows trustworthy rational people, so he accepts their words as true.

Therefore, the follower (with kasra) has conjecture on his side, while the follower (with fatha) has guessing, falsehood, and fabrication on his side. Therefore Allah the Exalted tells us: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Scripture except wishful thinking, and they do not but assume.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:78]. These, then, accept what is told them, because they are unlettered, and what is said to them is probable; and if they had reasoned with their minds, they would not have concluded that it was probable speech.

As for the others, Allah the Exalted says about them: ﴿So woe to those who write the scripture with their own hands and then say, "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price...﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:79]. These are the ones from whom guessing, falsehood, false speech and slander come.

Therefore, if the disbelievers are among the unlettered, they are of the people of conjecture, and the saying of Allah the Exalted applies to them: ﴿They follow not except assumption...﴾ [Yunus 10:66].

And if they are of the leaders and chiefs, these are the ones to whom the saying of Allah the Exalted applies: ﴿And they do not but guess.﴾ [Yunus 10:66]

(1) Allah, the Lord of Might, says: ﴿So when the two groups saw each other, the companions of Musa said, "Indeed, we are overtaken." He said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me." So We inspired to Musa: "Strike the sea with your staff," and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain. And We brought the others near there. And We saved Musa and those with him, all of them. Then We drowned the others. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:61-68]. "Al-farq" is a split or a part of it; "al-tawd" is a great mountain. [Cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (3/336), and Lisan al-'Arab: root f-r-q.]

(2) Allah, the Lord of Might, says: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water." He said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy." And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾ [Hud 11:43]. The son of Nuh, out of his ignorance, believed that the flood would not reach the mountaintops, and that if he clung to a mountain's summit it would save him from drowning. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/446].

(3) The Lord of the Judi: Mujahid said: it is a mountain in al-Jazirah, and it is the one on which Nuh's ship came to rest. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/446]. It was also said: it is Mount Ararat in eastern Turkey in Anatolia.

(4) Qist: He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ [al-Fath 48:4]. And He also says: ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him.﴾ [al-Muddaththir 74:31].

(5) "Al-mudabbirat amran": these are the angels who arrange the affair from the heaven to the earth by the command of their Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

(6) "Al-muhayminun": those who are absorbed in the worship and obedience of Allah. Among the angels are those who have no occupation but worship: you find some standing who do not bow, some bowing who do not prostrate, and some prostrating who do not rise. There are also the Karubiyyun, who are the nearest angels to the eight bearers of the Throne. He, the Exalted, said of them: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who believe...﴾ [Ghafir 40:7].

(7) "Istajara bihi": sought his protection. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah...﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:6]. And "ajara": undertook to protect. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿...and He protects, and none can protect against Him...﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:88], meaning that He undertakes the protection of whoever seeks refuge in Him, and no one can grant protection to one whom Allah wills to punish. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

(8) This refers to what happened in the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with Abu Bakr from Makkah to Madinah, when they entered the cave; Allah caused a tree to grow at its entrance, placed two doves sitting on eggs there, and a large spider that sealed the cave's entrance with threads covered in dust, as if it were the dust of years.

(9) Zann: what arises in the soul from an indication; it is a probable doubt, and its verb is among the verbs of probability, of the pattern of nasara. Zann is a verbal noun, and zann is also the name for that thought which arose in the soul. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they have no knowledge of it. They follow not except assumption, and indeed assumption avails nothing against the truth.﴾ [al-Najm 53:28]. Its plural is zunun. Zann is used metaphorically in the sense of certainty, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account.﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:20]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

(10) Kharṣ: lying and speaking without knowledge. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Killed were the liars (al-kharrasun).﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:10]. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, the liars. [Lisan al-'Arab: root kh-r-s, adapted].

(11) Ifk: he lies and fabricates falsehood; al-ifk with a kasra on the hamza is lying; affak is an intensive form, meaning one who lies much. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar.﴾ [al-Jathiyah 45:7]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].

(12) Buhtan: fabrication and lying. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿...nor bring a slander they invent...﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 60:12]. [Lisan al-'Arab: root b-h-t].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 10, verse 67:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day to see by. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.﴾ (67)

After the Truth, glorified is He, had explained faith and the believers, and what the disbelievers might claim concerning the Prophet of the message, and after He had explained the method (manhaj), He now brings speech about His signs in the universe, as confirmation of what is sought through what exists.

What is sought is that one believe in a Messenger who conveys a method (manhaj) from Allah, so that this method may be beneficial to us. If anyone wants proof of this, let him look at the blessings that were found for the human being before he was given obligations (taklif): are they in his interest or not in his interest?

Since the signs present in the universe, which have been subjected to the human being, benefit him in his life, why would he not give thanks to the One who gave him all those blessings? The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gave the human being many blessings before obligation, and as soon as he reaches puberty he becomes obligated.

So Allah, glorified is He, has not obligated anyone except after overwhelming him with blessings beneficial to him, in the belief of the servant and in the truth of reality.

So when obligation comes to you, measure what is demanded of you against what was found for you. If you believe that the cosmic signs which preceded obligation were beneficial to you before "do this" and "do not do this" were demanded of you, then take from them a reality of truth that confirms the truth of what is demanded of you as obligation. Just as they benefited you in the first, so Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, will benefit you by following the obligation, and face the movement of life in the light of this obligation, so that you may be happy (1).

We know that the basic nature of the human being is that he rests first in order to move, then he tires, then he rests. For this reason we find the obligations came in the same pattern: the Truth, glorified is He, gave you rest until the age of puberty, and you took and enjoyed the blessings of Allah, the Exalted, until the age of puberty. You rested by choice, and you rested in what you desired. Then "do" and "do not do" come, so that you commit to what suits you in all your circumstances.

If obligation is going to take some of your effort, there is a time interval for rest. In your life you find a time for rest and a time for movement, and rest makes you strive actively toward movement, and movement takes from you the effort after which you wish to rest.

So: movement needs rest, and rest needs movement. The Truth, glorified is He, came to the time period called "the day," and showed us that just as He divided human existence into two stages:

The first: what precedes puberty, in which there is no obligation.

The second: what follows puberty, in which there is obligation.

Likewise Allah, glorified is He, divided "the day" into a time for rest and a time for movement, and He said, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day to see by..﴾ (67) [Yunus].

Just as the Truth, glorified is He, created the day for us and in it a time for rest and a time for movement, so the Truth, glorified is He, legislated the method of religion so that the movement of life may be upright, because the human being, the vicegerent on earth, must move, and his movement must be according to the requirement of "do this" and "do not do this." Whatever has no "do" or "do not do" concerning it is permissible: if he wishes, he does it, and if he wishes, he does not do it (2).

Every action and every prohibition requires movement. Beware of imagining that a prohibition does not require movement, because you are moving in some matter and then the decision to stop comes to you. You may suppose that stopping requires no movement, because it has deprived you of the capacity to carry out what you were doing. But you forget that there is an inner movement: the drives that kept pressing you to do what your soul desires and what does not accord with the method of Allah, and you restrain those drives and curb their momentum (3), because Allah, glorified is He, has commanded you to do so.

As long as there is movement, fatigue must come from it; therefore Allah, exalted is He, has given you a right to rest.

Likewise with the life span of a human being: Allah, exalted is He, did not obligate the human being except after puberty, and He left him the first period of his life without obligation or accountability. Yet He did not entirely cut off obligation in that stage; rather He withheld accountability for what he "does" or "does not do," and He left the responsibility of training him in obligation to the father, for example. The father says to his son, "Do not lie." If he lies, the father punishes him. The same is the case from the parent: the command and prohibition are for the child, and command and prohibition require reward or punishment.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explains this matter to us when he says: "Command your children to pray at seven years old, and strike them for it at ten years old" (4).

The one who here commands the son to pray is the father, and he is also the one who punishes for abandoning prayer, and he is the one who rewards his son if he wishes to make prayer beloved to the son and to give the son a delight in worship.

When the father obligates his son to pray, the son obeys, because the father is the one who fulfills the son's needs and achieves his interests, and the son knows that his father will only require of him what achieves those interests; and he does it because he loves him. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made command and prohibition something beneficial to the child, so that there is a basis of acceptance in the soul.

When puberty comes, obligation comes from Allah, and command comes from Allah, and reward and punishment come from Him, glorified is He.

So: command and prohibition before puberty come from the father, so that the human being becomes accustomed to receiving command and prohibition from his Lord and the Lord of his father.

If life and conduct in it in the light of the method of Allah, exalted is He, requires movement in "do" and "do not do," then the human being must need rest from movement. For this reason Allah, glorified is He, shows us that He placed in "the day" night and day, and for every task. So beware of putting the task of one thing in the place of another, lest affairs become confused. But circumstances may compel you to that: there are those who stay awake for guarding, and there are those who stay awake to work in bakeries or prepare breakfast for people. For this reason there is a precautionary measure of destiny (qadar), and so the Truth, glorified is He, said in another verse:

﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and day and your seeking of His bounty..﴾ (23) [al-Rum]. Because the Truth, glorified is He, knew from eternity that there are interests that can only be achieved at night; whoever works at night rests by day. Had the verse come in general terms, we would have said to one who sleeps by day: No, this is not the time for quiet and rest (5).

But the Truth, glorified is He, willed to place the precautionary measure of destiny, so that the one whose work is connected with the night may rest.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein..﴾ (67) [Yunus]. We know that there is a difference between "creating" (khalq), "making" (ja'l), and "possessing" (mulk). The example of creating: He, glorified is He, created time, then came to this time to make from it night and day (6).

So: making (ja'l) is directing a created thing to a task. An example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, though He is exalted above any comparison or similitude: you find the potter holding the clay in order to make from it a jug. He first prepares the clay by mixing water with earth and kneading them together, then makes from the clay a jug, or a flowerpot, or a rose vase. In doing so he is transforming a created thing into something that has a task.

All time belongs to Allah, glorified is He, and from it He made the portion of night and the portion of day. Just as He created the human being and directed one part of him to be hearing, another part to be sight, another part to be a brain, and another part to be a lung, all of that is taken from what Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, created. That is, He, glorified is He, made things from what He had already created so that they might perform a task for the created being.

In our life, to the highest likeness of Allah, we find someone spinning threads from cotton, and someone weaving cloth from those threads, and after that we find someone taking this cloth to make a robe, or trousers, or a shirt, or a blanket.

So: making (ja'l) is taking from a created thing for a task. Creating may result in possession, and making may also result in possession: whoever shapes a portion of clay is its owner, and whoever makes a jug from clay possesses it.

Thus we find that creating and making may both result in some kind of ownership; but the ownership that follows creating and making makes you benefit from things even though you may not own them. For this reason we find the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿Or who owns the hearing and the sights..﴾ (31) [Yunus].

The Truth, glorified is He, created cattle for us, subjected them to us, and made them ours. When the Truth, glorified is He, says "owns," His ownership never ends for anyone, whether among creatures through creating or making, but it remains owned; therefore we said that transplanting organs is a presumption over what the created being does not own, rather it is owned by the Creator, glorified and exalted is He.

The Truth, glorified is He, mentions night and day, saying: ﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day to see by..﴾ (67) [Yunus].

The sentence might have been expected to say: "He made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day for you to move about."

But He, glorified is He, willed to bring here the miraculous Qur'anic expression, and said: ﴿and the day to see by﴾.

Is it the day that sees, or is it we?

Is the day seeing, or is it seen by?

In former times they had not reached the scientific reality that we have reached now. They used to believe that light goes out from the eye onto the thing seen, so that you see it, until the Arab Muslim scientist Ibn al-Haytham came and showed by experiment that light is reflected from the seen object to the eye, as evidenced by the fact that if the object is in light while you are in darkness, you see it, and if the situation is reversed, you do not see it.

So the Qur'an has preceded all theories, and has shown us that the day brings light, so that light is reflected from creatures and existing things to the eye, and you see them.

So: the day is the one that makes things visible, because it brings the light necessary for this light to be reflected from the objects to the eyes.

We find the Qur'an, when it deals with night and day, saying: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day..﴾ (37) [Fussilat], and saying: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible..﴾ (12) [al-Isra']. The day's sign is "visible," as Ibn al-Haytham the Muslim scientist demonstrated, though in outward appearance it is the one that makes things visible.

The Truth, glorified is He, gives us a living experience with Musa (peace be upon him), in His saying to Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Musa? He said: It is my staff, I lean upon it and beat down leaves for my sheep, and I have in it other uses. He said: Throw it down, O Musa. So he threw it down, and behold, it was a serpent slithering.﴾ (17–20) [Ta-Ha]. Allah willed this so that Musa might learn by experience what would happen with his staff before Pharaoh, then before the magicians, with the assurance from Him that Musa, when he sees it turn into a serpent before his eyes at first glance, would be frightened; so the Truth, glorified is He, reassures him by saying: ﴿..Take it and fear not; We shall return it to its former state (21) [Ta-Ha]. The first time the staff turned into a serpent was an experience for preparation, so that Musa (peace be upon him) would not panic or fear at the moment of undergoing the practical experience, and so that he would step forward to present the miracle while being completely confident before Pharaoh.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, said to Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿And put your hand into your bosom (12) [al-Naml].

The jayb (bosom) is the opening through which the neck passes in a robe, and it is called the "qubba." No one should suppose that the pocket meant here is the place where money is put, because the place for money in former times was inside the robe, like the waistcoat (sidiri) worn by the people of the countryside. The pocket where we put money was called a jayb only because the hand does not reach the pocket except by entering the opening through which the neck comes out.

The Truth, glorified is He, said to Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿And put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without harm..﴾ (12) [al-Naml], and He informs him: ﴿among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people; indeed they were a corrupt people (12). So when Our signs came to them, visible..﴾ (13) [al-Naml]. Thus the signs were "visible" (11), as if they were saying to the eye: "Look at me."

Here in the verse which is the subject of our reflections, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day to see by..﴾ (67) [Yunus]. He did not say "that you may move therein," but brought what guarantees the safety

1 Confirming His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. And for you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you request."﴾ [Fussilat 30–31]..
2 Because the word "do" (افعل) includes the command of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) concerning obligations, obligatory acts, sunnahs, recommended acts and preferred acts. And the word "do not" (لا تفعل) includes the prohibition of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) concerning the forbidden and the disliked. As for other than these, it is permissible..
3 "Curb their momentum" (تكبح جماحها): restrain them from sins. Derived from kabh the animal, meaning pulling it toward oneself with the bridle and striking its mouth so that it stops and does not run. [Lisan al-Arab, root k-b-h]..
4 Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/187) and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (495), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As. The wording is Ahmad's..
5 Naama (نام) fulan nawman: he lay down or dozed, and by it he became calm and secure and trusted; and he neglected his need and did not concern himself with it. Anama: he caused him to sleep. Tanawwama: feigned sleep. Istanama: slept and became calm. Sleep is among the signs of Allah, for it is rest and tranquility, and rest with tranquility gives strength for movement and steadiness in thought and concentration. [al-Mu'jam al-Wajiz, adapted]..
6 He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear? (71) Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see? (72) And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and that you may be grateful (73)﴾ [al-Qasas]..
7 Al-dau' (الضوء), with a fatha on the dad, and al-du' with a damma, and al-diya' (الضياء), and al-diwa' (الضواء): the light that spreads from luminous bodies. Al-dau' may be specified for what issues from a self-luminous thing, such as the light of the sun, and it may be specified as light (nur) for what is derived from light, such as the light of the moon. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿It is He who made the sun a diya' and the moon a nur..﴾ (5) [Yunus]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted]..
8 Allah made the sign of the night the moon, and made the sign of the day the sun, and made the sign of the day "visible," i.e., luminous, illuminating the whole universe; as for the moon, He effaced its sign, which is the darkness of the moon within it. Adapted from Tafsir Ibn Kathir (3/27)..
9 That is: We shall return it to its original state (a staff)..
10 Al-jayb: the throat and chest. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿and let them draw their head-coverings over their bosoms (jуyub)..﴾ (31) [al-Nur]..
11 Basara bihi: he saw it with his eyes, so he is baseer; basura bil-amr: he knew it as if he had seen it with his eyes. His saying: ﴿So she saw him from afar..﴾ (11) [al-Qasas] means she saw him from one side of the house. Absara: he saw. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And see, and they will see (179) [al-Saffat], meaning: look and watch. Absarahu: made him see, and made him know as one who sees. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And see them, and they will see (175) [al-Saffat]. Al-Baseer is one of the beautiful names of Allah; al-baseer is one who has two eyes by which he sees, the opposite of blind. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Are the blind and the seeing alike?..﴾ (50) [al-An'am]. Al-basira: the light of the heart and clear proof. Among the figurative usages is their saying: "a day that is mubsir," meaning luminous. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein and the day mubsiran..﴾ (67) [Yunus]; and His saying: ﴿And We made the sign of the day mubsira..﴾ (12) [al-Isra']; and His saying: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a mubsira..﴾ (59) [al-Isra'], meaning a clear miracle; and His saying: ﴿..when a visitation from Satan touches them, they remember, and behold, they are mubsirun (201) [al-A'raf], meaning those who know the truth. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted]..

Here is the same verse and its nearby material, which the translation itself does not repeat. The verse text itself refuses their claim. An example: when you say "So-and-so took a house," it means that So-and-so had a prior existence before taking the house, and by that existence he took it. So when it is said, ﴿They say: God has taken a son...﴾ [Yunus 68], this is their acknowledgment of God's perfection and self-subsistence before He took a son.

They differed about this son. Some of them said the angels are God's daughters, and the Truth, glorified is He, refuted them in that. Others said ʿUzayr is the son of God, and they were the Jews(1), and God, glorified is He, refuted them in that. A group of Christians said the Messiah is the son of God(2), and the Truth, glorified is He, refuted them in that(3).

Then, what is the motive for God to take a son?

Has He exhausted His strength so that a son would help Him?

Could He, glorified is He, God forbid, become weak so that the strength of a son would extend Him or He would depend on it?

It is like when an old man confronts a young man, and the young man attacks the old man, so it is said to the young man: "Beware, for this old man has a son stronger than you," and the young man is restrained. Or the old man says to the young man: "My sons surpass you in strength," and in this there is pride in children.

The Truth, glorified is He, wants to negate all these claims, so that the movement of life is cohesive and interconnected, not conflicting and not contradictory. Therefore the mover must be one God from whom all commands proceed, so there is no conflict among those commands. For if the commands proceeded from a plurality, the movement of life would collide, dissipating energy and corrupting what is good.

Therefore the command must proceed from one commander to whom every order is submitted. This God is exalted above everything you know of contingent things. He has transcendence in His essence, so no essence resembles His essence; transcendence in His attributes, so no attribute resembles His attribute; and transcendence in His acts, so no act resembles His act(4).

To guarantee this matter, God must be one. But some people made partners for God, and whoever did not make Him a partner imagined that He has a son and offspring.

We say to them: your statement, ﴿They say: God has taken a son...﴾ [Yunus 68], turns back on you, because the meaning of taking a son is that divinity existed first independently, and by this divinity a son was taken.

Among the polytheists some said the angels are God's daughters.

The Truth, glorified is He, responded to them: ﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? (21) That, then, is an unjust division (22)﴾ [al-Najm]. All perfection belongs to God, glorified is He; it is an essential perfection. For this reason it comes in the middle of the verse, where He says, ﴿Glory be to Him! He is the Self-Sufficient...﴾ [Yunus 68]. "Glory be to Him" (subhanahu) means transcendence, and "the Self-Sufficient" means the one who needs no helper, as you seek help from your children. He is eternal in existence, so He does not need a son like humans, who are contingent beings that begin and end. That is why they love to have children, as the poet says:

*My son, O my self, after I am gone*

It is said: "He who has no son has no memory." When a human knows he will certainly die, he wants to continue living through his offspring.

For this reason, when a son is born to a person, the person feels joy and happiness, and the ignorant one is the one who grieves when his wife bears him a daughter, because the daughter will not carry the name to those after her, whereas the son and the grandson carry the grandfather's name, so the grandfather feels that he is preserved in male descent over two generations.

So taking a son is either seeking help or self-pride, and the Truth, glorified is He, is free of both need for help and free of pride, because you take pride in someone stronger than you, and there is no one stronger than God, Most High. He, glorified is He, does not need extension, because He is the First and the Last. Accordingly, the idea of God taking a son is invalid in every form.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, states, as a contrast to that idea, ﴿Glory be to Him(6)﴾, because it cuts off every possibility preceding it, and He follows it with ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient﴾, because He is self-sufficient of taking a son and self-sufficient of everything. His saying ﴿Glory be to Him﴾ is transcendence, and transcendence is the elevation of the one made transcendent above sharing anything with Him, in essence or in acts.

When something is mentioned that is an attribute of God and also an attribute of His creation, beware of taking this attribute to be like that attribute.

If you encounter a rich person among humans, wealth among humans is accidental, but God's richness is in His essence, glorified is He.

You are living(7), and God, glorified is He, is living. But is your life like His life? No, because His life was not preceded by non-existence, whereas your life was preceded by non-existence; His life is not followed by non-existence, whereas non-existence will follow your life.

God exists and you exist, but His existence, glorified is He, is essential existence, whereas your existence is accidental existence.

When the Truth, glorified is He, says that He has a hand, ﴿The hand of God is over their hands...﴾ [al-Fath 10], His hand cannot be like your hand, because His essence is not like your essence, and His attributes are not like your attributes. He, glorified is He, is the Supreme Power, and He cannot be subject to anyone's power.

For this reason, when God, glorified is He, manifests Himself to His creation, He will manifest in a form that differs from every imagination of the servant, and this form differs from one servant to another. If the form in which God, glorified is He, manifests were something within human power, that would mean there is a human mind that has been able to encompass it. Whatever occurs to your mind, God, glorified is He, is other than that, because what occurs to the mind is within power, since it is a thought, but God, glorified is He, never becomes something within power.

When you give a problem in arithmetic or geometry, for example, to a student and he solves it, that means his mind has mastered it. But if you bring a preparatory-school student a geometry problem set for engineering college students, his mind will not be able to master it.

Thus, if a human being grasped something of God other than what God has said about Himself, God would become something within power, but the Truth, glorified is He, is exalted above that, because He is the Supreme Power who never becomes something within power.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, teaches us to say the word ﴿Glory be to Him﴾ as a declaration of God's transcendence, which is the obligatory transcendence above everything that occurs to a human about God. This glorification or transcendence is an essential attribute of God, before anything existed and after He created creation. So all creatures must glorify Him, and glorification began with creation.

Glorification is a continuous act that does not stop or end. For this reason you find the Qur'an's proofs in the transcendence-declaring surahs(8) confirm this, as the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed...﴾ [al-Isra' 1].

Beware of thinking that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, traveled by his own decision. Rather, the one who took him by night is the Truth, glorified is He. Do not think that distance can restrict the absolute will of the Truth, nor place, nor time, because the act is ascribed to God, Most High, and we cannot measure an act ascribed to God by the measure of time and place, or according to the law of relative motion, because the Truth, glorified is He, has absolute power, whereas you are a mere contingent human bounded by time and place.

If you walk from here to Alexandria, for example, on your feet, you will cover the distance in weeks. If you ride an animal, you may take days to reach Alexandria. If you ride a car, you will cover the distance in two hours. If you ride a rocket, you will arrive within minutes. That is, the more powerful the means of arrival, the less time the arrival takes, and this is a summary of the theory of motion. If the one who made the night journey is God, glorified is He, who is the power of powers, then it cannot be measured against the will of another power, nor can the matter be measured by the nearness or farness of place or by the manner of time that you know.

Beware of understanding God's night journey to be like your journey, because an act draws its strength from its agent, and as long as the agent is God, glorified is He, no one can limit His acts by time.

The Truth, glorified is He, opened the surah of al-Isra' with the word of glorification, and its first verses speak about the most precise matter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke of concerning his own person: that he was taken on the night journey. Through the event of the night journey, He established the reality of the ascension (mi'raj), and that the cosmic laws (nawamis)(9) were broken for him. He told us of what we know so that we would believe His account of what we do not know, and so that we would measure what we do not know by what we know, and thus his truthfulness, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his account of what we do not know becomes confirmed for us.

Therefore the word "glory be to Him" is for transcendence, and it belongs to God from eternity, before He created creation, for He bore witness to His own essence that He is one God. Then the angels bore witness, and the glorification of every creature God has brought into existence is repeated.

You find the surahs of the Noble Qur'an in which glorification comes affirming that He, glorified is He, is transcendent, and that glorification is His from before He created creation, and then He created creation so that they would glorify Him. In surah al-Hadid He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Hadid 1], and He, glorified is He, says in surah al-Hashr: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies God...﴾ [al-Hashr 1]. Did everyone in the heavens and everyone on earth glorify Him once and that was the end of it? No, because God, glorified is He, says: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies God, the King, the Holy...﴾ [al-Jumu'a 1], and He, glorified is He, says in surah al-Taghabun: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies God. To Him belongs dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Taghabun 1]. So glorification belongs to God from eternity, and creation and all existence glorify Him, after God created it: heavens, earth, and what is in them. Nothing remains except you, O human, so glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.

In the verse about which we are reflecting, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿They say: God has taken a son. Glory be to Him...﴾ [Yunus 68]. The reason for glorification and transcendence above having a son is given in His saying ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient﴾, because taking a son is only done out of need, either for help, or for reliance, or for pride, or for extension. All of these are invalid with respect to Him, glorified is He, who is the Supreme Truth. He, glorified is He, says in another verse: ﴿And they say: God has taken a son. Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah 116]. Qunut means acknowledging servitude to God, submitting to Him, and obeying Him.

In the verse we are reflecting on, He, glorified is He, says: ﴿You have no authority for this. Do you say about God what you do not know?﴾ [Yunus 68]. The "in" (inna) here may come for negation, as in the Truth's saying: ﴿Their mothers are none but those who bore them...﴾ [al-Mujadila 2], and in His saying here: ﴿You have no authority for this...﴾ [Yunus 68], meaning: you have no proof indicating that God, Most High, has taken a son.

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, ends the verse with His saying: ﴿Do you say about God what you do not know?﴾ [Yunus 68], meaning: you do not possess any information from God about that. There is no information about God except from God, and no one may claim knowledge about his Lord, for He, glorified is He, is the one who knows about Himself.

1. The Lord of Glory, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿And the Jews said: ʿUzayr is the son of God...﴾ [al-Tawba 30].
2. God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And the Christians said: the Messiah is the son of God...﴾ [al-Tawba 30].
3. God, Most High, says: ﴿That is their saying with their mouths, imitating the saying of those who disbelieved before them. God fight them! How are they deluded?﴾ [al-Tawba 30].
4. This is the confirmation of His saying: ﴿There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura 11]. He, glorified is He, has no likeness in His essence, in His attributes, or in His acts.
5. "Daza" in judgment means to be unjust. "Qisma dayzaa" and "dawzaa" mean unjust, containing neither right nor justice. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root ḍ-y-z, adapted]
6. "Sabbaha" (yusabbihu) in the pattern of fataha means: to swim, to float and pass through water. Metaphorically, "the horse swam" means it ran as if swimming in water, and "the stars swam" means they moved in their orbits. God, Most High, says: ﴿Each in an orbit swims﴾ [al-Anbiya' 33], and they were treated as rational beings because of the regularity of their movement. "Sabbih ism rabbika" means: declare His name free of every deficiency and describe Him with every perfection. Or say: "Subhan Allah," meaning I declare God free of deficiency and describe Him with perfection. It is in the accusative as a verbal noun, standing in place of its verb. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted]
7. "Hayya" (yahya) like "radiya" (yarda), and "hayya" with assimilation, yahya, hayatan and hayawanan, is the opposite of "mata" (died), so he is living. It is specific to every being with a spirit, and it is metaphorically applied to the earth. God, Most High, says: ﴿So We gave life to the earth with it after its death﴾ [Fatir 9]. It is also borrowed to mean righteousness and faith. God, Most High, says: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life﴾ [al-An'am 122]. "Al-Hayy" (the Living) is among the Beautiful Names of God: ﴿God—there is no god but Him, the Living﴾ [al-Baqarah 255]. The present life is contrasted with the afterlife: ﴿...and the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ [Al ʿImran 185]. "Al-Mahya" is a noun of place/time meaning life: ﴿Say: my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am 162], meaning: my life and my death.
8. You find glorification in the past tense: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Hadid 1]; in the present tense: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies God, to Him belongs dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Taghabun 1]; in the imperative: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la 1]; and as a verbal noun: subhanahu. With this we notice that the past glorifies Him, the future glorifies Him, and the present mentions Him, and the universe with time is in continuous glorification: ﴿...and there is nothing but that glorifies with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed He is Forbearing, Forgiving﴾ [al-Isra' 44].
9. The laws of the universe: the secrets God, glorified and exalted is He, placed in the universe, including laws that regulate the motion of its parts and components.
10. "Qanata" (yaqnutu), like "nasara" (to be humble and submissive): to submit to His hand. "Qanata al-mu'min bi-Llah" means he obeyed Him and acknowledged servitude to Him. "Qanata fi salatihi" means he was humble and calm. "Qanata" also means he supplicated and prolonged the supplication. Qunut is obedience and supplication. God, Most High, says: ﴿And whoever of you is devoutly obedient to God and His Messenger and does righteousness, We will give her reward twice﴾ [al-Ahzab 31], and His saying: ﴿And they say: God has taken a son. Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah 116], meaning: submissive, acknowledging divinity, obedient. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 69:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent falsehood against God will not prosper.﴾ (69)

When the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, speaks of faith, its fruit and its end, He brings prosperity (al-falah) as the result of that faith. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿He has indeed prospered who purifies it﴾ [al-Shams 9], and He says: ﴿The believers have indeed prospered﴾ [al-Mu'minun 1], and He also says: ﴿It is those who are the successful﴾ [al-A'raf 157]. All of these come from the root "falah," which is taken from a tangible matter connected to the life of a living being. The requirements of a living being's existence are: a soul, water, and food. Breathing comes from the air that surrounds the earth, water descends from the sky or is extracted from what seeps into the ground, and food comes from the earth, and everything whose origin is the earth is extracted through farming (al-falahah).

Therefore we say: farming (al-falahah) is the sustaining cause of life. Just as a person farms the land, ploughs it, sows seeds in it, then waters it, and then it ripens and the fruit comes out, and it is said: "aflaha," meaning his cultivation produced a good yield. The Truth, glory be to Him, willed to name the good faithful harvest "falah."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) explained to us that this world is the field of the Hereafter. So if you want fruit, then exert effort.

Beware of supposing that religion, when it takes something from you in this world, diminishes what you have. No, rather it multiplies for you what you have. [2]

The example I always give—and to God belongs the highest example—is that we find the farmer who plants a feddan with wheat. He takes from his storehouse an ardeb to use as seed in the earth. If his wife were foolish, not knowing the principles of agriculture, she would say to him: "You took from the wheat. How can you leave your dependents while you diminish their sustenance?"

This woman does not know that he took an ardeb of stored wheat so that after the harvest he would return with ten or fifteen ardebs of wheat.

Likewise, what God, glory be to Him, desires in this world may appear to diminish things for you, but He gives you the fruits of the Hereafter and increases them.

So then: "falah" is a word taken from "falaha al-ardh," meaning he ploughed the land, split it, and planted it, in order to take the fruit.

Just as you take your share of fruits in proportion to your share of toil and work, so it is with the matter of the Hereafter and the matter of this world.

An example of this: the farmer who ploughs the land, carries fertiliser to the land on the beast [3], then wakes early at the times of irrigation. You find this farmer in a state of ease and joy on the day of harvest, and his condition differs from one who neglects the land, spends his time at the café, stays up all night in front of the television, and then comes the day of harvest to grieve over a crop he did not cultivate well.

The words of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Indeed, those who invent falsehood against God will not prosper [4] (69)﴾ [Yunus].

That is: those who say about God, or concerning God, without knowledge from God, are the ones who will not prosper.

I explained earlier that everything related to God, glory be to Him, is known only through God. But what drives them to fabrication?

Yes, every movement in life must have as its motive some benefit, and views differ on benefit and what follows from it. The lazy student wandering the streets, refusing to learn, is found failing and not successful in his future. As for the student eager for his studies, he is the one who obtains the standing befitting him in society. The first student had limited horizons and did not see the extent and magnitude of the benefit, but confined the benefit to a immediate pleasure, sacrificing a better lasting good. What led these people to fabricate lies against God is the collapse of the self. Every self has an existence and has a standing, so if its standing collapses, a person feels he has no worth in his society.

The example I gave earlier was the barber-surgeon of the village, who used to treat everyone. Then one of the village's youths graduated from the faculty of medicine and opened a clinic. If the barber-surgeon is wise, he goes to the doctor to work in his clinic as a nurse or as a stretcher-bearer (tamrigi). But if pride in sin takes hold of him, he persists and is stubborn, yet he will not be able to repel the doctor's knowledge.

Likewise, the gang of disbelief and the leaders of misguidance, when they are confronted with the arrival of a messenger from God, they think he will take sovereignty for himself, although any messenger of God's messengers, peace be upon him, gives sovereignty only to its rightful owner, namely the Highest Truth, glory be to Him.

When he takes from them the sovereignty that used to guarantee them standing, prestige, status and greatness, they are struck by nervous collapse and try to resist the Messenger in defence of worldly power.

An example of this is the arrival of the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah, when some were working to install Abdullah ibn Ubayy as king [6]. Therefore that man opposed Islam, and when he could not, he embraced it outwardly as hypocrisy, and remained hostile to Islam, although if he had embraced Islam sincerely and drawn near to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he would have gained many times what he would have taken had he become king.

Thus it is with the leaders of misguidance and the imams of disbelief: they are anxious for themselves and fearful for worldly power, because the Messenger, when he comes, levels people among themselves; therefore they stand against the call to preserve worldly power. Hence the Truth, glory be to Him, says regarding the cause of their fabrication of lies:

﴿A brief enjoyment [7] in this world, then to Us is their return; then We shall make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve (70)﴾

1 Zakaha: purified it and cleared it of the defects of body and soul.
2 The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿What is with you will end, and what is with God remains...﴾ [al-Nahl 96], and His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of God will be repaid to you...﴾ [al-Anfal 60], and His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like...﴾ [al-An'am 160], and His saying: ﴿If you lend to God a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you...﴾ [al-Taghabun 17].
3 The beast (dabbah), namely the she-camel that is ridden, i.e. its back. Its plural is mata-ya. [Lisan al-Arab: root (m-t-y)].
4 Yaftaruna al-kadhib: they lie, or they speak without knowledge. La yuflihun: they will not succeed nor triumph. The Exalted said: ﴿And he has failed who fabricates [a lie]﴾ [Ta-Ha 61].
5 This contradicts the logic of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the concept of the call, for the disbelievers offered him wealth, kingship, authority and status, and he chose the Lord of all, and said his words which time has recorded and conscious minds have preserved: "By God, if they placed the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left, on condition that I abandon this matter, until God makes it manifest, or I perish in it, I would not abandon it." Cited by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/266).
6 Ibn Ishaq related in the Sirah that the people of Abdullah ibn Ubayy had "strung beads for him so they might crown him and then make him king over them. Then God sent them His Messenger while they were in that state. When his people turned away from him to Islam, he was resentful and saw that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had robbed him of kingship. When he saw that his people had refused anything but Islam, he entered it unwillingly, harbouring hypocrisy and rancour." Sirah Ibn Hisham (2/216).
7 Al-mata': enjoyment, meaning everything one benefits from and desires to possess, such as food, household furnishings, merchandise, tools and wealth [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit]. The intended meaning is that God, glory be to Him, leaves the disbelievers to enjoy the transient goods of this world, since the whole world is not worth a gnat's wing in God's sight, but He will punish them for their disbelief with a severe punishment in the Hereafter and deprive them of the bliss of Paradise. Mata' also refers to a righteous wife, in agreement with the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The world is enjoyment, and the best of its enjoyment is a righteous woman."
Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, Book of Suckling, chapter "The best enjoyment of the world is a righteous woman," hadith (59), from Abdullah ibn Amr. In Abu Nu'aym's Hilyat al-Awliya (3/310) there is the addition: "If he looks at her, it pleases him, and if he commands her, she obeys him."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 70:

So it is no wonder that the leaders of disbelief and the imams of misguidance are distressed that a new caller to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, should strip them of leadership and sovereignty. They fear that the new caller to Allah will take authority from all of them, not for his own sake, but for the sake of the One whose will he serves.

Had the caller to Allah been seizing temporal power for himself, we would say: it is one self against another self. But the Prophet (ﷺ) made clear that he returns, even in matters that concern him personally, to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

Allah, the Truth, also reveals to us the meager gain they are defending, that it is ﴿a brief enjoyment in this world...﴾ (70). This is because each of them loves to deceive himself, through the foolishness of assessing benefit. The word "dunya" (this world) must contain the real essence of the thing it is attributed to.

Names, as we know, are the marks of what they name. When you say that so-and-so is tall, you are giving him the mark of height.

When you say "dunya," it derives from "al-dunuww" (nearness) or "al-dana'a" (baseness). If you consider nearness to be the road that leads to the summit, this is an acceptable view, because the first step in reaching the highest is nearness, and when you adhere to the method of Allah, you attain height and elevation in the Hereafter.

So, to whoever describes the world as base in every respect we say: No, rather it is a "dunya" on the condition that you take it as a path to the heights. Whoever does not take it that way makes his own station the base one. As for the one who takes it as a path to elevation, he is the one who has succeeded by following the method of Allah.

Thus the world is not base, because religion's concern is not the Hereafter; rather its concern is this world. The method of religion obliges you with "do" and "do not" in this world, and the Hereafter is the abode of recompense. Recompense for a thing is not the same as its subject matter. You can make the world beneficial to you if you make it a field for the Hereafter.

Beware of acting on the basis that the world's age is millions of years, for as one who lives in the world it does not concern you whether its life is long or short. What concerns you in the world is the measure of your stay in it. Your lifespan in it is uncertain, and indeed the whole duration of the world is uncertain. There are those who die at six months old and those who die at a hundred years, and each enjoys according to the measure of his life, then returns to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

As for those who went astray and fabricated lies against Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, they will not escape Allah, because their return is to Him, like all His creation. Those misguiders did not heed the outcome of the matter, nor the One in whose hand is the outcome of the matter, and they did not refrain.

But whoever looks to the outcome of the matter and does good in this world, his return is to good reward and Paradise. Whoever does not look to the outcome of the matter and fabricates lies against Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, then his destination and final place (2) is punishment, in confirmation of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Then We shall make them taste a severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ (70) [Yunus]. The degree of punishment varies with the one punished. If the one punished is weak, his punishment is weak; if he is of medium strength, his punishment is medium; but if the one punished is the strongest of the strong, his punishment must be severe. He, the Truth, says: ﴿Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ (102) [Hud]. After the Truth, subhanahu wa ta'ala, spoke of the principle of glorifying divinity above taking a son, He is the Self-Sufficient to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He showed us that we must take the method from one source, namely the messengers who convey from Allah, the Exalted. The Truth, subhanahu wa ta'ala, willed to speak to us about the procession of messages, because speech that is purely theoretical has no reality to support it, so the theory may be dismissed.

But if speech has a reality in the cosmos that supports the theoretical speech, this is proof of the soundness of the theoretical speech. Therefore, when we wish to magnify a certain issue in a social ill, we try to make a narrative out of it, that is, a matter that did not actually happen, but we imagine it as real, in order to demonstrate the theoretical point within an imagined reality.

The Truth, subhanahu wa ta'ala, relates to us in the Qur'an stories from the procession of messengers, to show the disbelievers: you will not be able to stand before this call, and before you is the record of history, and the events of the messengers with their peoples, those supported by the believers, and the stubborn and opposing disbelievers. If some of the earlier peoples did triumph over their messenger, then the disbelievers have the right to hope for victory over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (4).

This speech must be directed at people who have some knowledge of some events of the procession of messages. But perhaps their knowledge of it has faded, because time has lengthened over it.

1 The Lord of Might, subhanahu wa ta'ala, described the world, saying: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for one who fears Allah...﴾ (77) [An-Nisa'] and the Exalted said: ﴿The likeness of the life of this world is only like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, of which men and cattle eat, until when the earth takes on its adornment and is decked out, and its people think they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it a harvest as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who reflect﴾ (24) [Yunus].
2 Al-ma'ab wa al-ma'al: the return and the destination.
3 Alim: an intensive form of alam (pain), and shadid: an intensive form of shiddah (severity), meaning: extremely painful.
4 Many verses of the Noble Qur'an urge the disbelievers and others to reflect on the end of those who denied and the guilty, such as the Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth, then look how was the end of the deniers﴾ (11) [Al-An'am], and the Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see how was the end of the guilty﴾ (69) [An-Naml].

Here the Almighty says: ﴿And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, "O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of the signs of Allah are burdensome to you, then in Allah I have put my trust. So resolve upon your affair with your partners, then let not your affair be a source of distress to you; then carry it out against me and give me no respite."﴾ (71)

One might ask: why did Allah, glory be to Him, mention the story of Noah (peace be upon him) here, and not the story of Adam (peace be upon him) or Idris (peace be upon him), who were prophets before Noah?

From this arose the doubt that Adam was not a messenger, because some people thought that a messenger must bring his message to an existing community of human beings. These people did not realise that a messenger is sent first to himself.

If Adam (peace be upon him) was the first of creation, then he was sent to himself, and then he conveyed the message to those of his offspring who would come after him.

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, gave Adam (peace be upon him) a test in Paradise. There was a command and there was a prohibition, which is the verse: ﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in abundance wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree"﴾ (35) [al-Baqarah]. He was warned about Satan(2). Then Adam (peace be upon him) fell into the seduction of Satan, and Allah sent him down to the earth, chose him (ijtiba')(3), and accepted his repentance. His test remained with him: if he disobeyed his Lord, punishment would befall him, and he was warned against following Satan, lest he depart from the obedience of Allah, exalted is He.

Thus, the Almighty gave him the method (manhaj) and commanded him to carry out his mission on earth: first within himself, and then to convey it to those after him.

Just as the Almighty taught him all the names, Adam taught the names to his children, and they spoke [them]. Just as Adam conveyed the names to them, he conveyed to them the method. Allah, glory be to Him, taught him the names so that he might populate the world, and taught him the method so that he might act well in the world and thereby reach a good reward in the Hereafter.

Read the words of the Almighty: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he erred﴾ (121) [Ta-Ha], and the Almighty follows it with His words: ﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾ (122) [Ta-Ha]. The meaning of ijtiba' is being chosen for the message, first for oneself and then, after that, for those who come after. The Almighty is the one who said: ﴿And if there comes to you guidance from Me﴾ (38) [al-Baqarah]. Guidance (huda) is the method sent down to Adam (peace be upon him), and the message is nothing but the conveying of a method and guidance from Allah, glory be to Him, to creation.

Since the Almighty is the one who said: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ (15) [al-Isra'],

then those who came before Noah (peace be upon him) were those to whom Adam (peace be upon him) had conveyed [the message]. The evidence is what came in the account of the two sons of Adam in the words of the Almighty: ﴿And recite to them the news of Adam, in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice(4)...﴾ (27) [al-Ma'idah]. They had both offered a sacrifice to Allah, exalted is He.

Thus, knowledge of divinity was present among the sons of Adam, by the words of the Almighty: ﴿when they offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He said, "Allah only accepts from the righteous."﴾ (27) [al-Ma'idah]. So they acknowledged the existence of Allah, exalted is He, and also knew the prohibition, because in one of the two verses he said: ﴿"If you extend your hand against me to kill me, I shall not extend my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (28) [al-Ma'idah]. Thus, those who came after Adam (peace be upon him) knew the one God and knew the method. So, as for those who say that Adam (peace be upon him) was not a messenger, we say to them: understand from Allah well. You should have said: "This is a matter we do not understand," and they should have asked the people of remembrance (ahl al-dhikr) so that they would understand from them that Adam (peace be upon him) was a messenger, and that among his children were Qabil and Habil, who spoke about piety.

As for why the Almighty brought up the story of Noah (peace be upon him) here, we should know that Adam (peace be upon him) is the first human being, and that he conveyed to his children the method that had been conveyed to him, and guided them to what would benefit them. Then time passed and heedlessness arose, so Idris (peace be upon him) came, then heedlessness followed him, until Noah (peace be upon him) came.

Here the Almighty brings us the news of Noah (peace be upon him) in His words: ﴿And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people...﴾ (71) [Yunus]. Al-naba' is the important news that catches the attention, and it is the clear, evident matter.

The Almighty says: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news, about which they are in disagreement﴾ (1-3) [al-Naba']. So al-naba' is the important, striking news. Here comes the news of Noah (peace be upon him), who conveyed to his people, that is, addressed them. He testified for himself that he was a messenger conveying a method.

The word qawm (people) in the language is applied only to men(6). The Qur'an clarifies this in the words of the Almighty: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women [ridicule] women, perhaps they may be better than them...﴾ (11) [al-Hujurat].

So qawm are men, and the woman's affair is built on privacy, while movement in the world is for the man. We have explained this in the Almighty's address to Adam (peace be upon him) about Iblis, when He said: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not remove you both from Paradise and [thus] you will suffer﴾ (117) [Ta-Ha].

Because the address was to Adam, the Almighty said: ﴿and [thus] you will suffer﴾ (117) [Ta-Ha], and He did not say "you two will suffer" (tashqaya), which indicates that the woman has no share in the work outside the home that requires hardship. The woman settles (taqirru(7)) in the home to embrace the children and prepare a dwelling for the man with her tenderness, emotion, and stability.

As for standing and movement, they belong to the man.

The Almighty says: ﴿So let him not remove you both from Paradise, and [thus] you will suffer﴾ (117) [Ta-Ha]. So toil belongs to the man, and what it requires is standing, not sitting.

Then the Almighty says, on the tongue of Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿O my people, if my standing [among you] is burdensome to you...﴾ (71) [Yunus]. Here Noah appeals to his people with expressions of tenderness, that is, he uses the form that makes the listeners feel that he is one of them and they are of him, and that he cannot deceive them, for they are his family. This is like the words of a deputy who addresses the people of his electoral constituency: "My family, my clan, my voters," all of which are called expressions of tenderness.

Likewise the words of Luqman to his son: ﴿O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice﴾ (13) [Luqman], and his words: ﴿O my son, indeed, if it is the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted﴾ (16) [Luqman], and his words: "O my son, establish prayer..." (17) [Luqman]. These are expressions of tenderness, and in them is companionship for the listener, so that he draws near and responds to the truth.

﴿O my people, if my standing [among you] is burdensome to you...﴾ (71) [Yunus]. The letters kaf, ba', ra' come with two meanings. The first: the greatness of age (kibar al-sinn), which is from kabura yakburu. The second: greatness and magnification, but magnification comes to show that it is a matter difficult for the soul, like the words of the Almighty: ﴿Terrible is the word that comes out of their mouths. They say not except a lie﴾ (5) [al-Kahf]. That is, this word that came out of their mouths is a difficult and arduous matter, namely their saying: ﴿They say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾ (4) [al-Kahf]. This word is magnified in the eyes of the believer, and it is a difficult matter that cannot be accepted, for there is no believer able to accept the claim of a creature of Allah's creation that He, exalted is He, has a son.

Sometimes the greatness comes from another direction, like the words of the Almighty: ﴿Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you invite them﴾ (13) [al-Shura]. That is, it was grievous to the polytheists, difficult for themselves, and burdensome to them, what you call them to, namely that God is One, the Unique, and there is no authority except His, exalted is He.

Thus, if a word contradicts faith, it is magnified in the eyes of believers, and if a word invites disbelievers to faith, it is burdensome to them.

Here, on the tongue of our master Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿If my standing [among you] is burdensome to you...﴾(10) (71) [Yunus].

We know that our master Noah (peace be upon him) remained among his people a thousand years less fifty years. That is, his life among his people was very long, and his reproach of the disbelievers made him burdensome to them.

Or [it means]: ﴿if my standing among you is burdensome to you...﴾ (71) [Yunus]. We know that our master Noah (peace be upon him) remained among his people a thousand years less fifty years. That is, his life among his people was very long, and his reproach of the disbelievers made him burdensome to them.

Or [it means]: ﴿if my standing among you is burdensome to you...﴾ (71) [Yunus]. It means that he burdened them with what they could not bear, because Noah (peace be upon him) wanted to take them out of what they were accustomed to, the worship of idols, and that was hard for them.

So the principle of worshipping the One God is difficult for them. Or, the basis for the preacher or conveyer [of the message] is that he should be on the level of standing while they are seated. Our master Jesus (peace be upon him) used to speak to the disciples (hawariyyun) while standing, and standing is an indication that the effort of guidance falls upon our master Jesus (peace be upon him), while the disciples sit to listen to him at ease.

Thus, the words of the Almighty: ﴿If my standing among you is burdensome to you...﴾ (71) [Yunus] are as if to say: "If what I call you to is difficult for you."

It is also correct to take it from the angle of the length of the admonition and the repetition over a thousand years less fifty years, or [it means] my standing was burdensome to you, in the sense that we have split into two parts, because the method I call to does not please you, and I would have loved for us to be one party.

Here is our master Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him, and please him), when he sensed that the caliphate required that he name his successor, some people said to him: "Why do you not appoint Abdullah ibn Umar over us?" Ibn al-Khattab said: "It is enough for the family of Khattab that one man from them be questioned about the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ)." Then he added: "I know that you have grown weary of my rule, because I am harsh(11) toward you."

So Noah (peace be upon him) sensed that he and his people had split into two parts: he took the side of Allah, exalted is He, whom he called to worship, and they took the side of the idols whose worship they were accustomed to.

Therefore the Almighty says on the tongue of Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿then in Allah I have put my trust...﴾ (71) [Yunus]. That is, I will not compromise on my call. We notice that if you say "I have put my trust in Allah," this may mean that you might say "and in so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so," but if you say ﴿then in Allah I have put my trust...﴾ (71) [Yunus], you have restricted your trust to Allah alone.

Thus Noah (peace be upon him) confronted his people, and his store in this was reliance and trust in the One who sent him, exalted is He. He tried to guide them, but they did not respond, and he said to them: ﴿So resolve upon your affair with your partners, then let not your affair be a source of distress to you...﴾ (71) [Yunus]. The meaning of "resolving the affair" is: gathering the scattered opinions into one opinion. That is, agree, O people, upon one opinion, and you will not harm me. Gathering the affair of the generations which our master Noah (peace be upon him) kept trying to guide requires effort, because a generation of reason spans twenty years.

Our master Noah (peace be upon him) kept calling the people for as long as he lived among them, that is, a thousand years less fifty. How many generations, then, did Noah keep treating?

They were many generations. Nevertheless, he gained only a small number of believers(12), who fit in one ship, along with the animals as well. Moreover, his son also went out with the disbelieving people, and Noah (peace be upon him) called him to board with him and to believe, but he refused and preferred to remain on the side of disbelief, with the destruction that this entailed for the disbelieving people. He thought he was able to take refuge in a mountain that would protect him from the flood, and the son of Noah did not consider another soldier of the soldiers of Allah, exalted is He, standing as an obstacle on the way to the mountain, namely the waves.
