So the words of Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿then in Allah I have put my trust...﴾ (71) [Yunus] carry an implicit store of faith, for there is no one who can protect against Allah among the creatures of Allah, because all of creation, its inanimate things, plants, and animals, submits to the command of Allah, exalted is He, in supporting Noah (peace be upon him), and nothing will lag behind.

Thus was the trust of Noah (peace be upon him) in Allah, exalted is He, with the faithful store it contains, embodied in: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth...﴾ (120) [al-Ma'idah], and ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth...﴾ (284) [al-Baqarah]. Nothing will leave His dominion, exalted is He.

1 Kubura: became great and was hard upon you. Maqami: my residing among you. Tadhkiri bi-ayat Allah: my calling you to faith in Allah, exalted is He. [So you resolved to fight and expel me, but I believed in Allah, trusted in Him, relied on Him and put my trust in Him.] Fa-ajma'u amrakum: resolve on what you resolve and call upon your partners. Ghummah: confused and ambiguous, that is, be united as one hand against me. Iqdu ilayya: that is, carry out what is in your hearts and finish with it. La tunzarun: do not delay and do not give respite. The intensity of Noah's (peace be upon him) faith in Allah, exalted is He, and his trust in His support of him, is what led him to challenge his disbelieving people with this challenge; so Allah gave him victory, and the drowning and destruction of his enemies by the flood. [Abridged from Tafsir al-Tabari, with adaptation.]

2 Shaytan: every rebellious transgressor among humans and jinn. Satan is from the jinn, created from fire, and he is an enemy to humanity who entices them to evil, except for whomever Allah protects through his faith. The Almighty says: ﴿And We protected it from every accursed devil﴾ (17) [al-Hijr], meaning He protected the heaven from the mischief of the devils. And Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ (6) [Fatir], and He says: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils from mankind and jinn...﴾ (112) [al-An'am]. [From al-Qamus al-Qawim, with adaptation.]

3 Ijtiba': chose him and selected him. Its confirmation is the words of the Almighty about Adam: ﴿Then his Lord chose him, and accepted his repentance and guided [him]﴾ (122) [Ta-Ha].

4 Qurban: that by which a servant draws near to Allah or to the alleged gods. One of the sons of Adam was a shepherd, and he drew near with the best, fattest, and finest of his flock, giving it willingly. The other was a farmer, and he drew near with the worst of his crops, not giving it willingly. Allah accepted the offering of the shepherd, who offered the best of what he had, willingly. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2/42).

5 Basattu: I extended.

6 Qawm: a group of men with no women among them, and the word qawm is used to include the whole nation, men and women, as in the people of Noah and the people of Abraham. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab (root q-w-m): "Women may be included in it by way of following, because the people of every prophet are men and women."

7 Al-qarr fi al-bayt: settling in it, as in the words of the Almighty: ﴿And stay in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former times of ignorance﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab].

8 Mithqal habbat min khardal: the weight of a grain of mustard. Khardal: a herbaceous plant that grows in fields and on the edges of roads, whose seeds are used in medicine, and from which seeds are taken to season food. The singular is khardalah. It is proverbially used for smallness, as one says: "I do not have a mustard seed of such-and-such." [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root kh-r-d-l.]

9 ﴿Terrible is the word that comes out of their mouths...﴾ (5) [al-Kahf]: the saying of the disbelievers that Allah, exalted is He above what they say, has a son is a word with great error, because Allah, glory be to Him, is free of consorts, children, partners, and equals. The Almighty says: ﴿There is none in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ (93) [Maryam]. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ (68) [Yunus], regarding the affirmation of a son for Him, and a son implies homogeneity and resemblance, while Allah, exalted is He, is not homogeneous with anything and does not resemble anything.

10 Al-maqam: a verbal noun (masdar mimi) meaning standing, and the name of the place of physical standing; it is used figuratively for rank and literary station. His words: ﴿And take from the station of Abraham a place of prayer﴾ (125) [al-Baqarah] mean the place where he stood, the Sacred Mosque. His words: ﴿And treasures and a noble station﴾ (58) [al-Shu'ara'] mean a place with good things. His words: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ (164) [al-Saffat] mean a known rank. His words: ﴿O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of the signs of Allah are burdensome to you...﴾ (71) [Yunus] mean my standing in calling to Allah and reminding you, and maqam here is a verbal noun (masdar mimi).

11 Shadid: harsh and strict.

12 Qalil min al-mu'minin: a small number of believers.

Al-Maqam (with a damma on the meem) is a mimi noun (a noun of place or manner formed from the verb's stem) from the quadriliteral causative form aqama, meaning "to remain" or "standing/dwelling." It is also a noun of place and a noun of time. The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you [to remain], so return," and a party of them sought permission from the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed," and they were not exposed. They only intended to flee.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 13] mean: there is no staying for you in safety with the mujahideen, so return to your homes... [al-Qamus al-Qawim, with adaptation]..

11 Sayyidina Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) did not want it as a kingdom; rather, he wanted it to be by opinion and consultation, to set an example for the generations that in times of stability the matter belongs to consultation, in confirmation of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And their affair is [decided by] consultation among themselves..﴾ [Ash-Shura: 38]. But he answered with a clever reply that carries what he intended and what was intended from him..

12 He says: And the confirmation of that is the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We said, "Load into it [the ship] of each kind two [of every pair], and your family, except those against whom the word has already preceded, and those who believe." And none believed with him except a few.﴾ [Hud: 40]. From Ibn Abbas: they were eighty persons, including their women. From Ka'b al-Ahbar: they were seventy-two persons. It was said they were ten. And other things were said. Whatever their number, it is very small compared to the length of Noah's stay among them..

The meaning: if you turn away from my call to worship the true God, then I am not calling you to someone like yourselves, a man like me. Rather, I call you to One who is above me and above you. I do not want to seize temporal authority from you, nor do I seek status, for all status belongs to God, exalted is He.

God does not need any status from you, because His majesty is intrinsic to Him. Rather, [I want] to curb your tyranny and your domination, so that you may live in the light of the true method, so that your lives may be righteous, and all of that is for your own benefit.

﴿And if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward...﴿ (72). So would Noah (peace be upon him) side with his enemies?

A person sides with an enemy because he fears that the enemy will inflict evil upon him, but Noah (peace be upon him) does not fear them, because he relies on God alone. Rather, he points them to the sources of strength in them, and he knows that their strength is limited, and that their evil, however far it reaches, does not take effect, and there may be no evil from them at all. So is there any benefit that would return to Noah (peace be upon him) and that they could withhold from him?

No, because he declares that he takes no reward for his call.

They, then, cannot harm him, nor can they benefit him, and he does not want any benefit from them, because his position, through his faith in God who sent him, is a strong position.

He does not ask them for a reward. The word "ajran" (reward) (2) means: the price of a benefit. Prices are usually found in exchanges; they may be a price for objects and essences, or a price for a benefit.

An example of this: a person wishes to buy an "apartment" in a building, so he goes to a man who owns a building and asks him to sell him a number of shares in exchange for the value of the apartment.

And there is another who wants to rent an apartment, so he goes to the owner of the building to pay him the rent of an apartment in the building, that is, he pays him the value of the benefit of the apartment, and a reward is paid only for seeking a pressing benefit.

Noah (peace be upon him) should have asked them for a reward, because he guides them to the truth. This is according to the basic principles of valuing things, since he offers them a fundamental benefit. But he declares that he does not seek a reward, as if he were saying: my work should have had a reward, because its benefit returns to you, and it would have been obligatory for me to take a reward for it.

But Noah (peace be upon him) waived the reward from them, because he desired the higher reward. If he had taken it from them, he would have taken according to their capacities, but the reward from God is according to the capacities of God, glory be to Him, and there is a difference between the capacities of one whose giving is limited, which is man, and one whose capacity to give has no end, which is God, glory be to Him.

Here He says: ﴿And if you turn away...﴾ (72) [Yunus]: this turning away and aversion does not harm me nor benefit me, because you do not possess harm for me, nor do you possess benefit for me, for I will not take a reward from you.

And it is remarkable that all the messengers (peace be upon them), when addressing their peoples, address them with this phrase: ﴿I do not ask you for any reward for it...﴾ (86) [Sad]. Except in the story of our master Abraham (peace be upon him) and the story of Moses (peace be upon him). Concerning the story of Abraham, the word of the Truth, glory be to Him, comes: ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham (69), when he said to his father and his people: What do you worship? (70) They said: We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them (71). He said: Do they hear you when you call (72), or do they benefit you or harm you? (73) They said: Rather, we found our fathers doing so (74)﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara]. And the Truth, glory be to Him, did not bring anything there about not asking for a reward.

Also, in the story of our master Moses (peace be upon him), the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿He said: My Lord, I fear that they will deny me (12), and my breast will be constricted and my tongue will not speak, so send for Aaron (13). And they have a charge against me, so I fear they will kill me (14). He said: No! Go, both of you, with Our signs; indeed, We are with you, listening (15). So come to Pharaoh and say: Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds (16), that you send with us the Children of Israel (17)﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara]. And here too we find no statement from Moses (peace be upon him) about not asking for a reward.

As for here, in the story of Noah (peace be upon him), we find the word of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And if you turn away, I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only from God, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims (72)﴾ [Yunus].

The same meaning also came in the story of Hud (peace be upon him), where the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿The people of 'Ad denied the messengers (123), when their brother Hud said to them: Will you not fear God? (124) Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger (125). So fear God and obey me (126). And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds (127)﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara]. The same meaning also came concerning the people of Thamud, when the Truth, glory be to Him, said: {The people of Thamud denied the messengers (141), when their brother Salih said to them: Will you not fear God? (142) Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger (143). So fear God and obey me (144). And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds (145)} [Ash-Shu'ara].

The same statement also came on the tongue of Lot (peace be upon him). The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers (160), when their brother Lot said to them: Will you not fear God? (161) Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger (162). So fear God and obey me (163). And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds (164)﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara]. And the same statement came on the tongue of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), in the word of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿The companions of the thicket denied the messengers (176), when Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not fear God? (177) Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger (178). So fear God and obey me (179). And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds (180)﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara].

Thus, the majority of the messenger procession speak about the reward on their tongues: ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it...﴾ (164) [Ash-Shu'ara]. It is as if the messengers (peace be upon them) say to the humans to whom they were sent: If you had perceived the reality of the matter, it would have been obligatory that we receive a reward for the benefit we offer you, but we do not want a reward from you; rather, we will take our reward from the Lord of the worlds, because the benefit we offer you cannot be valued by any human, and the one capable of valuing it is the Lawgiver of the method, glory be to Him, who sent it down to His messengers.

Here is the Noble Qur'an, coming on the tongue of the Messenger of God Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, except love for kinship...﴾ (23) [Ash-Shura]. As for why the matter of reward did not come on the tongue of our master Abraham (peace be upon him): we know that Abraham (peace be upon him), when he first called, called his uncle, and the uncle had a share in raising Abraham, and has over our master Abraham the right of fatherhood.

Likewise our master Moses (peace be upon him): he called Pharaoh, and Pharaoh was the one who raised Moses, and Pharaoh's wife wanted him to be the delight of her eye and her husband's, until Pharaoh later reminded him of that and said: ﴿Did we not raise you among us as a child, and did you not remain among us for years of your life? (18)﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara].

As for here, in the call of our master Noah (peace be upon him), the Qur'an's word comes on Noah's tongue, clarifying the matter for Noah's people: "And if you turn away, then there is no grief for me, nor distress; for you will not harm me, nor prevent any benefit from me, because you did not ask me to bring you guidance so that I might take my reward from you. Rather, the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who sent me, and He is the One who will give me my reward, and He, glory be to Him, has commanded me to be among those who submit to Him in truth and sincerity."

In our lives we find that a friend sends a worker from his side to his friend to fix something; the worker takes his wage from the sender, not from the one to whom he is sent, and this is a logical and natural matter.

1 Yumali': yu'awinu wa-yusa'idu (he helps and assists). Abu 'Ubayd said: it is said of a people when they unite in their opinion upon a matter: "they have colluded (tamala'u) upon it." [Lisan al-Arab, root m-l-')
2 Al-ajr: the recompense for a deed; plural ujur. Al-ajr: the reward; God rewards him (yajurahu) with a reward, and gives him reward, i.e., grants him the reward. [Lisan al-Arab, root '-j-r]
3 Al-'ukuf upon a thing is to dwell in it and persist in it, i.e., they remain persistent in worshipping idols. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir (3/337)]
4 Ashab al-Aykah: they are the people of Madyan, according to the correct view, and the Prophet of God Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) was from among them. The reason the Exalted did not say here "their brother Shu'ayb" is that they were attributed to worshipping the Aykah, a tree they used to worship. [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/345)]
5 Labithta: lived and remained among us.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 73:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ship(1), and We made them successors(2), and We drowned those who denied Our signs. So see how was the end of those who were warned.﴾ (73)

It is as if the matter that befell them from Allah, the Glorified, as a consequence of their hostility to faith, could have included something else, because one does not say, "We saved you from such-and-such," unless the thing you were saved from was about to befall you. And this was indeed the case with the Flood. Allah says: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water. And We caused the earth to gush forth with springs...﴾ [al-Qamar 11-12]. It was to be expected that the earth would drink the rainwater, but what happened was that the rain poured from the sky and the earth also burst forth with water. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the waters met for a matter already decreed﴾ [al-Qamar 12]. That is, that event was predetermined, lest anyone say that this matter was merely a natural phenomenon.

No, it was a decreed matter. The ship had been built by Noah, peace be upon him, because Allah had commanded him to do so in His saying in Surah Hud: ﴿And construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation...﴾ (37) [Hud].

And Allah says in the verse that follows: ﴿And he was constructing the ship, and every time a chieftain(4) of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said, "If you mock us, then we will mock you just as you mock."﴾ (38) [Hud].

Noah, peace be upon him, boarded the ship, and there boarded with him those who had believed in Allah, the Exalted, and they carried with them of the birds and animals two of every kind, male and female.

And the saying of Allah: ﴿And We saved him and those with him...﴾ (73) [Yunus] suggests that those who went up on the ship were the rational among mankind. So how are we to understand the matter of the animals and birds going up onto the ship?

We say: the basic principle regarding the existence of these animals and birds is that they are subjugated to serve man, and it was necessary that they be present in the ship, because as subjugated creatures they glorify Allah(5) and worship the Truthful, glorified is He. So how could their knowledge exceed the knowledge of the rational ones, some of whom disbelieved? Moreover, is not that crow, which taught Cain how to conceal his brother's nakedness(6), among the subjugated creatures? It is a bird, yet it knew what man did not know!

And the Truthful, glorified is He, is the One who says: ﴿So Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the nakedness of his brother...﴾ (31) [al-Ma'idah]. Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says in the verse we are now discussing: ﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. So see how was the end of those who were warned.﴾ (73) [Yunus]. The word "al-fulk" (the ship) is one of the words that is applied to the singular and also applied to the plural.

The saying of Allah: ﴿We saved him﴾ tells us that the act is from Allah, the Exalted. When He, glorified is He, speaks of any act of His, speech about the act comes in the manner of His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder(7) and indeed We will be its guardian.﴾ (9) [al-Hijr].

But when He speaks of His own essence, He uses a word that affirms oneness, in the singular pronoun form, as in: ﴿Indeed, I am Allah...﴾ (14) [Ta-Ha].

And here the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We saved him and those with him in the ship...﴾ (73) [Yunus]. The word "anja" (to save) denotes plurality, while the word "naja" indicates that there is intense effort in the saving and that the act is repeated.

And the saying of Allah: ﴿And We made them successors(8)...﴾ (73) [Yunus] means: the successor (khalifah) is one who comes after a predecessor. The word "khalifah" is used once for the superior, as in the case here, where the righteous were made successors to the righteous. After Allah, the Exalted, saved the believing elements in the ship, He drowned the rest.

Thus, the righteous upon the ship begot righteous ones after them.

And the word "khalifah" is used once for the lesser, as in the saying of the Truthful, glorified is He: ﴿Then there succeeded them successors who neglected prayer and followed desires...﴾ (59) [Maryam]. Here the word khalifah conveys a lesser status. And there is a criterion which the Truthful, glorified is He, has set for evaluating the successor, which is His saying: ﴿Then We made you successors in the earth after them, to see how you would act.﴾ (14) [Yunus].

And since man is free to choose between faith and disbelief, he will attain his status according to what he chooses.

The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, as He made successors those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security...﴾ (55) [al-Nur]. So then: the successor is either a successor to a righteous person, or a righteous person who succeeds a corrupt one.

And here the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We made them successors and We drowned those who denied Our signs...﴾ (73) [Yunus].

The signs, as we said before, are either signs of reflection which guide to faith in the Creative Power, and these are all the signs of the cosmos: everything in the cosmos indicates that this universe was created in a particular form and for a purpose, as evidenced by the fact that the things in this universe are arranged with wise order.

And if you wish to know the precision of this creation, look at what has a hand in it for you and what does not; you will find that everything that does not have a hand for you is of an astonishing degree of uprightness. The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, but each in an orbit is swimming.﴾ (40) [Ya-Sin].

As for what has a hand in it for you, our choice, when it intervenes, may corrupt things.

Thus we have seen that the cosmic signs draw attention to the existence of the Creator, glorified is He, and they are the basis for rational proof of the existence of God. Or the signs are the wondrous matters that came through the hands of the messengers, peace be upon them, to convince people that they are truthful in conveying from Allah, the Glorified and Exalted.

Then there are the verses of the Noble Qur'an of which the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿He it is who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise, they are the foundation of the Book...﴾ (7) [Al 'Imran]. These are the verses that carry the methodology.

And when the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs...﴾ (73) [Yunus], He teaches us that He drowned those who denied the cosmic signs and did not pay heed to the wondrous artistry of Allah, the Glorified, and the wisdom in the formation of these signs, and their arrangement and regularity(10). They also denied the miraculous signs, and likewise they denied the signs of the rulings that their messengers brought.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, concludes this verse with His saying: ﴿So see how was the end of those who were warned(11)﴾ (73) [Yunus]. The address here is to everyone capable of looking, and the first of them is our master Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for he is the first addressed by the Qur'an.

When you say "look" (fa-nzur), you are drawing attention to a sensible matter; if you direct your gaze toward it, the light comes from the thing looked at, and so that the dimensions of the thing are drawn, and you see it.

The discussion here is about unseen matters, which were sensible events that occurred once and then became a report. If a reporter informs you of them, your belief in them depends on the degree of trust in him.

Whoever saw the staff of Moses, peace be upon him, swallowing the ropes that the magicians had thrown, believed, just as whoever witnessed the fire being unable to burn Abraham, peace be upon him, believed; and whoever saw Jesus, peace be upon him, healing the blind and the leper(12) and raising the dead by Allah's permission, believed in what he saw. As for one who did not see those miracles, his faith depends on the measure of his confidence in the one who reported them. If the reporter is Allah, the Glorified, and it is in the Noble Qur'an, then our belief in those miracles is a necessary matter, because we believe in the truthfulness of the one who conveys from Allah, the Exalted.

We understand that the messages before the message of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, were messages limited in time and place, but Islam came to organize people addressed from the time Allah sent His Messenger Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, until the Hour is established.

Therefore the Qur'an came as signs that remain until the Hour is established, and this is the reason the Qur'an came as a lasting rational miracle, by which every person who calls to the methodology of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, can say: "Muhammad is a messenger from Allah, the Exalted," and that is his miracle.

When the Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿So see (fa-nzur)﴾, its like is the saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?(13)﴾ (1) [al-Fil].

The event of the Elephant occurred in the year in which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was born. Naturally, our master the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not see the event of the Elephant, but those who saw it were those living at that time. This draws our attention to the difference in the mode of perception: your eyes may see a matter, and your ear may hear a report, but it is possible for your senses to deceive you. As for the report coming from Allah, the Exalted, even if it is absent from you now and not heard by you, take it as stronger than sight with the eye.

Someone may say: why did the Truth not say, "Have you not known," but rather said, "Have you not seen" (1) [al-Fil]?

I say: to show us that knowledge taken from Allah concerning an unseen matter must be received by you with acceptance more than your reception of what is seen with the eye.

Thus, (fa-nzur) means: know the matter as if it were embodied before you, because you believe in Allah, the Exalted, as if you saw Him, and your informant from Allah, the Glorified, is a messenger in whose message you believe. Every report coming from Allah and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cannot be infiltrated by doubt, and doubt can never infiltrate the truthful informant.

Someone may say: why did the Truth not say, "So see how was the end of the disbelievers" instead of the Truthful, glorified is He, saying: ﴿So see how was the end of those who were warned﴾ (73) [Yunus]? Here we say:

Indeed, the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, has made clear that He does not punish before warning(14). He warned first, and did not seize the people in their ignorance.

"So see" (fa-nzur), as we know, is an address to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the address to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, includes his community as well. This report came as consolation to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: if your people, O Muhammad, encounter what the people of Noah, peace be upon him, encountered, then know that their end will be like the end of the people of Noah.

In this there is a warning and a threat to the opponents of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

1 Al-fulk: the ship.
2 Khalafahu yakhlifuhu (from the pattern nasara): came after him and became his place. Khalfan and khilafah and khalfah: became his successor. Allah says: ﴿Evil is what you did as my successors after me (150)﴾ [al-A'raf]. Al-khalf: a generation of people after another generation, i.e., one generation after another; al-khalf is a righteous or unrighteous offspring. Allah says: ﴿Then there succeeded them successors (169)﴾ [al-A'raf]. Al-khalf (with fatha): a part, a replacement, a righteous or unrighteous offspring. Al-khalifah is one who succeeds another or acts in his place. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, I am making in the earth a successor (30)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Its plural is khulafa' and khala'if. Allah says: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah (69)﴾ [al-A'raf], and He says: ﴿And it is He who has made you successors of the earth (165)﴾ [al-An'am]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted].
3 Ma' munhamir: abundant rain.
4 Mala': a group.
5 Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving (44)﴾ [al-Isra'].
6 Yuwari sawat akhihi: conceals the body of his brother Abel, whom his brother killed without right, i.e., buries him.
7 Al-dhikr: the Noble Qur'an. Allah says: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them and that they might give thought (44)﴾ [al-Nahl].
8 Khala'if: plural of khalifah, one who succeeds those who came before him. It is also pluralized as khulafa'. Allah says: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah (69)﴾ [al-A'raf].
9 Al-fulk: the orbit in which a celestial body swims. Its plural is aflak. [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit: root f-l-k].
10 Rutabatuha: i.e., its movement in a single system that never deviates. Allah the Glorified says: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, but each in an orbit is swimming (40)﴾ [Ya-Sin].
11 'Aqibah: punishment, recompense, and end. Al-mundharin: a passive participle indicating those upon whom warning fell, namely the people of Noah, whose prophet warned them, but they did not believe; so they deserved the punishment and torment.
12 Al-kamah: blindness with which a person is born. Al-baras: a skin disease consisting of white patches appearing on the body. See Lisan al-'Arab.
13 Companions of the Elephant: the army of Abraha the Abyssinian when they came to demolish the Ka'bah, and Allah tore them to shreds and sent down upon them birds from the sky, pelting them with stones of sijjil, and made them like eaten chaff. This coincided with fifty-five nights before the birth of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He did not see the event with his own eyes, but Allah's report to him admits only of truth, so it is as if he had indeed seen it.
14 Allah the Glorified says: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them (24)﴾ [Fatir], and He says: ﴿And We would not punish until We sent a messenger (15)﴾ [al-Isra']. The nadhir (warner) and the indhar (warning) is nudhr. Allah says: ﴿There came to us no bringer of good tidings nor warner (19)﴾ [al-Ma'idah]. The nadhir here is the messenger who warns of punishment. Nudhr is a verbal noun meaning warning, as in His saying: ﴿And by those who scatter, scattering (5), and those who deliver a reminder, as an excuse or a warning (6)﴾ [al-Mursalat], and His saying: ﴿...And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe (101)﴾ [Yunus], which may mean the warnings. Or the mundharun are the messengers, plural of nadhir, as in His saying: ﴿Warners had already passed before him and behind him (21)﴾ [al-Ahqaf], where the nudhr are the messengers who warned.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 74:

Then the Truthful One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says:

﴿Then after him We sent messengers to their peoples, and they brought them clear proofs(1). But they were not such as would believe in what they had denied before. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors.(74)﴾:

The word "ba'atha" (sent forth, raised up) here deserves reflection. Ba'th (raising/sending forth) is used only for something that existed and then came to an end, so that God sends it forth again.

The phrase "ba'athna" (We sent forth) draws our attention to the fact that when Allah, glory be to Him, first created creation, He gave the method (manhaj) to Adam, peace be upon him, and Adam conveyed it to his children. Every obliteration or alteration of the method by humankind is a causing of the method to die.

When the Truthful One, glory be to Him, sends a messenger, he does not originate a method; rather he raises up what already existed, in order to remind (people) of the sound innate nature (fitrah).

This is the difference between the impression left by the word "ba'th" and the word "irsal" (sending). The word ba'th makes you feel that a thing existed, then the thing ended, then that thing was raised again anew. It is like the resurrection (ba'th) on the Day of Resurrection: humankind lived and will continue in procreation, life and death until the Day of Resurrection, then all creation will die and be raised (yub'athu) for reckoning.

It is not reasonable that Allah, glory be to Him, would create humans, make them vicegerents on the earth, and then leave them without a method. And since heedlessness (ghafla) had befallen them after Adam, peace be upon him, the raising up (ba'th) of the method came through the tongues of the messengers (rusul) who convey on behalf of Allah, exalted is He.

After Noah, peace be upon him, the Truthful One, glory be to Him, sent messengers, and here Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

{Then after him We sent messengers..(74) [Yunus]: That is, after Noah. So the matter of Noah, peace be upon him, here means the vanguard of the caravan of messengership; for Noah, peace be upon him, has been said to be a messenger to all people as well, just like Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He was not sent as a messenger to all people; rather, his boarding of the ship is what made him a messenger to all people, because the inhabitants of the earth at that time were few.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, seized the disbelievers for their sins and saved the believers from the flood. The people were two kinds: believers and disbelievers. The believers boarded the ship, and Allah, glory be to Him, drowned the disbelievers.

Thus Noah, peace be upon him, became a messenger to all, by the particularity of those who remained, who were the ones addressed, with the particularity of time and place(5).

And here the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: "Then We sent messengers to their peoples.. (74)} [Yunus]. Has Allah related all the accounts of the messengers, peace be upon them? No, because He, glory be to Him and exalted, is the one who said: ﴿Of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you..(78)﴾ [Ghafir].

The Truthful, mighty and majestic, did bring the accounts of the steadfast messengers (ulu al-'azm) among them(6), just as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.(147)﴾ [al-Saffat].

As for the one whom Allah sent to people fewer than a hundred thousand, his mention may not come, and we know that a messenger used to come to a isolated nation, because the world was in a state of isolation. For example, for a thousand years we did not know of the existence of the continent of America; indeed, we did not know all the continents and lands until after aerial survey in the modern age, and there may be regions in the world that we know as an image but not as a reality.

We know that the offspring of Adam, peace be upon him, lived on the earth, then spread out (insāḥa) across the earth, because the provisions that sufficed Adam's offspring in his time no longer sufficed after the offspring multiplied, so the sustenance became narrow in the area of the earth where they were, and some of them spread out to the rest of the earth.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on the earth many a refuge and abundance..(100)﴾ [al-Nisa']. Thus some of the offspring of Adam, peace be upon him, moved to places of rain (mawaqi' al-ghayth)(10), for migration is toward places of water, because it is the origin of life.

Historians of civilizations observe that some civilizations arose along the banks of rivers and valleys, while the nomadic peoples (al-badawa) were dispersed in the deserts, like the Arabs. They originally settled at the Ma'rib Dam, and after the dam collapsed and flooded the land, the people feared the flood, because the two enemies that humans could not overcome are fire and water.

When the people saw the rushing of water, they went out to the deserts and dug the wells from which they took water in proportion to their need, because they knew they were not in a position to confront water with strength.

Thus isolations arose among the Arab tribes, and it was similar in the rest of the earth; therefore diseases differed according to the nations. And for this reason Allah, glory be to Him, sent a warner (nadhir) to every nation, and He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And there is no nation but a warner has passed among them..(24)﴾ [Fatir]. Allah, glory be to Him, related to us the accounts of some of them and did not relate the accounts of others.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah..(78)﴾ [Ghafir], and here the Truthful One says: ﴿Then We sent messengers after him to their peoples, and they brought them clear proofs..(74)﴾ [Yunus].

Are these the messengers whom Allah did not mention? No, because the Truthful One afterward sent Hud to the people of 'Ad, Salih to Thamud, and Shu'ayb to Madyan, and He did not mention these here. Rather, after Noah, peace be upon him, He brought the account of Moses, peace be upon him, as if Allah, glory be to Him, willed here to bring us the account of the springs of messages (uyun al-risalat)(12).

Since the Truthful One sent messengers to peoples, every people had a messenger, and every messenger was sent by Allah to his people.

The word "qawm" (people)(13) in the verse is a plural in the construct (jam' mudaf), and "rusul" is a plural; matching a plural with a plural requires distribution into individuals, just as we say: "Go on, ride your cars," and the address is to all of you, meaning: each one of you should ride his car.

Each messenger came to his people with the proofs (bayyinat), that is, the clear signs indicating the truthfulness of their conveyance from Allah, exalted is He.

Then the Truthful One says in the same verse: ﴿But they were not such as would believe in what they had denied before. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors.(74)﴾: That is, if all people had believed, the procession of messengership would have ended, for the procession of the faith of all humanity would not have continued, but heedlessness came(14), and Allah, exalted is He, sealed the hearts of the transgressors. Sealing (tab') — as we know — is stamping.

The meaning of that is that a sealed heart does not let out what is inside it, nor does what is outside it enter it. So as long as some have loved disbelief, Allah, glory be to Him, has sealed these hearts so that faith does not enter them and disbelief does not leave them. The sealing here is attributed to Allah, exalted is He.

Some who seek out loopholes in the method of Allah say: the cause of their disbelief is that Allah is the one who sealed their hearts.

We say: Notice that He, glory be to Him, made clear that He sealed the hearts of the transgressors; transgression (i'tida') occurred from them first, and the meaning of transgression is that they did not reflect upon the signs of Allah and disbelieved in the method that was sent down to them. They are the ones responsible for the cause of the sealing of the hearts through transgression and aversion.

The sealing came because of their determination upon what they had loved and become accustomed to. The Truthful One, mighty and majestic, said in the hadith qudsi: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners from partnership (shirk)"(15).

And to Allah belongs the highest likeness: you say to one who persists in his error: as long as you love that matter, then glut yourself with it.

Such as those whom Allah, glory be to Him, has sealed upon their hearts are like those who denied before and were transgressors.

1 Bayyinat: that is, with the proofs, evidences and demonstrations of the truthfulness of what they brought them. [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/426)].
2 Tab': is the sealing upon the heart, but it is not erased nor undone ever. As for khatm (sealing), it may be undone and may have a known duration, and it may be accepted with sincere repentance. The Qur'an has come with both: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing and sights Allah has sealed (108)﴾ [al-Nahl]. And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their sights is a covering..(7)﴾ [al-Baqarah].
3 Nahaja (to take a road, from the pattern fataha): nahjan, he traversed it. Nahaja al-tariq lahu: he made it clear. Al-nahj, al-manhaj and al-minhaj: the clear road and the path, sensory and abstract. Allah said: ﴿For each We have made among you a law and a method..(48)﴾ [al-Ma'idah], that is, a way, a path, or a religion; here it is abstract.
4 Risala: a noun for what is sent, derived from the verbal noun; the message of the messenger is what he was commanded to convey from Allah to people and his call to people to what was revealed to him. Rasul: the one sent. Rasul is also a verbal noun in the sense of risala, and when described by a verbal noun it does not take feminine, dual or plural forms. Al-Zamakhshari said: rasul may mean "one sent" and may mean "message," and the Qur'an in Surat Ta-Ha used it in the sense of "messengers," so it had to be made dual. He says: ﴿Indeed we are two messengers of your Lord..(47)﴾ [Ta-Ha]. But in the verse of al-Shu'ara' it is in the sense of message, so it is permissible to treat it the same whether singular or dual when described by it; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds(16)﴾ [al-Shu'ara']. And irsal comes merely for sending and release, such as: ﴿So send with me the Children of Israel..(105)﴾ [al-A'raf] (al-Zamakhshari, with adaptation).
5 As for the message of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, it is for the general time and place, and this is among what Allah particularized His messenger and his community with. It is indicated by the hadith of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "I have been given five things that no one before me was given: I was helped with terror over a distance of a month's journey; the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, so whichever man of my community is overtaken by prayer, let him pray; spoils of war were made lawful for me though they were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given intercession; and a prophet used to be sent to his people specifically, but I was sent to all people generally." Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (335) and Muslim (521) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.
6 The steadfast messengers (ulu al-'azm) are: Muhammad, Ibrahim, Nuh, Musa and 'Isa, peace be upon them. Allah said: ﴿So be patient as the steadfast messengers were patient..(35)﴾ [al-Ahqaf].
7 He is Yunus, peace be upon him, whom Allah, glory be to Him, delivered from the belly of the fish, then sent to his people, who were the people of "Nineveh" in the direction of Mosul, and their number was a hundred thousand or more than a hundred thousand, according to the differences among the exegetes. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn p. 396] and [Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/22)], and [Safwat al-Tafasir by al-Sabuni (3/24)]. Adapted.
8 Insāḥa: from al-siyaha, which is going about the earth, or migration from one place to another. [Lisan al-'Arab: root s-y-ḥ].
9 Muraghaman kathiran: al-muraghama is abandonment and distancing. The meaning: he finds many places suitable for emigrating to in order to live there. [Lisan, adapted].
Wsi'a: that is, far from the constraint of the polytheists. It was also said: sa'a, that is, abundance in provision. [Mukhtasar Tafsir al-Tabari], adapted.
10 Al-ghayth: the rain.
11 Inn: negating in the sense of (ma). That is: there is no nation to which Allah did not send one to warn them. Khala: passed and preceded. Allah said: ﴿Thus We have sent you to a nation before which nations have passed away..(30)﴾ [al-Ra'd].
Nadhir: an intensive form from warning, that is, one who warns them much of Allah's punishment if they do not believe in Him. Allah said: ﴿There has come to you Our messenger, making clear to you after a lapse of messengers, lest you say, "No bringer of good news came to us nor a warner."(19)﴾ [al-Ma'idah].
12 Uyun al-risalat: the greatest and most important of them are mentioned in detail, and others are mentioned in summary.
13 Qawm: a group of men without women. Allah said: ﴿Let not a people ridicule a people..(11)﴾ [al-Hujurat], then He said: ﴿Nor women, women..(11)﴾ [al-Hujurat], which shows that what is meant by qawm here is men only; the word qawm is also used to include the whole nation, men and women, such as the people of Noah and the people of Abraham. [al-Qamus al-Qawim]. See also [Lisan al-'Arab, root q-w-m].
14 Ghafla: a forgetfulness that befalls a person from lack of watchfulness and lack of alertness. Allah said: ﴿You were in heedlessness of this..(22)﴾ [Qaf], that is, unaware of the reckoning of the Resurrection and unaware of events after death. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
15 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (3985) and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4202) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.
16 Al-sadir fi ghayyihi: one who persists in his error, continuing on it, not caring about anything and not minding what he does. [Lisan, root s-d-r].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 75:

The Truthful One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿Then after them We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they were arrogant, and they were a guilty people.﴾ (75)

Both Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, are messengers (rasul). The sending (al-ba'th) of each of them went through stages. The basis of this is that God, exalted is He, said to Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.﴾ (Ta-Ha, 13). The Truthful One, glory be to Him and exalted, said to Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.﴾ (Ta-Ha, 43). Then Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, to strengthen his arm through his brother, so the Truthful One, glory be to Him and exalted, said: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Moses.﴾ (Ta-Ha, 36). This is because Moses, peace be upon him, wanted his speech to be understood, and Moses hoped of his Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, through his saying: ﴿And loosen the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech.﴾ (Ta-Ha, 27-28).

After that came the charge of the message upon Aaron along with Moses, peace be upon him.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.﴾ (Ta-Ha, 24).

So the original mission was that of Moses, peace be upon him; then God, glory be to Him, joined Aaron to Moses in answer to Moses' request. The proof of this is that all the signs sent with that mission were in the hand of Moses, and when Moses is the messenger and Aaron is joined to him, it is necessary that Aaron too becomes a messenger.

Therefore we find the Qur'an expressing this: ﴿Indeed, we are two messengers of your Lord...﴾ (Ta-Ha, 47), meaning: they are two messengers from God.

In another verse the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So come to Pharaoh and say, "Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds."﴾ (al-Shu'ara', 16). Thus the two of them were sent on a single task, and neither had a separate, independent message; rather their message is one and not multiplied, though the sender is plural, namely Moses and Aaron. An example of this, and to God belongs the highest likeness, is when a king or a president sends a delegation to another king, and they say: "We are the messengers of King so-and-so."

In the mission of Moses and Aaron, the prominent matter in casting the signs was for Moses. But Aaron also has a原 messengerly standing (asala risaliyya) of his own; therefore the Truthful One, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, we are two messengers...﴾ (Ta-Ha, 47).

That is because Pharaoh was haughty, repugnant (samij), base of people (radhl al-khalq). If Aaron spoke to strengthen the arm (azr) of his brother, Pharaoh might say: "What business is it of yours?"

But when the two of them enter upon him and declare that they are two messengers, then if Pharaoh rejects Aaron, it is as if he rejects Moses too.

I say this so as to close the door on one who wishes to attack the Qur'an (yatawarrak) by asking: what is the meaning of the Qur'an saying once "rasul" and once "rasula"? In this there is a sufficient answer to these attackers.

The Truthful One says here, in the verse about which we are reflecting: ﴿Then after them We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs (mala'ihi) with Our signs, but they were arrogant...﴾ (75). The mala' (chiefs): they are the nobles of the people, their notables, their dignitaries, and those close to the holder of supreme authority, and they are called "mala'" because they fill the eyes, that is, the eyes see no one other than them.

Pharaoh, as we know, did not become Pharaoh except through the chiefs, for they are the ones who installed him over them. Haman, for example, supported the idea of Pharaoh, and the priests affirmed that Pharaoh is a god.

Every Pharaoh has chiefs who make him; the popular proverb in Egypt says: "They said to Pharaoh, 'Who made you Pharaoh?' He said, 'I found no one to check me.'"

That is: he found no one who said to him, "Be sensible." Had he found someone to say that, he would not have become a tyrant.

The signs which God, exalted is He, sent with Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs are miracles indicating the truthfulness of the prophethood of Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, and among them is what draws attention to the truthfulness of the conveyance from God.

Or the signs are the method that establishes the existence of the Supreme Creator, but Pharaoh and his chiefs were arrogant. Arrogance (istikbar) is the seeking of greatness, just as "istakhraja" means seeking extraction and "istafhama" means seeking understanding. Whoever seeks greatness is only feigning it, because he knows that his qualities do not give him this greatness.

The Truthful One concludes this verse with His saying: ﴿...and they were a guilty people.﴾ (75). The worst of crimes is that which transgresses upon the self (nafs). It may be acceptable for a person's crime to extend to his enemies, but for crime to extend to the self is a matter with no excuse (mandūha). The crime of Pharaoh and his chiefs led them to Hell, abiding therein forever, cursed, and in a great and humiliating punishment.

1 Mala'ahu: his people. It is said: they are the nobles of the people, their faces, and their leaders whose word is relied upon. [Lisan al-Arab, root m-l-')
2 al-'Uqda: applied to the impediment of the tongue and difficulty of speech. God says, relating from Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿And loosen the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech.﴾ (Ta-Ha, 27-28).
3 Tagha: exceeded the limit. From it God's saying: ﴿Those who transgressed in the lands﴾ (al-Fajr, 11), that is, they oppressed and exceeded the limit in disobedience. And God said: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ (al-Haqqa, 11).
4 Samuja al-shay': became ugly. And samj and sameej: that in which there is no good. [Lisan al-Arab: root s-m-j, adapted]
5 al-Radhl and al-radhil: the base of people; it is said: the mean. It is said: the poor quality of anything. [Lisan al-Arab: root r-dh-l]
6 al-Azr: strength and firmness; azara and aazara: he helped him and supported him. [Lisan al-Arab: root a-z-r]
7 al-Tawrik: attributing a fault or deficiency to a thing and imputing it to it contrary to fact, and carrying the meaning of projecting one's defect onto another. [See Lisan al-Arab, root w-r-k] The intended meaning is that they load the Qur'an with their own contradictions.
8 God says: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs, so ask the Children of Israel when he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched."﴾ (al-Isra', 101). The signs with which Moses, peace be upon him, was sent are: the staff, the bringing forth of his hand white without defect, the years of drought, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood.
9 al-Mandūha: latitude in a matter. The intended meaning: this act of theirs has no reasonable cause and no justification. [Lisan al-Arab: root n-d-h, adapted]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 76:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So when the Truth came to them from Us, they said, "This is clearly magic."﴾

The Truth had come to them through the tongues of the messengers, peace be upon them. Everyone must understand that when he receives from a messenger a message of truth, he should understand that it is not a thought originating from the messenger himself, but that the Supreme Creator, glorified and exalted is He, has sent him with it.

Therefore, one who rejects the Messenger does not reject a peer of his, because the Messenger is one who conveys from Allah, the Exalted, and it is Allah, glorified is He, who sent him. A person must recognise the worth of the message that comes from the Truth, for He, glorified is He, is the Supreme Truth, and He is the One who created everything by truth: a heaven created with truth, an earth created with truth, a sun that runs with truth, rain that falls with truth, and everything stable and moving according to laws that the Truth, glorified is He, willed.

If man were to gain control over the laws of existence without a method, he would corrupt them, because corruption only comes from that in which man has a part, and which he enters without the method of Allah.

Corruption comes only from man's choosing alternatives in which he does not submit to the method of Allah, the Exalted.

Therefore, if you want your life to be upright with the uprightness of the higher created beings, in which you have no part, then comply with the method and balance of the Truth, for He, glorified is He, is the One who said: ﴿And the heaven He raised high and set the balance. That you not transgress within the balance.﴾ [Ar-Rahman]. That is: if you wish that your affairs be balanced and regulated with the regulation of the other created beings, then let the will of choice given to you be subject to the method of Allah, the Exalted, and proceed within the framework of this Lordly method.

When we reflect on the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿So when the Truth came to them from Us...﴾ [Yunus, 76]:

we find in this statement a direction that the Truth did not come from the persons of the messengers; these persons have no bearing on the matter. Beware of attacking a message of truth that came to you from a man you do not like, but rather debate the truth itself, and do not enter the maze of searching for who brought this truth. Look at those who disbelieved in Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): they are the ones who said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two towns?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf, 31]. By this they introduced the one upon whom the Qur'an was revealed into the judgement, whereas reason required that they look at the Qur'an in itself, and take wisdom from whatever vessel it came out of.

And you, too, should benefit from this matter: take wisdom from whoever speaks it, and do not look at the one from whom the wisdom came. If you dislike him, you refuse to take wisdom from him, and if you love him, you take it. No, you must take wisdom as long as it has come with the truth, for if you do not take it, you have lost yourself.

The truth is what is stable, and even if it appears at times that someone has obliterated the truth and falsehood has prevailed over it, this means the appearance of corruptions; then people cry out seeking the truth.

The spread of corruptions is what makes people summon the truth and become zealous for it, for when falsehood grips people, you find them turning to the truth to hold fast to it.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking ornament or goods, is foam like it. Thus does Allah strike the example of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but that which benefits people remains on the earth. Thus does Allah present examples.﴾ [Ar-Ra'd, 17]. Here the Truth, glorified is He, strikes the example of rain descending from the sky onto the mountains, so every valley below the mountains takes in accordance with its capacity, and people and the earth are watered. But the torrent, as it descends upon the mountains, carries some silt and chaff, and the silt settles in the valley floors so that they benefit from it, while the chaff and filth float on the surface of the water. Those floating things are called foam, and when you put them in the fire they emit sounds called (al-tashtasha).

An example of this: when we light a fire to smelt iron, we find that the dross is what floats, and the pure iron remains at the bottom.

This foam that is on the water is pushed to the sides. An example of this is what we see on the sea shores when the waves cast refuse onto the shore, the filth thrown by ships; the sea expels it with its waves. This foam passes away as scum, while what benefits people remains on the earth. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Thus does Allah strike the example of truth and falsehood...﴾ [Ar-Ra'd, 17]. So Allah, glorified is He, leaves room for falsehood, but does not hand over the truth to it; rather He leaves falsehood so as to rouse people's zeal for the truth, and if they do not defend the truth with zeal, He Himself defends it.

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿So when the Truth came to them from Us, they said, "This is clearly magic."﴾ [Yunus, 76]. Because they were well known for magic, they thought that the signs which came with Moses, peace be upon him, were clear magic, that is, obvious and manifest magic.

(1) The lam in the word "لسحر" (*lasihr*, "is indeed magic") is for emphasis. The meaning: what you have brought is nothing but strong, manifest magic. Magic is every matter whose cause is hidden and which is imagined to be other than its reality through deception and trickery. The Exalted said about the magicians of Pharaoh: ﴿He said, "Rather, throw." Then their ropes and staffs appeared to him, because of their magic, to be moving.﴾ [Ta-Ha, 66].

(2) Ta'abbi (*al-ta'abbi*): refusal and aversion. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (أ ب ى)].

(3) Because the balance of measures is the stability of the Truth, and when the Truth is established and takes its path, the measures of life are set right, and when they are set right we find no one deprived and no one wronged.

(4) The two towns are Makkah and al-Ta'if. Opinions differ on identifying these two men. It is said they are al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. It is also said they are 'Umayr ibn 'Amr ibn Mas'ud and 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, and it is said: Ibn 'Abd Yalil. The intended meaning is that he was a great man from one of the two towns. See Ibn Kathir (4/127).

(5) The books of biography have transmitted to us that al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said in describing the Qur'an: "By God, it has a sweetness, its root is fruitful, its branch is laden with fruit, and the nearest thing to it is that you say it is sorcery. It brings a speech that is sorcery, by which a man is separated from his father, from his brother, from his wife, and from his clan." (Sirah of Ibn Hisham, 1/270). Despite his words in praise of the Qur'an, yet out of conformity with his people and to preserve his standing among them, he denied the Qur'an and accused Muhammad (ﷺ) of sorcery.

(6) On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The word of wisdom is the lost property of the believer; wherever he finds it, he has the best right to it." Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2687) and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4169). Al-Tirmidhi said: "A gharib hadith which we only know from this route, and Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl is weak in narration because of his memory."

(7) Zabad: the foam that rises on the surface of sea water when its waves are agitated. A sea that is *muzbid* is one whose waves are churning, casting up foam. Zabad al-ma': its scum and debris. Plural: azbad. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (ز ب د)].

(8) Rabiyan: rising high, for it is at the highest surface of the water. [Lisan: root (ر ب ى)].

(9) Jufa' al-sayl: what the torrent casts up of foam, filth and the like. [Lisan: root (ج ف ى)].

(10) Mathal: a remarkable attribute by which another is likened. The *mithal* depicts meanings in the form of persons, making them more firmly fixed in minds because the mind is aided by the senses. The examples of the Qur'an are of two kinds:
- An apparent, explicitly stated kind, such as His saying: ﴿Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire; but when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, not seeing.﴾ [Al-Baqarah, 17].
- A hidden kind, such as His saying: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever, between that, justly balanced.﴾ [Al-Furqan, 67], which conveys the meaning of the proverb "the best of matters is their middle." [See: al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an 4/41].

(11) On the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one loves praise more than Allah; for this reason He praised Himself. And no one is more jealous than Allah; for this reason He forbade indecencies." Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih (2760) and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4634).

Almighty Allah then says:

﴿Moses said: "Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' Yet magicians do not prosper." (77)﴾

In this verse is what clarifies the response of our master Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, "Is this magic?" (77)﴾ [Yunus]. Those who distort the Qur'an say: How can the Qur'an come to affirm that they said, "This is clear magic," and then in the following verse say that they asked, "Is this magic?"

These distorters understood that the phrase ﴿Is this magic?﴾ was part of their own words, but it is the speech of Moses, peace be upon him. It is as if Moses, peace be upon him, asked a question so that they would reconsider their judgment: is what he brought magic? This is a rhetorical question of denunciation, intended to affirm that this is not magic. It came in the form of a question because he was confident that the sound answer would be that what he brought is not magic.

Had the words of Moses, peace be upon him, come as a mere statement, they could have admitted truthfulness or falsehood, but they came in the form of an inquiry, because the one who denies him would answer with stammering(1).

An example of this, and to God belongs the highest similitude: when you go to buy cloth, the seller tells you it is pure, unmixed wool. You take a match and set fire to a thread of the cloth. If the wool burns the way plastic or synthetic cloth burns, you say to the seller: "Is this pure wool, man?" Here the seller will answer only with agreement, or with the silence of one unable to conceal the truth.

Thus, if you put the matter as a denunciatory question, this is more eloquent than saying it as a bare statement, because the listener must answer.

The saying of Almighty Allah on the tongue of Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿Do you say of the truth when it has come to you... (77)﴾ [Yunus] indicates the necessity of looking at the truth in itself, detached from the one who brought it.

For this reason Moses, peace be upon him, did not say: "Do you say of the truth when we have brought it to you: it is clear magic?"

The wise statement in the noble verse is an affirmation of the necessity of looking at the truth detached from the one who brought it.

Almighty Allah ends this verse with His saying: ﴿...Is this magic? Yet magicians do not prosper. (77)﴾ [Yunus]. Thus, our master Moses, peace be upon him, issued the judgment that magic does not benefit, but the signs that he brought from Almighty Allah have prospered: his staff, which became a serpent, swallowed all that they had cast of their ropes and all that they had made of magic(2).

Almighty Allah willed that Moses' staff be a miraculous sign(3) of the same kind as what that people excelled in.

When Almighty Allah sends a miracle to a people, He makes it of the kind in which they excelled, so that the miracle is a challenge in the field in which they have experience, skill(4) and knowledge. You would not challenge a man who has no knowledge of engineering to build you a building; rather, you challenge an engineer to build you a pyramid, because contemporary sciences have not reached some of what the ancients discovered and did not record in their papers, or no discovery has been found that explains how they removed the air between each stone and the next so that the stones held together.

The saying of Almighty Allah here: ﴿...Yet magicians do not prosper. (77)﴾ [Yunus] shows us that "prosperity" (falah) is taken from the sensory process that the farmer undertakes: the effort of plowing the land, sowing seeds, irrigating the land, and awaiting the fruit after expending all that effort.

Falah is also taken from "falaha al-hadid," meaning he split iron, such as in lumps or pieces, and iron is not made fit unless it takes the appropriate shape for use.

The saying of Almighty Allah: ﴿...and magicians do not prosper (77)﴾ [Yunus] is a reminder to us that magic is a kind of imagination (takhyil), not a real fact.

For this reason Almighty Allah said in another place in the Qur'an: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people (116)﴾ [al-A'raf]. And Almighty Allah also said: ﴿...their ropes and their staffs appeared to him, by their magic, to be moving (66)﴾ [Ta-Ha]. Thus magic is only imagination(5), not a change of reality.

Because the miracle of Moses, peace be upon him, challenged all powers(6), Pharaoh declared general mobilization among everyone connected with magic, in which they excelled, or even those with a suspicion of knowledge of magic(7).

And because magic is merely imagination, we found the magicians, when they gathered and cast their ropes and staffs, and then Moses cast his staff, that behold, his staff had turned into a serpent that swallowed(8) what they had made. What did the magicians do here? Almighty Allah says in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿So the magicians fell down prostrate. They said: "We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses." (70)﴾ [Ta-Ha]. Because the magician sees what he does in its reality, while they had only imagined to the eyes of the people; they see their ropes as mere ropes and their staffs as mere staffs.

As for the staff of Moses, peace be upon him, it was not imagination; rather the magicians found it a true living serpent, and it had indeed swallowed what they made. So they fell down prostrate (khirru(9) sajidin) and declared belief in the Lord of Moses and Aaron.

They did not, then, declare belief in Moses and Aaron, but declared belief: ﴿in the Lord of Aaron and Moses (70)﴾ [Ta-Ha], because they knew by experience that what Moses cast was not magic, but the act of a supreme Creator.

The steadfastness of Moses, peace be upon him, at that moment stemmed from the training he had received from his Lord. Almighty Allah asked him: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Moses? (17) He said: "It is my staff; I lean upon it and beat down (with it) leaves for my sheep..." (18)﴾ [Ta-Ha].

Moses answered Almighty Allah both briefly and at length, out of intimacy and prolonging companionship with Almighty Allah. When he saw that he had prolonged the intimacy, he abbreviated and said respectfully: ﴿...and I have in it other uses (18)﴾ [Ta-Ha]. Thus the desire for intimacy with Almighty Allah overtook him first, and then he perceived the courtesy of addressing Almighty Allah. Almighty Allah trained him regarding the matter of the staff when He first commanded him to cast it, and it became before him a moving serpent. Had it been of the kind of magic, he would not have felt fear of it, and he would have seen it as a mere staff.

Thus the difference between the miracle of Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh is that the magicians of Pharaoh bewitched the eyes of the people, and it appeared to the people, by their magic, that their staffs and ropes were moving. But in the miracle of Moses, peace be upon him, in the casting of the staff, they knew by experience that the staff's reality had changed.

The staff, as we know, is originally a branch of a tree. Almighty Allah could have made it turn into a fruitful tree, but it would have remained a plant.

Almighty Allah willed to elevate it to the higher level of vegetation, which is the animal stage, so it became a serpent that swallowed all that the magicians cast.

1. Al-lajlaja and al-talajluj: hesitation in speech, confusion and disorder in it. Hence it is said: "The truth is clear (ablaj), and falsehood is stammering (lajlaj)." That is, the truth is clear, strong and manifest, while falsehood is weak, disordered, and has no stability. [Lisan al-Arab, root (l j j), adapted]
2. Almighty Allah says: ﴿And We revealed to Moses: "Cast your staff," and behold, it swallowed what they falsely fabricated. Thus the truth was established and what they used to do was nullified. (117–118)﴾ [al-A'raf].
3. A miracle (mu'jiza) is an event that breaks the customary order, which Allah brings about at the hand of a prophet or messenger as confirmation of him and attestation of his mission, such as the miracles of Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them: the staff turning into a serpent, the splitting of the sea, and the healing of the blind and the leper. The Prophet ﷺ was given the eternal miracle of the Qur'an, and he ﷺ had sensory miracles such as water gushing from between his fingers ﷺ.
4. Dirba: habit, experience, or training.
5. The magic of Pharaoh's people was of the type of magic of imagination and deceiving the eyes, based on the fact that sight may err and fixate on a particular thing to the exclusion of others; therefore Almighty Allah said: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people (116)﴾ [al-A'raf]. And He said: ﴿...it appeared to him, by their magic, to be moving (66)﴾ [Ta-Ha].
6. Magic is intense influence. If it comes from a created being, it is imagination and trickery; if it comes from the Creator, it is a miracle and a change of the nature of a thing by His power, glory be to Him. Therefore Moses, peace be upon him, triumphed over the magicians, because Allah aided him against them with His powers, which none can repel.
7. This is because Pharaoh, in his cunning, made the chiefs around him the ones who confronted Moses, saying to them: ﴿...Indeed this is a knowing magician (34), who wants to drive you out of your land with his magic. So what do you advise? (35)﴾ [al-Shu'ara']. Their reply to him was: ﴿Put him off, and his brother, and send into the cities gatherers (36) who will bring you every knowing magician (37)﴾ [al-Shu'ara'].
8. Luqf: swift seizing and taking up. [Lisan: root (l q f)]
9. Kharra: fell and dropped. The meaning is that they hastened to prostrate to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
10. Atawakka'u 'alayha: I bear and rely upon it; I lean on it. [Lisan: root (w k')], adapted.
11. ﴿And beat down with it leaves for my sheep (18)﴾ [Ta-Ha]: that is, I shake the tree with it so its leaves fall for my sheep to graze. Quoted by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/145).
12. Other uses (ma'arib ukhra): that is, other interests, needs and benefits besides these.
13. Awjasa: that is, fear and dread settled in his soul and heart. [See Lisan, root w-j-s]. This fear occurred to two prophets mentioned in the Qur'an. The first is Abraham, peace be upon him, when the angels came to him in human form to give him glad tidings of Isaac and Jacob. This is mentioned in the Qur'an twice. The first is in Surah Hud: ﴿And certainly Our messengers came to Abraham with glad tidings. They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace," and it was not long before he brought a roasted calf. But when he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he regarded them with suspicion and felt fear of them. They said, "Fear not; we have been sent to the people of Lot." (69–70)﴾ [Hud]. The second is in Surah al-Dhariyat, verse 28.
The second prophet is Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿They said, "O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw." He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him, by their magic, to be moving (66). So Moses sensed fear within himself (67). We said, "Fear not; indeed, you are the superior (68)"﴾ [Ta-Ha].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 78:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿They said: "Have you come to us to turn us away from that which we found our fathers upon, and that you two may have greatness (al-kibriya') in the land? We are not going to believe you two."﴾ (1)

Here we find the sorcerers of Pharaoh attributing the coming of the miracle, the transformation of the staff into a serpent, to Musa (peace be upon him), although Musa (peace be upon him) had attributed the coming of the miracle to Allah, the Exalted.

It was the duty of the one to whom the messenger was sent, Pharaoh and his chiefs, to look at what the messenger brought to him, not at the person of the messenger.(2)

Had Pharaoh said to Musa, "You have been brought," that would have meant that Pharaoh was declaring belief that there is a higher God. But Pharaoh did not believe at that moment; therefore his words came as ﴿Have you come to us?﴾, attributing the coming to Musa (peace be upon him) in Pharaoh's own speech.

And why the coming?

The Truthful, glorified is He, says on the tongue of Pharaoh and his people: ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away from that which we found our fathers upon...﴾ (78) [Yunus]. Al-iltifat (turning away) is the turning of the face away from something faced. As long as a person is engaged with a thing, all his gaze and direction are toward it. The people of Pharaoh were in corruption and misguidance, and before them there was nothing but that corruption and that misguidance.

Musa (peace be upon him) came to turn their faces away from that corruption and misguidance, so they said: ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away from that which we found our fathers upon...﴾ (78) [Yunus]. Thus they disclose the reality of their position: they used to imitate their fathers, and imitation comforts the imitator, so he does not employ his mind or thought in anything to be convinced of it and build his conduct upon it.(5)

The common proverb depicts this position with great depth when it says: "Like the deaf man at the wedding procession" (mathal al-atrash fi al-zaffa), meaning that one who lacks hearing does not hear what is said by any crowd, but walks with the people wherever they walk, and does not know a direction for himself.

The imitator only disables his thought: he does not choose between alternatives, does not distinguish right to do it, and does not recognize error so as to avoid it.

Pharaoh and his chiefs were in misguidance, the very misguidance of the fathers, and misguidance does not burden a person with the toil of thinking or the hardship of choosing; rather it may fulfil immediate desires.

As for distinguishing right from wrong and following the method of heaven, it restrains desire and obliges a person not to slip loose, unlike misguidance, which prolongs the term (amad)(6) of desire. So the imitator is between two states:

The first state: he does not employ his mind, but does as those who preceded him did, or as those among whom he lives do.

The second state: he sees that what people do does not bind him to an obligation, but the messenger who comes binds him with a method, so he does not earn, for example, except from what is lawful, does not commit what is reprehensible, and does not slander anyone; thus the method restrains his movement. But if he follows the movement of his misguided fathers, the movement widens toward desires.

For this reason I always say: this matter of imitation must be drawn to the law of upbringing. The young, as long as they have not reached puberty, you notice that they have no selfhood and imitate their fathers; but as soon as a selfhood forms in them, they begin to rebel, and may say to the fathers: "You have old traditions that do not suit this age." But if the young take in sound religious values, they will submit to the law of truth and restrain themselves from desires.

We find the children of families that do not follow God's method in raising children suffering from their children when bad companions (aqran al-su') dominate them, so they turn to what widens the circle of desires, such as addiction and other corruptions.

But the children of committed families observe God's method, so they do not imitate anyone of the people of evil, because the conscience of each of them has learned to distinguish between error and right.

Moreover, imitation of the fathers may make the children mere repeated copies of their fathers.
