But training and educating children to employ the mind in all matters, this is the upbringing by which societies develop toward the better, if the fathers follow God's method, and the son's selfhood is formed in the light of the method of the Truthful, glorified is He. Then the son does not rebel heading toward evil, but may rebel toward developing the good so as to increase its goodness.

Imitation, therefore, needs careful examination, because the person you imitate will not be responsible for you, since the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all...﴾ (33) [Luqman]. Therefore the matter of the son must arise from his own self, and likewise the matter of the father, and every person must employ his mind between the alternatives.(8)

For this reason you find the Qur'an saying, on the tongues of those who imitated their fathers: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers upon..."﴾ (170) [al-Baqarah]. If the matter were imitation, then why does the son learn? Why do children not sleep on the ground and not buy beds? Why do they strive for development in things and tools that make life easy?

So imitation is the cancellation of mind and thought, and in cancelling them is the cancellation of development and progress toward the better.

Therefore the Qur'an urges us to use the mind so that we may choose between alternatives. And if the method has come from heaven, then let him be guided by what came to you from one above you, and this chosen guidance is the ascent toward the virtuous life.

The Truthful, glorified is He, says: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers..."﴾ (104) [al-Ma'idah]. That is, they declared that they had no need of the heavenly method, so the Qur'an responded to them: ﴿...Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ (104) [al-Ma'idah]. Thus we find that the Qur'an has brought two positions in two different verses concerning the imitators:

The first verse is that in which the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿...Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers upon." Even though their fathers did not reason anything and were not guided?﴾ (170) [al-Baqarah].

The second verse is the saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿...Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers did not know anything and were not guided?﴾ (104) [al-Ma'idah]. In this verse they declared contentment with what their fathers were upon.

There is a difference between the two verses: the one who reasons is not the same as the one who does not know, because the one who reasons is able to deduce, whereas the one who does not know takes from the deduction of others.

Therefore those who were content with what their fathers had and said ﴿Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers...﴾ (104) [al-Ma'idah], these are the ones who exaggerated in pride in what their fathers had; therefore the statement that they do not know was made concerning their fathers.

That is: they have no thought and no knowledge at all, but live in darknesses of ignorance.

And here the Truthful, glorified is He, says on the tongue of Pharaoh and his people: ﴿They said: "Have you come to us to turn us away from that which we found our fathers upon, and that you two may have greatness in the land..."﴾ (78) [Yunus]. That is: have you come to turn us, and to change our faces or our direction or our path, and to take us away from the way of our fathers whom we imitate, so that you and your brother may take greatness in the land?

Thus it becomes clear that they believed the greatness they possessed in the land had been achieved by their imitation of their fathers, and they love to preserve it. The matter here includes two points:

The first: abandoning what the fathers were upon.

The second: the loss of greatness and majesty in the land.

An example of this: when one warrior says to another, "Throw down your sword," which differs from saying, "Bring your sword," for throwing down the sword is stripping of strength, whereas taking the sword means adding another sword to what the warrior who was ordered possesses.

Here they found in the call of Musa (peace be upon him) a compound calamity. The first: abandoning the creed of the fathers.

The second: the seizing of greatness, that is, temporal power, rank, lordship, majesty, consultation (al-ta'mur), and settled interests; each one of Pharaoh's inner circle takes his share according to his nearness to Pharaoh.

For this reason they declared non-belief, and said what the Truthful, glorified is He, ends with in the noble verse under discussion: ﴿And we are not going to believe you two.﴾ (78) [Yunus]. That is: the people of Pharaoh and the chiefs acknowledged what they were eager for of worldly gains and greatness in it, and rejected belief in what Musa and Harun (peace be upon them) brought.

1 Litalfitana (to turn us away): to bend us and divert us from the gods of the fathers and grandfathers.
2 Lakuma: i.e., to Musa and Harun (peace be upon them).
3 Al-kibriya': greatness and leadership. [Ibn Kathir 2/426]
4 Among what Pharaoh said about Musa, disparaging his person, is what the Lord of Might related in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Pharaoh called out among his people, saying, "O my people, does not the dominion of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flow beneath me? Then do you not see? Or am I better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf]. This is because Musa's tongue would not flow with speech, and he expressed that in his supplication: ﴿He said, "My Lord, expand for me my chest, and ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech."﴾ [Ta-Ha].
5 This imitation was forbidden by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his hadith. On the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not be an imma'ah (one who is a mere follower), saying: 'If the people do good, we do good, and if they wrong, we wrong. Rather, accustom yourselves: if the people do good, you do good, and if they do evil, do not wrong.'" Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2007), and he said: "Hasan gharib; we do not know it except from this route."
6 Amad al-shahwah: its ultimate end. And al-amad: the limit of a term. This word occurs three times in the Qur'an. He, Exalted, says: ﴿Say, "I do not know whether what you are promised is near or whether my Lord will appoint for it a distant term."﴾ [al-Jinn] meaning a distant time. And He, glorified, says: ﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a great distance﴾ [Ali 'Imran], meaning in utmost remoteness. And He, Exalted, says: ﴿Then We sent them forth that We might know which of the two parties was more precise in computing what they had remained as a term﴾ [al-Kahf], meaning a period and a time.
7 Aqran: plural of qarn (with the qaf kasrah and the ra' sukun), meaning an equal and a counterpart. The intended meaning of aqran al-su' is evil companions and comrades of wickedness and vices. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (q-r-n), adapted]
8 Al-bada'il: that from which a person may choose; these are the places of choice in obligation, so he may choose between faith and disbelief, obedience and disobedience. He, Exalted, says: ﴿And a soul and He who proportioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness. He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who instills it [with corruption]﴾ [al-Shams].
9 Alfayna: we found. Alfa al-shay' wajadahu (he found the thing). He, Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray﴾ [al-Saffat], and He says: ﴿And they found its master at the door﴾ [Yusuf], meaning they found him.
10 Hasbuna: suffices us. There is a difference between the saying of these disbelieving imitators of their fathers here and the saying of the believers with this word, "hasbuna." The believers said: ﴿...Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾ [Ali 'Imran], and they said: ﴿Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger...﴾ [al-Tawbah]. The believers were content with what came to them from Allah and entrusted the matter to Allah, despite the enmity of their fathers toward them and despite the fact that their position would harm them in their worldly life and might cut off their provision. They had looked to the Hereafter, whereas the disbelievers live their worldly life with all its pleasures and desires.
11 Al-kibriya': greatness and dominion. It is the perfection of essence and the perfection of existence, and it is not attributed to anyone but Allah, Exalted. The author of "al-Qamus al-Qawim" said: it is greatness, tyranny, authority, and dominance, and with respect to Allah, Glorified, it is true greatness, strong authority, and complete dominance. [adapted]
12 Al-ta'mur: consultation about a matter and mutual exhortation to it. Consultation is called ta'mur because those consulting accept one another's command. From it is His saying, Exalted: ﴿And there came a man from the farthest part of the city, running. He said, "O Musa, indeed the chiefs are conferring about you to kill you..."﴾ [al-Qasas]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim; see also Ibn Kathir 3/383]
13 Bitanat al-rajul: his inner circle. [Lisan al-'Arab: root (b-t-n)]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 79:

The Truth, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And Pharaoh said, "Bring me every learned sorcerer."﴾ (79)

Pharaoh knew the prominence of the sorcerers in his realm, and it is enough that he himself made the people imagine that he was a god. When his command came, he told his aides to bring the sorcerers, and as soon as he gave the order, the sorcerers were brought.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, mentions in the verse that follows:

﴿So when the sorcerers came, Moses said to them, "Throw down what you are going to throw."﴾ (80)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 10, verse 80:

The interval between Pharaoh's utterance of the command and its execution is the narrowest of time-spans, so that we understand that the command of one who holds authority admits of no postponement or delay in execution from the people.

When the Qur'an addresses a matter, it gives an exact picture of the reality, and does not bring in things that would spoil the picture.

The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, "Throw down what you are going to throw."﴾ [Yunus]. In this verse is a summary of the whole situation. When the magicians learned that Pharaoh needed them in a predicament (1) concerning the ruling, this was a difficult and harsh matter, and they had to hasten to him.

The Truth, glorified is He, did not give here the full detail of that situation, because the story comes with its different points in other places in the Qur'an, and each verse clarifies the point that it mentions (2).

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, did not say here that Pharaoh's agents called out in the cities (3) for the magicians to come, as came in other places in the Qur'an (4).

Nor did He tell us that the magicians wished to benefit from this matter, and said to Pharaoh (5):

﴿...Surely there will be a reward for us if we are the victors.﴾ [al-A'raf]. Placing such a condition clarifies for us the nature of relations in that society. Their request for a reward means that their work with Pharaoh before that had been under compulsion and without pay; and when the opportunity came to them and they saw Pharaoh in a crisis, they demanded the reward.

Pharaoh promised them the reward, and likewise promised them that they would be among those brought near (6); for if they were victorious with magic over Moses' miracle, that work would be a safeguarding and protection of the kingdom, and they would necessarily become part of the beneficial inner circle. Pharaoh's promise to them was a spur to their resolve, so that they would hasten to nullify Moses' miracle, so that Pharaoh's throne might be secure.

The Truth, glorified is He, willed brevity here in this verse, about which we are now reflecting, and brought the remaining scenes in other places in the Qur'an.

And here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, "Throw down what you are going to throw."﴾ [Yunus]. And the magicians threw down their staves and ropes.

1 al-Warta: a beast whose sheep falls into a pit from which it cannot escape. It is said: "The sheep became trapped (tawarratat al-ghanam)" when they fell into a predicament; then it became a metaphor for every hardship a person falls into. And "Fulan became entangled in the matter (tawarta/istawrata fihi)" when he became confused in it, so that the way out of it was not easy for him. [Lisan al-Arab: root w-r-t].
2 This is a feature of the Qur'anic narrative, referring to its stories, except the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him.
3 al-Madain: plural of madina, meaning large towns. This plural occurs in the Qur'an specifically in the story of Moses three times; the singular occurs 14 times, of which 4 are specifically concerning the city of the Messenger (ﷺ) [al-Tawba: 120, 101] [al-Ahzab: 60] [al-Munafiqun: 8].
4 This is in the words of the Exalted concerning Pharaoh's magicians: ﴿They said, "Put him and his brother off, and send into the cities summoners."﴾ [al-A'raf], and the Exalted said: ﴿They said, "Put him and his brother off, and send into the cities summoners."﴾ [al-Shu'ara'].
5 Pharaoh (fir'awn): arrogance and tyranny (fir'anah) means pride and oppression. The Pharaoh mentioned in the Book of God is said by some not to take the diptote form because he has no namesake, and like Iblis regarding one who is named from "iblas" (despair). Ibn Sayyidah said: "Fir'awn is a foreign proper name, and for this reason it is not declined." Al-Jawhari said: "Fir'awn is the title of al-Walid ibn Mus'ab, king of Egypt, and every tyrant is a pharaoh, and the tyrants are the pharaohs; one may act like a pharaoh, and it is fir'anah, i.e., cunning and arrogance." It is said: "Fir'awn in the Coptic language means the crocodile." It is said in al-Qamus al-Qawim: "Fir'awn is a title by which every king in Egypt in ancient times was called; the Pharaoh of Moses was Merneptah, and it is said Ramesses II. The lesson lies in the events, not in the person of Pharaoh." The Exalted said: ﴿Go to Pharaoh, surely he has transgressed﴾ [Ta-Ha]. And God knows best.
6 Omitted. The magicians, when they asked for a reward by saying: ﴿...Surely there will be a reward for us if we are the victors﴾ [al-A'raf], Pharaoh said: ﴿...Yes, and surely you will be among those brought near﴾ [al-A'raf]. Nearness to him increased them beyond the reward; therefore his punishment of them was severe after they followed Moses, because what he had promised them was great, so the punishment came in proportion to it.

Then the Almighty and Exalted says after that:

﴿So when they had cast, Moses said, "What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will render it baseless. Indeed, Allah does not put right the work of corrupters."﴾ (81)

We know that the Almighty and Exalted here willed brevity, but He explained in detail what happened in another verse, in which He said, concerning the magicians: ﴿They said, "O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw."﴾ [Al-A'raf] (115). We know that confrontation requires each opponent to strike fear into his adversary in order to weaken his morale.

Here Moses, upon him be peace, made clear to them that what they had brought was magic and mere illusion.

Allah the Almighty had informed His prophet Moses, upon him be peace, that his staff would become a real serpent, whereas their staves and ropes would be merely an illusion (1) to the eyes.

Moses, upon him be peace, told them the judgment of Allah the Almighty concerning that illusion: ﴿...What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will render it baseless. Indeed, Allah does not put right the work of corrupters.﴾ [Yunus] (81). Thus came the decisive word that ended the matter and issued the verdict on what Pharaoh and his chiefs (2) and the magicians had done. All their works were corrupting the earth. Had it not been so, Allah the Almighty would not have sent to them a messenger supported by a miracle of the kind in which they had excelled. They had indeed excelled in magic, so Allah the Almighty sent down a real miracle that swallows up what they had made. If they excelled in illusion, Allah the Almighty created the universes by the word "Be," and He, the Almighty, creates realities, not illusions.

Therefore, the Almighty and Exalted says after that:

﴿And Allah will establish the truth by His words (3), though the criminals dislike it.﴾ (82)

(1) Khayal (illusion, imagination) is what appears to you in waking or in sleep as an image. Zill (shadow) is what your mind conceives of something. Khayal is one of the faculties of the intellect by which one imagines and conceives things.
Allah says: ﴿...It appears to him from their magic that it moves about﴾ [Ta-Ha] (66), meaning: it resembles to him and is pictured to him, because of their magic, as moving like serpents, while in reality they are not serpents, but he imagined and fancied it (Al-Qamus al-Qawim).
(2) Mala'uhu: the household of Pharaoh and those who return to them.
(3) Yuhiqq: establishes and manifests. Bi-kalimatihi: by His promises [Tafsir al-Jalalayn, p. 186].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 82:

The matter that He, glory be to Him, wills is accomplished by the word "Kun" (Be), and the thing comes to be.

And the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [Yasin]

"Kun fayakun" (Be, and it is) is a phrase that is somewhat long when the thing desired comes about, but there is no shorter expression among humans, because the kaf and the nun have a duration, whereas what Allah, glory be to Him, wills does not need time from Him. The meaning of the command "Kun" is that the thing exists before the word "Kun," because every existent thing only comes into being and emerges by the will of Allah, exalted be He.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, wishes to show us that the truth comes only through the tongues of the messengers, and their miracles are evidence of their messengership, in order to place the noses of the criminals in the dust (1), and to relieve the world of their misguidance and their corruption.

(1) Al-Ragham: dust. The meaning is: their humiliation and their punishment for their disobedience and their crime.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 83:

The Truthful (al-Haqq) subhanahu then says:

﴿None believed in Musa except a few (dhurriyya) of his people, out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs (mala'ihim) that he would persecute them (yaftinahum). Indeed Pharaoh was haughty (la'al) in the land, and indeed he was among the extravagant (al-musrifin).﴾ (10:83)

When the magicians, who were Pharaoh's army and equipment for confronting Musa, declared their faith, Pharaoh punished them and said: ﴿You believed in him before I gave you permission...﴾ (20:71). This shows that the idea of divinity was still dominating his mind; therefore the people feared to declare their faith. Hence the Truthful (al-Haqq) subhanahu said: ﴿None believed in Musa except a few (dhurriyya)...﴾ (10:83). The word "dhurriyya" indicates the young who had not been touched by the leaven of corruption that was spreading. Just as the young possess a energy of purity, and live free of problems, and had not reached the rank of leadership that is coveted, yet they believed: ﴿out of fear (ala khawf) of Pharaoh and their chiefs...﴾ (10:83). The phrase ﴿ala khawf﴾ indicates elevation (isti'la'), like our saying "on the horse" or "on the chair," and the one who is elevated in this case is in control of "that over which he is elevated"; whoever rises above is riding the one below, and the one below bears the burden.

But among the uses of "ala" is that it comes with the meaning of "ma'a" (with).

An example of this is the saying of the Truthful subhanahu: ﴿and they give food in spite of their love for it (ala hubbihi)...﴾ (76:8), i.e., they give food together with their love for it.

When the Truthful subhanahu uses one particle in place of another, there must be a reason for it. An example is the saying of the Truthful subhanahu: ﴿Then I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you upon (fi) the trunks of palm trees...﴾ (20:71). The Truthful subhanahu used the particle "fi" (in) instead of "ala" (upon), to indicate that the crucifying will be a strong crucifixion, such that the parts of the crucified enter into the thing upon which he is crucified.

Likewise the saying of the Truthful subhanahu: ﴿and they give food in spite of their love for it (ala hubbihi)...﴾ (76:8): as if they were the ones elevated over love, so that it might carry them wherever they wish.

Likewise the saying of the Truthful subhanahu: ﴿ala khawf...﴾ (10:83): i.e., they were above fear, which leads them into corridors where pains are expected.

And here they believed: ﴿out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs that he would persecute them...﴾ (10:83). The speech here from the Highest (al-Haqq al-A'la) subhanahu shows us that the fear was not of Pharaoh, because Pharaoh only exercises intimidation through those around him. Their likeness is that of the night-raiders (zuwwar al-fajr) in any state that gives no weight to human dignity.

Pharaoh, given his position and rank, does not carry out torture himself; rather his henchmen (zabaniyatuhu) do it.

The indication here shows the fear was of Pharaoh's partisans and chiefs.

The Truthful subhanahu said here: ﴿yaftinahum﴾, and did not say "yaftinuhum" (they persecute them), to show us the point that the henchmen do not inflict torture out of desire of their own, but they practise torture out of the desire of Pharaoh. Thus the pronoun came once in plural and once in singular, so that every word in the Qur'an attracts its meaning.

When the exegetes wished to clarify the meaning of (dhurriyya) they said: the intended were Pharaoh's wife (Asiya), Pharaoh's treasurer, the treasurer's wife, Pharaoh's hairdresser, and those among the people of Musa, peace be upon him, who believed and concealed their faith.

All these were prevented, by fear of Pharaoh's punishment, from declaring faith in the message of Musa; for Pharaoh was a tyrant in the land, claiming divinity, and whenever Pharaoh saw a person undermining his claim to divinity, he would surely strike at him with a deadly blow.

Therefore they were in fear of this blow, for Pharaoh, through his henchmen, had already slaughtered the sons of the Children of Israel and spared their women, and they feared these henchmen who carried out what Pharaoh wanted.

Hence the pronoun came in the plural expressing the group in His saying: ﴿and their chiefs (mala'ihim)...﴾ (10:83), and the pronoun came singular expressing Pharaoh the commander in His saying: ﴿that he would persecute them (yaftinahum)...﴾ (10:83). They feared that Pharaoh would persecute them through the torture carried out by his helpers.

The Truthful subhanahu says: ﴿...Indeed Pharaoh was haughty in the land, and indeed he was among the extravagant.﴾ (10:83). The "musrif" is one who exceeds limits. He exceeded in his extravagance and claimed divinity.

The Truthful subhanahu has related what came on the tongue of Pharaoh: ﴿...I am your Lord, the Most High.﴾ (79:24).

The Truthful subhanahu also said: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than me..."﴾ (28:38). Pharaoh was exalted in the land with the exaltation of a tyrant among humans over other weak humans.

The Truthful subhanahu said on the tongue of Pharaoh: ﴿Does not the dominion of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flow beneath me?...﴾ (43:51). Thus Pharaoh was extravagant to the utmost degree.

Footnotes:

1. Dhurriyya: a group (jama'a) of the offspring of Pharaoh's people [Tafsir al-Jalalayn p. 186]. It is also said: of the Children of Israel [Mukhtasar Tafsir al-Tabari p. 239].
2. Mala'ihim: the family of Pharaoh, his close associates and those who agreed with him.
3. Yaftinahum: turns them away from their religion through his torture of them.
4. "Ali fi al-ard": a haughty tyrant. The "land" here means the land of Egypt.
5. Al-musrifin: those who exceed the limit by claiming lordship. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn p. 186].
6. Khawf is fear of the occurrence of something disliked, or the loss of something loved; khawf is the opposite of security. The Most High said: ﴿He who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear (khawf)﴾ (106:4). And He said: ﴿Whoever fears (khaafa) from a testator an injustice or sin and makes reconciliation among them, there is no sin upon him...﴾ (2:182), i.e., he was alarmed at the expectation of the testator's wrong and oppression. His fear made him afraid. The Most High said: ﴿...and We frighten them, but it increases them only in great transgression﴾ (17:60). "Khawwafahu fulanan" means he made him fear; it takes two objects. The Most High said: ﴿That is only Satan who frightens his allies...﴾ (3:175).
7. Among the meanings of the particle (ala): elevation (isti'la'), which is its most common use, as in the saying of the Most High: ﴿Those messengers—We preferred some of them over others...﴾ (2:253). And location in time (zarfiyya), as in the saying of the Most High: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of heedlessness of its people...﴾ (28:15), i.e., "fi hin ghaflatin" (in a time of heedlessness). And accompaniment (musahaba), as in the saying of the Most High: ﴿...Indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing﴾ (13:6), i.e., "ma'a dhulmihim" (with their wrongdoing); and the saying of the Most High: ﴿and they give food in spite of their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ (76:8), i.e., with their love of wealth. Among its meanings also: that it means "min" (from), as in the saying of the Most High: ﴿Woe to the defrauders (al-mutaffifin), who, when they take a measure from people, take in full﴾ (83:1-2), i.e., from people. Other meanings of "ala" include: transgression (mujawaza), causation (ta'lil), reversal (idrab), and being equivalent to "bi" (with). See the detailed explanation in [al-Nahw al-Wafi: (2/509-512)].
8. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (4/3296). On this view the pronoun in "qawmihi" refers to Pharaoh. Al-Qurtubi mentioned another view, attributed to al-Farra', which makes the pronoun possibly refer to both Musa and Pharaoh at once, on the basis that the dhurriyya were people whose fathers were Copts, i.e., Pharaoh's family, and whose mothers were of the Children of Israel.
9. The "sparing of women": i.e., leaving them alive. The Children of Israel were under harm and oppression before Musa came to them, and Pharaoh's striking at them was continuous; therefore they said to Musa: ﴿We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us...﴾ (7:129). The Most High also said about the period of Pharaoh's harm to the Children of Israel before Musa's coming: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a group among them, slaughtering their sons and sparing their women. Indeed, he was of the corrupters﴾ (28:4).
10. Al-misr: a great city. The Most High said: ﴿Go down to a city (misran)...﴾ (2:61), i.e., a great and large city. Misr without tanwin is our dear country (Egypt). The Most High said: ﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife...﴾ (12:21) [al-Qamus al-Qawim].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿And Moses said: "O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims."﴾ (84)

Here there are two conditions, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you have believed in Allah...﴾ (84) [Yunus], and the answer to this condition came in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿...then rely upon Him...﴾ (84) [Yunus]. Then He brought another condition, which is: ﴿...if you are Muslims...﴾ (84) [Yunus]. Thus the first condition came with its answer, then another condition came, and this other condition is the first condition itself, which is submission (Islam) to Allah, because belief in Allah requires submission and that they be Muslims.

An example of this in our lives: when the headmaster of one of the schools wants to punish a pupil who has violated the school's orders and regulations, and the pupil pleads with the headmaster, the headmaster responds to this plea by saying: "If you come next Saturday, I will accept you into the school, provided that your guardian is with you." The guardian's coming here is tied to the date set by the headmaster for the pupil's return to the classes, and thus we find that the other condition is linked to the first condition.

Here this becomes manifest in the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿...If you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims⁽¹⁾﴾ (84) [Yunus].

Faith (iman), as we know, is an inward process of the heart and conscience, while Islam is an outward process. At times the individual carries out the teachings of Islam⁽²⁾, and at other times he departs from carrying out the teachings despite his faith in Allah; and at other times you find someone carrying out the teachings of Islam out of hypocrisy, without a foundation of faith.

For this reason, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds...﴾ (25) [Al-Baqarah], and He, glorified is He, explains this matter with a decisive definition in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed."...﴾ (14) [Al-Hujurat]. Faith is an inward process of the heart; therefore the divine command comes: ﴿Say, "You have not believed; but say 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts..."﴾ (14) [Al-Hujurat]. That is: you perform the outward obligations of Islam, but faith has not yet entered your hearts.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿If you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him...﴾ (84) [Yunus]. Thus we see that reliance (tawakkul) is required by faith, and that a person must entrust his affairs at all times to the One in whom he has believed. Therefore faith benefits only with submission: if you are Muslims together with your faith, then rely upon Allah, exalted is He.

But if you have merely believed and have not surrendered the reins to Allah in the obligations, to Allah's "do" and "do not do," then this reliance is not valid.

Thus confirmed for us is what we said before: that whenever you see a construction containing a condition that precedes, with an answer following the condition, and then another condition comes, know that the last condition is the one that is first in meaning, because it is a condition within the first condition⁽³⁾. Likewise here, reliance does not arise except with submission together with faith.

(1) Because there is no connected faith except with submission, and no connected submission except with faith; between them there is a true mutual necessity for reaching the intended meaning.

(2) Islam is submission to Allah the Exalted and to what the Messenger ﷺ brought of the laws and rulings. It is the outward submission to all the rulings of Islam. As for faith (iman), it is the belief of the heart and its firm assent that admits no doubt. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds..."⁽¹⁴⁾﴾ [Al-Hujurat].

(3) Two or more conditional particles may follow one another, either directly connected or indirectly connected. In direct succession, the consideration is for the first particle; it alone requires a condition and an answer. In indirect succession, each particle has its own conditional verbal clause that directly follows it, and each particle after this is separated from the conditional particle before it and requires an answer clause subject to several rules, among them that if the succession is without conjunction, the answer belongs to the first particle alone unless an indicator specifies otherwise. As for the subsequent particles, the answer of any of them is omitted because the answer of the first particle indicates it. See the detailed treatment in [al-Nahw al-Wafi: 4/490, 489].

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿So they said, "In Allah have we put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial (fitnah) for the wrongdoing people.(85)"﴾

That is: they responded to the call of Musa (peace be upon him) merely by their saying: ﴿In Allah have we put our trust.﴾

When the prepositional phrase (al-jar) precedes what it governs (al-majrur), this indicates restriction and confinement of the matter: here the trust is restricted and confined to Allah, the Exalted, and there is no trust in anyone other than Him.

Then comes their supplication: ﴿...Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.(85)﴾ [Yunus]. Fitnah (trial, test): it is, as we have said, not blameworthy in itself; rather, what is blameworthy is that the outcome should turn out against the interest of the one who undergoes the trial.

It is said: "fatanta al-dhahab" (I tested the gold), meaning I refined the gold and extracted it from all impurities. We know that goldsmiths mix it with other elements so that it holds together, because gold not mixed with other elements does not hold together.

The fitnah about which they said: ﴿...Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.(85)﴾ [Yunus] is the fitnah of fear that some of them might turn away from faith if Pharaoh prevailed over them and tortured them. It is as though they were saying: "O Lord, do not give Pharaoh power over us with severe punishment."

This is if they were the ones being tested. But what if they were the ones who test others?

In that case, if they did not follow the religion in its true sense, Pharaoh and his household would not have known that those who declared their faith were truly Muslims, and if they deviated from the religion, the people of Pharaoh would say about them that they are not people of true faith.

We find our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who is the father of the prophets and has his great station in prophethood, saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve...(5)﴾ [al-Mumtahanah].

The supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) teaches us the necessity of adhering to the teachings of the religion, so that no one looks at a Muslim or a believer and says: "This is one who declares faith yet acts contrary to the teachings of his religion."

For this reason, our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him) would perform the commands with more than what was required of him, and the Truthful (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says of him: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them...(124)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. That is: he would complete every act with intention and excellence, because he was an exemplar (uswah), so he did not perform any act of faith with a superficial appearance.

Thus: if they were the ones being tested, they were warding off the trial from themselves; and if they were the ones who test, then they must adhere to the teachings of the religion, so that no one accuses them of falling short in their religious duties, lest the disbelievers increase in disbelief and misguidance.

The saying of the Truthful (al-Haqq), glory be to Him: ﴿...Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.(85)﴾ [Yunus] came to indicate their preoccupation with the matter of religion, whether as testers or as those tested.

1 Al-fitnah: a place of punishment. [Kalimat al-Qur'an, by Shaykh Hasanayn Muhammad Makhluf].
2 "Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people": a) do not let them prevail over us so that they think they are upon the truth and are thereby tempted by us. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn, p. 186].
3 Ibtala: tested. Bi-kalimat: commands and prohibitions which Allah assigned to him.
4 Uswah: a good exemplar.

Almighty Allah says next:

﴿And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.﴾ (86)

Here the noble verse makes clear that if they were preoccupied with the affair of others among the disbelievers, this means they were hoping for the faith of the enemy, that perhaps this enemy would return to the right guidance of faith.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself." (1)

They wanted faith for the enemy even though he was a wrongdoer.

In this way Allah, glory be to Him, teaches creation that it is folly of enmity for a person to invoke evil upon his enemy, because what wearies you about your enemy is his evil, while it is in your interest to invoke good for him, because this good will extend to you.

The believer should pray for his enemy to be guided, for when he is guided, the benefit will extend to you. This is one of the distinguishing marks of faith: that its benefit extends to others.

When they called upon Allah, saying that He not make them a trial for the wrongdoing people, this makes clear to us that wrongdoing has degrees, and that Pharaoh and his chiefs were at the peak of wrongdoing, because Almighty Allah Himself said: ﴿...Indeed, association [with Allah] is great injustice.﴾ (13) [Luqman]. The peak of wrongdoing is that you take the right of another and give it to one who is not its owner. Pharaoh and his chiefs committed shirk against Allah, glory be to Him, so Pharaoh thought he was a god, and those around him confirmed him.

Thus the peak of wrongdoing is shirk with Allah, glory be to Him; after that it descends to wrongdoing in major sins, then to minor sins.

As for their words in supplicating the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.﴾ [Yunus] (86): that is, make us in a place of safety (najwah) (2) away from these people.

What used to frighten the ancients was torrents of water when they rushed forth, and none would be saved except one who was on a high mound; the najwah is the elevated place. This is the origin of the word "najah" (salvation).

Here Almighty Allah says on their tongues: ﴿And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.﴾ [Yunus] (86). Mercy is protection from the disease coming to pass. Almighty Allah says: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy...﴾ (82) [al-Isra']. Healing is when the disease has already occurred, while mercy is that the disease does not come.

(1) Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (13), and by Muslim in his Sahih (45), Kitab al-Iman, from Anas ibn Malik, with the wording: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not believe until he loves for his neighbour—or he said, for his brother—what he loves for himself."

(2) Najwah: the elevated part of the ground. It is said: "He is in najwah from this matter," meaning: far from it, free of it, safe. [Al-Mu'jam al-Wasit, root n-j-w]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 87:

And after that, the Truth, glory be to Him, willed to honour Musa (peace be upon him) and his people, so He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, said:

﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother: "Settle your people in Egypt in houses, and make your houses into places of worship (qiblah), and establish the prayer, and give good tidings to the believers."(87)﴾

We have already explained that Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both) were two messengers with one message, and that the revelation came to both of them with one message.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, chooses a prophet as a messenger, He chooses him by a creation and a natural disposition (fitrah) that qualifies him to bear the message and to speak the intentions of God, exalted is He.

If created beings have made self-moving machines out of inanimate materials that have no thought and no deliberation (ruwayah), such as the clock that rings the alarm or the radio that broadcasts at a set time, and if humans have made such things, how much more so God, glory be to Him, the Creator of all creation and the universe and the Sender of the messengers?

He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, chooses His messengers in such a way that the constitution of the messenger allows him to carry out the task entrusted to him in any circumstance.

And His saying here, the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother..(87)﴾ [Yunus]: shows us that the revelation included both Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both), so that when a situation arises that requires Musa to speak, Harun can also speak in the same matter, because the faith-charge is one and the method is one.

This happened after Pharaoh and his people had drowned and the field was clear for them, so the command came to them to settle in Egypt and to have houses there.

But we may ask: is this Pharaoh a person who drowned and ended?

No. Pharaoh is not the name of a person but a classification of a office; the title of every ruler of Egypt in ancient times was "Pharaoh." Therefore there is no need for us to occupy ourselves with whether he was Thutmose I, or Ramesses, or something else. Suppose that the Pharaoh meant here drowned; does that not mean the coming of a new Pharaoh?

We know from history that ruling dynasties succeeded one another, and they were all pharaohs, and some of them oppressed the believers, and the successor of the Pharaoh must have been fiercer and more charged against these people.

And His saying, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, in the noble verse that is the subject of our reflections: ﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother that you settle your people in Egypt in houses..(87)﴾ [Yunus]: we find in it the word "Egypt" (4), which, when used without qualification, is understood to mean "the region."

Here in our country we have made the word "Egypt" a proper name for the region extending from the Mediterranean to the Sudanese border, that is, the Nile Valley.

And once again we have made "Egypt" the name of the capital of the Nile Valley. We also say of the railway station in Cairo: "Misr Station."

And the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, here: ﴿..that you settle your people(87)﴾ [Yunus]: we understand from it that tabawwu' (settling) is taking a place that is considered a mubaa'ah (dwelling place) (5); that is, a place of return to which a person returns.

Tabawwu', then, is settling in a certain place, and a person who takes a place as a homeland returns to it if he travels to another country for a period.

Leaving the homeland is merely a journey that requires return, and likewise the house is for a person; one of us roams all day in the field, the factory or the office, and after that returns to the house for spending the night (baytutah) (6).

The houses which God, glory be to Him and exalted is He, commanded to be established for the people of Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both) had a condition, which is the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿and make your houses into a qiblah..(87)﴾ [Yunus].

The qiblah is the direction toward which we pray.

An example of this is the mosque, which is the qiblah of whoever is outside it; when the muezzin calls to prayer the mosque is our qiblah to which we go, and when we enter the mosque we face inside toward the qiblah, and our orientation toward the qiblah is what controls our row arrangement.

And the command here from the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿and make your houses a qiblah and establish the prayer..(87)﴾ [Yunus]:

So the establishment of houses here is conditioned on making them a qiblah for establishing the prayer, far from the eyes of the opponents who oppress them, just as with the early Muslims when Islam, in its beginning, was weak in Mecca, and the Muslims at that time prayed in the heart of their houses; this is the secret of not reciting the prayer aloud during the day, and not reciting aloud serves to ensure that the opponents do not notice the place of the worshippers.

As for reciting aloud at night and at dawn, the purpose was that it teach them how to recite the Qur'an.

And here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿that you settle your people in Egypt in houses and make your houses a qiblah..(87)﴾ [Yunus]: it may be that what is meant is that the houses should face one another.

Even today, if you look at the Jewish quarters (sahat) in any country of the world, you will find that they live in one neighbourhood and refuse to melt into the other neighbourhoods.

In every country they have a quarter in which they live, called by the name "the Jewish quarter." In Egypt they had "alleys" each of which was called by the name "the Jewish alley."

God, glory be to Him, willed that and said in His Mighty Book: ﴿And humiliation and wretchedness were struck upon them..(61)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. They protect themselves by being together, so if some matter frightens them, it becomes easy for them to gather.

Or ﴿and make your houses a qiblah..(87)﴾ [Yunus]: that is, that the planning of the places and streets on which the houses are built be in the direction of the qiblah.

And any architectural error like the one present in the square plan of the building of the Imam al-Husayn mosque in Cairo: this error requires facing slightly to the right, which causes some confusion for the worshippers, because a slight deviation to the right during prayer requires that each row be shorter than the row behind it.

When we pray in the Sacred Mosque in Mecca, we find some worshippers who want to make the rows equal and straight, and we find someone who alerts that the row is straightened by the length of the longest side of the Ka'bah, and then the row bends.

Likewise in the upper floors built in the Sacred Mosque we find the rows bent, facing the Ka'bah.

For this reason I always say when I pray in the Sacred Mosque: the meaning of the Imam's saying "straighten your rows" is: make your shoulders (manakib) against the shoulders of one another. As for outside the Ka'bah, it suffices that we face the direction in which the Ka'bah is; we, outside the Ka'bah, do not pray toward the very body of the Ka'bah, but we pray in its direction; because if we were praying toward the very body of the Ka'bah, the length of a row in any mosque would not exceed twelve and a quarter metres, which is the longest side of the Ka'bah.

And the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, here: ﴿and make your houses a qiblah(9)..(87)﴾ [Yunus]: that is, plan in establishing the houses that they be on the qiblah; some people try to do that, but the planning of streets and neighbourhoods does not help with that.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and establish the prayer..(87)﴾ [Yunus]: from this command we understand that the prayer involves the continuation of loyalty (wala') (10) to God, exalted is He. We testify that there is no god but God once in a lifetime; we pay zakat, if we have wealth, once a year; we fast, if we are not ill, one month, which is the month of Ramadan; and we perform Hajj, if we are able, once in a lifetime.

There remains the pillar of prayer, which is repeated five times every day, and if a person wishes he may add more; and it is as if the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, here draws attention to the pillar of the religion, which is the prayer.

But who chose the place in the verse that is the subject of our reflections? Is it Musa and his brother Harun? Or is the address to all the people?

We observe here that the command to tabawwu' is to Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both), while the command to make (ja'l) is required of Musa, Harun and the followers; therefore the making (ja'l) comes here in the plural form.

The Truth, glory be to Him, ends the noble verse with His saying: ﴿..and give good tidings to the believers(87)﴾ [Yunus]: In this there is an admonition and an indication that Musa is the origin of the message; therefore the command to bring the good tidings to the believers came to him.

We observe here in this verse that the Truth, glory be to Him, used the plural in tabawwu', used the plural in making the houses, and then used the singular at the end of the verse to alert us that Musa (peace be upon him) is the origin of the message to the Children of Israel.

Good tidings for righteous deeds means: the announcement of Paradise.

1 Tabawwu'a: took and made (ittakhadha wa-j'ala). Qiblah: a place of prayer in which you pray so that you are safe from fear. Pharaoh had prevented them from praying. Aqimu al-salah: complete it. Wa-bashshir al-mu'minin: with victory and Paradise. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn: p. 186].
Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir (2/429, 428) that God the Exalted commanded Musa and his brother Harun (peace be upon them both) that they should tabawwa', that is, take for their people in Egypt houses. The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿and make your houses a qiblah..(87)﴾. From Ibn 'Abbas: he said: they were commanded to take them as mosques. From Ibrahim al-Nakha'i he said: they were fearful, so they were commanded to pray in their houses, and so said more than one of the scholars of tafsir; and this, God knows best, was because the affliction from Pharaoh and his people had intensified against them and they had constricted them, so they were commanded to pray much, like His saying: ﴿O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer..(153)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said in the tafsir of this verse "qiblah" means: facing one another. [From Ibn Kathir, with adaptation.]
2 Al-ruwayah: consideration and thinking about matters, and it is the opposite of spontaneity [al-Mu'jam al-Wasit: root r-w-y].
3 Tabawwa': alighted and dwelt.
4 The name "Misr" occurs in the Qur'an four times as a proper name for the land of Pharaoh: in His saying: ﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother that you settle your people in Egypt in houses..(87)﴾ [Yunus]; in His saying: ﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife: "Honour his lodging..."(21)﴾ [Yusuf]; in His saying: ﴿..and he said: enter Egypt, if God wills, secure(99)﴾ [Yusuf]; and in His saying: ﴿And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people: "O my people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine..."(51)﴾ [al-Zukhruf]. As for His saying: ﴿Go down to a city (misran), for you shall have what you ask(61)﴾ [al-Baqarah], the word Misr occurs there with tanwin, indicating that it is not meant as the Pharaonic Egypt, the non-declinable proper noun, but is a common noun meaning a city, that is, a town.
5 Mubaa'ah: the place in which a person alights and dwells. [Lisan al-'Arab: root b-w-'; adapted].
6 Baytutah: the verbal noun of the verb bata yabit, since the house is the place of spending the night and of lodging. [Lisan al-'Arab: root b-y-t; adapted].
7 Sahat: plural of sahah, which is the area of the houses; it is also the open space between the houses of the neighbourhood; and the courtyard of the house is its bahah. [Lisan, root s-w-h]. From it is His saying: ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment? But when it descends upon their courtyard, evil will be the morning of those who were warned(176-177)﴾ [al-Saffat], that is, upon their dwelling-place or the homes they inhabit...
8 Manakib: plural of mankib, which is the joint where the upper arm bone and the shoulder bone meet. [Lisan al-'Arab: root n-k-b].
9 Qiblah: the direction. God says: ﴿We have seen the turning of your face toward the heaven; so We shall surely turn you to a qiblah that pleases you. So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque..(144)﴾ [al-Baqarah]; it is the direction toward which we turn in our prayer. The meaning of the verse here is that they should build their houses facing the qiblah; or: make them a qiblah for people to turn toward to attain good.
10 Wala': love and support. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And what is it with them that God should not punish them, when they bar from the Sacred Mosque, and they were not its guardians? Its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know(34)﴾ [al-Anfal].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 88:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And Moses said, "Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world. Our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment."﴾

Adornment (zīnah) is that which exceeds the necessities of life and its first foundations. Sustaining life is by food, any nourishment that stills hunger, and by drink that quenches thirst.

As for when food is varied, this is part of the luxury of life. And from the luxury of life is clothing that merely covers the nakedness, rather than a garment distinguished by the quality of its weaving, its design and its tailoring.

Likewise, from the luxury of life is the place in which a person sleeps, such that it is furnished with the finest furnishings (riyāsh). But what necessity requires for sleep is a place on the ground, and any bedding that protects from the coldness or heat of the ground.

So then: what exceeds the necessities is the adornment of life, and adornment comes from wealth, and the principal reserve of wealth is gold, followed by silver in second place.

And among the foundations of the economy: gold is considered the value-reserve for the wealth of any state, no matter what stones more precious than gold they may discover.

And these precious stones, such as diamond for example, if they are broken or scratched, their value decreases; but gold, however much it is crumbled, you can re-melt it and extract gathered gold.

The ancient Pharaohs ruled Egypt as far as the sources of the Nile, and they used to conscript people for all works, including extracting gold, whether from mines or from sifting the sands of some mountains to extract gold from them.

You may be able to extract gold from certain places, but the difference is always in the economic value of extracting gold: when the mine is abundant in yield, containing many veins of gold, then extracting gold becomes economically profitable.

But if the cost is higher than the economic value of the gold extracted, no one extracts this gold.

And if you look at the adornment of the Pharaohs, you find the mask of "Tutankhamun" a marvel of beauty; likewise their palaces were at the peak of luxury, and it suffices that you see the colours from which the wall paints were made in those days, to know the precision of craftsmanship and the extent of luxury, which is far more than necessities.

In this noble verse the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And Moses said, "Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world. Our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way..." (88)﴾ [Yunus]: They did not merely go astray, but they wanted to lead others astray too; therefore they bore the burden of their own misguidance and the burden of leading others astray.

Did God, glory be to Him, give them wealth and adornment for the purpose of misguidance and leading astray?

No. That is not the cause of the giving; rather there is the lam of consequence (lām al-ʿāqibah), just as you give your son ten pounds and say to him: "Do with it as you wish, and I hope you will dispose of it in a way that returns good to you." And this son may go and buy something useless and not beneficial, instead of buying books that would benefit him.

Here you gave this son purchasing power, but he did not handle it well, and his choice of play led him to amusement. This is what is called the lam of consequence, and the lam of consequence is not intended to be the cause of the act, but comes to show the consequence of the act.

When the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wished to save Moses, peace be upon him, in his infancy from being killed, He revealed to the mother of Moses, peace be upon them both, by His saying: ﴿When you fear for him, cast him into the river (al-yamm) and do not fear or grieve..." (7)﴾ [al-Qasas]: No mother would readily carry out such a command, because it is a certain death; for if the child is snatched or lost, all of that is a presumed death, whereas casting him into the water has no presumed death in it, but a certain death, unless God, exalted be He, saves him.

But the mother of Moses, because of her faith in God, did what God, glory be to Him and exalted, had revealed to her; for what comes from God finds no contender in the natural disposition (fiṭrah).

As for the whisperings of Satan, they find a thousand contenders in the soul, and likewise the suggestions of the self.

Therefore the mother of Moses carried out what God revealed to her, even if it was contrary to reason and logic.

When the family of Pharaoh picked him up, and they used to kill infants, and the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, placed love for Moses in their hearts, He said: ﴿"...And I cast upon you love from Me..." (39)﴾ [Ta-Ha]: At the moment they saw Moses, peace be upon him, as a child, they loved him, and so they did not kill him. Thus the will of God and His promise to his mother were carried out: ﴿"...Indeed We will return him to you and make him of the messengers" (7)﴾ [al-Qasas]: that is, Moses, peace be upon him, had a prior mission which the Truth, glory be to Him, intended for him.

Therefore we find that there are successive commands which the noble Qur'an brought concerning the matter of Moses' mother casting her son: ﴿When We inspired to your mother what is inspired (38), [saying]: Put him into the chest (tābūt), then cast it into the river, and let the river deposit him on the bank (sāḥil)... (39)﴾ [Ta-Ha]: all of them are commands from the Truth, glory be to Him. Then Pharaoh's wife finds him and says to her husband: ﴿"[He is] a comfort of the eye (qurrat ʿayn) for me and for you..." (9)﴾ [al-Qasas]: Did Pharaoh know that this child whom he picked up would become his enemy?

No. He picked him up and gave him a life of luxury so that he would be a comfort to his eye, and this is the cause of the picking up; but the consequence ended in his being an enemy. And if the cause had been enmity, Pharaoh would not have picked him up, or would have killed him at the moment of picking him up.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, leaves in His creation things that break the schemes of men; Pharaoh took him and raised him, and the consequence was other than what Pharaoh had expected.

The saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, here in the verse we are discussing: ﴿so that they may lead [people] astray (liyuḍillū)﴾ — from it we understand that He, glory be to Him and exalted, did not give them wealth in order that they go astray, but they themselves chose misguidance. God, glory be to Him and exalted, has given wealth and status to many people and they intended by it good; and thus we see human choice: he may go astray or be guided.

Moses, peace be upon him, said, to relieve himself: ﴿"Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world. Our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts..." (88)﴾ [Yunus]. The meaning of ṭams is the effacing of features, as in the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿before We efface faces and turn them back on their backs..." (47)﴾ [al-Nisa']. The meaning of ṭams here is: the effacing of the features of those faces, so that they become one piece without forehead, eyebrows, eyes, nose, lips or chin.

So then: ṭams is the destruction of the form by which a thing exists. Moses' supplication here, peace be upon him: ﴿"obliterate their wealth..." (88)﴾ [Yunus]: that is, transform it (imsakhhā).

And some narrators said that it was transformed: whoever owned some ingots of gold found them stones, and whoever owned precious stones such as diamonds found them glass.

Or [the meaning is]: ﴿"obliterate their wealth" (88)﴾ — that is, destroy them, because wealth was a means of misguidance.

As for his saying, peace be upon him, after that: ﴿"...and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment" (88)﴾ [Yunus]: that is, O Lord, tighten the bonds upon those hearts, so that what is in them of disbelief does not come out, and what is outside them of faith does not enter; because these people have slandered grievously, and that the bonds remain upon their hearts until they see the painful punishment. And why did Moses, peace be upon him, invoke against the family of Pharaoh in this way, and did not supplicate as our master Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did: "O God, guide my people, for they do not know"? The answer: God, glory be to Him, must have informed him that these are a people in whom the call to faith will not succeed.

The fear of Moses, peace be upon him, was not from the misguidance of Pharaoh's people, but from the continuation of their leading others astray.

So then: Moses, peace be upon him, invoked against them with what came in this verse: ﴿"...Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment" (88)﴾ [Yunus]. And in another place of the noble Qur'an the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might... (85)﴾ [Ghafir]. Thus the difference becomes clear to us between the faith of compulsion and constraint (iljā' wa-al-qaṣr) and the faith of free choice (ikhtiyār).

When the Messenger comes calling to faith, it becomes the right of the hearer of his call to believe or to disbelieve; for God, exalted be He, created man and gave him the right of choice; but the faith of compulsion and constraint does not benefit a person.

An example of this: Pharaoh, when the punishment came upon him, declared faith. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿"...until, when drowning overtook him, he said, 'I believe that there is no deity except He in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims.' (90)"﴾ [Yunus].

And if Moses, peace be upon him, invoked against the people of Pharaoh, Noah, peace be upon him, had preceded him in such supplication, as the Qur'an reports in His saying: ﴿"...My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant (diyāran) (26). Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers (27)"﴾ [Nuh].

1 "Obliterate their wealth" (uṭmis ʿalā amwālihim): Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid said: that is, destroy it. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others said: God made it stones inscribed...
2 "Harden their hearts" (ushdud ʿalā qulūbihim): seal them. This supplication came from Moses, peace be upon him, out of zeal for God and His religion, against Pharaoh and his chiefs, whom it became clear to him had no good in them and from whom nothing would come. [Cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 2/429].
3 ra'ā: to see with the eye, like abṣara. And to see with thought and heart, in the sense of knowing. And ra'ā: to believe. And ra'ā in his sleep a vision: a dream. And ru'yā: a dream in sleep. And ra'ā here is the visual sense; that is, until they see the punishment with their own eyes and witness it directly.
4 Al-riyāsh and al-rīsh: abundance of livelihood, means of living, wealth, furnishings, and fine, luxurious clothing. God, exalted be He, says: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your nakedness, and as adornment (rīsh). But the clothing of righteousness—that is best. That is among the signs of God that they may remember (26)﴾ [al-A'raf].
5 That is: the reason for Pharaoh's picking up Moses was not that he would be an enemy to him, but that he would adopt him as a son; and his wife added that he would be a comfort to her and to Pharaoh. But the consequence was other than that; that is, what happened was the opposite of what Pharaoh intended.
6 Al-yamm: abundant water that has gathered. What is meant by it here: the Nile in Egypt.
7 Pharaoh and his henchmen used to slaughter the sons of the Children of Israel and spare their women, after Pharaoh heard the prophecy that a boy from the Children of Israel would bring about his end. God, exalted be He, says: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people factions, oppressing a group among them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters (4)﴾ [al-Qasas]. And He says: ﴿...and We show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them what they had been fearing (6)﴾ [al-Qasas].
8 Al-tābūt: the box in which Moses' mother placed her son before casting him into the river, to protect him from the water.
9 Al-sāḥil: the riverbank near Pharaoh's palace.
10 Qurrat ʿayn: joy and happiness. [Kalimat al-Qur'an, Shaykh Hasanayn Muhammad Makhluf].
11 The root "ṭamas" occurs in the Qur'an in five places: God's saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, so they would race to the path (66)﴾ [Ya-Sin]; His saying: ﴿And they had sought from him his guests, so We obliterated their eyes, [and said], "Taste My punishment and warning" (37)﴾ [al-Qamar]; His saying: ﴿And when the stars are obliterated (8)﴾ [al-Mursalat]; His saying: ﴿Believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces..." (47)﴾ [al-Nisa']; and His saying: ﴿"Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts..." (88)﴾ [Yunus].
12 Said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi: their wealth and dirhams became inscribed stones, in their shape, whole, halves and thirds, and no mine remained for them except that God obliterated it, so no one benefited from it after that.
13 Al-qaṣr and al-qasr: compulsion by force against one's will. From it: "I confined myself to the thing" when I restrained myself to it and obliged myself to it. See [Lisan al-'Arab, entries qaṣara, qasara].
14 God, exalted be He, says: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve..." (29)﴾ [al-Kahf], and He says: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture, We test him, and We made him hearing and seeing (2). Indeed, We guided him to the way, either grateful or ungrateful (3)﴾ [al-Insan].
15 God, exalted be He, says: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before and were of the corrupters" (91)﴾ [Yunus]. It was said: this is from the speech of God. And it was said: it is from the speech of Gabriel or Michael, peace be upon them. Pharaoh, who said: ﴿"...I am your most high lord" (24)﴾ [al-Nazi'at] and said: ﴿"I know of no deity for you other than me..." (38)﴾ [al-Qasas], came, now, when he witnessed death and the sign of God confirming the truth of Moses, and he uttered faith. And the Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Do they await only that the angels come to them, or your Lord comes, or some of the signs of your Lord come? On the day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith. Say, "Wait, indeed we are waiting"(158)﴾ [al-An'am].
16 Diyaran: anyone. That is, the uprooting of every disbelieving soul from the people of Noah, until this extended to his son from his loins. Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4/427) cited the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "If God had shown mercy to anyone from the people of Noah, He would have shown mercy to a woman, who, when she saw the water, carried her child and climbed the mountain. When the water reached her, she lifted the child onto her shoulder. When the water reached her shoulder, she placed the child on her head. When the water reached her head, she raised her child in her hands. Had God shown mercy to any of them, He would have shown mercy to this woman." Ibn Kathir said: this is a strange hadith, and its narrators are trustworthy.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 10, verse 89:

Almighty God responded to the supplication of Musa, peace be upon him:

﴿He said: "Your supplication has been answered, so go straight and do not follow the way of those who do not know."﴾ (89)

It should be noted that the one who supplicated was Musa, peace be upon him, but the words of the Almighty, ﴿Your supplication has been answered...﴾ (89), indicate that Harun, peace be upon him, also supplicated along with Musa.

We have said before: if we look at the primacy in the mission, we find that Musa, peace be upon him, is the primary one in it, and Harun came to strengthen his arm (1). If we look at the nature of the two, each of them is a messenger, and the two have one message.

Since the Almighty has sent the two for one task, if one of them is affected by something, the other must be affected by the same thing. Therefore, there is nothing to prevent that Harun, when he heard his brother supplicating with such a supplication, also supplicated with the same supplication, or that he—i.e., Harun—supplicated with this supplication secretly.

Supplication (du'a') means that you turn to one who is able to accomplish what you are unable to accomplish. You only supplicate in a matter whose causes have become difficult for you. So you say: "I have a Lord in whom I believe, and He is able over causes, because He is the Creator of causes, and capable of giving without causes." The true believer confronts events not with his own means, but with the power of the One in whom he believes, and He is the Highest Causer, the Almighty.

That is why you find Musa, peace be upon him, and his people, when they reached the shore of the sea, with the people of Pharaoh pursuing them behind them. The people of Musa said: ﴿...Indeed, we are to be overtaken.﴾ (61) [al-Shu'ara']. Musa, peace be upon him, replied: ﴿...No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ (62) [al-Shu'ara'], i.e.: do not arrange the matter according to human arrangement, for with me is the Lord of humankind. Then deliverance came to him: ﴿So We inspired to Musa, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted, and each portion was like a great mountain (2).﴾ (63) [al-Shu'ara']. Thus, supplication is only a turning in distress to one who is able over a matter you are unable to accomplish.

The matter that occupied Musa and Harun, peace be upon them, was the continuation of the people of Pharaoh in their misguidance and their insistence on misguiding others. So each of them must have supplicated the same supplication. We find something like this among non-prophets, and we call it "al-takhatur" (telepathy), i.e., the meeting of thoughts in a single moment.

An example of this in Islamic history: at the moment when our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was preoccupied with thinking about the Muslim army fighting in one of the battles, and 'Umar was in Madina delivering a sermon from the pulpit, he suddenly said: "O Sariya (3), the mountain!" This is a phrase that has no place in the logic of a sermon, but his thought was preoccupied with the commander who was fighting, and the commander heard the matter from a distance, so he withdrew to the mountain.

It is said regarding this matter: a thought became occupied with a thought, just as you seek someone on the telephone and the person you want to speak with replies, saying: "I was about to call you on the phone." This means the two thoughts were synchronized together.

If this is what happens in our ordinary lives, then what of what happens in the matters of the purified ones, and at their highest level, which is prophethood?

Or it may be that the one who supplicated was Musa, and Harun was only an affirmer (4), and the affirmer is one of the two supplicants. Since the Almighty accepted the supplication of Musa, peace be upon him, He also accepted the supplication of the one who affirmed with him.

Some people think that the answering of supplication is the fulfilment of the request immediately upon the supplication. But the truth is that the answering of supplication is agreement to the request; as for the timing of the fulfilment of the request, it may be delayed for some time, just as happened with the supplication of Musa, peace be upon him, against Pharaoh and his chiefs. When Musa supplicated and Harun affirmed, the answer came: ﴿Your supplication has been answered...﴾ (89), after forty years, and Allah the Almighty brought about the obliteration of their wealth.

The heavens are not employed by the one who supplicates, accepting any supplication; rather, the acceptance of a supplication requires determining the time at which it is carried out.

These are matters within the will of Allah the Almighty; the Almighty, exalted, is far above being an executor of any supplication, but He is the One in whose hand are the keys of every matter. So when a supplication is answered, He, by His will, places the carrying out of the supplication at the fitting time, for if it were answered immediately, it might cause harm.

The Almighty, exalted, says: ﴿And man supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good, and man has always been hasty.﴾ (11) [al-Isra']. Therefore the Almighty determines the time of applying the supplication in the field of execution and reality.

He, exalted, says: ﴿...I will show you My signs, so do not seek to hasten them.﴾ (37) [al-Anbiya'] (5).

A person knows that he may have supplicated for things, and Allah the Almighty fulfilled the supplication and it was evil, and how many a thing a person supplicates for which Allah the Almighty did not fulfil, and its non-fulfilment was good.

Thus: the Supreme Power watches over us and knows what is in our interest, for we are not gods who command the execution of supplications; rather, above us is the Highest Wise One, the Almighty.

That is why we say in explaining the words of the Almighty: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them (6)...﴾ (11) [Yunus]: because a person may supplicate for evil against himself (7). Do you not hear a mother who supplicates against her son or daughter despite her love for them? If Allah answered her supplication against her children whom she loves, is that not an evil for the mother?

A child may say to his mother in anger: "O Lord, let some incident happen to me so that you may be relieved of me." Suppose Allah answered this supplication: would that please the one who supplicated against himself, or please his mother?

Of course not. So if Allah the Almighty has delayed in answering your supplication for evil, then this is good for you, and you should take the Almighty's delay in answering your supplication for good as good for you.

That is why the Almighty willed to say to Musa and Harun, peace be upon them: ﴿...Your supplication has been answered, so go straight and do not follow the way of those who do not know.﴾ (89) [Yunus]: i.e., remain upon the straight path, and do not involve yourselves in what you have no knowledge of. Is it not the Almighty who says: ﴿And Nuh called to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges." He said, "O Nuh, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose work was other than righteous. So do not ask Me for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you (8) lest you be among the ignorant."﴾ (45-46) [Hud]? i.e., be courteous with your Lord when you supplicate, and relieve yourself, and leave to the wisdom of the All-Wise the answering or not answering; the answer may be immediate or deferred until its appointed time, and both are good.

1 'Adud (arm) in man and others is the forearm, which is what lies between the elbow and the shoulder; the intended meaning of 'adud here is: help and assistance. The Almighty says: ﴿We will strengthen your arm through your brother and grant you both authority...﴾ (35) [al-Qasas].
2 Firq: a part. Tawd: a great mountain. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: (3/336)].
3 He is Sariya ibn Zunaym al-Dili. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab appointed him over an army and sent him to Persia in the year 23 AH. The matter came to 'Umar's mind while he was preaching on Friday that the said army had met the enemy while they were in the bottom of a valley and had resolved to flee, and near them was a mountain. So during his sermon he said: "O Sariya: the mountain, the mountain!" and he raised his voice, and Allah cast it into Sariya's hearing, so he led the people to the mountain, and they fought the enemy from one side, and Allah granted them victory and they prevailed. [al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba by Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani: 2/52, 53].
4 Ta'min: it is their saying "Amin" behind the supplicant, from which comes ta'min in prayer behind the imam...
5 'Ajul: an intensive form of 'ajal and 'ajala, meaning haste. The intended meaning: man is disposed to love good and to hasten in seeking it for himself, and insists in supplication, even if the matter is evil, while in his ignorance he thinks it is good. The Almighty says: ﴿Man was created of haste...﴾ (37) [al-Anbiya']. And the Almighty says: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it...﴾ (1) [al-Nahl].
6 'Ajala ya'jilu - 'ajalan and 'ajalatan. Ista'jala - isti'jalan. The Almighty says: ﴿Did you hasten the command of your Lord...﴾ (150) [al-A'raf], and He says: ﴿And what hastened you from your people, O Musa?﴾ (83) [Ta-Ha]. 'Ajjal al-amr: sought it before its time out of desire. 'Ajjal al-amr: preceded it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim].
7 Same as note 6 (repeated in source).
8 Al-ajal: the duration of time; the intended meaning here: lifespan.
9 'Ajl. It is established in Sahih Muslim the prohibition against supplicating against oneself, children and wealth. On the authority of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We travelled with the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, in the expedition of Batn Buwat, while he was seeking al-Majdi ibn 'Amr al-Juhani, and the camel was ridden by us in turns, five, six, or seven at a time. A man from the Ansar's turn came around on his camel, so he made it kneel, mounted it, then urged it on, and it lurched somewhat. He said to it: "Damn you, may Allah curse you." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Who is this one cursing his camel?" He said: "I am, O Messenger of Allah."
