Allah, glory be to Him, removed the punishment from them, and here He says: ﴿...And We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world(12) and let them enjoy for a time(98)﴾ [Yunus]. Among the implications of the story of Yunus, peace be upon him, is not only his anger but also his story with the fish. After his anger at his people, he boarded a ship, and the waves tossed it violently and it was about to sink with its passengers; so they threw the goods into the sea to lighten the ship, but its tossing continued, so they agreed to cast lots over whoever would be thrown into the sea, and the lot fell upon the Prophet of Allah, Yunus, peace be upon him.

It is like when we board a lift and find the red light lit as a warning that the load is excessive, and that the lift will not work unless one or more get out until the permitted number remains; usually those who get out are the best of those present in character, so that they may facilitate the work of the others.

Likewise was the matter with the ship on which Yunus, peace be upon him, had boarded: it nearly sank, so they cast lots, and it became incumbent upon Yunus to go down into the sea.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then he drew lots and was among the losers(141)﴾ [al-Saffat]. Yunus, peace be upon him, went down into the sea, and the fish swallowed him and gulped him down.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says about the presence of our master Yunus, peace be upon him, in the belly of the fish:

﴿And had he not been among those who glorify (Allah)(143), he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected(144)﴾ [al-Saffat].

And here, in the verse about which our reflections are being made, the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world...(98)﴾ [Yunus]. The punishment of disgrace in the life of this world can be seen embodied in one who slanders and acts arrogantly toward people, and then people see him in humiliation and abasement; this is the punishment of disgrace in the world, and surely the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful and more severe.

The Truth, glory be to Him, ends the verse by saying: ﴿...and let them enjoy for a time(98)﴾ [Yunus]. That is: they were saved from destruction by the punishment until their appointed terms ended in natural death.

1 "Al-musabbihun" (المسبحون): they are those who pray to Allah, the Exalted, before the trial and the punishment that befell him. It was also said: al-musabbihun are those who remember (Allah), by his saying often in the belly of the fish: ﴿...There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers(87)﴾ [al-Anbiya']. ﴿...to remain in its belly until the Day they are resurrected(144)﴾ [al-Saffat]: the belly of the fish would have become a grave for him until the Day of Resurrection. [Abridgement of Tafsir al-Tabari, and Tafsir al-Jalalayn].

2 "Qira" (القرى): it is the food of guests. And "qaryah" in the language: a metropolis or a large city, like Egypt (Misr), Mecca, al-Ta'if, Nineveh, and others that the Qur'an has indicated; the word "qaryah" occurs in it with this meaning 37 times, not counting its dual (once) and its plural (19 times).

3 The Truth, glory be to Him, says of it: ﴿And this is a Book that We have sent down, blessed, confirming what is before it, that you may warn the Mother of Towns and those around it...(92)﴾ [al-An'am], and He says: ﴿And thus We revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the Mother of Towns and those around it...(7)﴾ [al-Shura].

4 This is because the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, met a Christian boy belonging to Utbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabi'ah, called Addas. When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was about to eat from the grapes of their orchard, he said: "In the name of Allah," then ate. Addas looked at his face and said: "By Allah, this is not the speech of the people of this land." He, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: "From which land are you, Addas, and what is your religion?" He said: "I am a Christian, and I am a man from the people of Nineveh." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "From the town of the righteous man Yunus ibn Matta." Addas said to him: "What do you know of Yunus ibn Matta?" The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "That is my brother; he was a prophet, and I am a prophet." Addas bent over the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, kissing his head, his hands and his feet. Narrated by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (2/421).

5 "Al-Nun": the fish. "Dhu," "dha," "dhi" mean "possessor of." That is, the possessor of the fish, who is Yunus, peace be upon him.

6 He is Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Mutanabbi, a wise poet, born in Kufa in the year 303 AH, raised in Syria, then he travelled in the desert seeking literature, the Arabic language and the history of people. He died killed at al-Nu'maniyyah in Baghdad in the year 354 AH at the age of 51 (al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 1/115).

7 "Tahaffuz": anger. "Al-hafiza": anger. It is said: "Al-hafa'ith dhahabat al-ahqad" (anger removes grudges): that is, if you see your close one wronged, you become angry for him, even if you have a grudge against him in your heart. [Lisan al-Arab, root h-f-z].

8 When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, despaired of his people in Mecca, who had harmed him and harmed the Muslims, he turned to al-Ta'if seeking the support of Thaqif, spoke with them and presented Islam to them, but they only refused the matter, and incited their fools and slaves against him, who reviled him and shouted at him, until people gathered around him and drove him to a wall (orchard) belonging to Utbah ibn Rabi'ah and Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah. The foolish ones of Thaqif turned back from him, and he made for the shade of a grapevine and sat in it. Here the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, supplicated his Lord, saying: "O Allah, to You I complain of the weakness of my strength, the scarcity of my resources, and my lowliness before people. O Most Merciful of the merciful, You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To a distant one who frowns at me? Or to an enemy whom You have given power over my affair? If there is no anger from You upon me, I do not mind, but Your well-being is more expansive for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your Face by which the darknesses are illumined and by which the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, from that Your wrath should descend upon me or Your displeasure should alight upon me. To You belongs the reproach until You are pleased, and there is no power nor strength except by You." [Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 2/420, 419], with adaptation.

9 See the details of this story in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (2/419-421).

10 This agrees with what al-Zajjaj said: "The punishment did not actually befall them; rather they saw the sign that indicates the punishment, and had they seen the very punishment, faith would not have benefited them." Al-Qurtubi chose this in his tafsir (4/3312).

11 Al-Qurtubi related it in his tafsir (4/3312) from the statement of Ibn Mas'ud.

12 The commentators differed as to whether the punishment of the Hereafter was removed from them together with the worldly punishment, or whether only the punishment in this world was removed, on two opinions:
*The first: it was only in this worldly life, according to the apparent meaning of the noble verse.
*The second: the punishment was removed in this life and in the Hereafter, by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more(147), so they believed, and We let them enjoy for a while(148)﴾ [al-Saffat]. He applied the term "faith" to them, and faith is a means of deliverance from the punishment of the Hereafter. This is the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best. [Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2/433)].

13 "Saahama": he drew lots, that is, took part in the casting of lots. "Al-mudhadin": the defeated, when the lot fell upon him. [Ibn Kathir 4/20, with adaptation].

14 "Iltaqamahu": he swallowed it swiftly. Allah says: ﴿Then the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy(142)﴾ [al-Saffat], and "al-mulim" is one who has committed a sin for which he is blamed.

Almighty and Glorified Allah says next:

﴿And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed - all of them entirely. Would you then compel the people until they become believers? (99)﴾:

Allah, the Exalted, makes clear to us that if a battle occurs between a messenger prophet and his believing followers on one side, and those who have disbelieved him on the other, then Allah, the Exalted, must surely send punishment upon those who disbelieved. Beware lest you understand that Allah, the Exalted, needs the worship of people; for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Eternal and Everlasting, possessing all the attributes of perfection before He created creation. By His perfection He created creation, and His strength, glory be to Him, is in His very essence. He is the Creator before He created creation, and the Provider before He created provision and the provided-for. Creation is a manifestation of the attributes of perfection in Him, and He is the One who brought everything into existence from non-existence.

For this reason they call His attributes, glory be to Him, "attributes of the essence" (ṣifāt al-dhāt), because they exist in Him before the thing to which they relate comes into being.

When you say "Living" (ḥayy) and "Giver of life" (muḥyī), this does not mean that Allah, the Exalted, is described as "Giver of life" only after He found someone to give life to. No, He is the Giver of life, and by this attribute He gives life.

And to Allah belongs the highest likeness, and He, glory be to Him, is exalted above every resemblance: We see a painter or artist who has made a beautiful painting. Here we see the trace of the talent for painting that he exercised, and the painting is nothing but a trace of this talent.

So Allah, the Exalted, therefore possesses all the attributes of perfection before He created creation, and with the attributes of perfection He created creation.

Beware lest you understand that something new has occurred to Allah, the Exalted; nothing new occurs to the Truth, glory be to Him. He, glory be to Him, does not benefit from His creation; rather, it is He who benefits them.

We know that faith is required of man, who is the apparent species to us and of whom we are part, and it is required of another species about which Allah, blessed and exalted, has informed us: the jinn (2). As for the rest of the cosmos, it is glorifying (3), believing in Allah, the Exalted. The cosmos consists of countless worlds, and each has a system from which it does not deviate. If Allah, glory be to Him, had willed to bring both the two weighty ones - mankind and jinn - under the system of subjugation (taskhīr), it would not have been difficult for Him. But this subjugation establishes His power, not His beloved-ness (maḥbūbiyya).

For this reason, the Truth, glory be to Him, left man free to believe or not to believe, and this is what establishes His beloved-ness if you come to Him as a believer. This differs from the faith of compulsion and coercion. So the faith required of man or jinn is faith of choice.

As for the faith of compulsion and coercion, every world in the cosmos believes in the Truth, glory be to Him, and glorifies Him.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification...(44)﴾ [al-Isrā']:

This is not glorification of indication and symbol; rather, it is true glorification, by the evidence of His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿but you do not understand their glorification(44)﴾ [al-Isrā']. For if Allah had given you understanding of their languages, you would know the glorification of the creatures, by the evidence that He taught Solomon, peace be upon him, the speech of birds (5), and he heard the ant say: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you while they do not perceive(18)﴾ [al-Naml]. And the hoopoe said to Solomon, peace be upon him, what he had seen about Bilqīs, queen of Sheba: ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appear pleasing to them and has averted them from the way, so they are not guided(24)﴾ [al-Naml]. Thus: everything in the cosmos glorifies Allah, the Exalted, following His method, glory be to Him, except for the chosen ones of the two weighty ones: man and jinn; for each of them has intellect and possesses the distinction of choosing between alternatives.

And from the greatness of the Truth, glory be to Him, is that He created choice for man so that the believer comes to Him by choice; and if the Truth, glory be to Him, had willed to compel man to faith, He would have done so.

I say this lest anyone say: "Why all these matters of creation, sending messengers, the denial of some people, and then the destruction of the deniers?"

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed - all of them entirely. Would you then compel the people until they become believers?(99)﴾ [Yūnus]. So Allah, the Exalted, created man and subjected to him all kinds of creatures, and did not compel him to faith; rather, He, glory be to Him, says to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers(3)﴾ [al-Shu'arā'].

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was a sincere lover of his people and his kin; he tasted the sweetness of faith and grieved that they did not believe. So the Truth, glory be to Him, reminds him that his duty is only to convey the message, so he should not burden himself beyond measure.

The Truth, glory be to Him, willed to grant man the right of choice and subjected the cosmos to him; among people there are those who believe and those who disbelieve, and even among believers there are those who obey at one time and disobey at another. This is the will of the Truth so that the cosmos may be in balance. Every good quality, if there are those who oppose it, this is what Allah, glory be to Him, willed for man. So do not grieve, O Messenger of Allah; for the Truth, glory be to Him, willed that.

And if someone becomes angry that others did not acknowledge His good attributes, we say to him: The Truth, glory be to Him, is the Creator of the cosmos and the Provider; they disbelieved in Him and denied Him, and made partners for Him; so have they taken on the character of Allah?

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed - all of them entirely. Would you then compel the people until they become believers?(99)﴾ [Yūnus]. He, glory be to Him, desires the faith of love and the faith of choice.

1 Qabīlan: "tulzimuhum wa tulji'uhum" (compel them and force them). That is: this is not incumbent upon you, O Muhammad, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him; rather Allah, the Exalted, leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, as He, the Exalted, said in this: ﴿And had your Lord willed, He would have made mankind one community, but they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them...(118-119)﴾ [Hūd]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills...(272)﴾ [al-Baqara]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills...(56)﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ]. And other verses showing that Allah, glory be to Him, is the Doer of what He wills, guiding whom He wills and misguiding whom He wills, by His knowledge, wisdom and justice, glory be to Him. [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr: 2/433] adapted.
2 This is in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me(56)﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt].
3 The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them exalt Him...(44)﴾ [al-Isrā']. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise(1)﴾ [al-Ḥashr].
4 The glorification of indication and symbol we certainly observe in the motion of inanimate matter, and in the motion, growth and breathing of plants, and the motion, growth, breathing and instinct of animals, and the motion, growth, breathing and reasoning of man; every motion has a mover, and in motion there is glorification. Beyond that we find that the earth and heaven weep, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep for them, nor were they reprieved(29)﴾ [al-Dukhān]. Weeping issues from emotion, and emotion issues from knowledge; these levels are a glorification in truth which the intellect does not grasp, though the heart may perceive it.
5 The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says concerning Solomon, peace be upon him: ﴿And Solomon inherited David. He said, "O mankind, we have been taught the speech of birds, and we have been given of all things. Indeed, this is evident bounty"(16)﴾ [al-Naml].
6 Bākhi': that is, destroying yourself, i.e., through what you eagerly desire and grieve over for their non-belief. This is a consolation from Allah, the Exalted, to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, regarding the non-belief of those disbelievers who did not believe in him. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So let not your soul go out in pursuit of them in regrets(8)﴾ [Fāṭir]. And as His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself over their traces(6)﴾ [al-Kahf].
Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and others said: "Bākhiʿun nafsaka" means "qātilun nafsaka" (killing yourself). And the poet said:
"Unquestionably, O you who would destroy yourself with grief
over a thing the decrees have snatched from your hands."
[Mentioned by Ibn Kathīr in his tafsīr (3/331), adapted.]
7 Al-Shatat: injustice and exceeding measure in anything. The meaning is: do not wrong yourself, and do not exceed the limit in grief over them. From it is His saying, the Exalted, concerning the two adversaries who asked David to judge between them, saying to him: ﴿...so judge between us with truth and do not exceed, and guide us to the sound path(22)﴾ [Ṣād].

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 10, verse 100 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:
﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah, and He places defilement upon those who do not use reason.﴾
Thus does the Truth, glorified is He, make clear to us that no one believes except by the permission of Allah, the Exalted. For the meaning of "to believe" is that your faith be a faith of innate nature (fitrah), resulting from reflection upon the heaven with its constellations (abraj), the earth with its wide pathways (fijaj), seas that surge, and winds that blow. All of this points to the existence of the Creator, glorified is He.

But does Allah, glorified and exalted is He, leave people to their innate nature?

No. Rather, He sends Messengers to them to remind them of the signs present in the cosmos, and so that the heedless may pay attention, for He, glorified is He, does not wish to seize people unawares.

Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says:
﴿...Your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware.﴾ [al-An'am: 131]
Thus the Truth, glorified is He, alerts them that there are matters that must be mentioned. The Truth, glorified is He, is making clear to us: beware lest you understand that anyone goes out of My dominion except by My will. For by creating him as one who chooses, I have permitted him to disbelieve or believe, and permitted him to obey or to disobey.
All of this is so that My attribute of being loved may be established.

Therefore no one believes except by the permission of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and no one disbelieves except by His permission; for whoever He created as one who chooses, He knows, with His own pleasure, what will come from the creature. The disbeliever did not disbelieve by compulsion, and the believer did not believe by compulsion from Allah, glorified is He.

When the Messenger comes to present the matter of faith, a person recalls the faith of innate nature and says: "This Messenger has come with this method to set my life in order, so I must lend him my attentive hearing."

When a servant turns to Allah, the Exalted, He grants him permission to enter the enclosure of faith.

When one of us goes to meet another servant who has lordship and rank, and that lord perceives, by a favour from Allah, the reason for which the other servant came, the lord says to his aides: "Do not admit him." He says this because Allah, glorified is He, has informed him of the rancour, hatred and hypocrisy in the heart of the other servant.
But if another servant knocks on his door, you find him ordering his aides to admit him and make room for him, because he knows what is in that heart of love, desire for a sincere meeting, and affection.

If this happens among servants, who are all changeable, then what of the Truth, glorified is He?

And Allah, glorified is He, is the One who said in a hadith qudsi: "Whoever remembers Me in his self, I remember him in an assembly better than it."

What of the servant who enters faith in Allah not burdened with any belief other than Allah?

So: draw near to Allah, glorified is He, and to the remembrance of Allah. If you remember Allah in yourself, Allah remembers you in Himself; and if you remember Him in an assembly, He remembers you in an assembly better than it. The assembly in which you mention Him is an assembly of sinners, while Allah, glorified is He, will mention you in a pure assembly.

The Truth, glorified is He, also says in the same hadith qudsi: "If he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit." And the cubit is longer than the span.
And He says: "And if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running."

Walking may tire the servant, so the Truth, mighty and majestic, hastens toward him. And He, glorified is He, in all His lordship, as soon as He knows that a servant's heart has been purified of enmity toward Allah in some matter, opens before him the doors of His love, makes his creatures love him, and grants him an entrance of truthfulness in every affair and an exit of truthfulness from every straitness. He is the Truth who says:
﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety.﴾ [Muhammad: 17]

We note that the Truth, glorified is He, emphasises in the verse about which we are reflecting that had He willed, all who are on earth would have believed together, to show us that even Iblis, who entered into argument with Allah, would have believed had the Truth, glorified is He, willed it.

The Truth, glorified is He, brought this emphasis to settle the matter concerning all His creatures and created things, so that not one of them is exempt.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says in the same verse:
﴿...Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ [Yunus: 99]
Allah, glorified is He, wished to alert His Messenger ﷺ and all the believers that: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 256]. For the requirements of religion are not only the outward requirements that the eye can see; there are other requirements that are hidden. Suppose you compel a body, can you compel a heart? The Truth, glorified is He, wants hearts, not bodies.

Thus compulsion is not suitable in the matter of religion. But a person must not drag compulsion beyond its proper place or sphere. For you may find a Muslim who does not pray, and his friend rebukes him, and he replies: "There is no compulsion in religion." This is an incorrect use and a mistaken inference, for compulsion in religion is forbidden only in the first matter of belief.

But whoever declares that he is a Muslim, and testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, has thereby declared his commitment to all the rulings of Islam, and he is counted among Muslims. If he violates a ruling of Islam, he must be held to account.

There is no compulsion in religion regarding the first matter of belief, and you are free to enter Islam or not. But if you enter Islam, you are bound by its rulings, because you have believed in it and have become counted among its adherents. Guard the limits of Islam and do not break them, for example — God forbid — if you steal, your hand is cut off; if you commit adultery, you are stoned or flogged; if you drink wine, you are flogged, because you accepted the principles and law of Islam.

If someone sees a Muslim stealing, let him not say that Islam encourages theft; rather, if he sees him punished, he knows that Islam punishes whoever commits a crime. So: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 256] concerns the prohibition of compulsion regarding the root of religion. But after you believe, you are bound by the secondary matters of religion, and you are punished if you transgress its limits.

The Messenger ﷺ said: "The likeness of one who upholds the limits of Allah and one who violates them is like people who drew lots for a ship; some of them got the upper deck and some the lower. Those in the lower part, when they needed water, would pass by those above them, and they said: 'If only we made a hole in our share and did not harm those above us.' If they are left to what they want, they will all perish; but if they take hold of their hands, they will be saved and all will be saved."(10)

So: the observance of the branches of religion is an obligation upon whoever enters religion without compulsion, and whoever violates a ruling is punished.

There is something more severe than that, which is the ruling on one who apostatises from Islam: it is execution.(11)

Someone may say: this matter represents brutality. We say to him: whoever commits himself to the religion knows from the outset that if he believes and then apostatises, he will be killed; therefore he has no right to enter Islam except with certainty of faith.

This condition is for the sake of the religion, not against it. Do not enter the religion unless you are certain that its commands are above your desires, and know that if you enter the religion and then abandon it, you will be killed. In this there is a making difficult of the entry into religion, so no one enters it except one who is confident of his faith-based certainty; and this is a point counted in favour of the religion, not against it.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says:
﴿...and He places defilement upon those who do not use reason.﴾ [Yunus: 100]
The rijs (defilement) is: punishment, and it is sin. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, places it upon those who do not use reason, because the matter of religion, when presented to the intellect without desire, must lead the intellect to faith.

Therefore you find the intellectual elite, when they study religion, turning toward Islam, because it is the religion that cures the thirst (ghullah) of the seeker. As for those who took religion as an inheritance from their fathers, they remain in their state. Some of the intellectual elite in the world who turned to embracing Islam did not turn to it because of seeing the conduct of Muslims, for the conduct of those ascribed to Islam in our time has strayed from the religion.

Therefore those intellectual elite who turned to Islam studied its principles, and distinguished between the principles of religion and those who adhere to religion. This is fairness in intellectual inquiry, because when religion forbids an action, that prohibition is not a permission from religion for the occurrence of such a forbidden act, as is shown by the assignment of punishment according to the gravity of the crime.

The Truth, glorified is He, has said:
﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 38]. This is a permission of the possibility of theft occurring; and likewise regarding adultery and other crimes for which the Truth, glorified is He, prescribed penalties proportionate to the harm that falls upon the self or society from their occurrence. So if you see a Muslim stealing, remember the punishment Islam imposed on the thief; and if you see a Muslim committing adultery, remember the penalty the Truth, glorified is He, set for the adulterer.

The same is true of all crimes.

Great thinkers of the world who turn to Islam study the principles of religion separately from the conduct of contemporary people who have strayed from the principles of the upright religion.

Here is "Guénon", the French thinker, who says: "Praise be to Allah who guided me to Islam before I knew the Muslims. For if I had known the Muslims before Islam, there would have been a possibility of a shaking in the soul that would make me hesitate to enter this religion of exalted station."

So: the use of refined reason must lead to Islam, because it is the innate nature of Allah, and Islam develops it and elevates it, and reason is the basis of accountability.

Defilement, sin and punishment fall only upon those who do not employ their reason; and the employment of reason that weighs values negates defilement, for they will turn to religiosity by the permission of Allah, the Exalted, to enter into faith in Him.

If someone asks me: What is reason? And what is the basis of accountability?

We find that the word "'aql" (reason) derives from 'iqal al-ba'ir, which is the cord tied around a camel's knee so that it does not rise, and it remains still; and when its owner wants to make it rise, he unties the cord.

The people of the Gulf place on their heads a head covering (ghutrah) and fasten it with a woven cord in the form of two rings, and they call these two rings "al-'iqal," because it prevents the head covering from being moved or blown away by the wind.

So: Allah, glorified is He, willed reason for us to restrain us from unrestrained rushing and disorder in the pursuit of the desires of the self, for He, glorified is He, created the human soul and knows that it loves immediate desires; so He willed for the human being to curb the surge of those desires by reason.

When a person considers fulfilling an immediate desire, he finds his reason whispering to him: "You will enjoy the immediate desire for a few minutes, and you may be taking it from another — from his womenfolk or from his wealth. Would you allow another to take his immediate desire from you?"

So: you must know that reason was willed by Allah, glorified is He, for you to restrain you from a movement in which there is desire and by which you achieve a pleasure that is not yours, and whose consequence is wearisome.

Whoever thinks that reason opens a door to irresponsible rushing in the name of freedom is mistaken. We say to one who holds such a thought: reason is the basis of accountability, and it is what clarifies for you the horizons of responsibility in every conduct.

It is from the justice of the Truth, glorified is He, that He did not impose obligation on the insane, because the insane person's judgment on things and actions is abnormal, for he lacks the faculty of choosing between alternatives.

Likewise Allah, glorified is He, did not impose obligation on one who has not matured by reaching puberty, because he has not attained the full faculties, and the capacity to beget a like of himself has not become sound in him.

We have previously given the example of the fruit, and said: it is not said that the fruit has ripened and its taste has become acceptable and palatable unless the seed within it is able to grow into a tree if we plant it in the earth.

For example, when you cut open a watermelon and find its pulp white, you do not eat it, and you are careful to eat the watermelon whose seeds have turned black, because that is a sign of its ripeness; and when you take that pulp and plant it, it produces watermelon for you.

So: the human being's completion through puberty enables his reason to weigh conduct before undertaking it, and obligation falls only upon the sane, mature person who is not compelled by a force that overpowers him to do what...

(1) Rijs: imagination and misguidance. [Ibn Kathir 2/433]. Al-Zajjaj said: rijs in the language is a name for everything in deed that is found repugnant, and God exaggerated in condemning these things and named them rijs. Rijs has other meanings: it is punishment, like rijz; it is sin; and it is doubt, as in His saying: ﴿...Allah only wishes to remove from you the defilement, O people of the house, and to purify you with thorough purification﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33].

(2) Abraj: plural of burj. These are the stations of the celestial spheres in the sky, or they are the stars. It is said: they are the stars. [See Lisan al-'Arab: root b-r-j].

(3) Fijaj: plural of fajj, which is the wide road between two mountains. From it is His saying: ﴿And Allah has made the earth for you a spread-out carpet, that you may walk therein in roads, fijaj (wide paths)﴾ [Nuh: 19–20]. He also said: ﴿And We placed in the earth firmly set mountains lest it shake with them, and We made therein wide passages as roads, that they may be guided﴾ [al-Anbiya': 31]. And He said in the singular form: ﴿...and upon every lean camel; they come from every deep pass﴾ [al-Hajj: 27].

(4) Bihar tazkhar: meaning its water has increased and its waves risen. Zakhara al-qawm: they surged for a call to arms or war. [Lisan al-'Arab, root z-kh-r]. These phrases are from a sermon delivered by Qass ibn Sa'idah al-Iyadi in the pre-Islamic period, whose opening was: "O people, listen and take heed: whoever lives dies, whoever dies is gone, and all that is coming is coming." See al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin by al-Jahiz (1/308).

(5) Irhaf al-sam': intense listening. Rahafah in the language means softness and gentleness. [Lisan: root r-h-f].

(6) A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7405) and Muslim (2675), and its complete text is: "I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. By Allah, Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his lost camel in the desert. Whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; whoever draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him hastening."

(7) From Abu Hurairah, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah does not look at your bodies nor at your forms, but He looks at your hearts." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2564), Ahmad in his Musnad (2/539, 285), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4143); the wording is Muslim's. The hearts have feeling, choice, love and hatred; the forms are matter that moves according to perception that has been affected by feeling, and feeling that has placed alternatives before it to choose from, which is called (al-nuzu').

(8) In the Islamic law, there are two penalties for adultery: stoning or flogging. Stoning is inflicted on the married adulterer who has been made chaste by marriage. Flogging of one hundred lashes applies to the unmarried or one who has not previously married, who is flogged one hundred lashes in application of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The adulterer and the adulteress, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes; and let not pity for them detain you in the religion of Allah, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day; and let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

(9) Istahamu: they cast lots.

(10) The hadith is related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2493), Ahmad in his Musnad (4/268), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2173), who said: hasan sahih.

(11) On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever changes his religion, kill him." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6922), Ahmad in his Musnad (1/323, 283, 282, 217), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (2535).
- The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said in another hadith on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud: "The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah may not be shed except in one of three cases: a life for a life, a married adulterer, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6878) and Muslim (1676).

(12) Ghullah in the language: intense thirst; it is borrowed for what a person longs to know and study, like the thirsty man seeking water.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 100 (part 2 of 2):

13 The Lord of Might, glorified is He, says: ﴿And do not approach adultery. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way.﴾ [al-Isra' 32]. He, glorified is He, also says: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterer - lash each one of them with a hundred lashes. And let not pity for them overtake you in the religion of Allah, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ (2) ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulterous woman or a polytheist, and the adulterous woman is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist; and that has been made unlawful for the believers.﴾ (3) ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses - lash them eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever after. And those are the defiantly disobedient,﴾ (4) ﴿except for those who repent after that and reform. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (5) [al-Nur].

14 Ghubb al-amr (the outcome of a matter): its consequence and its end. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry (gh-b-b)].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warnings avail not people who do not believe."﴾ (10:101):

Here the Truth, glorified is He, speaks to us about the world of dominion (ʿalam al-mulk) that you see, and does not speak about the world of the unseen realm (ʿalam al-malakut) that is hidden from you. It is as if, once you are convinced of the world of dominion and say: this world has a Creator, a mighty, powerful God, and you believe in Him, then the breezes of the unseen blow upon you, so that you reach the world of the unseen realm. This is because you have discovered within yourself your trustworthiness with your own self, you have declared the Creator, glorified is He, and you have seen the beauty of His making in the sky and the stars, and you have been amazed by the precision of the order by which those stars move.

You see the exact timing of the rising of the sun and the moon and the schedules of total or partial eclipses, and you are dazzled by the precision of the Organizer, the Creator, glorified and exalted is He. You will not find traffic jams between the stars that would stall the moon or the earth, nor will any star stop because its fuel has run out. Rather, as Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each is traveling in an orbit.﴾ (36:40) [Yasin]. In our lives, when we see precision of craftsmanship in things far less than the sky, the sun and the moon, we honour the craftsman. Humanity has honoured the designer of the telegraph and the designer of the television set, so what of the Creator of the whole universe, glorified is He?

It is enough for us to know that the sun is eight light-minutes away from us, and a light-second equals three hundred thousand kilometres. And this is one sun that you see, apart from thousands of other suns in the early galaxies, and every galaxy contains millions of solar systems. It is enough for you to know that the Truth, glorified is He, swore by the sun,(3) and said of the star Sirius:

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾ (53:49) [al-Najm], because Sirius is larger than the sun.

When you contemplate the heavens and the earth, you find in the earth lofty mountains, and when you pass over them you are astonished by the precision of their formation and the precision of their cohesion. You find within them treasures and minerals in varying degrees, and you may find the surfaces of the mountains composed of fertile materials in a fragile form. When rain falls upon them, it carries them with it down to the earth, because they are merely particles like iron filings, and the earth that the heat of the sun has cracked absorbs them.

A clear example of this is the silt (ghareen)(5) that the Nile carried into the Delta during the flood before the building of the High Dam. The waters of the Nile in the days of the flood resembled the substance "tahina" (sesame paste), because of how thoroughly they were mixed with the particles of silt, and it is in such silt that the fertility is found from which we take our sustenance (aqwat).(6)

Had all the mountains been fragile in their formation, the rain would have removed them at once, turning them into a mere layer half a metre added to the surface of the earth, and fertility would have vanished from the earth after some years. But Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, willed to make the mountains cohesive, and made only their surface fragile, so that rain falls every year once, to carry fertility to the earth.

Whoever contemplates the engineering of creation in regard to sustenance finds the mountains to be storehouses of provision.

Human beings need iron to make from it what benefits them, whether tools for ploughing the land or any other tools that help in shaping life, and you find iron stored in the mountains.

Likewise we find other materials such as phosphate, manganese, marble, turquoise, or gases.

So then: what is buried (al-matmur)(7) in the mountains is either for sustenance, or a means to sustenance, or a means to luxury beyond sustenance.

When rain falls upon the mountains, it takes the fertility from the fragile layer(8) on the surface of the mountains, and the other materials remain as wealth for people. In Africa, for example, there are mines of coal and diamonds, and in other lands you find oud wood, which is the roots of trees. If you were to cut the earth like a slice from the earth's circumference to its centre, you would find fertile land together with desert, with water, with mountains, equal in goodness with the slice opposite the first slice.

The kinds of bounty may differ from one location on the earth to another. For if you calculate, for example, what the rain has given the Nile of fertility from the mountains since the day Allah, mighty and majestic is He, created the Nile in the land of the Nile valley in Africa, and calculate what petroleum (oil) has given in the desert of the UAE, for example, you will find that the giving of the Nile equals the giving of petroleum, although the discovery of petroleum happened only recently.

Every sustenance is measured out from storehouses of time, and every sustenance has its time: there is a time for coal and a time for petroleum. All of that is by an engineered system established by the Wise, Allah, glorified is He.

Since the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said ﴿they reflect﴾ in the context of looking at the heavens and the earth, this is a call to contemplate the wonders of the heavens and the earth.

Among those wonders: lofty mountains have a summit and a base, like the pyramid, whereas valleys are the opposite of mountains, because the valley lies between two mountains, and the head of the valley is at its bottom, while the head of the mountain is at its summit.

When rain falls it passes over the narrow summit of the mountain in order to reach the bottom of the narrow valley floor, and whenever rain falls it takes from the surface of the mountain in order to fill the broad area of the valley. And whenever creation increases, Allah, glorified is He, increases the expanse of sustenance.

An example of this you find in the silt coming from the sources of the Nile, reaching the Nile valley and the Delta. This Delta had been before merely salt marshes, and the Truth, glorified is He, willed for it to be transformed into fertile land.

When we contemplate this, we see that everything in the universe has been brought into being by the Truth, glorified is He, with precise measure.

What corrupts the universe is that we do not multiply what has multiplied; rather we wait until the earth is crowded with its inhabitants, and then we think about reclaiming new lands, when we should have done that earlier.

Whenever rain falls upon the mountains, they loosen and what is in them of minerals appears, which humans discover and exercise their minds in using.

When the believer sees that, his faith increases, and whenever the believer applies a legal ruling that is an obligation commanded to him, he finds the light of faith shining in his heart.

Let any Muslim try this experiment: let him live one week in the light of the methodology of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, then weigh and evaluate himself to know the difference between the beginning of the week and the end of the week. He will discover in this week that he prays at the times of prayer, he will find that he sweats in his work to earn what is lawful, and he will find that he spends his wealth on what is lawful.

Weigh yourself with certainty at the end of the week, and you will find that your self has become wonderfully transparent, so that you find the light and radiance of faith making harmony between you and the whole universe in its simplest details and its most complex.

An example of this: you may find a man of those upon whom the application of Allah's methodology has bestowed transparency, whose wife asks him: "What shall we cook today?" He says to her: "Let us make do today with what is left of yesterday's food," and then he is surprised by a relative visiting him from the countryside, who has come bringing goodness with him.

The man has reached a degree of transparency that makes him harmonious with the whole universe, so the provision of Allah, exalted is He, reaches him from any place.

You also find transparency in the most complex matters. Did not Ya'qub, peace be upon him, say: ﴿Indeed I smell the scent of Yusuf...﴾ (12:94) [Yusuf]. Yusuf's brothers, peace be upon him, were still at the gates of Egypt, leaving it to meet their father, carrying Yusuf's shirt, which Yusuf had instructed them to throw over their father's face so that his sight would return to him.(10)

The scent of Yusuf, peace be upon him, reached his father Ya'qub, because Ya'qub, peace be upon him, had lived in harmony with the universe, and there was no harm between him and the universe.

The living example of this is the joy of the universe at the coming of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of his birth. The universe rejoiced at the arrival of the Messenger (ﷺ), because the universe worships and glorifies Allah, glorified is He. So when one comes who calls the servants to monotheism, the universe must rejoice; but as for one who disobeys Allah, exalted is He, the whole universe hates him and curses him, and the two curse each other.

The universe rejoiced at the coming of the Messenger whom Allah, glorified is He, willed to receive the divine message, so that the balance of man with the universe would be set right.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth..."﴾ (10:101) [Yunus]. The whole universe is before them, so why do they not look? They see but do not perceive insight, like one who hears but does not hear; therefore Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿...But signs and warnings avail not people who do not believe.﴾ (10:101) [Yunus]. So their disbelief deprived them of insight and reflection.

Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Then do they await only the like of the days of those who passed away before them? Say: "Then wait; I am with you among those who wait."﴾ (10:102):

1. "Say: look at what is in the heavens and the earth": a command to the disbelievers to look and take heed at the created things that point to the Maker and the One capable of perfection. The "signs" here mean the proofs and demonstrations of Allah's divinity and oneness, and the verse indicates the general scope of looking into the dominion of Allah for everyone who wishes to remember or reflect. "The warnings" (al-nudhur): the messengers, plural of nadhir, and it is the Messenger (ﷺ). "For a people who do not believe": that is, concerning those for whom it was already decreed in Allah's knowledge that they would not believe. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/3314], adapted.
2. "It is not for the sun to overtake the moon": al-Thawri said: this means that this light does not overtake that light, nor that light this light. ʿIkrima said: it means each has its own dominion, so it is not for the sun to rise at night. "Nor does the night outstrip the day": Mujahid said: they pursue each other rapidly, one stripping the other away; the meaning is that there is no interval between night and day, but each follows the other without delay or lag, because they are subjugated and ceaselessly moving. "Orbit" (falak): plural aflak, the orbits in the sky in which the stars and planets revolve, so that they seem to swim in space. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/573], adapted. "This is evidence of the might and knowledge of the Almighty, the All-Knowing."
3. The Truth said in Surat al-Shams: ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ (91:1). Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned the sun in His Mighty Book thirty-two times, and indeed He, glorified is He, made an entire surah bear the name of this star.
4. Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatada, Ibn Zayd and others said of "al-Shiʿra" (Sirius) that it is the blazing star that is called Mirzam al-Jawza, and a group of the Arabs used to worship it in the pre-Islamic period. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/259].
5. Ghareen: what remains at the bottom of a basin or pool of water or mud, and it was said: it is the mud carried by a torrent that stays on the surface of the earth, moist or dry, and likewise "ghurayl." Al-Asmaʿi said: ghareen is when a torrent comes and settles on the land, and when it dries you see a thin mud on the surface of the earth that has cracked. [Lisan al-ʿArab: root gh-r-n].
6. Aqwat: plural of qut, which is provision; the word is applied to everything on which one feeds from the provision of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.
7. Tamara al-shay': he hid it and concealed it. Matmur: a passive participle from tamara, meaning hidden and concealed; the intended meaning is the bounties of Allah hidden within the earth, awaiting Allah's permission to appear.
8. The fragile thing that is not cohesive: "hashama al-shay' al-yabis hashman" means he broke the dry thing into pieces. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿...like the crushed stubble of the one who builds the enclosure﴾ (54:31) [al-Qamar], meaning like the broken firewood and wood crushed in the hand of the dying man, i.e., the maker of the pen. [al-Qamus al-Qawim p. 303, abridged].
9. This experience is the spiritual training (al-tarid al-imani): the Muslim who abandons sins and adorns himself with acts of obedience is illuminated by Allah with overflowing bounties and breezes of grace.
10. This is because Yusuf, peace be upon him, after his brothers recognised him, said to them: ﴿He said: "No reproach upon you today; may Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. Go with this shirt of mine and throw it over my father's face; he will regain his sight. And bring me your whole family."﴾ (12:92–93) ... ﴿When the caravan departed, their father said: "Indeed I smell the scent of Yusuf, if you did not think me senile."﴾ (12:94). That is, "unless you think me to be in error of judgment and senile."
11. Nudhur: plural of nadhir, meaning the Messenger with his proofs, signs and demonstrations.
12. Khalaw: passed on and preceded. That is, what they await in their disbelief is only the like of the punishment and chastisement that befell the nations that came before them. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn p. 188].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 102:

And those who do not believe remain in their transgression, wandering in confusion (1), as though they await that the events of those who came before them and did not believe will recur with them. The Messenger has come to them with clear proof, like all the deniers before them.

We know that the day (2) is a unit of time: after it comes the week, after the week the month, then the year. And as humankind advances, it divides the day into hours, divides the hours into minutes, and divides the minutes into seconds.

As events progress through time, we find measures becoming more precise. The day, as we have said, was made by Allah, glorified and exalted be He, a unit of time, consisting of night and day.

However, the day may be mentioned while what is meant is the notable events that took place within it, as when we say: "the Day of Dhu Qarad" (3), "the Day of Hunayn" (4), and "the Day of Uhud."

So the day may be meant as the prominent event that occurred in it. When we look into history and find a book called "The Days of the Arabs" (Ayyam al-Arab), we find "the Day of Bu'ath" (5) and "the Day of Awtas" (6), and each day represents a war.

Thus the day is a temporal frame, but it may be intended to mean the event that took place on such a day.

An example of this: you may find someone from the contemporary era who lived in earlier times, who recalls the bygone days and says: "Prices were low in the past, and everything was available," and someone responds to him saying: "Those were days," meaning: they were days of prosperity in which it occurred.

So the day may be attributed to the event that happened in it.

Here the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿Then do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?...(102)﴾ [Yunus].

Among those who passed away were the people of Noah, peace be upon him, whom Allah drowned, and the people of Pharaoh, whom Allah, exalted be He, also drowned.

And Allah, glorified be He, says: ﴿So each We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those seized by the Shout, and among them those We caused the earth to swallow, and among them those We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.(40)﴾ [al-Ankabut]: these are days in which events occurred that they know of. So do they await days like these?

Of course, it was not proper for them to acquiesce in disbelief, lest calamities like those that befell those who preceded them into disbelief recur with them.

In colloquial speech we find the natural proverb that expresses the faith of human nature, as you hear someone say: "There will be a day for you, O oppressor," meaning that the day on which Allah, exalted be He, takes vengeance on the oppressor becomes a well-known day, because the oppressor only transgresses against the creatures of Allah. Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, brings upon him a mighty event in which Allah afflicts him and makes him taste the sum of what he inflicted upon people by oppression. As for His saying, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿...Say: Then wait, indeed I am with you among those who wait.(102)﴾ [Yunus]: His saying here, ﴿Then wait﴾, contains a threat, and His saying ﴿indeed I am with you among those who wait(102)﴾ contains good tidings, because the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, will await that day to see their punishment, while for him, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, victory will be realized on that day.

1 Yu'mihun (يعمهون): they wander in confusion and hesitation in misguidance. Ibn al-Athir said: confusion (al-'amah) in insight is like blindness in sight. [Lisan al-Arab, root '-m-h].

2 Al-yawm (اليوم): in astronomy, it is the duration of one rotation of the earth around its axis, lasting twenty-four hours; its plural is ayyam. Ayyam al-Arab: their battles. Ayyam Allah: days in which His blessing and His punishment were manifested. [al-Qamus al-Qawim, p. 374].

3 Dhu Qarad (ذو قرد): a place with water in the land of Najd, at a distance of one day from Madinah on the side toward the lands of Ghatafan. Most books of biography hold that it occurred before al-Hudaybiyyah, while al-Bukhari in his Sahih held that it was three years before Khaybar, and mentioned it after al-Hudaybiyyah. See: Sirat Ibn Hisham (3/281) and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (4/178-193).

4 It occurred in the eighth year after the Hijrah, after the conquest of Makkah, and Allah, exalted be He, said concerning it: ﴿Certainly Allah has given you victory in many battlefields, and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you, despite its vastness, and you turned back retreating.(25)﴾ [al-Tawbah].

5 Yawm Bu'ath (يوم بعاث): a day on which the Aws and the Khazraj fought each other. Victory on that day went to the Aws over the Khazraj. The leader of the Aws that day was Hudayr ibn Simak al-Ashhali, father of Abu Usayd ibn Hudayr, and the leader of the Khazraj was Amr ibn al-Nu'man al-Bayadi, and both were killed. [Sirat Ibn Hisham 2/555].

6 The Day of Awtas is the same as the Day of Hunayn, and it occurred in the eighth year after the Hijrah, after the conquest of Makkah. Awtas: a valley in the abode of Hawazin, where the battle of Hunayn took place.

7 Al-hasib (الحصب): everything thrown into the fire to fuel it. Allah said: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel (hasab) for Hell...(98)﴾ [al-Anbiya']. Hasabahu: he pelted him with pebbles. Allah said: ﴿Or are you secure from He who is in the sky that He will send upon you a hasiban (violent wind carrying pebbles)...(17)﴾ [al-Mulk], that is, a fierce whirlwind that pelts you with pebbles and destroys you, and violent winds do even more than that.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Then We save Our messengers and those who believe. Thus it is incumbent upon Us: We shall save the believers.﴾

Allah, glorified is He, had previously saved His messengers and those who believed in them, so that the landmarks of truth and goodness would remain.

Among the landmarks of goodness and truth, there must necessarily remain the landmarks of evil, for were it not for the coming of evil in the events that afflict people, people would not have aspired to goodness.

We always say: the pain that afflicts the patient is one of the soldiers of wellbeing, because it alerts the person to the fact that there is an imbalance which must be sought a diagnosis for with the physician, and that he must find a treatment for it.

Pain exists in the hours of wakefulness and consciousness, but it disappears during sleep, and in sleep there is a self-restraint of pain.

His saying, glorified is He, here: ﴿Then We save Our messengers and those who believe. Thus it is incumbent upon Us: We shall save the believers﴾ [Yunus, 103]: this statement establishes the survival of the elements of goodness in this world.

Whenever people increase in disbelief, Allah, exalted is He, increases the support. In whatever land the faith is slandered, the believers are wronged and tyrants multiply, you will find in it some people devoted wholly to Allah, exalted is He, in order to comprehend the reality of values; and when the world becomes constricted for the wrongdoers and tyrants, you will find them going to these devoted servants of Allah and asking them to pray for them.

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has bound Himself to save the believers in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿...Thus it is incumbent upon Us: We shall save the believers﴾.

1: That is, Allah, glorified is He, has saved His previous messengers and those who believed with them from the punishment, and He will save the Prophet ﷺ and his companions and those who believe in him when the disbelievers and polytheists are punished. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn, p. 188, with adaptation]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 104:

Then the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Say: O people, if you are in doubt concerning my religion, then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, who causes you to die; and I have been commanded to be among the believers.﴾ (10:104)

Shakk (doubt) means: placing two matters on two equal pans of a balance.¹

Here, the Truthful, glorified is He, commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to present to the disbelievers the matter of the religion, and to place it on one pan, and to place on the opposite pan what they believe in.

He leaves the judgment to them in this matter.

They are, then, in doubt: is this religion true or false?

The Messenger's (ﷺ) presenting the matter of the religion for judgment means that the matter of religion is also noticed by any disbeliever, and he sometimes becomes aware of the value of the religion.

So: if you are in doubt about the religion that was sent down to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whether the Messenger (ﷺ) and those with him will be victorious over them, or they will have the upper hand?

When the Messenger (ﷺ) presents the matter of the religion to them and leaves the judgment to them, this is his (ﷺ) confidence that the matters of his religion, if a person looks at them to judge, then the person must incline toward faith.

The Truthful, glorified is He, settles the matter of associating partners with Him, and His command continues to the Messenger (ﷺ) to say: ﴿So I do not worship those you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah...﴾ (10:104). That is: he (ﷺ) cannot possibly worship the partners and worship Allah, because he will worship none but Allah: ﴿but I worship Allah﴾ (10:104).

Then He, glorified is He, brought the proof about which there is no dispute, the strong proof, which is that the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He alone is deserving of worship, because He is ﴿the One who causes you to die⁽³⁾﴾, and there is no one who can determine or resist the decree of Allah, glorified is He, when He causes him to die.

There are two matters here. The first: the matter of worship in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So I do not worship those you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah who causes you to die...﴾ (10:104).

It was necessary that both matters come together: the matter of the Messenger not worshipping those besides Allah, and the matter of Allah, exalted is He, being singled out alone for worship.

The separation is clear, determining the severing of relations between the camp of faith and the camp of polytheism, as He, glorified is He, stated in His saying: ﴿Say: O disbelievers. I do not worship what you worship. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾ (109:1-6). Those who say that there is repetition in Surah (al-Kafirun)⁽⁴⁾ do not pay attention to the fact that this matter is an emphasis on severing relations, so that this severing continues throughout all time; it is not a temporary severing of relations.⁽⁵⁾

This is the first severing of relations in Islam, in a decisive manner in which there is no opportunity for understanding or for compromise, and each camp remains in its state.

The Truthful, glorified is He, says in Surah an-Nasr: ﴿When the help of Allah comes and the victory, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt with praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ (110:1-3). Here the matter is confirmed: after the Messenger (ﷺ) severed relations with the camp of polytheism, the help of Allah, glorified is He, and His victory came, and the people hastened from the camp of polytheism to the camp of faith.⁽⁶⁾

So they came to faith. This is the first matter:

﴿So I do not worship those you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah...﴾ (10:104). They used to worship idols made of stone.

When you look at the kinds of creation in existence, the most honored of them is man, for whom the Truthful, glorified is He, subjected the rest of the kinds to be in his service. The kind lower than man is the animal. Then comes the kind lower in rank than man and animal, which is the plant. Then comes inanimate matter as the lowest kind in rank, and they have taken the lowest kinds as gods, and this is the peak of loss.

The second matter comes in the saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿...and I have been commanded to be among the believers⁽¹⁰⁴⁾﴾. So if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to worship those beneath Allah, glorified is He, this means that he will worship none but Allah, exalted is He.

This is not a negative position; rather it is the peak of affirmation, because worship requires receiving the method of Allah by obeying His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

¹ Shakk: the opposite of certainty (yaqin), its plural is shukuk. The Exalted said: ﴿Their messengers said: "Is there doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth?..."⁽¹⁰⁾﴾ [Ibrahim]. [Lisan al-Arab: root sh-k-k].

² Al-mira', al-mumara, al-tamarri and al-imtira': disputation and doubt. The Exalted said: ﴿...So do not argue concerning them except with an apparent argument, and do not inquire about them from any of them⁽²²⁾﴾ [al-Kahf]. And He said: ﴿Then will you dispute with him over what he sees?⁽¹²⁾﴾ [al-Najm]. Likewise al-miryah (with a kasra or damma on the mim), and He said: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it...⁽⁵⁵⁾﴾ [al-Hajj]. [Lisan al-Arab: root m-r-y], with adaptation.

³ Yatawaffakum: He causes them to die and seizes their souls. It derives from completing a number, meaning He seizes your souls entirely, so that not one of you is lacking. From this is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death...⁽⁴²⁾﴾ [az-Zumar], meaning He completes the term of their lives in this world. [Lisan: root w-f-y].

⁴ Surah al-Kafirun was revealed concerning a group of Quraysh who said: "O Muhammad, come, let us worship your god for a year and you worship our gods for a year. If what you have brought is better than what is in our hands, we will have shared in it and taken our share of it; and if what is in our hands is better than what is in yours, you will have shared in our affair and taken your share." He said: "I seek refuge in Allah from associating anything with Him." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Say: O disbelievers...⁽¹⁾﴾ to the end of the surah. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to the Sacred Mosque, where the chiefs of Quraysh were, and recited it to them until he finished the surah, and they despaired of him at that point. [Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 261].

⁵ The statements of the exegetes and scholars of our righteous predecessors all converge on what the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) stated here. Some of them, including al-Bukhari and others, said that what is meant by ﴿I do not worship what you worship⁽²⁾ nor are you worshippers of what I worship⁽³⁾﴾ is the past, and ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped⁽⁴⁾ nor are you worshippers of what I worship⁽⁵⁾﴾ is the future. Others said: this is pure emphasis. There is another view, supported by Imam Ibn Taymiyyah, that what is meant by His saying ﴿I do not worship what you worship⁽²⁾﴾ is negation of the act, since it is a verbal sentence, while ﴿nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped⁽⁴⁾﴾ is negation of his being suited to that at all, since negation by a nominal sentence is more emphatic; so it is as if he negated the act and its being within his capacity, and its meaning is negation of occurrence and also negation of legal possibility. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/561).

⁶ There was a span of more than 15 years between Surah al-Kafirun and Surah an-Nasr. Surah al-Kafirun was revealed at the beginning of the call, when Quraysh attempted to turn the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) away from continuing his call. Then the separation occurred, then the Hijrah, then the military campaigns, until Allah's victory was completed with the conquest of Makkah, and the people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and that was Surah an-Nasr. This confirms what the Shaykh stated about the extension of the severing of relations with the camp of polytheism, so that it encompasses all time with respect to the matter of faith, past, present and future.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 10, verse 105

Then Allah, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿And that you set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth (ḥanīfan), and never be among those who associate others with Allah.﴾

Since the address is directed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is, like every address from Allah, glorified is He, to His Messenger ﷺ, in fact an address containing a command for every believer.

When the believer worships Allah, glorified is He, he is receptive to His commands. For this reason the command here is that the face of the believing person should not turn to anything other than Allah, the Exalted. So Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿Set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth…﴾ [Yunus].

So he does not turn right or left in worship. Since the believer worships Allah and does not turn away from Him to anything else, the believer should know that there is also a hidden shirk (ash-shirk al-khafī), in which a person worships those who are stronger or richer than him, and other such persons by whom a person is tempted.

We have already come to know the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And who is better in religion (dīnan) than one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the creed (millah) of Abraham, inclining to truth (ḥanīfan)…﴾ [An-Nisa' 125]. Al-ḥanf (inclination) originally means a bending in the shin. You find some people, when they walk, their legs appear apart and their feet turned inward; this is a crookedness in the make-up.

As for what is meant here by the word ḥanīfan, it means: turning away from the crooked path, that is, he walks in uprightness.

But why does such an expression come?

Because the religion does not come with a new Messenger and a new miracle except when corruption has spread; so the religion comes to call people to turn away from this corruption. In this is the balancing of the conduct of individuals and society.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ warns us against falling into hidden shirk after believing in Allah, the Exalted.

The speech about this second shirk comes in the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿…and never be among those who associate others with Allah.﴾ [Yunus]. This second shirk is the least level of the shirk of worship, but it is that you assign to a human being, or to any thing, a role alongside Allah.

For example, if you see a role for the doctor or the medicine, say to yourself: the doctor is the one who prescribes the medicine as a healer, but Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who cures, as evidenced by the fact that the doctor may err once and order a medicine that causes harmful complications for the patient. The believer must not be tempted by any of the causes.

We mention another example of this: a country of wide agricultural land announced in one year that it had planted a large area of land with wheat sufficient for all the inhabitants of the earth; the ears sprouted and ripened. Then a violent wind came and destroyed the wheat crop, so that country was compelled to import its wheat from other countries.

¹ ḥanīfan: inclining away from all the paths and methods of misguidance, toward the path of truth alone.
² al-khafī (the hidden): it is showing off and seeking reputation and fame. On the authority of Shaddād ibn Aws, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The thing I fear most for my community is associating others with Allah. I do not say that they will worship the sun, the moon, or an idol; rather, [it is] deeds done for other than Allah, and hidden desire." Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4205).
³ ad-dīn (religion): obedience, submission, the law, recompense, creed, method, and the straight path [al-Qamus al-Qawim, abridged, p. 239].
⁴ al-millah (with a kasra on the m and a doubled l): the law and religion. Allah, exalted, says: ﴿…Indeed, I have left the creed of a people who do not believe in Allah and who are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers﴾ [Yusuf 37]. And Allah, exalted, says: ﴿The creed of your father Abraham; He named you "the Muslims" before [this]…﴾ [al-Hajj 78]. [Lisan al-Arab: root m-l-l], with adaptation.
⁵ al-ḥanf in the feet: the turning of each of the two feet toward the other with its big toe. A man is aḥnaf and a woman is ḥanfa', and by this "al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays" was named; his name was "Ṣakhr," because of a ḥanf that was in his foot. Al-Jawhari said: al-ḥanf is crookedness in the leg. Abu 'Amr said: al-ḥanīf is one who inclines from good to evil or from evil to good. One says ḥanafa 'an ash-shay' and taḥannafa: he turned away. Al-ḥanīf is the Muslim who turns away from the religions, that is, inclines toward truth; it is also said: he is the one who faces the qibla of the Sacred House upon the creed of Abraham, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet. Allah, exalted, says: ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was ḥanīfan, a Muslim…﴾ [Aal 'Imran 67]. It is also said: al-ḥanīf is the one who inclines away from error and distances himself from it in order to head toward truth; and this word has become a designation for the Muslims. [Lisan al-Arab: root ḥ-n-f, with adaptation].

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And do not invoke, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you nor harms you; for if you did, you would then be among the wrongdoers.﴾ (10:106)

Does the polytheist, from among these people, at the very moment he worships an idol and calls upon it besides Allah, the Exalted, get any response from it? And when he worships it, does the idol say to him: "Do this, and do not do that"?

Indeed, the idols which the polytheists have taken as gods have no method [of their own], and none of them benefits or harms. When benefit comes, the idol does not know how to prevent it, and when harm comes, the idol is unable to repel it.

So then: calling upon anyone besides Allah—glory be to Him and exalted—is a supplication to one who neither benefits nor harms.

And whoever does this will be among the wrongdoers, because injustice (ẓulm) is giving a right to one who has no right to it, whether it is at the summit [of wrongdoing] or below the summit.(1)

1 That is: whether it is injustice at the summit—namely, by associating partners with Allah—or injustice below the summit, by wronging people through taking their rights and transgressing against them.

The Almighty then says:

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it but He; and if He intends for you good, there is none to repel His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants, and He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.﴾ (10:107)

This is the speech of Lordship, which is free of need of creation. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, created people and called them to believe in Him and to love Him, because He loves them, gives to them, and takes nothing from them, for He is free of need of all His creation.

The mention of harm here is with the word "touch" (mass). ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it but He..﴾ (10:107). We know that there is "massa", "lamasa" and "isaba" (different verbs of touching and striking).

His saying, glorified is He, about harm here points to mere touching, that is, simple harm. Do not say: as long as the harm is small, creatures can bring it about. No one has power over harm or benefit, whether the harm be little or great, and whether the benefit be abundant or scant, except by permission from Allah, exalted is He.

The Almighty, glorified and exalted is He, mentions harm here with touching, that is, the lightest of contacts, and none removes it except Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

And of His greatness, exalted is He, is that He mentioned with touching the harm and the removal of it, and this is mercy.

Then He, glorified is He, comes with the opposite, which is "good." When the Almighty speaks of it, He affirms that none repels it.

We find the word ﴿yusibu﴾ (He causes to reach) in describing the coming of good to a human being: ﴿He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants﴾.

The Almighty concludes the verse with this beautiful ending in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿.. and He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.﴾ (10:107). Thus the image of the majesty of good manifested upon the servants becomes clear to us: in evil He touches with it and removes it, and in good He causes it to reach His servants and does not withhold it.

Allah, exalted is He, is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful, because if He dealt with people, even the believers among them, according to what they do, He would punish them. But He, glorified is He, is Forgiving and Merciful, because His mercy preceded His anger(1). Therefore we find Him, glorified is He, in verses of blessing saying: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it(2)..﴾ (16:18).

The Almighty used the conditional "in" (if) and did not say "idha" (when) — "if you count the favor of Allah" — because this is a matter that will not happen, just as the inclination to counting is a presumption that it might be enumerated. One may count money, and an observer may count the students of a school, but no one can count or enumerate the grains of sand, for example.

The Almighty said: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it.. (16:18)﴾. This is a doubt about your counting the favor of Allah.

It is remarkable that counting implies gathering, and gathering is of many things, yet He, glorified is He, used here the singular word ﴿ni'mah﴾ (favor) and did not say "ni'am" (favors), as if every single favor contains within it diverse favors.

So we will not be able to count the favors folded within one favor.

The Almighty mentioned the counting of favors in two verses. The first verse says: ﴿.. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is ever a wrongdoer and ungrateful(3) (14:34)﴾.

The second verse says: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful (16:18)﴾.

The beginnings of the two verses are the same, but the endings of each differ. In the first verse: ﴿.. Indeed, mankind is ever a wrongdoer and ungrateful (14:34)﴾, and in the second: ﴿.. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful (16:18)﴾. This is because a favor has a bestower and a recipient, and the recipient, by his sins, does not deserve the favor, since he is a wrongdoer and ungrateful. But the Bestower, glorified and exalted is He, is Forgiving and Merciful. So in one verse the focus is on the Bestower, and in the other the focus is on the recipient.
