As for the side of the one receiving the favor, we find him a great wrongdoer and ungrateful, because he takes the favor and does not thank Allah for it.

Did not the heaven say: "O Lord! Permit me to drop fragments upon the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks."

And the earth said: "Permit me to swallow up the son of Adam, for he has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks."

And the mountains said: "Permit me to fall upon the son of Adam."

And the sea said: "Permit me to drown the son of Adam, who has eaten of Your goodness and withheld Your thanks."

This is the universe, jealous for Allah, exalted is He, wishing to punish man. But Allah, glorified is He, Lord of all, says: "Leave Me with My servants; if you had created them, you would have shown them mercy. If they repent to Me, then I am their beloved; and if they do not repent, then I am their physician."

1. On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah decreed the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: Indeed, My mercy has overcome My anger." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3194) and Muslim (2751).
2. Al-ihsa': counting and enumerating.
3. Zalum: an intensive form of (zulm), meaning one who wrongs himself or others much, or both together. Kaffar: an intensive form of (kufr), meaning one who is extremely ungrateful. Kufr linguistically means covering, from covering a thing when one hides it. So it is as if the human, by not thanking Allah for the favor, has concealed it, that is, covered it up and not given its due of remembrance and thanks.

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿Say: "O mankind, the Truth has come to you from your Lord. Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own soul, and whoever goes astray, only goes astray to its detriment. And I am not a guardian over you."﴾ (108)

So, God the Exalted did not fall short with creation. He created for you the intellects (ʿuqūl), and it would have sufficed that you reflect with them to believe, without the coming of a messenger. These intellects were to reflect upon the Mighty One who created the whole universe. Rather, it is they who seek that the Mighty send them a messenger with what He, glorified is He, wants from His servants. So when a messenger comes to tell them that he is a messenger from God and bears the message from Him, their ears should have been alert to what he says.

So the servants were to be guided by their intellects. For this reason we find that the philosophers, when they sought knowledge, said: there is a "material philosophy" that tries to recognize the materiality of the universe, and there is a "metaphysical philosophy" (metaphysics, i.e. what lies beyond matter) that investigates what is behind matter.

So the philosophers, then, knew that there is something behind matter.

Indeed, the pure intellect, at the moment it sees the precise order of the universe, should have said: behind the visible, perceptible universe there is a hidden power.

The philosophers did not go on to investigate what lies behind matter except because they took from matter that behind it there is something concealed.

The concealed that lies behind matter is what declares itself; it is a matter we do not know by the intellect.

Long ago we gave an example of this, and we said: suppose we are sitting in a room, and the doorbell rings. Everyone in the room knows that someone is at the door, and none of them disagrees about that fact.

This is what the philosophers said when they acknowledged the existence of a power behind matter, but they exceeded their task and wanted to make us know the quiddity or reality of this power, and did not heed the self-evident truth that this power cannot be known by the intellect. For as long as we have known that someone is knocking at the door, we do not say "it is he," nor do we leave the matter to conjecture; rather, we leave it to him to define for us who he is and what he wants, because it is for him to inform about himself.

Ask him to declare his name and attributes; these are matters that cannot be known by the intellect.

So the error of the philosophers is that they did not stop at intellectually grasping that there is a power beyond matter, and they wanted to move from intellection to conception, whereas conceptions do not come through the intellect but through informing.

Here the Truthful One, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: "O mankind, the Truth has come to you from your Lord..."﴾ (108). The truth, as we know, is what is established and never changes at all. That the truth should come from the Lord who takes charge of nurturing, who created from nonexistence and provided ('amad) from ('adam)[^3], who does not impose upon us the obligations of faith except after maturity, who created the whole universe and made us vicegerents in it,

He, then, is trustworthy over us. If the truth comes from Him, glorified and exalted is He, then why do we not make the method (manhaj) part of the upbringing?

Why have we taken the upbringing of food and clothing and the dominance of races?

It was necessary, then, that we take from the Nurturer, glorified and exalted is He, the method by which we manage the movement of life, so that we do not corrupt it.

When the Truthful One says: ﴿The truth has come to you from your Lord..﴾ (108), the meaning is that no one has any excuse to say, "No one informed me of God's purpose," for the Truthful One has left the intellects to reason, not to conceive.

And conception came through the communication from God, exalted is He, when the Truthful One sent a messenger who says: I am a messenger from God, and He is the power that created the universe. And it was incumbent upon us, after his miracle was confirmed, to say to the messenger: Welcome, for you are the one we were seeking. Tell us: what does the Supreme Power want to communicate to us?

Then the Truthful One says in the same verse: ﴿Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own soul..﴾ (108),

because the outcome of his guidance does not return to the One who created and guided him, but returns to himself, in harmony with the universe, the reforming of the self's essence, peace of mind, tranquility, and attentiveness to cultivating the universe without corrupting it. This state is the opposite of what the one who has strayed from guidance lives.

The Truthful One says about this category of people: ﴿And whoever goes astray, only goes astray to its detriment..﴾ (108). The word ﴿ḍalla﴾ indicates that the person who goes astray once had a beginning of guidance, but he strayed from it.

The Truthful One concludes the verse by saying: ﴿And I am not a guardian over you.﴾ (108). You entrust a person only because your time does not suffice, and likewise your power, your knowledge, and your movement. Here the messenger informs the people: I am not able to ward off error from you or compel you to guidance, for I am not a guardian over you; rather, my only task is the communication (balāgh)[^5] from God, glorified and exalted is He. If you listen to this communication with hearts emptied of anything else, you will be guided.

And if you are guided, then the good is for you, for the reward will be eternal bliss that you receive in exchange for applying the method that restricts the desires of the soul, but it guides to a life of bliss that a person does not miss, and in which blessings do not escape a person.

If a person among us is willing to toil in order to learn a craft, a trade, a skill, or a profession, so that he may benefit from mastering that work for the rest of his life,

is it not incumbent upon this person to devote himself to the worship that sets his mind right and hastens him toward the goal, in harmony with the self and with society, and as a refinement and correction of the desires of the soul, and that he thereafter attain the eternal bliss of the Hereafter?

As for the one who considers it too much for himself to strive and exert effort in acquiring knowledge or learning a profession or craft, he lives in constriction and lack of advancement, for he does not exert effort in learning.

We see the one who learns and exerts effort rising in social and economic standing, so that he reaches, for example, the level of a doctorate, or a precise specialization that brings him abundant provision.

And whenever the fruit that a person desires is more ripened (ʾaynaʿ)[^6] and lasting, the service for its sake is longer.

Compare your service to your religion in this world with what awaits you of the bliss of the Hereafter, and you will find the distance between the gifts of this world and the gifts of the Hereafter vast, with no comparison.

As for the Truthful One's saying: ﴿...whoever goes astray, only goes astray to its detriment (ʿalayhā)..﴾ (108): you find in it the word ﴿ʿalayhā﴾, which indicates dominance over the self, i.e., by straying—God forbid—you dominate your own self and drive your head down into the abyss.

On the other hand, you find the Truthful One's saying: ﴿Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own soul..﴾ (108).

And you find that the "lām" here indicates possession; therefore it is said: "So-and-so has it (lahu)" and "So-and-so has it against him (ʿalayhi)."

[^1]: al-Wakīl: the guarantor entrusted with people's provision and affairs, and the guardian who preserves people's deeds. God the Exalted said: ﴿...And We did not make you a guardian over them, nor are you a trustee (wakīl) over them (107)﴾ [al-Anʿām], and God the Exalted negated this from His Prophet and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ)...
[^2]: Philosophy: a Greek word meaning the search for truth. Metaphysics: what is beyond nature and the cosmos, i.e., the unseen matters that are not subject to the laws of matter...
[^3]: al-ʿAdam, al-ʿUdm, and al-ʿUdm: the loss of a thing and its disappearance. Similar in the vowelling of the letters of the word: al-Rushd and al-Rushd; al-Ḥuzn and al-Ḥuzn. Similar is the Exalted's saying: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become distinct from error...(256)﴾ [al-Baqara]. And the Exalted's saying: ﴿...Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance (rushd)(10)﴾ [al-Kahf]...
[^4]: al-Ḥaqq: the established, firm matter, the opposite of falsehood (bāṭil). al-Ḥaqq is among the Most Beautiful Names of God; al-Ḥaqq is the Qur'an; al-Ḥaqq is justice, truthfulness, wisdom, resurrection, and the perfection of the matter; al-Ḥaqq is the established reality in which there is no disagreement. The Exalted said: ﴿Surely, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Surely the promise of God is true, but most of them do not know (55)﴾ [Yūnus]. Al-Ḥaqq is what is obligatory upon you for another [al-Qāmūs al-Qawmī, adapted, pp. 164–165].
[^5]: This is affirmed in many verses of the Qur'an, including the Exalted's saying: ﴿But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them; your duty is only the communication (balāgh)(48)﴾ [al-Shūrā]. And the Exalted said: ﴿...And upon the Messenger is only the clear communication (balāgh al-mubīn)(54)﴾ [al-Nūr]. So all that is required of the Messenger is to convey his message, and that this communication be clear, manifest, and evident...
[^6]: ʾaynaʿa: to ripen. And al-yanʿ: ripeness. From it is the Exalted's saying: ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and its ripening (yanʿihi)(99)﴾ [al-Anʿām]...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 10, verse 109 (part 1 of 2):

After that, the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says at the close of Surah Yunus:
{And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges, and He is the best of judges (109).}

Since the Truthful One, glory be to Him, has placed on the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ) the words ﴿O mankind, the Truth has certainly come to you from your Lord...﴾ (108) [Yunus], this means conveying the theoretical method of Allah, the Exalted. People must trust the method, and the Messenger must be the first to put the method into practice. For, God forbid, if he deceived all the people, he would not have deceived himself.

So, after the conveying (1) from the Truthful One, and informing people that the guidance does not return its benefit to the Truth but to the human being, who thereby possesses himself and possesses the reins of his life, so that he walks with peace of mind in this world toward the bliss of the Hereafter, and that misguidance returns only through a person's domination over himself, so that he rides himself to the places of destruction:

The Messenger (ﷺ) is not your agent, bringing you good when you do no good, and turning away evil from you while you do what deserves evil.

It was incumbent upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to be the model and the example:
﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often (21)﴾ [al-Ahzab].

Here the Truthful One says: ﴿And follow what is revealed to you... (109)﴾ [Yunus]. That is: it is incumbent upon you to be the example. When you follow what is revealed to you, you will encounter obstacles from those who live on corruption and are not pleased that reform should exist. So resolve firmly to follow what is revealed to you, and to be patient. The command to be patient is evidence that there are many obstacles, and you must be patient and give the example to others (4), with confidence that if there were no good in following the method, you would not have endured it, until the judgment of Allah comes: ﴿...and be patient until Allah judges...(109)﴾ [Yunus]. There is no one more just or more judicious than Allah, glory be to Him.

This surah, which ends with this noble verse, addressed the matter of faith in Allah, the pinnacle of the belief in one God, from whom we must receive the message, glory be to Him, because He is the Lord who created from non-existence, and sustained from non-existence. He did not impose duties upon us except after the passing of the years of childhood until maturity, so that He might be certain that the one charged deserves to be charged, after he has benefited from the good things of the whole existence, and has confirmed the truth of lordship.

The meaning of lordship (rububiyyah) is upbringing (tarbiyah), and that the one who nurtures brings the one nurtured to the perfection that is hoped for from him.

This matter has been confirmed in the universe.

So, let us listen to the Lord, glory be to Him, who created, when He explains to us our mission in life through a method by which the movement of life is set right, and by which the affairs of the human being are set right with the goal that he knows before he takes any step.

It is impossible that the Creator, glory be to Him, would create the creature and then neglect it; rather, He must lay down for it a law for preserving itself (5). For every craft, its maker establishes its law and determines its purpose from its making. If we oppose that, we would have altered (6) and changed affairs, and introduced the world into labyrinths, and every person would have his own goal and his own method, and every mind its own thought, and the universe would become contradictory, because desires would clash, and the strength of individuals would weaken, because the struggle between rivals (7) weakens the power of the individual to deal with the matter that must be dealt with.

Therefore Allah, glory be to Him, willed unity (8) in belief and unity in method.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, also willed to set before us an applied example across the procession of the messages. So in this surah He mentioned to us the story of Noah, peace be upon him, and the story of Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them both, and He mentioned between them other stories.

Then He mentioned the case of Prophet Yunus, peace be upon him.

Then He concluded the surah with His words, glory be to Him: ﴿And follow what is revealed to you... (109)﴾ [Yunus], as a conveying from Allah, the Exalted.

And as long as you convey, and your nation is a nation reckoned, until the Hour, as the inheritor of prophethood, and there is no prophethood after you, O Muhammad (ﷺ), with abundant peace.

The Truthful One also willed that your nation should carry the call to the method that was sent down to you. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will be a witness that he has conveyed, and the nation must be a witness that it has conveyed and delivered the message of Allah to the world (9). This is the honour of the mission of the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

No other nation has possessed this honour. Before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the call of any messenger would weaken, its obligations would grow dim (10), and people would become heedless of it, so Allah, glory be to Him, would send another messenger. But the matter changed after the message of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. There is no longer any prophethood or messengerhood, but there are now those who carry the method of Allah, the Exalted.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the example, because he is the conveyer of the method of Allah, and he is the example in applying the law of preserving the human being and his movement, and the applied model, so that people are not burdened beyond what their humanity can bear. For this reason he insisted that he was a human being, and the Noble Qur'an made this clear without any ambiguity: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you...(6)﴾ [Fussilat], to confirm the truth of the example. For if he (ﷺ) were not a human being and asked people to do as he did, they would say: "We cannot, because you are not like us."

For this reason we note that the Qur'an emphasises the humanity of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but he (ﷺ) surpasses humans by the choice of Allah, glory be to Him, to be a messenger to whom revelation is sent. His first messengerly duty is to convey this revelation, and his second duty is to confirm through his conduct that he is convinced of this revelation and applies it to himself.

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example (11)...(21)﴾ [al-Ahzab].

In terms of wealth, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among the least of people in possessions. He was not arrogant nor tyrannical. He was a behavioural model in which all virtues were balanced. He did not seek anything for himself; indeed, he withheld from his relatives and family rights which he had established for others among the Muslims. His relatives were not granted the right to inherit anything of what he owned after his death, and he deprived them of it, so that every act proceeding from him (ﷺ), or from those who are related to him, would be an act done purely for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.

This conduct is the opposite of the conduct of human authorities and temporal powers. These authorities, first of all, overflow with good upon themselves, then they pour it out upon the circles nearest to them according to degrees of nearness. The one closest takes first and most, and whoever is more distant in kinship takes less according to the degree of his distance.

But whoever is within the circle of kinship with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not take even what a poor person in the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) takes. It is as if Allah, glory be to Him, is showing us by this that it is shameful for a person to be attributed to the household of the Prophethood and to be a recipient of zakat.

So, the following that Allah commanded is the following of revelation in conveying, and following what is revealed in application. This will require facing many hardships, and the one who follows will meet obstacles from the tyrants who profit from corruption on earth. They will necessarily oppose these callings in order to preserve their temporal power. So the Truthful One, glory be to Him, commands His Messenger (ﷺ) to be patient, and in the command to be patient there is an indication that the Messenger (ﷺ) is facing obstacles, so let him prepare himself to bear these obstacles with patience (12).

And in another verse, the Truthful One commands him to be patient and to persevere, he and the believers. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿O you who believe, be patient and endure and remain steadfast (13)...(200)﴾ [Al 'Imran]. That is: if you are patient, your opponent may also be patient, so here you must outlast him. The word "be patient" makes clear that the callers to the method of the Truthful One, glory be to Him, must encounter hardships. Otherwise there would be no need for it to come. For if the world were moving straight, what need would there be for a method?

But the method has come, because corruption has spread over the universe, and it needs reform, and it needs confrontation with the corrupters. This is what burdens those who call to Allah, the Exalted. Let every caller prepare himself for this, since he has risen to call to the method of the Truthful One, glory be to Him.

Every caller to Allah who is not harmed by anything has his share of the inheritance of prophethood reduced, because the one who suffers harm is the one who takes a share of the inheritance of prophethood. Harm comes only in proportion to the danger the caller to Allah, glory be to Him, poses to corruption and the corrupters, and they are the ones who gather against him.

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah make radiant the man who hears my saying, understands it, preserves it and conveys it, for many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to one who understands better than he does" (16).

So, we, the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), have inherited from him the conveying, and we have inherited from him the excellent example: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often (21)﴾ [al-Ahzab].

So the saying of the Truthful One, glory be to Him: ﴿And follow what is revealed to you... (109)﴾ [Yunus] is evidence that revelation is in the process of being sent down, because the Qur'an was not revealed all at once. Rather, revelation kept descending upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) throughout his life (17).

Thus the life of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the station of receiving revelation.

The saying of the Truthful One: ﴿...and be patient until Allah judges... (109)﴾ [Yunus] clarifies for us that He, glory be to Him, has set a limit in which one hopes that the matter will not remain patience, and that the issue will be decided soon by a judgment from Allah, the Exalted.

The word ﴿judges﴾ makes clear that there are two parties, each claiming to be in the right, then someone comes to decide the case. The proof is either confession or witnesses. Naturally the disbelievers will not confess to their disbelief, and witnesses may be upright, or they may be among those who conceal their wickedness behind an outward appearance of uprightness. If Allah, glory be to Him, is the Judge, He does not need witnesses, because He is the best of witnesses. And Allah, glory be to Him, does not merely judge without the capacity to enforce the judgment; rather, He judges and enforces.

So, He, glory be to Him, has witnessed, judged and executed, and no power can stand before the power of Allah, the Exalted, or stand before the judgment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

In our time we see powers differing. We find a strong state that has dominated a weak one, so the weak turns to the United Nations and the Security Council, and each of them issues resolutions. Even if we assume the justice of the ruling, where is the power of enforcement? It does not exist.

But the power of the Supreme Truth, glory be to Him, is the power of the best of judges, because He, glory be to Him, is the one who witnesses, and He does not need anyone to deceive Him in testimony, for if you conceal yourself from the judgment of the earth, you will not conceal yourself from the judgment of heaven (18).

After that, the Truthful One judges with a judgment free of desire, because the bane of judgments is that desire enters them and makes them lean. The Truthful One, glory be to Him, has no desire, because He has no interest among His servants. He is the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, and He will not take any benefit from a creature (19).

The Truthful One reassures us that His Messenger (ﷺ) also does not speak from desire.

The Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire (20) (3). It is only a revelation that is revealed (4)﴾ [al-Najm]. That is: be reassured by his judgment, because he does not speak from desire. There is nothing in himself that he wishes to achieve except calling creatures to worship the Creator well, glory be to Him.

Someone may say: "But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, altered some rulings for the Messenger."

We say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would exercise independent reasoning (ijtihad) by his humanity in matters where Allah had not sent down a ruling. When Allah sends down a ruling, he (ﷺ) submits to the command of Allah, the Exalted. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not judge even in what he had reasoned about out of desire; rather, he judged by what he saw to be just. And when the Truthful One, the Exalted, sends down a different ruling, he conveys it to the Muslims and amends the judgment.

So, the amending of a ruling is the pinnacle of trustworthiness in conveying from Allah, glory be to Him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)

(1) Al-balagh: a verbal noun meaning sufficiency, or informing/conveying. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿This is a message for mankind, that they may be warned by it...(52)﴾ [Ibrahim]. And He says: ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship (106)﴾ [al-Anbiya], i.e., in what has been mentioned of reports and admonitions. The balagh of a thing is its limit and final point which it reaches, or its measure at which it ends. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿That is the extent of their knowledge (30)﴾ [al-Najm]. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim, adapted, 1/84, 83].

(2) Al-uswah: capability, and the highest model to be followed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is our example and our capability. God, glory be to Him, also said about Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah...(4)﴾ [al-Mumtahanah]. Then He said: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day...(6)﴾ [al-Mumtahanah].

(3) The word al-raja' (hope) occurs in the Qur'an with several meanings:
- One of them is seeking and hope for something to be achieved, such as His saying: ﴿Those hope for the mercy of Allah...(218)﴾ [al-Baqarah], and His saying: ﴿And women past child-bearing who do not hope for marriage...(60)﴾ [al-Nur].
- Another is fear, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us and are satisfied with the worldly life and at ease therein, and those who are heedless of Our signs (7), for those, their refuge is the Fire because of what they used to earn (8)﴾ [Yunus].

(4) He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So be patient as the steadfast messengers were patient...(35)﴾ [al-Ahqaf]. So patience is following the great messengers, who endured the harm of their peoples with a patience beyond the capacity of humans, such as Noah, Moses, Jesus, Abraham and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

(5) He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected (36)?﴾ [al-Qiyamah]. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (4/452): "The verse encompasses both states, i.e., he is not left in this world neglected, neither commanded nor forbidden, nor left in his grave neglected, not resurrected; rather, he is commanded and forbidden in this world, and gathered to Allah in the Hereafter."

(6) Ahalna al-umur: we have turned and changed affairs from the purpose for which they were set. In Lisan al-Arab: everything that has changed from straightness to crookedness has "hala" (deviated) and "istaha" (become altered). It is said: the man "hala" (turns) "yahul," like "tahawwala" (moved) from one place to another. [Root: h-w-l].

(7) Al-andad: the equals and peers.

(8) The messages in their essence proceed with monotheism, and upon it and by it. The Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein..."(13)﴾ [al-Shura].

(9) God, the Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger a witness over you...(143)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty; the religion of your father Abraham. He named you "Muslims" before, and in this [Revelation], that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer, give zakat, and hold firmly to Allah; He is your protector—and excellent is the protector and excellent is the helper (78)﴾ [al-Hajj].

(10) That is: the time lengthens upon them, so the message of the Messenger is forgotten, and distortion, alteration and change occur in it. Much of this happened to the Children of Israel.

(11) Al-uswah and al-iswah: the example/model. It is said: "i'tasi bihi," i.e., follow him and be like him. Al-Layth said: "So-and-so emulates so-and-so," i.e., he is pleased for himself with what pleases the other and follows him. Al-Harawi said: "Ta'assa bihi": he followed his action and imitated him. [Lisan al-Arab: root (a-s-a)].

(12) The Truthful One, glory be to Him, has been preparing His Prophet (ﷺ) for this, such as in His saying: ﴿And messengers before you were denied, but they were patient over what they were denied and were harmed until Our victory came to them. And there is no changer of the words of Allah. And there has already come to you some information about the messengers (34)﴾ [al-An'am].

(13) Be steadfast in obedience and in trials, and be steadfast against sins. And outlast the disbelievers, so that they are not more steadfast than you. And "rabitu," i.e., strive and persist in it and continue upon it. [Tafsir al-Jalalayn, p. 64]. The form "sabir" (on the pattern of "fa'il") indicates intensity of the act and exaggeration in it, i.e., intensity of patience and endurance, and persistence upon it until reaching the goal.

١٤ *al-Nadara* (radiance): the brightness and light of the face.

١٥ *Wa'aha*: he preserved it. He was like a vessel (*wi'a*) that holds what is put into it, even if he did not grasp its details.

١٦ Al-Tirmidhi reported it in his *Sunan* (2658), and Abu Nu'aym in *Hilyat al-Awliya'* (7/331), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

١٧ That is, it was revealed in stages (*munajjaman*), according to circumstances and events. This made the Qur'an, for the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fresh and moist, because it was revealed in a manner suited to their condition. It is well known that the Qur'an had another descent, when it was sent down all at once from the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*) to the lowest heaven. See *al-Itqan fi 'Ulum al-Qur'an* (1/116).

١٨ From Umm Salama, who said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "heard a dispute at the door of his room, so he went out to them and said: 'I am only a human being, and disputants come to me. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent than another, so I think he has spoken truthfully and I decide in his favour accordingly. Whomever I give, by judgment, a right belonging to a Muslim, it is only a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it.'" Reported by al-Bukhari in his *Sahih* (2458) and Muslim (1713).

١٩ He, glorified be He, says: ﴿It is not their flesh nor their blood that reaches Allah, but it is your piety that reaches Him﴾ [al-Hajj 22:37]. Allah, the Exalted, is free of need from all else. The people of the Jahiliyya, when they slaughtered their offerings and sacrificial animals for their idols, would place some of the flesh of their sacrifices on the altars and sprinkle their blood upon them. So the Mighty and Majestic made clear that what reaches Allah from them is piety and the sincerity of the heart towards Allah. (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/224, adapted.)

٢٠ *Al-Hawa*: the desire of the soul, its inclination and its love for something. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And he who restrains the soul from its desire﴾ [al-Nazi'at 79:40], meaning, prevents it from sins and appetites. When *hawa* is mentioned without qualification, it is only blameworthy, unless it is described in a way that removes it from that meaning, as when people say "a good desire" (*hawan hasan*) or "a desire that agrees with what is right." What is meant by the word in this verse is the blameworthy desire. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿So do not follow [your] desires, lest you depart from justice﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:135]. He says: ﴿So judge between the people in truth, and do not follow [your] desire, for it will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾ [Sad 38:26]. He says: ﴿Have you seen one who takes his own desire as his god?﴾ [al-Furqan 25:43]. He says: ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah?﴾ [al-Qasas 28:50]. He says: ﴿And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before﴾ [al-Ma'ida 5:77]. He says: ﴿And indeed, many lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge﴾ [al-An'am 6:119]. [Lisan al-'Arab, root (h-w-y), adapted.]
